author: Alfredo Seguel
title: Comunidad Kawésqar recuerda al Estado chileno los siete mil años de vida marítima como pueblo: ¿Usos consuetudinarios o lo que significa vivir el mar?
content:
La Comunidad Indígena Kawésqar Grupos Familiares Nómades del Mar publicó un artículo de opinión en el que reivindica más de 7,000 años de vida marítima, rechaza la salmonicultura por destruir el ecosistema del que dependen y advierte que el Estado verificará sus usos consuetudinarios en las próximas semanas. Exigen que ese reconocimiento no sea contradictorio.


“Vivir el mar no es folclore”: la comunidad kawésqar reivindica 7.000 años de vida marítima y advierte que la salmonicultura “rompe el círculo”


La Comunidad Indígena Kawésqar Grupos Familiares Nómades del Mar publicó un artículo de opinión titulado “Usos consuetudinarios o lo que significa vivir el mar”, en el que reivindica más de 7.000 años de vida marítima y advierte que la salmonicultura “rompe el círculo” ecológico del que depende su cultura. El texto, firmado por la propia comunidad, sostiene que para el pueblo kawésqar un uso consuetudinario “no es un dato que se anota en un formulario”, sino “la manera en que hemos vivido el mar durante más de siete mil años, y que seguimos viviendo hoy”. Y aclara: “

No es folclore que se muestra en una fecha, ni una costumbre del pasado que se recuerda con nostalgia

“.


El artículo describe las prácticas que sostienen esa forma de vida: navegar como pueblo canoero, pescar “lo justo, cuando hace falta, para seguir camino”, recolectar en la marea baja, bucear en apnea “como bucearon nuestras abuelas”, tejer el junquillo, tomar del bosque alimento y medicina, levantar el At y encender fuegos “donde hubo campamentos antiguos” para transmitir a los niños la memoria de quiénes son. “Cada una de estas prácticas es una hebra; ninguna se entiende sola, así son nuestras economías”, subraya la comunidad, que enfatiza que en su cosmovisión “todo está conectado” y que “el mar y la tierra no son dos cosas: son un mismo cuerpo del que formamos parte”.


La comunidad aclara que su forma de vivir el mar “es compatible con casi todo lo que ocurre en el borde costero” —pesca artesanal, pesca recreativa, navegación, turismo respetuoso e investigación científica— y desmiente que un Espacio Costero “expulse a alguien” o “levante un cerco sobre las aguas”: “Quien diga que pedir nuestro reconocimiento es cerrar el mar, miente, y lo sabe”.


La única actividad con la que no pueden convivir, afirman, es la salmonicultura, porque “carga el agua de materia orgánica hasta dejar el fondo sin oxígeno, vuelca antibióticos que alteran la vida marina, y sus escapes de salmones golpean a las especies nativas de las que dependemos”. Te invitamos a leer el artículo completo a continuación.


Usos consuetudinarios o lo que significa vivir el mar


Para nuestro la comunidad kawésqar, un uso consuetudinario no es un dato que se anota en un formulario. Es la manera en que hemos vivido el mar durante más de siete mil años, y que seguimos viviendo hoy. No es folclore que se muestra en una fecha, ni una costumbre del pasado que se recuerda con nostalgia. Es lo que hacemos cuando navegamos nuestros canales, al bajar a las riveras, sumergirnos en el agua o en el bosque. Vivir el mar, para nosotros, es todo eso junto, y no se puede separar en partes sin dejar de ser lo que es.


Navegamos, como lo hizo siempre un pueblo canoero, y mientras navegamos pescamos lo que necesitamos: no una faena industrial, sino lo justo, cuando hace falta, para seguir camino. Recolectamos en la marea baja, entre las rocas, el erizo y el marisco que el mar deja al descubierto. Buceamos en apnea, como bucearon nuestras abuelas, para alcanzar lo que la orilla no da. Recogemos el junquillo y lo tejemos, y en ese tejido —cestería, adornos— se sostiene no solo un oficio sino un bienestar del espíritu. Del bosque tomamos alimento y medicina, y los materiales con que se levanta el At, nuestra vivienda. Encendemos fuegos donde hubo campamentos antiguos, y alrededor de ellos traspasamos a los niños, hablando, la memoria de quiénes somos. Cazamos, también, como parte de esta vida. Cada una de estas prácticas es una hebra; ninguna se entiende sola, así son nuestras economías.


Porque en nuestra cosmovisión todo está conectado. De lo humano se pasa a lo animal, y de lo animal al territorio, en un círculo que no se puede romper. El mar y la tierra no son dos cosas: son un mismo cuerpo del que formamos parte. Por eso cuidar el territorio no es para nosotros una política ambiental, sino una forma de cuidarnos a nosotros mismos. Dañar el agua es dañar al pez, y dañar al pez es dañarnos. Esa es …

author: Kodao Productions
title: Migrant leader urges evacuation plan for OFWs in Riyadh
content:
A veteran migrant leader called on the Ferdinand Marcos Jr. government to immediately craft an evacuation plan for overseas Filipino workers (OFW) caught in the escalating war between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis of Yemen.


Migrante International chairperson emeritus Garry Martinez said the Philippine government must ensure that all the needs of the victims—as well as those of their families in the Philippines—are fully met.


Martinez issued the demand after the Houthis hit King Khalid International Airport with missiles since Friday, killing 12 and injuring at least 300 passengers and airport staff, including four Filipinos.


Three of the Filipinos sustained serious injuries requiring intensive hospital care, various media reports said.


“We urge Marcos to make public the evacuation blueprint in the event that the situation in the Middle East escalates,” Martinez said.


The leader said a comprehensive plan by the government is needed as the situation shows no sign of de-escalation.


“The government should stop thinking of potential remittance loss in this situation. The lives of OFWs are most important,” he said.


Philippine carriers suspend flights to Saudi


Meanwhile, Philippine Airlines (PAL) has extended its cancellation of flights between Manila and Riyadh until November 29, the country’s flag carrier announced on Monday, citing the “evolving security situation at Riyadh’s airport.”


PAL first canceled flights PR654 and PR655 last week. “(We) continue to closely monitor developments and assess conditions affecting the safe operation of its flights. Further updates will be provided as necessary,” PAL noted.


Josh Vasquez, PAL Middle East regional head, said Monday that flights from Manila to Dubai and Doha are operating as scheduled.


Budget airline Cebu Pacific (CEB) also extended flight suspensions between Manila and Riyadh as King Khalid International Airport announced operation stoppages until October 17.


“As this is a developing situation, some flight changes may take place in the next few days. We encourage passengers to regularly check their flight status and to update their contact details via the manage booking portal to receive timely flight notifications. We will continue to assess our Middle East flight operations and provide updates as necessary,” CEB added. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

content:
Canan Kebenç Özkan, Co-Spokesperson of the Democratic Local Governments Board of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the approach of local governments to the process, communal life, and Abdullah Öcalan’s status and position.


Canan Kebenç Özkan said the call for Peace and Democratic Society issued by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February had marked a new stage in the conflict, opening a period in which the Kurdish question must be resolved through peaceful means, on a democratic basis and through democratic politics, rather than through conflict.


Özkan said society was undergoing change and transformation, rebuilding itself on a democratic basis, while the state was becoming more responsive to society and democracy. However, she pointed out that the process was encountering obstacles at certain stages.


‘Öcalan’s role is vital’


Canan Kebenç Özkan said Abdullah Öcalan’s role could not be overlooked at this critical stage of the process, stressing that his contribution must be given the recognition it deserves.


Özkan said: “Öcalan’s vital role in this process absolutely cannot be ignored. His role must be properly recognised. At the same time, people across Kurdistan have very high expectations of the process. There is a strong social expectation that lasting peace will be achieved and a democratic foundation established.”


‘Öcalan’s voice must reach the Turkish public’


Canan Kebenç Özkan stressed that Abdullah Öcalan’s voice must reach the Turkish public for the process to advance successfully, achieve its ultimate goal, secure lasting peace and build a democratic society.


Özkan also said: “Öcalan’s role is vital for this process, of which we are all a part, to advance successfully, reach its ultimate goal, establish lasting peace and build a democratic society. First and foremost, Öcalan’s voice must reach the Turkish public. He must be able to meet with journalists, intellectuals and civil society organisations, and maintain contact with his own organisation in a way that enables the implementation of the law as the process of ending the conflict progresses.


For this reason, Öcalan must be provided with conditions in which he can live and work freely as soon as possible, participate directly in the process and oversee its progress. We believe that he must personally carry out this role, particularly in coordinating peace, disarmament and strategy.”


‘Öcalan’s freedom is a key factor in public trust in the process’


Canan Kebenç Özkan said people now wanted Abdullah Öcalan’s physical freedom to be secured and regarded it as one of the most important factors in their trust in the process.


Özkan continued: “The authorities must act immediately to prevent the process from being unnecessarily prolonged and ultimately derailed once again. As local governments, we continue to participate in and organise the actions and events organised by our party. However, the main demand we encounter in our meetings and activities with the public is very clear: People want to see Öcalan free. They believe this is one of the fundamental factors determining their trust in the process.”


‘The public’s main expectations are lasting peace and Öcalan’s freedom’


Canan Kebenç Özkan said the public’s foremost expectation was for peace to become lasting, stressing that one of the essential conditions for achieving this was Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom.


Özkan said: “The public’s most fundamental expectation from the process is lasting peace. One of the essential conditions for this is Öcalan’s freedom. People also want society to be rebuilt democratically and the state to become more responsive to society’s understanding of democracy and that of local communities. In Kurdistan, people want to live as free and equal citizens, with their own language, religion and beliefs. They demand a life of fraternity based on equal citizenship alongside Turkish, Arab, Syriac and Alevi peoples.


Strengthening local democracy is also one of the public’s main expectations. People want the state to become more responsive to local democracy, the conflict between central and local authorities to be eliminated, and local communities to be able to govern themselves. Politically, the fundamental issue is ensuring that Öcalan can live and work freely and that lasting peace is achieved. This is also the foundation of trust in the process.”

author: groundxero
title: “ভোট আমাদের অধিকার, তা এত সহজে কেড়ে নেওয়া যাবে না” – কলকাতার মিছিলে যন্তর-মন্তরের বহুস্বরের প্রতিধ্বনি
content:
মুখ্য নির্বাচন কমিশনার জ্ঞানেশ কুমারের পদত্যাগ ও এসআইআর প্রক্রিয়া বাতিলের দাবিতে আটটি বাম ছাত্র সংগঠনেরর উদ্যোগে ১১ অক্টোবর, কলকাতার শিয়ালদহ থেকে ধর্মতলা পর্যন্ত এক দীর্ঘ মিছিল সংঘটিত হয়।


 


সুদর্শনা চক্রবর্তী

প্রতিবেদন


 


একটা মিছিল মানে জনরাশি। যেখানে প্রতিটি ব্যক্তি মানুষের চিন্তাচেতনা কোথাও গিয়ে একটি সাধারণ বিন্দুতে মিলেছে বলেই তারা পা মেলাচ্ছেন জোটবদ্ধ হয়ে, মুষ্ঠিবদ্ধ হাত উঠছে আকাশে, সমবেত কন্ঠের স্লোগান শোনা যাচ্ছে দূর থেকে দূরে। সারা দেশের নজর যখন দিল্লির যন্তর-মন্তরে দেশের ছাত্র-যুবদের নাছোড়, জীবনপণ লড়াইতে, যেখানে শামিল সব বয়সের মানুষ, তখন মুখ্য নির্বাচন কমিশনার জ্ঞানেশ কুমারের পদত্যাগ ও এসআইআর প্রক্রিয়া বাতিলের দাবিতে আটটি বাম ছাত্র সংগঠন ও অন্যান্য বাম সংগঠনের উদ্যোগে ১১ অক্টোবর, কলকাতার শিয়ালদহ থেকে ধর্মতলা পর্যন্ত এক দীর্ঘ মিছিল সংঘটিত হয়।


ছবি: অর্ক


এই মিছিলেই কথা বলা গেল কয়েক জন ছাত্র-যুবদের সঙ্গে তাঁদের রাজনৈতিক ভাবনার স্পষ্ট ছবি বোঝার জন্য। তাঁদের কাছে প্রশ্ন ছিল দিল্লির যন্তর-মন্তরের আন্দোলনের প্রতি প্রতিক্রিয়া, তাঁদের প্রতি রাষ্ট্র ও পুলিসের দমন-পীড়ন, মহিলা আন্দোলনকারীদের প্রতি ঘটা সহিংসিতা ও রাজ্য তথা দেশে বিজেপি সরকারের বিষয়ে তাঁদের মনোভাব সংক্রান্ত।


 


স্নাতকোত্তর স্তরের ছাত্রী কলকাতার পার্ক সার্কাসের শবনম খাতুন বললেন, “যেভাবে জ্ঞানেশ কুমার এত জন ভোটারের নাম বাদ দিয়েছেন, আমরা চাই, যে ভুল্ভাবে তারা এই কাজটা করছেন, সেই প্রক্রিয়াটা বন্ধ করা হোক, জ্ঞানেশ কুমার নিজের অ্যাকাউন্টিবিলিটি নিন, আর যদি তিনি তা না মেনে নেন, তাহলে তাকে ইস্তফা দিতেই হবে। অউর হাম তামাম জনতা কি এঁহি রায় হ্যায় কে উনহে ইস্তিফা দেনা পড়েগা, হর হাল মে দেনা পড়েগা।


 


দিল্লি পুলিস পুরোপুরি বিক্রি হয়ে গেছে। তারা জানেও না যে সামনে দাঁড়িয়ে আছে সে কে। শুধু সরকারের কথা শুনে জনতার উপর লাঠি চালানোই তাদের কাজ হয়ে গেছে। আমরা জানি যে, তাদের উপরে অর্ডার আছে। কিন্তু তার মানে এই নয় যে, তারা নিজের বিবেক ভুলে গিয়ে সব আন্দোলনকারীদের উপর এমন জুলুম করবেন। এর জবাব ওদের দিতেই হবে।


 


দেখুন, ভোটারদের কাছে, আমাদের মূল জিনিস হল ভোট। যদি আমাদের থেকে আমাদের ভোটই ছিনিয়ে নেওয়া হয়, তাহলে কীকরে বলব যে এই সরকার সিস্টেম মেনে গঠিত না কি ভোটচুরি করে তৈরি হয়েছে। সামনের নির্বাচনে কে থাকবে না থাকবে তা তো জানি না, কিন্তু আমি চাই যেন একটা সঠিক প্রক্রিয়া, সঠিক সিস্টেম মেনে কাজ হোক। ভোটচুরি, গদ্দারি যেন না হয়।


 


ভোট হামারা অধিকার হ্যায় অউর হামারা অধিকার ইতনি আসানি সে ছিনা নেহি যা সকতা। আর যখনই আমাদের অধিকার কেড়ে নেওয়ার চেষ্টা করা হবে তামাম জনতা একজোট হয়ে রুখে দাঁড়াবে। 


 


বিজেপি ধর্মের ভিত্তিতেই দেশ চালাতে চায়। হিন্দু থাকবে, মুসলমানদের হঠাতে হবে। এইভাবে যারাই শাসন করতে চেয়ে ইতিহাসে দেখুন, তাদের পরিণতি খারাপই হয়েছে। হিন্দুস্তানকে চালানোর জন্য, আমাদের সংবিধান যেভাবে বলে সেভাবেই একটি সরকারের উচিৎ দেশ চালানো, ধর্মের ভিত্তিতে নয়।”


 


যাদবপুর বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের পদার্থবিদ্যা বিভাগের প্রথম বর্ষের ছাত্র কৌশিক মন্ডল মনে করেন, “ছাত্রছাত্রীদের উপর যে অত্যাচার নামিয়ে আনছে…জ্ঞানেশকুমার আজ শুধু গণতন্ত্রের উপির একটা বড় আঘাত নামিয়ে আনছে তাই নয়, সব রকমভাবে আমাদের অধিকার কেড়ে নিতে চাইছে। উচ্চশিক্ষার উপর চরম আঘাত আনা হচ্ছে। কলেজ-বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের পড়াশোনার ক্ষেত্রেও একটা অবৈজ্ঞানিক সিস্টেম চালু করেছে। এই কারণেই গোটা দেশ জুড়ে আন্দোলন শুরু হয়ে গেছে।


 


দিল্লিতে ছাত্র-যুবদের আন্দোলনে প্রবল রাষ্ট্রীয় দমন-পীড়ন দেখে ভয় তো একেবারেই পাচ্ছি না, বরং মনে করছি বাঁধন যত শক্ত হবে, সে বাঁধন তত তাড়াতাড়ি টুটে যাবে। আমরা এই আন্দোলনকে আরো দীর্ঘতর, আরো শক্তিশালী করার জন্য আমরা লাগাতার চালিয়ে যাব।

আমি বাঁকুড়া থেকে যাদবপুর বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ে পড়তে এসেছি, এবং এখানে যে গণতান্ত্রিক পরিবেশ আছে তা হরণ করার প্রক্রিয়া হিসাবেই তার উপরেও আঘাত নামিয়ে আনা হচ্ছে।”

 


 


কলকাতার যোগমায়া দেবী কলেজ-এ ভূতত্ত্ববিদ্যার স্নাতক স্তরের চূড়ান্ত বর্ষের ছাত্রী পূর্ব মেদিনীপুরের মণীষা প্রধান স্পষ্টই জানালেন, “শুধু আজকে নয়, আমরা ইতিহাসের ধারাপথে এটা দেখে এসেছি যে, রাষ্ট্রের বিরূদ্ধে কোনো আন্দোলন করলে রাষ্ট্র নারী-পুরুষ নির্বিশেষে তাঁদের উপর এক বর্বরোচিত আক্রমণ নামিয়ে আনে। বিভিন্ন বাম সংগঠনের মহিলা কমরেডরা তাঁদের জান-প্রাণ দিয়ে এই লড়াইটা শেষ তক লড়ছেন। তাঁদের উপর যে ধরনের আক্রমণ পুলিসের তরফ থেকে করা হচ্ছে তা অত্যন্ত ঘৃণ্য ও নিন্দনীয়। কিন্তু তা সত্ত্বেও আমরা দমে যাইনি। বরং দেশ জুড়ে এই আন্দোলন আরোও বেড়ে চলেছে। জ্ঞানেশ কুমার ও নির্বাচন কমিশনের অবৈধভাবে ১৩ কোটি নাগরিকের নাগরিকত্ব বকলমে হরণ করা এসআইআর-এর মাধ্যমে – তার আমরা তীব্র বিরোধীতা করছি, জ্ঞানেশ কুমারের অপসারণ চাইছি। বৈধ নাগরিকদের নাগরিকত্ব হরণ করার যে চক্রান্ত তার জন্য আমরা এস আই আর-কে নিষিদ্ধ ঘোষণা করার দাবি করছি।


বাঁ দিক থেকে প্রথম মণীষা প্রধান


বিজেপি-আরএসএস-এর যে আদর্শ তা একেবারেই মনুবাদের আদর্শ, এবং তারা পিতৃতন্ত্রকেই একমাত্র বলে মনে করে যেখানে তারা মহিলাদের ভোগ্যপণ্যবস্তু হিসাবে দেখে। মহিলাদের তারা মানুষ বলে মনে করে না। তাদের কাজকর্মে তাই যে এটাই প্রতিফলিত হবে তা খুব স্বাভাবিক ব্যাপার। তাদের আক্রমণ, তাদের ভাষা প্রয়োগে এটাই বারংবার ফুটে উঠছে যে তারা মহিলাদের …

author: chuang
title: “Every War Is a World War”: Interview with a Member of Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine
content:
The following is an interview with friends from Taiwan who have formed the umbrella coalition Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine (TWAFP). The interview includes an overview of the rifts in the Taiwanese left, and the frustration of TWAFP organizers carving out their place amid divisions between pro-unification and independence, or pro- and anti-American positions, in the contentious and highly polarized politics on the island.


The organizer recounts their efforts to confront Taiwan’s growing ties with Israel and direct support for the genocide in Palestine. They speak with sadness that, even as Taiwan is now the fourth-largest supplier of arms to Israel, surpassing mainland China, most Taiwanese care little for the distant genocide and the struggle in Palestine seems far away. And yet, TWAFP has led successful demonstrations, pulled together a broad coalition of disparate groups in support of Palestine, and conducted research to expose Taiwan’s complicity in the ongoing genocide.


Be sure to read their

report


from 2025, outlining specific pathways of material component support for Israel, including radar, armor, and an array of military hardware.


See also a recent

piece

 submitted to us, outlining Taiwan’s deepening ties with Israel under the DPP government.


–

Chuang


Q: To begin, let’s just set the stage. Over the last few years, the Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine (TWAFP) has helped to organize the largest mobilizations against the genocide in Palestine seen in Taiwan. Can you tell us a little about how TWAFP formed and maybe review some of the protests it has organized?


A:

Taiwan Alliance for a Free Palestine (TWAFP)

 was founded in April of 2024. Prior to this, Taiwan had already seen several groups doing Palestine advocacy work arise spontaneously, including Palestine Action Front, Taiwan Palestine Solidarity Network, and Parallel Government. As its name suggests, TWAFP is an “Alliance” that brings together groups that were already involved in initiatives related to Palestine. In addition to the three groups already mentioned, the alliance also includes a migrant worker organization, the

Taiwan International Workers’ Association (TIWA)

; the human rights organization, Taiwan Association for Human Rights; the cultural collective, Taiwan Rave & Punk Solidarity Front for Palestine; the gender issues group, Queer Margins; and the Christian group, Taiwan Olive Branch Peace Collective. From 2024 to today, we have organized one petitioning campaign, issued two open letters, held one candlelight vigil, hosted one book club meeting, staged five protest actions, held three press conferences, and organized three marches. In the future, we plan to engage in a number of other activities, many of which may be smaller in scale.


Q: TWAFP also did some very interesting research on material links between Taiwan and Israel. We can link to the report here, but can you briefly go over the main findings, and maybe go over any new information that you’ve found since that report was released? For example, have there been more details since then?

      


A: In September of 2025, we released our report,

Taiwanese Companies’ Complicity in Israel’s Ongoing Genocide

, which identified specific manufacturers assisting Israel in the production of military weapons, including via the production of components. For example: Gloria Material Technology Corp (GMTC) supplies superalloys and high-grade steel produced through electroslag remelting, while ADLINK Technology supplies embedded computing systems and industrial-grade computers. In another case, Transcom marketed its vertically integrated capabilities—spanning chip design to module production—to enter the Israeli defense supply chain and is now a key, long-term supplier of components for the EL/M-2084 multi-mission radar, which is a core element of the Israeli “Iron Dome” air defense system designed by Israeli defense company Elta.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Lai Plays It Safe Ahead of Elections in National Day Address
content:
LAI’S NATIONAL DAY address this year largely played it safe. Lai did not introduce any new major proposals, but emphasized that his administration would maintain its existing stances. Notably, Lai could have leaned into attacks on the KMT ahead of elections in November but did not.

Lai began by emphasizing national unity. Lai stated that despite differences in backgrounds, political views, and generations, Taiwan should be united by a responsibility to protect Taiwan and its future. Lai raised, then, that Taiwan recently saw the 30th anniversary of direct presidential elections.

Lai, then, went on to emphasize Taiwan’s resilience in a turbulent international world. The world has seen continued conflict, as well as tariff shocks, but Lai framed Taiwan as remaining committed to non-red supply chains, and becoming part of the foundation of the international order. In this sense, Lai emphasized strengthening ties between Taiwan and its allies, whether that be Eswatini, Palau, or Europe, though, of course, one notes that Eswatini is an authoritarian monarchy. King Mswati III of Eswatini was present at National Day celebrations this year in person.

Lai said that Taiwan should seek to be a “city on a hill” in providing a model for the world.

Lai touted Taiwan’s strong economic performance, along with the accomplishments of its athletes, as signs of Taiwan’s resilience. Nevertheless, Lai also stated that one could not only look at growth numbers in assessing a society, but also whether labor conditions were improving, if young people had opportunities, and if the elderly were cared for. As such, Lai stated that constructing social housing and expanding social welfare would continue.

Lai stated that opportunities for skilled migrant work and efforts to attract international talent would continue, even if priorities would continue to be on the domestic labor force. In this, Lai would be signaling that the expansion of new categories of employment to blue-collar migrant workers would continue, while attempting to allay rising anti-migrant backlash, with the view that the government provides opportunities to migrants but not Taiwanese workers. Lai also stated that efforts to fight drugs and scam centers would ensure social safety, with fines for drugs stiffened. As a “city on a hill,” Taiwan needs to show the world that democracy is effective in caring for society.

In this sense, Lai said that Taiwan would seek to increase its international competitiveness in critical technologies such as AI, semiconductors, and beyond. Taiwan could not only rely on TSMC as the “holy mountain” that protects Taiwan, in keeping the world invested in Taiwan’s defense, but that Taiwan needed a “mountain range.” Cash hand-outs that the government will implement in the near future aim to share Taiwan’s AI dividend with the public. Salaries for teachers, public servants, police, and members of the military would also be increased. Notably, in thanking police, firefighters, and members of the military for protecting Taiwan, Lai also thanked individuals involved in civil defense efforts.

Where elections were concerned, Lai stated that mutual respect was key, as well as that despite differences, political parties should all be committed to protecting Taiwan. Lai urged continued respect in society for sexual freedoms, probably a reference to a recent raid on a gay bar in Taipei. Lai also stated that presidential authority came from the people, referencing the continued divisions between the KMT-controlled legislature and DPP-controlled executive branch.

As for China, Lai did not especially hit out at China besides framing China as disrupting the international order and seeking to distort the history of World War II. Lai stated that defense continues to be important for Taiwan; hence, efforts to increase asymmetric capabilities would remain consistent. At the same time, Lai stated that this did not preclude dialogue, but that shoring up Taiwan’s defenses is in the interests of ensuring dignity and parity in conducting dialogue. Lai emphasized Taiwan as seeking to maintain the peaceful status quo, and that it values peace but will not give up its freedom.

Lai closed on the note of calling for the ROC–and Taiwan–to continue to strive.

Indeed, Lai’s speech was preceded by a speech by Han Kuo-yu as Legislative Yuan president in which he, too, called for unity, but also lashed out in vague terms at Lai for being “dictatorial.” It is probable that Lai …

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: Six years on, a mother grieves death of son killed in the ‘drug war’
content:
Lorna Carina Pepaño. Screengrab from the Philippine Truth Commission

“For me, justice and healing mean holding accountable those who carried out the killings, the perpetrators, those who gave the orders, and the highest-ranking officials behind the killings.”

Trigger warning: details of violence and death

Seeing her son’s body, his blood spilling in the streets, Lorna Carina Pepaño could not cry. That day, on May 18, 2020, her son Christian was shot dead by two unidentified men while buying medicines and coffee for Pepaño.

On the day of the incident, Pepaño ran to the scene of the crime without slippers. Many of the witnesses she talked to said that Christian was begging for his life, telling the perpetrators that he was not the person they were after. The witnesses also heard one of the gunmen saying that Christian was not the target.

Six years later, Pepaño mustered the courage to tell the story of her son during the fourth public truth-telling session organized by the independent Philippine Truth Commission on October 9, 2026.

“All I feel until now is anger,” Pepaño said in Filipino. “Back then, I was shouting, saying words I never thought I could say. Never did I think that my son would be killed that day. I have so many questions but not a single answer.”

The police medico-legal report revealed that Christian died of four gunshot wounds in the head and trunk. The manner of death was also specified as homicide. All four gunshot wounds were fatal, causing immediate death.

“I could not sleep (properly) for five months. I was only drinking coffee. My grandson was also deeply affected by the incident. He would wake up shouting in the middle of the night,” Pepaño added.

Pepaño deeply misses his son. Christian only finished primary school because he took care of his grandmother in the province in the early years of his life, while Pepaño was a security guard in Manila.

The year Christian was killed was supposed to be his 40th year. On his 39th birthday, Pepaño prepared a small feast and a gift – a smartphone – for Christian. It was the first birthday celebration they organized as a family because that was the only time Pepaño could afford it.

“It was his happiest birthday. We rented a videoke and he sang his heart out. He hugged me and thanked me for the celebration,” Lorna said. “I never thought that it would be his last birthday celebration.”

Forensic pathologist Raquel Fortun, who is also a Commissioner of the Philippine Truth Commission, conducted an autopsy of Christian’s body on February 15, 2024, almost four years after he was summarily killed. She confirmed the two gunshot wounds in the head, but could not confirm the two gunshot wounds in the trunk since the body was already in advanced decomposition and they could only recover bones.

“Christian was in a really bad shape with the fatal shots in the head alone,” said Fortun, noting that all wounds were sutured based on the police medico-legal report. “There is no full homicide investigation. We do not have scene documentation.”

The bottom line, she emphasized, is that killings continue during the administration of Rodrigo Duterte, because there is no proper investigation.

More than 30,000 were extrajudicially-killed during the Duterte administration, according to the report of independent human rights groups. Only five cases resulted in conviction, as monitored by the Philippine Truth Commission, while some remain on appeal.

The fourth truth-telling session happened a day after the International Criminal Court (ICC) released the public redacted version of the decision, declaring that Duterte is fit to stand trial based on the assessment of independent medical experts. The ICC also adopted measures for his participation in his trial, which is slated to start on November 30 this year.

“Christian’s case was not part of the ICC. We call that temporal jurisdiction. The ICC is limited to the crimes committed from 2011 to 2019, the temporal limitation does not apply to the Truth Commission,” former ICC Judge Raul Pangalangan, chairperson of the Philippine Truth Commission, said in a press conference.

He emphasizes that there are differences in the mandate of the Philippine Truth Commission and the ICC. The former is not limited to temporal jurisdiction or the timeframe when the Philippine government was a member-state of the ICC. But their main objective was to provide a platform for the victims to share their stories.

author: rti_admin
title: Her life ended in one night. Her justice is still in the queue
content:
“Who will answer?” And “We cheered because the courts made us wait!”

Every rape case begins with a person: a daughter, a sister, a mother who trusted the road home. The numbers can feel cold, but they are made of lives, and any honest conversation has to carry both the data and the grief.

In November 2025, the World Health Organization and its UN partners released their most comprehensive estimates yet on violence against women (https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240116962). Approximately 840 million women, nearly one in three, have experienced partner or sexual violence in their lifetime, and the rate has barely changed in 25 years (https://www.who.int/news/item/19-11-2025-lifetime-toll–840-million-women-faced-partner-or-sexual-violence). For the first time the report also estimated sexual violence by someone other than a partner: approximately 263 million women have experienced it since age 15 (https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/violence-against-women). Experts caution that this figure is significantly under-reported because of stigma and fear (https://www.who.int/news/item/19-11-2025-lifetime-toll–840-million-women-faced-partner-or-sexual-violence).

Behind “under-reported” are women who stayed silent because they feared blame, and families who chose “honour” over justice. Prevention gets almost nothing. Only 0.2% of global development aid in 2022 went to programmes that prevent violence against women, and funding has fallen further since 2025.

Daayra is a 2026 crime thriller co-written and directed by Meghna Gulzar, released in theatres on 18 September 2026, inspired by true events in which a young woman disappears from a highway. Her family goes to the police, but they do not take the case seriously. The next day, her body is found on a deserted stretch, and the case dominates the headlines. The four accused, including one juvenile, are arrested and shot dead before they can be produced in court. The country rejoices, while others allege the encounter was staged.

Reviewers describe two philosophies at the centre: One believes capital punishment is the best solution. The other believes in social upliftment, teaching people consent and boundaries.

Some critics felt the film plays it safe and takes no clear stand, though they credit it with the potential to generate discussion.

When people cheer the deaths of the accused, the easy reading is bloodlust. The harder and more honest reading is exhaustion.

While Daayra plays in theatres, Delhi is living its own version. On September 21, 2026, a 17-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped at a park near Delhi’s Kalkaji area. (https://www.newsgram.com/delhi/2026/09/28/miranda-house-students-protest-ground-report-kalkaji-rape-case-1). A birthday, a temple, a walk in a park turn into something worse than a nightmare. The case has been registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the POCSO Act, and the police arrested all three accused. Followed by a march on September 28th organized by Miranda House students.

Why should the classroom go online? Why should the campus be emptied, the gate avoided, the evening cancelled, the dupatta pulled tighter, and the phone kept in hand? Why is it always her world that gets smaller after a crime that was never hers?

We tell our daughters, sisters, mothers….to be careful. We never ask anyone to teach their progeny to be safe, irrespective of gender. We call it “protection,” but it is a curfew placed on the wrong people.

One protester said the country has endured this for years because we keep saying, “Koi Baat Nahi” it’s alright, it’s just one case. But a single case is a girl who will flinch at a temple bell, a mother who will never let go of her hand again, and a family that has to explain to an entire city why it must keep going.

In 2024, Indian courts had 206,777 rape cases for trial, but only 20,587 trials were completed, a pendency of 89.8%. Of those, 185,785 were still pending when the year ended, more than nine times the number of trials completed. The 24.4% conviction rate is measured only against trials that finished. (https://www.thestatesman.com/india/thousands-of-rape-cases-reach-indias-courts-but-how-many-end-in-conviction-what-ncrb-data-show-1503633430.html)

For girls, the picture is the same. In 2024, the conviction rate in rape cases involving girls was around 30%, with 86% of cases still pending, and in 97% of cases, the accused was known to the victim. (https://www.thedailyjagran …

author: Manila Today Staff
title: The cost of US imperialism that we are fighting against
content:
with added reports from Jessica Obciana and Kline Vergara

“Homes are destroyed, livelihoods are lost, nations are lost by interests that are made far beyond our own borders. Even now, initiatives like Pax Silica, supply chains for critical minerals and semiconductors are being reordered around the needs of the US war machine, and countries like us [the Philippines] are being asked to serve as suppliers and now become their targets, rather than being allowed to decide our own development,” said Dr. Giovanni Tapang, convener of the Stop the US-Israel War on Iran Network.

Various anti-imperialist groups gathered for the webinar Updates from the Resistance: The Current Situation in Iran, Palestine, Venezuela, and Cuba, co-organized by BAYAN, the International League of Peoples’ Struggle (ILPS) Philippines, the Philippines-Palestine Friendship Association (PPFA), and the Stop the US-Israel War on Iran Campaign Network, to express people’s solidarity in lambasting US imperialism following its sanctions, blockades, military aggression, and other forms of intervention and coercion against the people.

“This is the war machine that we are fighting against. And as we listen to those who are on the front lines, we learn of their resistance, deepen our understanding, and together strengthen solidarity to defeat this war machine,” Tapang added.

“We have seen the case of Venezuela: how this warfare has been attacking the Global South, attacking the country, and in many, many aspects, not only the political one, military, economic, and cultural, and in social consciousness. Venezuela is under siege now,” said Richard Lobo, Venezuela’s Chargé d’Affaires.

Venezuela possesses the world’s largest proven crude oil reserves, estimated at around 303 billion barrels as of 2023, according to the US Energy Information Administration.

Lobo noted that US intervention in Venezuela extends beyond economic sanctions to political, military, economic, and cultural intervention.

In January 2026, the US launched Operation Absolute Resolve as a large-scale military operation in Venezuela framed around drug trafficking and national security that led to the capture of President Nicolás Maduro and First Lady Cilia Flores and their transfer to the United States. Such an operation also targeted Venezuelan military infrastructure across Caracas and other locations.

Months after Maduro’s capture, the US laid out an agreement to gain access and control over an estimated 65 billion barrels of oil reserves, mineral wealth, and other resources.

Meanwhile, Lobo emphasized that the situation has only amplified the resistance among Venezuelans in defending their sovereignty and their right to determine the country’s political and economic direction.

“Even though we have been under attack […] the people there in Venezuela have been resisting and have been struggling. And one thing that I can say right now is that even with the kidnapping of our president, they believe the government is still in power,” Lobo stated.

More than 5,000 civilians have been killed in the US-Israel aggression against Iran, including 168 girls who were killed when a school was struck in March this year.

“Iran is experiencing aggression by the United States and Israel since the 1979 revolution against a very corrupt government, the Shah’s government. The United States has been trying to overthrow the revolutionary government in Iran, engaging in economic warfare for 46 years,” said Dr. Foad Izadi, associate professor at the University of Tehran.

The 1979 Iranian Revolution overthrew Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, whose government had maintained close relations with the US. The revolution fundamentally changed Iran’s relationship with the US, posing decades of diplomatic confrontation, economic sanctions, and political pressure.

“(The US) has also asked Iran to reduce its support for the Palestinian cause. As you know, Iran has been a strong supporter of Palestine. Not only with words, not only with speeches, but with military aid. Iran is the only country that is helping Palestinians with military aid,” said Dr. Izadi, noting that other governments should also learn from them by providing help to those countries fighting against aggression and genocide.

“Iran has learned that if you allow Israelis, genocidal people, the apartheid regime to get away with their crimes in Palestine, they they would want to take over the Middle East and go beyond,” he added.

author: ALR Editors
title: Announcing Asian Labour School Oct-Nov 2026 Semester
content:
Dear friends,


We are back with an amazing list of new and returning courses for the Asian Labour School. If you are interested in

acquiring democratic facilitation skills, navigating conflicts and taking collective care, working cooperatively, strengthening a union core or leading your own radical walking tours

, please check out the course information below and study with Asian Labour School.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Chie Matsumoto


We all have attended meetings where decisions were made by only a few members, most outspoken ones or someone at the top. We may have once thought, “Why am I even here?” and left without saying a word. Democracy starts in the smallest conversations, dialogues and meetings by raking in most diverse opinions and ideas, piecing them together to create something new and meaningful to all participants.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Facilitators: Emi Do and Matt Noyes


Worker cooperatives are enterprises that are owned and governed by workers. When all of our working experiences have been in profit-maximizing enterprises, or in workplaces that are structured hierarchically, it is no wonder that we can encounter challenges when attempting to work together cooperatively. In this course we will explore the challenges and tensions when there are no bosses to hate!


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Facilitator: Nash Tysmans


Movements are built through relationships. Yet the pressures of organizing (urgency, conflict, exhaustion, political disagreement, and unequal power) can strain those relationships and undermine our collective capacity. How can we build movements that are both effective in challenging injustice and caring in how we work together?


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Sithar Chhim


In order to win any campaign at workplace, unions need to be strong enough to pressure the company. Building a strong and representative committee is the only way to win over the bosses who have well organized structure at workplace compare to workers.


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)


Facilitator: Kevin Lin


Have you ever thought about leading your own radical walking tour to share with friends the significance of places and histories in your city? Leading and participating in a radical walking tour is not only educational but fun and always memorable. A walking tour provides a concrete sense of places, people, and histories. This course will walk you through the conceptualisation, research and logistics of a radical walking tour, and hear ideas and experiences from other participants across Asia.


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)

author: Tom Sullivan
title: Housing protests lead to general strike in Spain
content:
“I haven’t managed to defend my house, but I have tried so that others can learn how to defend theirs.” These were the words of an 87-year-old Madrid woman, Maricarmen, who posted a video from her hospital bed after Spanish authorities evicted her from the apartment she had lived in for the past 71 years. In the video, she promoted an upcoming protest at Madrid’s Plaza del Sol “so that we can eliminate this problem once and for all”.

Her eviction sparked a fire across the Spanish state. Within days, protesters had set up an encampment in the Plaza del Sol, famously the site of mass anti-austerity protests in 2011. They quickly spread to dozens of other cities, along with mass protests. A few days later came the first victory of the movement, when the vulture fund that had bought Maricarmen’s apartment building agreed to allow her to return with a new, eight-year contract and her rent capped at 30 percent of her pension.

But this victory only fuelled the protests. On Saturday 3 October, nationally coordinated rallies saw around half a million people protest across the country. Three days later, the country’s two major union confederations called a general strike.

Few recent examples illustrate the power of protest as clearly as the last two weeks in the Spanish state. When the authorities forced their way into Maricarmen’s apartment, she was meant to be just another of the nearly 70 people who are evicted from their homes every day across the country. But the footage of her being removed on a stretcher into an ambulance tapped into a rage that millions of people feel living at the whim of the housing market.

In Spain, it is particularly sharp. Over the last decade, rental prices have risen by more than 80 percent, according to the National Institute of Statistics. And the market is becoming increasingly concentrated in the hands of a small minority. From 2008 to 2025, the share of single property owners fell by 4 percent, while the share of people with at least ten properties rose by 35 percent, according to a recent government report.

These statistics prove the main point of the Tenants’ Union, the group leading the protests: the main problem is that under capitalism, housing is a commodity for investors to make a profit from and not a basic good provided to all people. They’ve combined this general perspective with a series of concrete demands, including automatic renewal of rental contracts, a 50 percent rent reduction, and the expropriation of empty properties.

Importantly, the union’s approach has been to spread the protests, while also raising new, more radical slogans as the movement developed. In the first few days, the movement played out under the generally defensive slogan “Not one more Maricarmen”. But as the movement exploded, the slogan shifted to “towards a general strike,” directly calling on the two major union confederations to call one.

Since Maricarmen’s eviction, the government of Pedro Sanchez’s Socialist Party (PSOE) and its junior partner Sumar, heavily influenced by the Communist Party, has scrambled to respond. It put forward two bills in parliament, including measures such as a pause on evictions until 2030 and indefinite rental contract extensions, with twelve months’ compensation for tenants if landlords break the agreement. However, the government is a minority in parliament and, among other parties, it relies on the centre-right Catalan independence party, Junts, to pass any laws. Junts joined the right to defeat the two bills.

Even though the government put forward the bills knowing they would be defeated, the fact that they included reforms like a pause on evictions until 2030 illustrates the power of the movement. Similarly, the movement’s rejection of the bills as inadequate testifies to mass popular support for genuine solutions to the housing crisis and a radical approach to achieving them. A recent poll published in elDiario.es showed 73 percent support for a general strike, 58 percent support for the main encampment in Madrid, and that 40 percent of people would be prepared to engage in a rent strike.

With the bills defeated, however, Sanchez is dissolving parliament and calling snap elections for 29 November. It’s a shrewd political move. His message will be simple: the right-wing parties used their majority to block housing reform, so a majority Socialist Party government is necessary to get real action.

But Sanchez’s record shows how fickle this message is. He is a …

author: AWSM
title: Why I Won’t Vote ~ A SYMPOSIUM #1
content:
Anarchy 37, March 1964, Why I Won’t Vote

Voting : “The instrument and symbol of a freeman’s power to make a fool of himself and a wreck of his country”

The saying that ” only a fool would put a loaded gun into the hands of an idiot ” is an especially apt analogy of government. An idiot (usually well-meaning) considers himself clever enough to run the affairs of a large number of people by taking a seat in parliament. A large number of people, acting like fools, vote for his party’s policy then spend the next few years grumbling about the results. The error in approach is that the voter thinks that he will get what he voted for. If he could vote for those who in fact control the country, say the Governors of the Bank of England, the directors of the industrial corporations and those behind the ministries, the illusion of democracy would be more understandable.

The real centres of power lie far beyond the people’s influence at elections. These remain constant whatever Party is ” in power “. In the terms of centralised ” democracy ” the only possible argument to justify voting is that marginal benefits may be gained. The state only incidentally attends to the well-being of its subjects. Its main concern is its power relation to other states, of which the most perfect expression is in war.

I am on the side of people anywhere who are prepared neither to live nor die for something that in the long run can only militate against survival and the conditions that make life worth living. Our immediate action must, by its nature, be to oppose that pathetic gesture, voting. It must be direct and direction. We can learn to live as free men and women only by organising against the condition we are in.

The Tenants Association, Consumers Association, and Direct Action in industry all provide opportunities for people to experience directing their own lives in positive ways towards positive ends.

Only by direct involvement in society can the individual hope to transform himself and his world. Freedom cannot be given, it must be taken; and the free society can only grow from experiments in the problems (ethical and organisational) of community.

Voting does not, and cannot, mean government by consent. By voting, one acts on the assumptions that certain men are fit to govern, and that a majority is necessarily right. Also should the state, acting in the name of a (frequently fictitious) majority, declare war, the individual loses the right to live, if he ever had it.

To me, voting is complicity with the State and a negative action, therefore I do not vote.

title: Yeah Nah Pasaran #300 w Emma Hagberg on ‘Comrades, Not Friends’ & The Revolutionary Front : October 8, 2026
content:
This week on Yeah Nah Pasaran! we talk to Emma Hagberg. Emma is the author of Comrades, Not Friends: The Revolutionary Front, Antifascism, and Class Struggle (PM Press/Working Class History, 2026), translated by Gabriel Kuhn and with a preface by Tomas Rothaus (both of whom have been previous guests of the show).

According to Hagberg, RF had ‘a strong collective identity, the view of fascists as class traitors, and the critique of an autonomous left that often had no place for working-class people’; Comrades was originally published in Swedish as 18.6 – Kamrater, Inte Vänner (B.E.L Publishing, 2024) and is also available in a German translation.

The Revolutionary Front (RF), 2001–2015, was the most militant organization on the left in recent Swedish history. Staunchly working class, the first generation of RF members engaged in numerous street battles with Swedish fascists. When the fascists retreated from the streets, RF attacked them in their homes. The police cracked down on the organization in 2013, raiding the apartments of several alleged members at the crack of dawn. The courts handed out prison sentences of up to six and a half years. Two years later, the organization folded.

See also : Presentation on the book about Revolutionära Fronten (Revolutionary Front) (April 13, 2025).

author: Lance Selfa
title: What’s up with Jacobin’s “Working-Class Win-o-Meter”?
content:
Every few months, 

Jacobin 

magazine announces what it purports to be a secret to win working-class voters based on a finding from its associated Center for Working Class Politics (CWCP). Its 14 September editorial “

Report: The Working Class Vote is Not Lost

” was the latest in this series.

CWCP’s latest innovation is the “Working-Class Win-o-Meter”, which Jacobin describes as “a data-driven road map for winning back working-class voters”. It purports to demonstrate the optimal combination of social and political appeals to move working-class voters to vote for a hypothetical Democratic candidate.

Two points should be made at the outset. When

 Jacobin

 and CWCP talk about “winning working class voters,” they don’t mean winning the working class to socialism. They mean “winning” the working class to vote for Democrats. And they define the “working class” as non-college-educated people with family incomes of between $30,000 and $150,000.

This supposedly groundbreaking survey and analysis is an exercise in political message-testing for Democratic candidates. It uses the definition of “working-class” that is the standard in lazy polling and media commentary, and thus adds no new insights. Attaching the labels of “socialist” and “working-class” doesn’t change the fact that what

 Jacobin

 and CWCP are engaged in is a completely conventional activity that regularly earns millions for Democratic Party consultants.

Without digressing into a long discussion of the inadequacies of the study’s understanding of class, it’s worth pondering why, under its definition, a non-college educated small business owner is “working class” but a college-educated nurse or K-12 teacher who is a union activist is not considered working-class. It’s the same sort of logic that 

had Democratic Socialists of America (DSA)-adjacent consultants and 

Jacobin

 fawning over

 working-class avatar “oyster farmer” Graham Platner as a US Senate candidate in Maine before Platner’s campaign imploded.

The study’s key findings include “lead with working-class economics” and “adopt culture and climate positions that resonate with working-class voters”. These takeaways are supposed to increase the hypothetical Democratic candidate’s support over what it calls a “Kamala Harris-2024 style Democrat.”

For working-class economics or economic populist policies, the winning positions come from a list of ordinary policies from tuition-free community college to protecting Social Security from cuts to capping prescription-drug prices. There is nothing wrong with these proposals. But they are hardly bold. In fact, many of them are the same poll-tested offerings that Democratic Party politicians have included in their campaigns for years.

The fact that they are repackaged here as keys to victory should emphasise how little the Democrats have done to implement these when they have held power in the past. And it’s noteworthy that “Medicare for All,” the signature proposal that social democrats like 

Jacobin

 and DSA have championed for more than a decade, didn’t make the list.

But what really gives the game away are the “culture and climate” positions the analysis considers

losing

 messages for Democratic politicians. For anyone who is familiar with 

Jacobin’s

 antipathy to 

“subcultural leftism”

, the losing positions won’t surprise: reducing funding for police, “abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE),” and letting “trans girls play in girls’ sports.” Other so-called “social issues,” such as defence of abortion rights, don’t significantly move the needle toward the Democrats, CWCP finds.

Mainstream Democratic Party campaigns in the midterm electoral cycle are following this script without even dialling up the “Win-o-Meter”. It’s an article of faith that serious Democratic candidates run on “kitchen-table issues” like the price of groceries and gasoline, and “don’t take the bait” by engaging with Republicans over “silly culture war” issues. Or they try to get ahead of the Republican attacks by pre-emptively jumping to the conservative side. For example, Texas U.S. Senate candidate James Talarico said he too 

opposes trans girls in girls’ sports

. As the liberal journalist 

Perry Bacon

 explained:

“‘Economic issues not cultural wars’ produces a party that both loses elections and abandons moral causes and vulnerable people. That’s not a theoretical argument—it’s the story of the Democratic Party of my entire adulthood. The …

author: Yuanyi Tham
title: Mega Anthropic data centre to blight Queensland
content:
Queensland is set to become home to Australia’s largest AI data centre. Last month, Liberal National Party Premier David Crisafulli announced a landmark deal with Anthropic to develop the Western Downs Digital Park, near the town of Dalby, about 250 kilometres northwest of Brisbane. Led by Singaporean developer Zerra DC, the site will be constructed in four phases, with the first building expected to be operational next year.

The data centre will occupy 725.5 hectares, an area twice the size of New York’s Central Park. Its estimated value is $32 billion, nearly five times the 2032 Brisbane Olympics infrastructure budget.

Data centres suck up huge amounts of power, driving up energy prices and accelerating climate change. When fully constructed, electro-mechanical engineer Dr Andreas Helwig told the ABC it would use the equivalent of 25 to 30 percent of Queensland’s total energy consumption.

The data centre will run primarily on electricity generated by coal and gas, drawn from the state’s electricity grid. Greenpeace estimates that the data centre would raise the grid’s emissions by 6.6 million tonnes, the equivalent of two million extra cars on the road.

Last month, Crisafulli wrestled with the federal government and eventually won a state exemption from the requirement that data centres run on renewable energy. The exemption, Crisafulli argued, was simply “common sense”; according to him (and now the Labor cabinet), environmental protections shouldn’t get in the way of AI investment opportunities.

While workers worry about AI’s impact on their jobs, power bills and the environment, Crisafulli has never been happier. He celebrated the data centre deal as the fruits of his five-day trip to the US in early September, where he met with the CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic. On the same trip, he met with US Vice President J.D. Vance and discussed Queensland’s potential to become the next link in the American critical minerals supply chain.

Crisafulli’s MAGA meetings highlight that this data centre is a story of more than just environmental degradation and corporate greed. Attracting investment in areas like AI and critical minerals is a part of a broader mission to strengthen Australia’s alliance with the US. The data centre boom is driven in part by the AI arms race between the US and China. In this context, striking a deal with the US’s largest AI corporation is not just a step towards turning Queensland as an AI investment hub. It also further integrates the Australian and US economies, so both countries are better placed to outpace competitors in the global tech arena.

Anthropic’s new project adds to the 225 other data centres currently in development in Australia and supported by both major parties. Politicians and tech billionaires have no compunction about the impact of their actions on people or the environment, so long as they are making money and moving up the imperialist pecking order. We need a political alternative that will fight for an immediate moratorium on data centres and a socialist society where we can all have a say in the future of our lives and the planet.

author: Paul Gregoire
title: Antisemitism envoy continues to push to outlaw criticism of Israel
content:
Jillian Segal, Australia’s unelected Special Envoy to Combat Antisemitism, continues to push to insert a Zionist definition of antisemitism — prejudice towards Jews — into all Australian institutions. This is because she knows it serves to stifle criticism of Israel.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese appointed Segal to the newly-created position on July 9, 2024.

The United States first appointed an antisemitism envoy in 2004. Canada, Greece, Israel, Romania, Britain and the European Union have antisemitism envoys. The Organisation of the American States also has an envoy.

Soon after being appointed, Segal attended a meeting of the Special Envoys and Coordinators Combating Antisemitism conference in Argentina.

Segal wants all public institutions to adopt the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) definition of antisemitism, which helps propagate Zionists’ narrative that any criticism of Israel is antisemitism.

The basic two-line IHRA definition, developed in 2005, was accompanied by 11 examples of prejudice towards Jews; seven of these specifically mention Israel. Since Albanese adopted Segal’s Plan to Combat Antisemitism, prominent Zionists have been regularly conflating any criticism of Israel’s genocide in Gaza with antisemitism.

Jamie Stern-Weiner writes in his 2021 doctoral thesis on the IHRA definition that representatives of the May 2016 IHRA plenary did not properly vote to adopt it. Kenneth Stern, one of its drafters, has since warned that Zionists are employing the IHRA to shield Israeli human rights abuses.

Zionism, developed by Jewish Austrian journalist Theodor Herz, rose in Europe in the late 1880s. It promoted that a new state, Israel, be founded on historic Palestine.

The federal Labor government ignored the envoy’s plan to combat antisemitism until the ISIS-inspired Bondi Beach mass murder on December 14, 2025. Four days later, Albanese suggested the envoy should be made a “permanent feature”.

Segal’s Plan revolves around getting all levels of government, public institutions and regulatory bodies to adopt the IHRA definition.

The Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (APHRA) was the first major institution to adopt it, in June, despite the backlash from many of its members. Health practitioners could now face discipline or even unemployment if they are critical of Israel’s policies.

The envoy’s next focus is on making arts funding dependent on the IHRA adoption.

Now the Tertiary Education Quality and Standards Agency is requiring that tertiary institutions adopt either the IHRA definition, or the February 2025 antisemitism definition established by peak body Universities Australia, by early January 2027.

The Universities Australia definition is based on the IHRA one.

Australia Palestine Advocacy Network in early October again called for “governments at all levels, universities, schools and other institutions to reject calls to adopt definitions of antisemitism”. It warned that the definitions being promoted “entrench anti-Palestinian racism and threaten political expression”.

Two recent court cases reveal that the judiciary has not been bullied into Segal’s views on antisemitism.

Justice Angus Stewart found in the July 2025 Federal Court case of Wertheim versus Haddad that “the ordinary, reasonable listener would understand that not all Jews are Zionists or support the actions of Israel in Gaza and that disparagement of Zionism constitutes disparagement of a philosophy or ideology and not a race or ethnic group”.

“Needless to say, political criticism of Israel, however inflammatory or adversarial, is not by its nature criticism of Jews in general or based on Jewish racial or ethnic identity,” Stewart said.

More recently, NSW Supreme Court Justice Desmond Fagan condemned the use of the IHRA definition in August in a case that involved a man on arson and graffiti charges which involved anti-Israel messaging.

Fagan found that the graffiti was not antisemitic, despite the repeated assertions of NSW authorities.

Despite this, Segal continues to push for institutions to incriminate those speaking out against Israel’s ethnic cleansing and apartheid-like policies.

[Paul Gregoire writes for Sydney Criminal Lawyers, where a version of this article was first published. Join a rally to protest three years of genocide in Gaza.]

author: Mary Ellen Murphy
title: Hospital doctors strike for wages, safe hours and public health
content:
In July, Victorian public hospital doctors voted 97 percent in favour of taking industrial action for the first time in 20 years. The reason is simple: the healthcare system is unsafe for patients and staff.

The Victorian healthcare system is in crisis. Systemic failures at every level compound one another. Limited access to primary care and community services leaves people more unwell and reliant on emergency departments for care. This results in long wait times, overcrowding and unsafe workloads.

Bed shortages, often caused by delays in discharging patients due to the lack of support services, are also an issue. For example, recent data from the Victorian Health Department shows that nineteen of 21 mental health units fail to admit acutely unwell patients from the emergency department within eight hours. This results in staff attempting to care for patients in under-resourced and unsuitable environments in which they are at greater risk of violence. The lack of suitable facilities for mental health patients and adequate staffing also contributes to the ongoing failures to meet goals for the reduction in use of restrictive interventions such as seclusion and restraint.

It is no wonder then that burnout is endemic among public hospital doctors like me working in this broken system. We are expected to be machines and cope with unsafe workloads, under-resourcing and excessive hours without complaint. The system relies on unpaid overtime, guilt and obligation to keep going.

Our industrial claims highlight the punishing hours and minimal protections Victorian doctors currently face. They include a pay rise in line with what the nurses won in 2024, better guarantees of overtime for all non-rostered hours worked, permanent employment as a default model (instead of many thousands of “junior” hospital doctors, many with over a decade of experience, being given only yearly contracts), maximum shift lengths of 12.5 hours (rather than the 14 hours commonly worked at the moment), at least four rostered days off per fortnight including two consecutive days, a maximum of four consecutive night shifts, minimum doctor-to-patient ratios for safe care and mandatory 30-minute paid rest breaks every five hours.

During the fourteen months of unsuccessful bargaining discussions, the Victorian Hospitals Industrial Association (the association of employers in the public health industry) backpedalled on its previous agreement to simplify overtime payments, arguing it would cost too much to pay doctors the hours they actually work.

It is not only at work that public hospital employees are coming under attack. Over the last few months, we have seen our regulator, AHPRA, conflate antisemitism with anti-Zionism to silence healthcare workers speaking up about Palestine, including outside of work and on social media. This violates democratic rights and sets a terrible precedent for other professions. Many healthcare workers feel particularly obliged to advocate for Palestinians based on our roles as health workers. We suffer moral injury when we are prevented from speaking out about the atrocities committed against our colleagues in Gaza and against the Palestinian people as a whole.

When confronted about the lack of a public response to this attack on our freedom of speech, the Victorian branch of the Australian Medical Association admitted it was scared to address it publicly for fear of backlash, and that the federal organisation was engaged in back-room discussions with AHPRA. This approach aligns more with a lobby organisation than a trade union.

A union’s strength comes from its members’ involvement and activity. This also protects unions when they want to speak out about political issues important to their members. There is a reason that the Australian Salaried Medical Officers Federation (the part of the Australian Medical Association that is engaged in bargaining) in New South Wales—the branch involved most recently in prolonged industrial action with an active rank and file—was the only branch of our union that put out a statement condemning the AHPRA adoption of the pro-Israel International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance definition of antisemitism.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Goldsmiths Strike Set to Become ‘Longest in UK University History’
content:
A work stoppage at Goldsmiths, University of London is due to become the longest strike in UK higher education history this week,

according to the union

 organising it. 


Staff represented by the Goldsmiths branch of the University and College Union (UCU) went on strike on 8 June in a bid to stop a third round of redundancies in five years amid sweeping cuts. 


It followed earlier industrial action in April in which staff stopped marking work. In response, the university docked 100% of the pay of those who took part.


Goldsmiths recently made an offer to staff that vice-chancellor Joanna Newman said involved “significant concessions”. But the union rejected it, arguing that “management are still committed to a series of compulsory redundancies despite the fact that the university has not run a deficit for five years.”


As a result, the strike is expected to become the longest of its kind in UK history on Friday 16 October, surpassing a

129-day work stoppage

 by staff at the University of Brighton in 2023. 


A UCU statement said: “Striking staff have received huge support from students who are bearing the brunt of the disruption caused by the dispute.” 


That disruption includes autumn term courses being cancelled or delayed and “replacement staff brought in at the last minute to cover for experienced lecturers,” it added. “Given these developments, students are now raising serious concerns about breaches in regulatory requirements and consumer rights law.”


Last week, Novara Media reported that Goldsmiths had

brought in “fake” teachers

 with little experience for an art psychotherapy course in order to break the strike.


A Goldsmiths spokesperson said: “We are committed to ensuring students receive first-class teaching, and all our programmes are being taught as scheduled.


“With thousands of new students welcomed by Goldsmiths over the last few weeks, any disruption has been minimised through proactive planning and support for students across all of our programmes.”

author: cnt.es
title: Coctelería Varone, un cóctel para acabar con la explotación
content:
La CNT acaba de empezar un conflicto con la coctelería Varone, en plena plaza Mayor de Zamora. El motivo es el despido de una trabajadora después de comunicarle que estaba embarazada; otra vez el mismo cuento.


En esta coctelería, aparte de los cócteles de su carta, tienen otro cóctel explosivo para las trabajadoras, el despido por ser mujer y quedarte embarazada, ya que el cóctel de vulneración de derechos les sale muy bien. Preparándolo de una forma muy intensa y esperando a que pasen las fiestas de San Pedro para despedirla, lo que viene a ser exprimir lo máximo posible y sacar todo el jugo a la trabajadora.


Una vez más comprobamos la doble tiranía que sufren las mujeres trabajadoras, por ser trabajadoras y por ser mujeres. Nos quieren sumisas, nos quieren dóciles, nos quieren como mercancía de usar y tirar. Y ya se nos han hinchado los ovarios, no nos vamos a callar y vamos a pelear porque esto es una injusticia que no vamos a permitir. Pelearemos para que la compañera vuelva a su puesto de trabajo y deje de ser una mercancía, ya que estamos hartas de los varones que quieren pisar nuestros derechos.

Pero esta vez la coctelería Varone ha dado con una trabajadora que no se va a quedar callada ante este abuso, una trabajadora que ha buscado apoyo entre las de su misma clase, una trabajadora que se ha llenado de fuerza y ha acudido a un sindicato de clase para luchar. Y en este conflicto, desde CNT queremos decir a la compañera que ya no está sola, a la vez que hacemos un llamamiento a la lucha y a apoyar a la compañera en este camino.


Es la organización entre la clase obrera la que nos permite cuidarnos, la que nos permite demostrar una vez más que contra los abusos de la patronal, el apoyo mutuo y la solidaridad son las armas más eficaces para responder a los ataques de los empresarios. Por eso pedimos a toda la clase trabajadora apoyar el boicot y las movilizaciones contra la coctelería Varone hasta conseguir la readmisión de la compañera.


JUNTAS LUCHAMOS CON MAS FUERZA. SI NOS TOCAN A UNA NOS TOCAN A TODAS.

¡READMISIÓN COMPAÑERA DESPEDIDA EN LA COCTELERÍA VARONE YA!

author: Unknown
title: Appel à la grève et la manifestation aux côtés des lycéen•es et étudiant•es en lutte !
content:
Le gouvernement joue le pourrissement. Opposons-lui la joie de la lutte

 

!


L'Union régionale parisienne des syndicats

CNT

 appelle l'ensemble des travailleuses et des travailleurs à se réunir en assemblées générales et, comme le font les lycéen•nes et étudiant•es, y construire les modalités de la lutte et au premier rang desquelles, la grève.


Mobilisons-nous en grève et en manifestation, non seulement le 13 octobre, aux côtés des lycéen·nes et des étudiant·es, ou encore le 5 novembre, comme y appellent également d'autres confédérations syndicales, mais chaque fois qu'il le faudra d'ici là et ensuite

 

!


Certains prétendaient que la jeunesse ne se mobilisait plus : elle leur a cloué le bec

 

! Depuis des semaines, jour après jour, elle se rassemble devant les lycées pour exiger les moyens humains et matériels nécessaires à une école publique de qualité. Jour après jour, elle descend dans la rue pour dénoncer le tri social et algorithmique à l'université, dont Parcoursup est le symbole.


Face à ce mouvement de révolte, le gouvernement a d'abord répondu par un nombre record d'interpellations et une répression d'une violence inouïe. Mais cette stratégie n'a pas suffi à étouffer la colère ni à faire rentrer les élèves dans le rang. Le gouvernement passe alors à l'étape suivante : interdire les rassemblements devant les établissements et imposer la poursuite des cours à distance. Et pour mieux enfumer tout le monde, il promet quelques remplacements de professeur•es et la mise en scène d'une «

 

démocratie interne dans les lycées

 

»… le temps d'une demi-journée. Mais la jeunesse ne tombe pas dans le panneau

 

! Elle amplifie la mobilisation dans la rue et sur les blocus. Elle y fait vivre une véritable démocratie directe en organisant des assemblées générales, d'où émergent de nouvelles revendications et s'inventent de nouveaux modes d'action.


Et le rapport de force qu'elle y construit ne sert pas seulement à défendre ses intérêts et à faire entendre ses exigences. Il ouvre aussi une perspective qui concerne l'ensemble des travailleurs et des travailleuses : combattre la résignation face à un ordre capitaliste qui creuse les inégalités et détruit la planète. En s'attaquant frontalement et avec enthousiasme à la machine austéritaire d'un gouvernement qui prépare 54 milliards d'euros d'«

 

économies

 

» sur les services publics, la culture, l'éducation et la santé, tout en augmentant de plus de 6 milliards le budget de l'armée, la jeunesse ouvre la voie à un mouvement social d'ampleur. Et en effet, puisque tout se dégrade pour tout le monde sauf pour les capitalistes qui battent les records de profits, l'heure est désormais à la convergence de l'ensemble des travailleuses et des travailleurs, du public comme du privé, et d'emboîter le pas à la révolte de la jeunesse.


C'est pourquoi l'Union régionale parisienne des syndicats

CNT

 appelle l'ensemble des travailleuses et des travailleurs à se réunir en assemblées générales et, comme le font les lycéen•nes et étudiant•es, y construire les modalités de la lutte et au premier rang desquelles, la grève.


Mobilisons-nous en grève et en manifestation, non seulement le 13 octobre, aux côtés des lycéen·nes et des étudiant·es, ou encore le 5 novembre, comme y appellent également d'autres confédérations syndicales, mais chaque fois qu'il le faudra d'ici là et ensuite

 

!


Lycéen•nes, étudiant•es, salarié•es : faisons front ensemble

 

!

author: Battlescarred
title: Gustave Lefrançais: A Link to The Past
content:
A short biography of Gustave Lefrançais, pioneering French libertarian communist

The text below is an article in the book by Nick Heath, The Idea: Anarchist Communism, Past, Present and Future.

Gustave Adolphe Lefrançais was born in 1826 in Angers. He became a teacher, was sacked for his progressive views in 1847 and took part in the 1848 events in France. He was subsequently sentenced to several months’ imprisonment for his activities with two different sentences. A communist influenced by Fourier and Pierre Leroux, he fled to England with the coup d’état by Louis Napoleon in 1851. Here he met with Déjacque “an old acquaintance of the 1848 clubs” who showed him around the London of the French exiles. This encounter was to radicalise his ideas considerably. Together with Déjacque and a dozen other exiles he set up a mutual aid association, La Sociale. As he wrote: 'All in the same precarious situation, with so thin resources, so thin that remaining isolated, we would surely die of hunger, and by associating our miseries, perhaps they will be less insupportable for each one'. He lived in poverty, teaching when he could, but also weaving baskets and selling tobacco at theatres during the Christmas season.

Returning to Paris in 1853, he associated with Proudhonists like Alfred Darimon and Georges Duchene and took part in militant activity with Alfred Briosne who advanced a theory of collectivism as a synthesis of individualism and communism. Lefrançais was critical of the mystical communists like Cabet and his followers, and the latter day Babouvists and Blanquists. According to police reports, he developed his ideas on collective property and the suppression of inheritance, as well as attacking marriage and advocating free union.

An active participant in the Paris Commune of 1871, he fought on some of the last barricades at the Bastille and Arsenal. He managed to escape and was condemned to death in his absence.

In exile in Switzerland, he immediately joined the Central Section of the International in Geneva, and found himself in the midst of a war between the Marxists and Bakuninists there. It did not take long for him to take sides. He attended the Sonvillier congress and took part in the “anti-authoritarian International. He chaired the Internal Congress of the Anti-Authoritarian International at St Imier on September 15th, 1872. He contributed to various anti-authoritarian Swiss papers and helped Reclus with his geographical work.

Returning to France with the amnesty, he stayed outside of the different political groupings, whilst speaking at many political meetings. He consistently criticised universal suffrage, and when he ran as a candidate in the 1889 elections this was just a protest against Boulangism and not a move towards electoralism.

Speaking of himself in the third person, he wrote: “He is very convinced that the future is with communism, that is to say with the complete disappearance of any individual property as instrument of production [...]. Only, while admitting as exact the communist formula: "To each according to his needs and each according to his abilities", he recognizes that the applications proposed by Gracchus Babeuf, Étienne Cabet and Louis Blanc do not respond sufficiently to the legitimate demands of individual liberty.” Memoirs, p318-319).

In an article written in the paper La Commune in 1874 he wrote that the revolution” can be nothing else than the incessant demand for the individual of his autonomy, that is to say, the absolute government of his faculties." In order for this to come about, it was necessary for "The suppression of government - of power - in the political order; that of wage labour, in the economic order. Now this double suppression can only be accomplished by the triumph of the communalist idea which is incarnated in the social revolution - the only legitimate one, the only one that interests us ".

Nettlau, in his Bibliography of Anarchy, describes the text by Lefrançais “Where are The Anarchists Going” of 1887, as one of the authoritarian critiques of anarchism. But in fact, Lefrançais, like Saverio Merlino after him in his Individualism in Anarchism, criticises both selfish individualism, in terms of anti-organisationalism and the dangers of illegalism and individual propaganda by deed. He remained a libertarian communist, who defended the ideas of the Paris Commune to the end, and who rejected “the evolution of a movement which privileged both philosophical …
