author: anred
title: Axel Kiciloff enfrenta reclamos de los trabajadores estatales y municipales
content:
La Asociación de Trabajadores del Estado cumplió el miércoles 7 de octubre un paro de 24 horas en toda la administración pública bonaerense y movilizó a la Legislatura provincial. El gremio exigió que el Presupuesto 2027 incluya los cargos para el pase a planta permanente de trabajadores precarizados. El paro afectó escuelas, hospitales y dependencias provinciales. En educación, la adhesión de auxiliares obligó a suspender clases en varios establecimientos al no garantizarse condiciones de higiene. En salud, hubo atención reducida y guardias mínimas según la adhesión por hospital.La protesta llegó después de la reunión paritaria del 24 de septiembre, que terminó sin oferta salarial por parte del gobierno de Axel Kicillof. Ese encuentro derivaba del último acuerdo de julio, de 7% acumulado —5% en julio y 2% en agosto sobre sueldos de junio— con compromiso de volver a discutir en septiembre.Sin propuesta, los estatales no cobraron aumento en octubre, salvo que se acuerde un retroactivo. El Frente Gremial Docente también concretó esta semana un paro de 48 horas por la misma situación.Por Mario Hernandez


¿Qué pidió ATE?: planta permanente, becarios y presupuesto


El eje central fue la creación de cargos en el Presupuesto 2027 para terminar con la precarización. El sindicato calculó cerca de 11.000 trabajadores bajo modalidades sin estabilidad.El reclamo incluyó:Pase a planta permanente de contratados, becarios de salud y otras formas de contratación precaria.Creación de cargos para áreas críticas del Estado provincial.Recomposición salarial para recuperar poder adquisitivo.Recategorizaciones y carrera administrativa, con avance hacia un Convenio Colectivo de Trabajo bonaerense.Mayor progresividad tributaria para financiar la mejora salarial.La columna partió desde Plaza Italia y recorrió Avenida 7 hasta la Legislatura, donde el gremio entregó un petitorio. Participaron Arévalo, el secretario gremial de ATE nacional Oscar De Isasi —referente provincial y candidato a diputado nacional en 2025 por Fuerza Patria— y el titular de la CTA Autónoma, Hugo Godoy.ATE bonaerense es un aliado del gobernador. El 2 de marzo había hecho un paro provincial en el marco de una jornada nacional, con el eje puesto en el ajuste del gobierno nacional de Javier Milei.La estrategia se repitió: el reclamo fue provincial, pero el discurso apuntó al impacto del recorte nacional sobre las provincias. En los comunicados, el sindicato insistió en que el Presupuesto debía sostener políticas públicas y reclamó recursos para conformar el Consejo del Salario Municipal.La marcha a la Legislatura y no a Gobernación fue un gesto en esa línea. Buscó que fueran los legisladores quienes garantizaran los cargos en la ley de leyes, en lugar de confrontar directamente con el Ejecutivo en plena negociación paritaria.El gobierno provincial reabrió la mesa la semana pasada sin oferta y ahora debe definir si convoca a una nueva reunión con propuesta salarial antes del cierre de la liquidación de octubre.


Los intendentes bonaerenses aplican su ajuste mileísta y hay protestas municipales


La Federación de Sindicatos Municipales Bonaerenses (FESIMUBO), junto con otros gremios, presentó una agenda que combina reclamos salariales y de condiciones laborales, pero también “institucionales”.El punto más caliente es la exigencia de una recomposición urgente que permita a miles de trabajadores y trabajadoras superar la línea de indigencia y de pobreza.A eso se suman la reapertura inmediata de las paritarias en los municipios y el pago de una suma fija de recomposición. También piden, desde hace años, el pase a planta permanente del personal precarizado y contratado. El pliego incluye pedidos de respuestas por la situación del IOMA y del IPS. Los gremios también reclaman que se ponga en funcionamiento el Consejo del Empleo Municipal, previsto por la Ley 14.656, que debería fijar pisos salariales y condiciones de trabajo unificadas.El deterioro del poder adquisitivo es el telón de fondo del conflicto. Según los gremios, en muchos municipios los sueldos básicos están entre los $300.000 y $400.000. Aunque hay diferencias entre los 135 distritos de la Provincia, en la billetera obrera no hay grieta: todos pagan salarios de hambre.Los intendentes dicen: “No hay plata”. Que las arcas municipales están ajustadas y no pueden conceder aumentos “por encima de lo que recaudan con las tasas locales”. El famoso “equilibrio fiscal…”El gobernador Axel Kicillof y su ministro Walter …

author: dev
title: Occupation, une école du commun
content:
« Finalement c'est calme, on rentre dans l'école, on change les serrures, on organise un passage filtré, on déplace des tables et des chaises pour faire des barricades, à 8h30 c'est acquis. L'école est à nous !

Mais c'est qui “nous” ?

 »


Année scolaire 1990-1991, collégienne. Notre petite ville est située à une heure d'Athènes. Ici, on ne connait pas des manifestations de rue. On n'a même pas un bar pour des jeunes pour aller écouter un peu de musique.

Sme

l

ls like teen spirit

. Ça pue la claustro, tout le monde rêve de se barrer d'ici. On passe notre temps avec une canette ou une barquette de frites au bord de l'eau, à regarder les courants. Oui c'est une île mais on ne vit pas du tourisme. Chantier de construction navale, grosse usine de béton, pollution.


Cette année là, une immense vague d'occupation de collèges et de lycées secoue le pays. Notre bâtiment partage la cour avec le lycée. On regarde, on apprend. Les lycéens font une AG, tient on va faire ça. Les premières occupations commencent en octobre contre une énième reforme du gouvernement, fin décembre 70% des écoles sont sous occupation. Mais c'est quoi une occupation ? Réveil à 6h du matin, première fois dans ma vie que je suis tellement motivée pour aller à l'école, avant même que le réveil sonne. En même temps, j'ai peur. Il y a eu des endroits où ça s'est mal passé. Les bruits courent, nos oreilles sont jeunes. Est-ce que les flics seront là pour nous empêcher ? ll paraît que… Chhuut, prends ton courage à deux main, dis rien aux parents, vas-y. Ton fréro sera là.


Finalement c'est calme, on rentre dans l'école, on change les serrures, on organise un passage filtré, on déplace des tables et des chaises pour faire des barricades, à 8h30 c'est acquis. L'école est à nous !

Mais c'est qui “nous” ?


Je n'ai jamais autant appris que pendant ces quelques semaines d'occupation. Les livres m'ont appris à me poser des questions parce que je les avait vécues. Toute mon expérience d'intelligence collective, de vie commune, de faire-ensemble n'a été que le prolongement de cette école. De ce qu'elle avait mis comme graine dans ma terre aride d'adolescente mal dans sa peau. Cette première occupation a été la plus grande école du commun. Je me revois avec deux amies, dans les toilettes du collège, en train de passer la serpillière. L'école est à nous, il faut faire le ménage. Jamais avant je n'avais senti sous ma peau ce que peut être le mot solidarité, responsabilité commune, qu'en tenant cette serpillière dans mes mains et en rigolant avec les amies, fière comme un sapin. Je crois que les parents nous ont pas reconnu après ça, c'était une sorte de dépucelage. Déjà les toilettes du collège, tout le monde le sait, en temps normal, c'est pourri, ça pue, on ne s'approche jamais, on s'organise pour aller à la maison. Et tant pis si tu es une fille “réglée”, il faut se débrouiller. Essayer le café du coin en sautant par dessus les grillages. Mais ça, c'était le temps normal. Nous vivions maintenant le temps de l'occupation. Dépucelage du commun.


Le lendemain du premier jour de l'occupation, des gamins ont essayé de pénétrer le bureau du principal pour essayer de détruire des documents, d'autres ont décoré les grands couloirs avec toutes sortes de grafitis, plutôt marrant d'ailleurs, mais qui risquaient de se retourner contre “nous”. Ils n'attendaient que ça : dégradation de biens publics, pour faire rentrer la matraque et tourner l'opinion publique. Première AG et premières questions : Quelles sont nos règles ici ? Comment veille-t-on à l'occupation ? A nous, à chacun et à chacune de nous ? Comment se surveille-t-on alors qu'il n'y a pas d'Autorité ? Si l'occupation reste ouverte aux personnes extérieures, comment fixer des limites ? Il n'est de plus grande école que cette expérience concrète, tangible et tendue : personne nous impose des règles.

Le commun est ce que nous avons à régler ensemble

.


Les règles redeviennent alors ce qu'elles ont été lorsque nous jouions dans le bac à sable avec d'autres enfants au parc ou en bas des immeubles entre-deux flaques d'eau. On l'oublie beaucoup, mais avant d'aller à l'école maternelle, c'est une évidence tangible : jouer, c'est jouer avec les règles. Celles-ci sont une matière plastique, une pâte à modeler, à expérimenter avec des manières de faire, de ne pas faire, et bien sûr des manières de rater encore, d'échouer mieux. Tiens ici ça va être le coin cuisine ! Et ici à côté de l'arbre, c'est… Nooon ! On n'a pas …

With authoritarian and fascist parties gaining substantial popular support all across the world, maybe it's time for anarchists to reconsider one of our movement’s most persistent assumptions: that "the people" are, in some latent sense, a revolutionary force waiting to be awakened by true believers.

As fascists and other authoritarians outnumber us by practically ten thousand to one in this rapidly collapsing empire, anarchists ought to take a sober look around them and abandon the comforting fiction that we live to serve "the people" and bring about their emancipation. That "the people" yearn for freedom and would stand with us if only we could inspire them with our good deeds and thoughtful theory.

The people are not automatically allies of liberation. Mass-society is much more often the social base through which domination reproduces itself. Again and again, when the masses have their privileges threatened, they rally to hierarchy, nationalism, nativism, patriarchy, and obedience, expunging class solidarity in favor of the promise of a higher place on the ladder of whiteness.

Anyone with any instinct for self-preservation ought to abandon the fruitless fantasy that our mission under this fascist social order is to educate the masses — to reveal their "true" interests and thereby set them on the path to class consciousness, even as an overwhelming majority of them toil feverishly to bring their fascist despots to power and to wage genocide on the most impoverished souls on the planet.

The idea that our zines and memes can compete with billionaires and the 24/7 algorithms that feed billions of people a relentless stream of authoritarianism, fear, and hatred is laughable.

I’ve long been rebuked within the milieu for rhetoric deemed too hostile, too alienating, too negative, too likely to frighten away the poor, innocent reactionary elements whose support we are apparently expected to cultivate.

The truth is I never cared about "converting" feckless authority-cravers to anarchy.

My mission was never to win over every liberal settler, every future landlord, every aspiring bureaucrat, every eager democrat, every left-wing Zionist, every comfortable professional, or every reactionary who might be persuaded to call themselves an anarchist. It was never to assemble the largest possible coalition by sanding down every point of conflict until anarchy became palatable to people invested in the existing order.

All I ever cared about was confronting the relationships and institutions through which domination is reproduced, and to foster solidarity with those ready and willing to resist them.

The people are not sacred. Their collective will is not inherently virtuous, nor is it beyond criticism. Their democratic "right" to choose fascism is not inviolable. Majorities forge domination much more effectively than the hapless, disconnected few who dare resist it.

Anarchists should be ready to confront, contest, and push back against the masses, while understanding how they become vehicles for …

title: Το δολοφονικό χέρι του φασισμού ξαναχτύπησε στην Ελευσίνα! – Συγκέντρωση Δευτέρα 12/10 18:30 Καμάρα
content:
ΑΝΤΙΦΑΣΙΣΤΙΚΗ ΚΙΝΗΤΟΠΟΙΗΣΗ- ΚΑΤΑΓΓΕΛΙΑ ΤΗΣ ΕΠΙΘΕΣΗΣ ΣΤΗΝ ΕΛΕΥΣΙΝΑ


Το δολοφονικό χέρι του φασισμού ξαναχτύπησε στην Ελευσίνα! Λαός και νεολαία θα το τσακίσουν!


Με πολύ πρόσφατη την αποφυλάκιση και την επανεμφάνιση στο πολιτικό σκηνικό του αρχιναζί Κασιδιάρη και λίγο μόλις καιρό μετά τις επιθέσεις φασιστοειδών σε μετανάστες στην Αθήνα και στη Λάρισα, και σε νέους ανθρώπους στην Αμοργό, το δολοφονικό χέρι του φασισμού ξαναχτύπησε. Στην Ελευσίνα αυτή τη φορά, όπου δύο άτομα, (μέλη, όπως αναφέρεται, της νεοναζιστικής οργάνωσης Propatria) μαχαίρωσαν έναν αντιφασίστα, νέο άνθρωπο, στήνοντάς του καρτέρι έξω από το σπίτι του το απόγευμα της Πέμπτης 8/10. Ευτυχώς γλύτωσε η ζωή του, αφού αστόχησαν να τον μαχαιρώσουν στην κοιλιά, ωστόσο φέρνει σοβαρά τραύματα στα πόδια, για τα οποία διακομίστηκε στο νοσοκομείο. Οι δράστες δεν έκρυψαν τη μαύρη ιδιότητά τους, δηλώνοντάς του πως «είναι φασίστες». Χαρακτηριστική ήταν η στάση του αστικού Τύπου, που προσπάθησε αρχικά να παρουσιάσει το γεγονός ως μια «απόπειρα ληστείας», αποκρύπτοντας τον χαρακτήρα της φασιστικής επίθεσης, όπως είχε συμβεί και στο παρελθόν με τις δολοφονίες Φύσσα και Γρηγορόπουλου.


Το φονικό χέρι των κάθε είδους νεοναζί το οπλίζει η ίδια η πολιτική του συστήματος της εξάρτησης και της εκμετάλλευσης. Η εντεινόμενη φασιστικοποίηση της πολιτικής ζωής, η εξυπηρέτηση των δολοφονικών σχεδίων ΗΠΑ-ΝΑΤΟ-ΕΕ-Ισραήλ, τα εθνικιστικά και σοβινιστικά κηρύγματα ενάντια στους γείτονες λαούς, η στοχοποίηση των προσφύγων και των μεταναστών, αλλά και των νέων ανθρώπων και των αγωνιστών, όλων όσων τολμούν να αμφισβητήσουν τη συστημική πολιτική της ντόπιας άρχουσας τάξης και των ξένων ιμπεριαλιστικών αφεντικών. Το οπλίζει η εξυπηρέτηση των πολεμικών σχεδίων των ισχυρών του πλανήτη, η στρατιωτικοποίηση των οικονομιών, η πολιτική της φτώχειας της εξαθλίωσης, της περιθωριοποίησης.


Η νέα αυτή δολοφονική φασιστική επίθεση δεν πρέπει να μείνει αναπάντητη! Το φασιστικό φίδι σηκώνει ξανά κεφάλι. Να μην το αφήσουμε! Μόνο ο λαός, οι εργαζόμενοι και η νεολαία μπορούν να το τσακίσουν

title: Résurgences du franquisme et contradictions : des livres aux relations avec Israël
content:
Texte publié dans le numéro 1886 du journal mensuel de la Fédération Anarchiste «

 

Le Monde Libertaire

 

» sorti en septembre 2026.


Le 29 novembre 2025, le «

 

Cercle Franco-Hispanique

 

» comptait organiser une messe en hommage à Franco pour le 50

e

 anniversaire de sa mort. Elle devait se tenir à la chapelle Notre-Dame-de-Consolidation tenue par la Fraternité Sacerdotale Saint-Pie-X et située dans le huitième arrondissement de Paris. Finalement annulée, cette messe met en lumière un réseau s'étendant à des sphères relativement groupusculaires de l'extrême-droite mais toujours bel et bien vivantes.


«

 

Francisco Franco, un caudillo pour l'Espagne

 

», «

 

Les griffes de Staline sur l'Espagne républicaine

 

», «

 

La trahison des gauches espagnoles

 

» ou encore «

 

L'Espagne ensanglantée : anarchistes, milices socialistes, communistes et révolutionnaires : 1880-1939

 

». Depuis la parution en 2022 de la traduction en français du livre «

 

Les mythes de la guerre d'Espagne

 

» de Pío Moa, le «

 

néo-franquisme

 

» semble s'installer en France via la littérature.


L'auteur des quatre livres aux titres enflammés cités plus haut n'est pour sa part nul autre que Michel Festivi. Ces «

 

ouvrages

 

» édités par Dualpha et Synthèse Nationale propagent ainsi l'idée d'une Espagne républicaine soumise à Staline, à l'

URSS

 et en définitive neutralisée par un homme providentiel s'appuyant sur les troupes espagnoles au Maroc.


Un éditeur comme Dualpha mérite que nous nous attardions un peu sur son histoire. Hébergé par le site internet francephi.com, Dualpha a été fondée en 1988 par Philippe-André Duquesne dit Philippe Randa. Dans le livre «

 

Histoire de la librairie française

 

», l'historien Julien Hage nous dresse une liste de librairies ayant publié ou publiant encore des livres tels que ceux cités plus haut : la «

 

Librairie française

 

» fondée en 1952 par l'ancien vichyste Henry Coston, Ogmios, installée en 1986 dans l'ancien immeuble du Parti Populaire Français de Jacques Doriot, la «

 

Librairie nationale

 

», la «

 

Licorne bleue

 

» ou encre «

 

L'Æncre

 

».


Aujourd'hui, seule la Librairie française est restée debout. Elle vend par exemple les livres de Michel Festivi mais aussi celui de Christophe Dolbeau qui estime que le coup d'État de Franco n'était rien de moins qu'un «

 

légitime réflexe d'auto-défense de l'Espagne éternelle

 

» (1). Des livres de Robert Brasillach y trônent de plus en bonne place si l'on en croit la collection pléthorique présentée sur le site de cet établissement (2). Situé au 202 rue Lecourbe dans le quinzième arrondissement de Paris, il vend aussi des livres aux éditions L'Æncre comme celui de Guillaume Faye intitulé «

 

Pourquoi nous combattons : manifeste de la résistance européenne

 

».


Le néo-franquisme redonne ainsi une nouvelle jeunesse à toute cette propagande. Le Figaro Histoire sort de son côté une interview de Pío Moa dans son numéro d'août-septembre 2022 consacré à «

 

l'épopée des conquistadors

 

» (3). Celui-ci y affirme que le «

 

discours communiste sur la guerre d'Espagne règne encore dans toute l'Europe

 

» et déplore que le franquisme ait «

 

perdu la bataille de la propagande et de la culture

 

» (4).


Cette dernière affirmation de Pío Moa se couple cependant avec les quelques désaccords qui subsistent aujourd'hui entre les néo-franquistes. Un exemple frappant est celui du député du parti d'extrême-droite Vox Hermann Tertsch et de la néo-nazie Isabel Peralta. Membre d'une obscure «

 

Sección de Asalto

 

» (en français «

 

Section d'Assaut

 

», en référence aux

SA

 de l'Allemagne nazie) et du parti

FE

-La Falange, cette dernière a également fondé en 2020 le «

 

Bastión Frontal

 

». Le 13 février 2020 durant un hommage aux soldats de la Division Bleue qui a combattu avec les nazis pendant la Seconde Guerre mondiale, elle déclare : «

 

l'ennemi sera toujours le même, même s'il porte des masques différents : le Juif, car rien n'est plus certain que cette affirmation : le Juif est responsable

 

» (5).


Immédiatement dénoncé par Vox, ce discours indigne dans le même temps des anciens de la Division Bleue qui nient avoir été responsables d'une façon ou d'une autre du génocide des juif·ve·s (6). Hermann Tertsch lui a participé en mars 2025 à une «

 

conférence internationale de lutte contre l'antisémitisme

 

» en Israël à l'invitation de son premier ministre …

author: Γιάννης Βολιάτης
title: Επίθεση φασιστών με μαχαίρι στην Ελευσίνα: Δεν μας τρομάζουν, θα τρομάξουν αυτοί!
content:
Επίθεση φασιστών με μαχαίρι στην Ελευσίνα: Δεν μας τρομάζουν, θα τρομάξουν αυτοί!


Επίθεση με μαχαίρι εναντίον αντιφασίστα αγωνιστή πραγματοποίησαν εχθές το μεσημέρι δυο νεοναζί στην Ελευσίνα, όπως έγινε γνωστό από την σελίδα

Antifa West Coast Reloaded

. Σύμφωνα με τις μαρτυρίες, ο αντιφασίστας κατάφερε να σπάσει στο ξύλο με άνεση τον έναν από τους δύο επιτιθέμενους, αλλά ο δεύτερος έβγαλε μαχαίρι και του κατάφερε πισώπλατα χτυπήματα στα πόδια, ενώ προσπάθησε να τον μαχαιρώσει και στο στήθος, ευτυχώς χωρίς επιτυχία.

Σε σημερινές του δηλώσεις σε ενημερωτικό μέσο


ο αντιφασίστας αφηγήθηκε το χρονικό της επίθεσης και της μεταφοράς του στο νοσοκομείο από περαστικό οδηγό ΙΧ:


«Γύρω στις 4:10 είχα βγάλει τα δύο σκυλιά μου βόλτα κάτω από το σπίτι μου στην Ελευσίνα. Ενώ έβγαινα από το σπίτι, πέρασε το μηχανάκι με τον έναν από τους δυο. Με κοίταξε, συνέχισε την πορεία του για δυο-τρία τετράγωνα και επέστρεψε μαζί με άλλον έναν.


Άρχισαν να μου φωνάζουν “έλα εδώ να σου πούμε” κλπ. Ο ένας δεν φορούσε κράνος και κατάλαβα ποιος είναι, είναι γνωστοί νεοναζί στην περιοχή. Θεωρούσα ότι έχουν έρθει να διαπληκτιστούμε λεκτικά. Επειδή είχα μαζί τα σκυλιά και ήταν κοντά και ένα ανήλικο κοριτσάκι, προσπαθούσα να αποφύγω να γίνει αυτό. Ήταν μέρα μεσημέρι. Τους έλεγα “Περιμένετε, φύγετε, τι θέλετε από μένα”. Αυτός που δεν φορούσε κράνος άρχισε να μου λέει “είμαστε φασίστες σας γαμ***ε σας κάνουμε, σας δείχνουμε, σε ξέρουμε”. Εγώ προσπαθούσα και πάλι να κρατήσω χαμηλά την ένταση και τους ρώτησα τι θέλουν από μένα. Μου απάντησαν πως προσωπικά δεν τους έχω κάνει κάτι αλλά ξέρουν ποιος είμαι και ξέρουν σε ποιον χώρο ανήκω, ότι είμαι αντιφασίστας. 


Θεωρούσα ότι αυτός έχει μαχαίρι και αυτό ήταν το λάθος μου. Κατέβηκε κάτω, μου επιτέθηκε και άρχισα να τον χτυπάω και τον πέταξα στο έδαφος. Όμως το μαχαίρι το είχε ο άλλος και όση ώρα τον χτυπούσα φώναζε στον δεύτερο που ήταν μαζί του “Σπάστον, δώστο, σπάστον”. Αρχίζω να νιώθω τις μαχαιριές και του λέω “τι κάνεις ρε ηλίθιε με μαχαιρώνεις;” Με μαχαίρωσε στα δύο πόδια και προσπάθησε να με μαχαιρώσει στο στήθος. Το απέφυγα αλλά έμεινε σημάδι που φαίνεται η προσπάθεια του.»


Τότε ήταν που έκανε την εμφάνισή του τυχαία ένας περαστικός με ΙΧ:


«Εκείνοι τράπηκαν σε φυγή και εγώ είπα στον περαστικό “Φίλε με έχουν σφάξει μπορείς να με πας στο νοσοκομείο;”. Έχανα αίμα, πίεζα τη φλέβα για να μη χάσω πολύ και με το άλλο χέρι μου πήρα τηλέφωνο τη μητέρα μου και της είπα “Αν δεν τα καταφέρω να ξέρεις με έφαγαν αυτοί, λέγοντας της ποιοι είναι”. Έβλεπα τους πίδακες του αίματος και δεν ήξερα αν θα είναι θανατηφόρο. Προς τιμήν του, ο περαστικός σταμάτησε, με έβαλε στο αυτοκίνητο και με πήγε στο κέντρο υγείας.


Είναι επίθεση θρασύδειλων, ήρθαν εξοπλισμένοι, με κράνη, με μαχαίρι και για να απεμπλακούν από την ίδια τους την ενέδρα, όταν είδαν ότι αντιστάθηκα και μπόρεσα να τους χτυπήσω, αποφάσισαν να με μαχαιρώσουν. Εγώ αυτό που έχω σαν επιθυμία είναι

το προοδευτικό κομμάτι της κοινωνίας, οι δημοκρατικοί άνθρωποι να απομονώσουν αυτά τα στοιχεία.

 Πέρα από όποια ιδεολογική διαφορά μπορεί να έχουμε όλοι με όλους, δεν γίνεται να ανεχόμαστε στους κόλπους της κοινωνίας μας τους νεοναζί, στα σχολεία και τις γειτονιές».


Σύμφωνα με τις πληροφορίες ο αντιφασίστας σύντροφος μεταφέρθηκε με το ΙΧ σε κέντρο υγείας και από εκεί με ασθενοφόρο στο Τζάνειο Νοσοκομείο. Έχει αποφύγει τον κίνδυνο.


Τα μαχαίρια ακονίζονται ξανά…


Είναι προφανές εδώ και αρκετό χρονικό διάστημα πως οι φασίστες έχουν βγει και πάλι από τις τρύπες τους. Και είναι φυσικό. Το καπιταλιστικό σύστημα σαπίζει, κατασπαράσσει το εαυτό του, γεννά πολέμους και γενοκτονίες για να καταφέρει να επιβιώσει και να αναγεννηθεί μέσω της πολεμικής βιομηχανίας και της σκληρής επίθεσης στην τάξη μας. Σε τέτοιες περιόδους είναι που εργαλειοποιείται από το Κεφάλαιο και το Κράτος η εθνικιστική ρητορική και η μισαλλοδοξία, ώστε να κρατηθεί η τάξη μας διαιρεμένη απέναντι στον πραγματικό εχθρό και να στραφούμε ο ένας απέναντι στην άλλη με βάση εθνικούς, θρησκευτικούς και άλλους ψευδείς διαχωρισμούς.


Είναι σε τέτοιες περιόδους επίσης που πριμοδοτείται και η δράση των φασιστών, ώστε να αποπροσανατολίσουν την τάξη μας αλλά και να παριστάνουν τον δήθεν “αντίπαλο” του συστήματος, ενώ ταυτόχρονα κάνουν την βρώμικη δουλειά του. Δεν είναι τυχαία η “αντισυστημική” ταμπέλα που προσπαθεί να αποδώσει στον εαυτό του ο προσφάτως αποφυλακισθέντας Κασιδιάρης, την ίδια ώρα που τα ΜΜΕ τον προωθούν με κάθε τρόπο, χτίζοντας την εικόνα του “νούμερο ένα κινδύνου για την Δημοκρατία”. title: AfD im Bundestag fordert Verbot von „Antifa“, indymedia.de und Roter Hilfe
content:
Die rechtsextreme AfD versucht in Deutschland auf Bundes- wie auf Länderebene Antifaschismus zu kriminalisieren, anzugreifen und zu verbieten. Wie läuft das im Bundestag und wie auf Ländereben?


In einem aktuellen Entschließungsantrag für den Deutschen Bundestag fordert die AfD im Rahmen ihrer „24 Maßnahmen gegen linksextremistische Gewalt und Terror“ unter anderem ein Verbot der „Antifa“ sowie der Roten Hilfe. Hinsichtlich der Antifa, richtet sich der AfD-Antrag exemplarisch gegen die„Antifa Süd“. Ferner wird ein Verbot und Abschaltung der Website de.indymedia.org gefordert.


Der AfD-Antrag- ein Sammelsurium an Forderungen


Erst am 06.10.2026 legte die AfD-Fraktion im Bundestag, darunter so berüchtigte Rechtsextremisten wie

Martin Hess

,

Gottfried Curio

,

Bernd Baumann

,

Maximilian Krah

, einen achtseitigen Entschließungsantrag (

als PDF

) vor, in welchem sie 24 Forderungen aufstellt.


Das Sammelsurium der Forderungen reicht von einer „erheblichen personellen Verstärkung der für die Aufklärung und Ermittlung im Bereich des Linksextremismus zuständigen Abteilungen der Sicherheitsbehörden“, über „regelmäßige Erstellung von internen Lagebildern durch das BKA zur aktuellen Gefährdungslage durch gewaltorientierte Linksextremisten mit Serien- und Musteranalyse“ bis hin zur Forderung der „dauerhafte(n) Räumungen aller besetzten Szeneobjekte, (…) wie beispielsweise der „Rigaer Straße 94“ in Berlin oder der „Roten Flora“ in Hamburg, die rechtswidrig von Linksextremisten in Besitz genommen wurden und von denen aus wiederholt Straftaten verübt worden sind oder die als Unterschlupf für linksextremistische Gewalttäter dienen“.


Aber auch ein „Verbot und Abschaltung der Website de.indymedia.org als Nachfolgeplattform von linksunten.indymedia.org“, wird gefordert, ferner die „konsequente Prüfung von Verboten nach dem Vereinsgesetz in Bezug auf linksextremistische Gruppierungen, die sich unter der Bezeichnung „Antifa“oder „Antifaschistische Aktion“ zusammengeschlossen haben“ sowie ein „Verbot der Roten Hilfe e.V. (RH), da diese bundesweit „linksextremistische und mithin verfassungsfeindliche Ziele von unterschiedlicher Intensität“ verfolgt“.


Begründung der AfD


Der Einstieg des Antrages der AfD bildet ein Verweis auf „die Vorgänge rund um die Berliner Wahlsiegerin DIE LINKE, an deren Wahlparty Vertreter aus dem Clanmilieu und Islamisten teilgenommen haben“, diese würden „dabei nur die Spitze eines Eisbergs dar(stellen), auf den Deutschland sicherheitspolitisch ungebremst zusteuert“. Anschließend geht es in einem wilden Parforceritt von einem „gezielten Brandanschlag auf das Stromnetz im Raum Berlin Steglitz-Zehlendorf zu Beginn des Jahres“, welchen der „Vulkangruppe“ zugerechnet wird, über einen weiteren „Anschlag (…) im Juni dieses Jahres in Reutlingen“ über welchen auf „der linksextremistischen Internetseite „Switch Off““ umfassend berichtet worden sei. Nicht fehlen dürfen „die konspirativ vorbereiteten Überfälle der sogenannten „Antifa-Ost“ oder auch „Hammerbande“ genannt, denn diese würden „das ganze Ausmaß der Eskalation (zeigen): Gezielte Angriffe auf Menschen, bei denen Opfer schwerste Verletzungen erlitten haben.“


Die RAF wird auch noch erwähnt, denn „bei den Hammerbandenprozessen handelt es sich (…) um die umfangreichsten Verfahren gegen Linksextremisten seit den RAF-Prozessen vor knapp 50 Jahren“, so die AfD.


Weitere Schlagworte „Missbrauch der Versammlungsfreiheit durch Linksextremisten“, Bekämpfung der „Gefahren durch linke Militanz“ vermittels der oben genannten Verbote, denn, so die AfD-Abgeordneten, „um diese Fehlentwicklungen aufzuhalten, müssen auch linksextremistische Strukturen zerschlagen werden. Vereinsrechtliche Verbotsverfahren gegen gewaltlegitimierende Strukturen der Antifa müssen vorrangig geprüft und konsequent umgesetzt werden“.


Die Rote Hilfe ist der AfD besonders ein Dorn im Auge, denn, so die Begründung des Antrags, die Rote Hilfe sei „mit rund 14.400 Mitgliedern und bundesweit rund 50 Ortsgruppen die größte und eine der wichtigsten Gruppierungen im deutschen Linksextremismus. Sie bietet nicht nur einen Legitimationsrahmen für die Begehung von Straf- und Gewalttaten“. Insbesondere befürworte und unterstütze sie „die Anwendung von Gewalt als Mittel der politischen Auseinandersetzung“.


Fazit und Ausblick


Der Bundestag hat am 08.10.2026 rund eine Stunde lang über den Antrag der AfD im Plenum

öffentlich beraten

. Vermutlich wird er im Anschluss daran an die Ausschüsse …

author: Redazione_web
title: L’esperimento spagnolo. Le tante luci di un’epopea proletaria
content:
La Rivoluzione Spagnola è stato l’esperimento più avanzato nel superamento della società basata sulla proprietà privata e sul dominio del governo. Questa rivoluzione è stata soffocata dalle truppe nazionaliste guidate dal generale Francisco Franco il 1° marzo del 1939. I nazionalisti erano sostenuti da una coalizione internazionale di governi imperialisti guidata dal Regno Unito e dalla Francia, che ha appoggiato l’intervento militare della Germania e soprattutto dell’Italia.


Questa coalizione internazionale si è tradotta in un’interpretazione storica che ha condannato senza appello l’esperienza rivoluzionaria spagnola. Una condanna su cui concordano, sia pure con motivazioni diverse, gli storici reazionari, quelli liberali e quelli marxisti delle varie scuole.


L’esperimento rivoluzionario spagnolo, fin da quando era in corso, attirò su di sé le critiche delle componenti interclassiste, antiorganizzatrici e individualiste del movimento anarchico, critiche che spesso hanno messo in secondo piano il valore di quella esperienza.


Scopo di questo articolo è mettere in evidenza le conquiste del proletariato spagnolo, al di là degli errori e delle carenze che non inficiano i risultati raggiunti, e l’utilità degli insegnamenti provenienti dai settantasei anni di lotte che precedettero il 19 luglio 1936 per il proletariato di tutti i paesi, in marcia verso la rivoluzione sociale.


Mi limiterò ad alcune considerazioni. La prima, e la più importante, è che il modello organizzativo del proletariato spagnolo, basato su un’organizzazione politica anarchica e su un’organizzazione di massa autonoma da ogni partito e tendenzialmente unitaria, tanto che al suo interno convivevano diverse tendenze oltre a quella anarchica, ha sconfitto per tre volte il fascismo. La prima volta quando pose fine alla pratica del pistolerismo, cioè all’assassinio sistematico degli attivisti sindacali e dei militanti anarchici da parte di gangster assoldati dai capitalisti. Sotto i colpi dei pistoleros cadde anche Salvador Seguì, segretario della CNT (Confederación Nacional del Trabajo): Fu allora che esponenti del movimento anarchico e sindacale decisero di rispondere eliminando il capo della reazione antiproletaria, il cardinale Juan Soldevilla y Romero, arcivescovo di Saragozza. Un atto che seppe fermare la pratica del pistolerismo.


La seconda volta quando nel 1929 il dittatore Miguel Primo de Rivera fu costretto alle dimissioni e l’anno dopo cadde la monarchia. La terza volta quando il colpo di Stato dei generali contro la repubblica e il governo di fronte popolare, iniziato il 17 luglio 1936, fu sconfitto in gran parte della Spagna dalla pronta reazione popolare ispirata dalla Federacion Anarquista Iberica. Nel dibattito storico è stata spesso sottovalutata questa reazione: è stato sostenuto che, dal punto di vista militare, il colpo di stato sia stato sconfitto dallo schierarsi di alcune unità delle forze armate con il governo legittimo. Ritengo che proprio questo conferma l’importanza della reazione popolare, che ha creato il clima politico in cui i militari fedeli alla repubblica hanno potuto schierarsi con il movimento proletario.


Questa riflessione è tanto più importante se si pensa che negli stessi anni il fascismo si andava affermando, dopo l’Italia, in altri stati europei dove era presente un movimento operaio organizzato egemonizzato dalle componenti autoritarie come i partiti socialdemocratici e stalinisti. Le consecutive sconfitte del movimento operaio tedesco (1914 entrata in guerra della Germania, 1919 sconfitta della rivoluzione dei consigli, 1933 nomina di Adolf Hitler cancelliere del Reich) dimostrano l’incapacità dell’organizzazione autoritaria e burocratica di resistere alla reazione.


Un luogo comune, condiviso anche in ambito anarchico, è che lo stalinismo abbia sconfitto la rivoluzione libertaria in Spagna, provocandone la fine. In realtà lo stalinismo ha subito in Spagna una sconfitta da cui si sarebbe ripreso solo con la guerra mondiale.


Negli ultimi mesi del 1936 l’Unione Sovietica inviò ingenti aiuti alla Repubblica spagnola; questo ebbe dei contraccolpi nella situazione interna aumentando il peso del Partito Comunista, che assorbì le scarse forze socialiste in Catalogna dando vita al Partito Socialista Unificato della Catalogna, al tempo stesso estese la sua influenza sulla gioventù socialista, che si unì a quella comunista. title: Eyewitness report: Strikers and students rock France, Anti-fascism and Palestinian liberation mixed with anger at president Emmanuel Macron and the establishment (Socialist Worker-UK)
content:
Anti-fascism and Palestinian liberation mixed with anger at president Emmanuel Macron and the establishment

On the streets of Paris (Picture: Guy Smallman)

There were protests in 40 cities across France on Tuesday as workers and parents joined the movement of secondary school students demanding a future.

In Paris, organisers said 100,000 packed the streets. They were overwhelmingly young school and university students.

Young people chanted anti-fascist slogans. They included, “La jeunesse emmerde le Front National”—“The youth tell the Front National to fuck off” in a reference to the previous name of the fascist RN. And, “Siamo tutti antifascisti”—“We are all anti-fascist”.

They sang the Internationale and the French national anthem La Marseillaise. And there were Palestinian flags and chants of “free Palestine”. Other home made placards referenced the student and worker uprising of 1968.

When the presidential candidate for the left wing LFI party, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, arrived at the start of the march, he was mobbed by crowds of people. Both young and older protesters greeted him with chants of “president Mélenchon”.

Mélenchon called on his supporters, including many members of parliament, to join the protests. He wore a white armband on Tuesday to symbolise his support for the high school students.

As the march arrived in Place de la Nation, hundreds of riot police attacked with huge clouds of tear gas and charged at the crowd with batons. Protesters threw fireworks and set bins on fire.

Nora, Sarah and Sonia, three university students, spoke to Socialist Worker about their reasons for joining the protest.

“We protest for the rights of high school students,” they said. “All the media talks about is violence. But there are real reasons behind their protests.

“The RN is fascist. It’s homophobic and Islamophobic”.

Another student, Alice, said that young people are worried about their futures, “We are all worried about fascism, every student is worried about that. And about finding a job, everything is kind of scary.

“High school students are very stressed. We went through that so we want to be here with them.”

Trade unionists linked arms and faced up to cops with tear gas.

Pierre works in the tax office and is part of the Solidaires union federation. He told Socialist Worker, “I am on strike today, in solidarity with the students against repression and because we have the same problems with austerity.”

Clement, from the CFDT union federation, told Socialist Worker, “The demands of the school students are totally legitimate. The buildings are crumbling, there are rats in the classrooms, there are 30, 35 or even 40 people in a classroom.

“It’s a terrible period with the far right rising across Europe. We could see fascism in France for the second time in its history.”

Clement added that the current president Emmanuel Macron has “rolled out the red carpet for the RN’s Marine Le Pen”.

Another protester mentioned that there are already fascists joining the police force and that Le Pen would use them to smash the movement on the streets if she was in office.

Meet the pupils’ blockade: ‘We are young, determined and revolutionary’

Macron’s austerity measures and repression, combined with the normalisation of racism against migrants has created the conditions for the far right to rise.

Le Pen is currently leading in the polls, while Mélenchon is currently in second place.

The best hope of beating Le Pen will be if the movement stays on the streets and links the anger of the students with the power of the organised working class.

Key opportunities to deepen the movement are coming this month. Total Energy workers are set to strike Thursday—and there is a day of action on 17 October.

Anti-fascists are planning to demonstrate against the far right RN party’s conference on 24 October.

If the movement of school students and strikes deepens, it has the power to transform the political situation in France.

title: Hande Ortaç ile ‘Sus’ üzerine: ‘Yazı benim mücadele alanım’
content:
Yasemin Seven Erangin [email protected]

Hande Ortaç’ın İletişim Yayınlarından çıkan “Sus” romanı, bir polis operasyonuyla başlayan hikayesi üzerinden şiddet, güç ilişkileri, adalet ve suskunlukla yüzleşiyor. Biri şiddeti iktidar kurmanın aracı olarak kullanan, diğeri ise maruz kaldığı sistematik şiddetin ardından öz savunmaya başvuran iki karakterin hikayesini karşı karşıya getiren roman, suçun yalnızca sonucuna değil, onu doğuran koşullara da bakıyor.

Romanın ilk cümlesinden itibaren güçlü bir “av” metaforu kuruyorsunuz: “Bir av partisinin en masumu avın ta kendisi değil midir?” Sus’u yazarken bu metafor sizin için ne ifade ediyordu?

Roman, tüm İstanbul’u etkisi altına alan bir polis operasyonuyla başlıyor. Avcılar kolluk kuvvetini temsil ediyor. Toplum için tehlikeli olduğuna inandırıldığımız bir katili kovalıyorlar. Roman ilerledikçe ortada iki katil olduğunu anlıyoruz. Hikayeler derinleşirken dışarıdaki av devam ediyor ve günün sonunda sadece biri yakalanacak.

Bu metaforda ısrar ediyorum çünkü söylemi kurma ayrıcalığına sahip olanların peşine düştükleri genellikle en güçsüzler oluyor. Güç sahibinin, iktidar yakınının işlediği suçların çoğunlukla cezalandırılmadığını, hatta alkışlandığını görüyoruz. Gerçek suçlu eğer erkten yanaysa avcıların cephesinde yer alıyor. Romanı yazarken bir avın sonunda mutlaka en masumun öldürüldüğünü hep aklımda tuttum.

Sus, suçun kendisinden çok suçu doğuran koşullarla yüzleştiriyor. Sizce adalet her zaman eşitlik demek midir? Bir insanı suça götüren koşullar, o suçun değerlendirilmesinde ne kadar belirleyici olmalı?

Adaletin eşitlikle değil hakkaniyetle daha sıkı bir ilişkisi olduğunu düşünüyorum. Kadın ve erkek benzer koşullarda, şiddet sarmalında büyümüş iki karakter. Fakat biri eril gücü ve şiddeti iktidar kurmanın aracı olarak görüyor, diğeri ise hayatının her aşamasında şiddet mağduru olmasına rağmen şiddeti araçsallaştırmıyor.

İkisi de birini öldürüyor ama eylemlerinin sebepleri arasında dağlar kadar fark var. Sonuç benzer olsa da iki olayı bağlamlarından bağımsız değerlendirmek mümkün değil. Hayat siyah ve beyazdan ibaret değil, aradaki tüm tonlar da vicdan ve akıl muhasebesi için.

Kadın karakteri, kendisine şiddet uygulayan kocasını öldürüyor. Bir kadının hayatta kalma mücadelesi hangi noktada öz savunmaya dönüşür?

“Öz savunma” kavramını indirgemeden verebilmek için olayları bağlamından koparmadan anlatmaya gayret ettim. Ataerkil şiddetin, karşısındakinin cezayı hak ettiğini düşünüp had bildirmeyi kendinde hak gören yaklaşımını deşifre etmeye çalıştım.

Sistematik şiddetin ve tacizin görünmeyen, konuşulmayan taraflarına yer vermek istedim. “Öz savunma”nın tek bir neden-sonuç düzlemine indirgenemeyecek kadar derin psikolojik bağları olduğunu düşünüyorum. Tek bir anı değil, tüm süreci anlatarak bunu görünür kılmak en büyük amacımdı.

Romanda şiddeti evde, iş yerinde, ilişkilerde ve dijital dünyada farklı biçimleriyle gösteriyorsunuz. Bu şiddet biçimleri aynı toplumsal kaynaktan mı besleniyor?

Dezavantajlı kesimlerin ve hassas kimliklerin sınırları hemen her karşılaşmada aşılabiliyor. Bu gruplara kadınlar ve LGBTİ+’nın yanında engellenen bireyler, çocuklar ve hayvanlar da dahil.

Genç bir kadın okulda, otobüste, sosyal medyada ya da iş yerinde tacize uğrayabiliyor. Medeni olduğunu düşündüğünüz sevgilinizden ya da iş için iletişim kurduğunuz birinden bile beklenmedik bir anda sınır ihlaliyle karşılaşmak mümkün. Bu hadsizliklerin, kontrol etme açlığının ve sınır ihlallerinin en büyük sebebinin güç ilişkilerinde olduğuna inanıyorum. Roman boyunca bu kuşatılmışlığı hissettirmeye gayret ettim.

Erkek karakteri üzerinden sosyal medya trollerini ve dijital dünyadaki kadın düşmanlığını da anlatıyorsunuz. Anonimlik şiddeti artırıyor mu?

Sosyal medya, avatarların ardına sığınarak insana sonsuz bir özgürlük ve hesapsız bir varoluş fırsatı sunuyor. Erkeklik de sıkı kurallara tabi. Makbul bir erkek olursan, oyunu kurallarına göre oynarsan ödülünü alacağın söyleniyor.

Erkeklikten pay alma itkisiyle sosyal medyanın sağladığı güvenli alan birleştiğinde şiddet artıyor. Yüz yüze olmamanın verdiği rahatlıkla şiddet kontrolsüz biçimde büyüyor. Romandaki erkek karakter de erkeklik normlarına uymadığı için zorbalanıyor, ardından şiddeti araçsallaştırmayı seçiyor. Sosyal medya onun için gizlenebileceği ve iktidar kurabileceği bir alan haline geliyor.

Romanın parçalı anlatım biçimi en başından beri tasarladığınız bir yöntem miydi?

“Sus” benim için bu dönemin yaralarıyla yüzleşme …

title: Mor Çatı’nın uluslararası konferansında kadın dayanışması öne çıktı
content:
Mor Çatı Kadın Sığınağı Vakfı, İstanbul Beyoğlu’nda “Kadına Yönelik Şiddetle Mücadelede Dayanışma Merkezleri - Uluslararası Deneyimler” başlıklı bir konferans düzenledi.


MA'nın haberine göre, Konferansın “Dayanışma Merkezleri: Kadına Yönelik Şiddetle Mücadelede Nasıl Bir Dönüşüm Yaşanıyor?” başlıklı ilk oturumunda Avrupa Şiddete Karşı Kadınlar Ağı (WAVE) temsilcisi Elena Floriani, Danimarka’daki Danner kadın örgütünden Ditte Specht ve Mor Çatı’dan Leyla Soydiç konuştu. Oturumu Mor Çatı gönüllüsü Elif Ege yönetti.


“Kadın örgütleri değişimin aktörleri”


WAVE temsilcisi Elena Floriani, kadınlara ve kız çocuklarına yönelik şiddetle mücadelede uzman destek hizmetlerinin önemine dikkat çekti. Bu hizmetlerin kadınların ihtiyaçlarını merkeze aldığını ve kendi yaşamlarına ilişkin kararlarını desteklediğini söyledi.


Kadın örgütlerinin tarihsel mücadelesine değinen Floriani, 1970’lerde feminist aktivistlerin ilk kadın sığınaklarını açarak şiddeti siyasi gündeme taşıdığını hatırlattı.


Kadın örgütlerinin yalnızca destek hizmeti sunmadığını, toplumsal değişime de öncülük ettiğini belirten Floriani, şöyle konuştu:


“Kadın örgütlerinin kadına yönelik şiddetle mücadele politikalarının oluşmasında en önemli itici güç olduğunu araştırmalar gösteriyor. Bu nedenle kadınlara yönelik uzman destek hizmetlerini yalnızca hizmet sağlayıcılar olarak değil, değişimin aktörleri olarak ele alıyoruz.”


WAVE’nin bu yıl yayımladığı

Değişimin Aktörleri

 (Agents of Change) başlıklı raporun bulgularını da paylaşan Floriani, kadın örgütlerinin kadınların güçlenmesinden yasal düzenlemelere ve kurumlar arası işbirliğine kadar birçok alanda etkili olduğunu söyledi.


Şiddete maruz bırakılan kadınlara destek vermenin yalnızca sığınakta bir yatak sağlamaktan ibaret olmadığını vurgulayan Floriani, “Kadınlara özgü bir yaklaşımı olmayan genel hizmetler, uzman destek hizmetlerinin yerini alamaz. Kadına ve kız çocuklarına yönelik şiddetle anlamlı bir mücadele için bu hizmetler vazgeçilmezdir” dedi.


Kadın haklarına yönelik tepkilerin, toplumsal cinsiyet karşıtı hareketlerin ve finansman kısıtlamalarının kadın örgütlerinin çalışmalarını zorlaştırdığını belirten Floriani, uzman destek hizmetlerinin korunması ve güçlendirilmesi çağrısı yaptı.


“Sığınaktan ayrılmakla mücadele sona ermiyor”


Danimarka’daki Danner kadın örgütünden Ditte Specht, kadına yönelik şiddetle mücadelede farklı sektörlerin ve meslek gruplarının işbirliği yapması gerektiğini söyledi.


Kadın sığınaklarında sunulan desteğin, kadınların sığınaktan ayrılmasıyla sona ermediğini vurgulayan Specht, şiddetten uzak bir yaşam kurmanın uzun bir süreç olduğunu belirtti.


Specht, “Kadın sığınaktan ayrıldığında da desteğimiz sona ermiyor; şiddetten uzak bir yaşama giden yol sığınaktan çıkmakla tamamlanmıyor. Hatta gerçek mücadelenin o zaman başladığını söyleyebiliriz” diye konuştu.


“Kadınlar kendi hayatlarının uzmanıdır”


Mor Çatı gönüllüsü Leyla Soydiç, şiddetin kadınların yaşamında uzun yıllar süren sosyal, ekonomik ve ruhsal sonuçlar yarattığını belirterek dayanışma merkezlerinin bu süreçte kadınlara eşlik ettiğini söyledi.


Erkek şiddetini yalnızca bireysel sorunlarla açıklamanın patriyarkayı ve güç ilişkilerini görünmez kıldığını ifade eden Soydiç, kadınların kendi yaşamlarına ilişkin kararları kendilerinin alması gerektiğini vurguladı.


“Zehirli ilişki” şiddeti görünmez kılıyor


Konferansın “Dayanışma Merkezlerini Çeşitlilikle Sürdürmek” başlıklı ikinci oturumunda Fransa, İspanya ve İtalya’dan kadın örgütlerinin temsilcileri deneyimlerini paylaştı. Oturumu Mor Çatı gönüllüsü Selime Büyükgöze yönetti.


Fransa Ulusal Kadın Dayanışma Federasyonu (FNSF) İletişim Birimi Sorumlusu Camille Lextray, kadınların maruz bırakıldığı şiddetin resmi istatistiklere bütünüyle yansımadığına dikkat çekti. Federasyonun Fransa genelinde 80’den fazla derneği bir araya getirdiğini belirten Lextray, yardım hatlarına başvuran kadınların ortalama üç farklı şiddet biçimi bildirdiğini, psikolojik şiddetin yüzde 85 ile ilk sırada yer aldığını söyledi.


Fransa’da aile içi şiddetin giderek “zehirli ilişki” olarak tanımlanmasına karşı çıkan Lextray, bu ifadenin şiddet uygulayan kişinin sorumluluğunu ve ilişkideki tahakkümü görünmez kıldığını belirtti.


Lextray, “Resmi istatistikler yaşananların yalnızca bir bölümünü gösteriyor. Biz resmi kayıtlarda görünmeyenleri ortaya çıkarmak istiyoruz” dedi.

title: Sustam: Those who sow insecurity reap revolt in France - Part One
content:
Student protests that began in high schools in France over educational conditions, staff shortages and deepening inequalities have spread to universities. The protests, which are continuing in many cities, particularly Paris and its suburbs, have brought into view not only discontent with the education system but also young people’s anger over a lack of prospects, poverty and social inequality.


Police interventions and far-right rhetoric criminalizing students have also reignited debates in France over security policies, racism and hostility towards migrants.


ANF spoke to Associate Professor Engin Sustam, a sociologist at Paris 8 University, about the causes of the student protests in France, their connection to the tradition of struggle stretching from 1968 to the present, and their potential to develop into a broader social opposition movement.


How do you assess the student protests that have spread from high schools to universities across France in recent weeks? What are the main social and political dynamics behind this movement?


For several months now, students across France, particularly high school students, have significantly expanded their protests and taken part in blockades, especially in Paris and its major suburbs, as well as in Bordeaux, Lyon and many other areas. High school students have even confronted the police much more forcefully, perhaps more forcefully than ever before in France’s history. According to today’s reports, the government has detained around 5,000 people.


You know the Seine-Saint-Denis area in particular. This is already a pilot area. Especially since La France Insoumise (LFI) won the municipality, policies have emerged that have turned the area into a place where, from the perspective of the police, the government or the security system, many things can be treated as terrorism or suppressed. But this, of course, affects the entire student movement.


Why did the students, particularly high school students, begin protesting? The movement started in Creil, outside Paris. Students said their needs had to be met and staff shortages addressed. There is a shortage of teachers for classes, while educational resources in classrooms are also inadequate. They have also raised many other issues, including lowering cafeteria prices and renovating school buildings.


‘The education system has become a tool of discrimination’


As the protests began to spread, however, they also reached the universities. University students then began raising issues such as Parcoursup, which, as you know, is a very important issue in France, as well as the Mon Master programme. There is a competitive system here. This is an issue that has emerged through the liberal policies that have increasingly taken hold in France, particularly under the Macron government.


Students are ranked according to their grades, placed on waiting lists and, after receiving a yes or no, can ultimately be rejected from those lists. This is more or less how Parcoursup creates discrimination. The education system has become a tool of discrimination.


The French National Student Assemblies also raised this issue during a Senate session in 2026, pointing to Parcoursup and similar systems. If you do not obtain the bac (baccalauréat) in high school, you cannot enter university in France. All of these mechanisms create discrimination in one way or another, and because students encounter this discrimination from high school onwards, I think they have now reached a breaking point.


The issue has also begun to go beyond students’ everyday needs. At universities, student meals are provided through student restaurants known as CROUS, but high school students do not have the same system.


There has also been a serious increase in sexual violence, gender-based violence and violence within high schools. There is also a very significant divide between central high schools, particularly those in central Paris and schools attended by students from more privileged classes, and high schools in the suburbs.


The protests have brought issues such as inadequate resources and staffing in education, student poverty, inequality and insecurity about the future to the fore. Do you think young people in France today are primarily protesting against the education system, or against the broader economic and political order?


At first, the students were focused entirely on the education system and, at the local level, even solely on shortcomings in …

author: Victoria Law
title: Mississippi Is in Danger of Executing Woman on Death Row, Despite Key Evidence
content:
Lisa Jo Chamberlin’s co-defendant confessed to coercing her into their crime. Will that be enough to stop her execution?

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Lisa Jo Chamberlin’s life has always been a tangle of drug use, abuse, and extreme violence. Her mother drank and used Sudafed heavily during her pregnancy. As a result, Chamberlin was born with Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD), a group of medical conditions, including poor reasoning and judgment skills, learning disabilities, and intellectual disability, that occur when a fetus is exposed to alcohol.People with FASD are more vulnerable to manipulation by others. For Chamberlin, that vulnerability led to a death sentence.

The 45 women on death row across the country make up 2 percent of the total number of Americans sentenced to death. The vast majority of women behind bars have experienced abuse before arrest. Ninety-six percent of women on death row had experienced gender-based violence before arrest, 80 percenthave intellectual or psychosocial disabilities, and 90 percent have no prior conviction for a violent felony. Chamberlin checked all of these boxes.

As a child, she suffered constant physical and sexual abuse from her father, her mother, her stepfather, her brother, and even her fourth-grade teacher. Her mother beat her with whatever was on hand, sometimes whipping her with a wooden spoon until it broke. When she was six, her 11-year-old brother put her into a closet with three neighborhood children, instructing them to touch her sexually. He also sexually abused her for years. Chamberlin told her mother, who dismissed her complaints.

When she was 12, Chamberlin began using drugs to numb the constant violence and abuse.

As an adult, her boyfriends used her substance dependency to exert control. They also physically and sexually abused her. Roger Gillett, who would become her co-defendant, strangled her, attempted to drown her, and raped her. He ordered her to move with him from Oregon, where her family lived, first to Kansas and then Mississippi in 2004. That was where Gillett killed two people.

Now 53, Chamberlin is the sole woman on Mississippi’s death row. If her appeals fail, she will be the first woman the state executes since 1944.

“In capital cases, women who have experienced some of the most extreme forms of gender-based violence and oppression are also among those who have received the least support from the legal system, from their communities, from their families, and from society,” Sandra Babcock, founder and director of the Cornell Center on the Death Penalty Worldwide, told Truthout. “There are two dynamics: One is that these women are among the most damaged and vulnerable survivors to become involved in the criminal legal system. But their experiences of violence and trauma go unrecognized by the legal system when they are charged with a capital crime.”

In Mississippi, Chamberlin and Gillett stayed with Gillett’s cousin, Vernon Hulett, and his cousin’s girlfriend, Linda Heintzelman. At first, they all got along. Then, after an auto accident between the two couples, they hatched a plan for Heintzelman to report the accident, collect insurance, and split it with Gillett and Chamberlin.

Heintzelman never filed the insurance claim, leading to tension between the two couples. When their hosts suggested that they move out, Gillett tortured and killed them. He and Chamberlin then placed their bodies into a freezer, loaded it into Heintzelman’s truck, and drove to an abandoned Kansas farm owned by Gillett’s grandfather.

There, police conducted a drug raid, arresting both. They later found the freezer and charged the couple with the deaths of Hulett and Heintzelman.

The pair were tried separately. Both were convicted and sentenced to death.

Chamberlin’s trial was marked by demonizing gender stereotypes. The prosecutor painted her as the mastermind behind the murders. He introduced testimony about Chamberlin’s sex life, including testimony from two jailhouse informants. Jailhouse informants’ testimonies, commonly motivated by law enforcement, are inherently unreliable and have been the leading cause in 46 percent of death row exonerations. author: AfricanFeminism
title: Naming the Violence: FGM Survivors Take Their Fight for Justice Online
content:
I was just 17 years old, in a WhatsApp group with peers discussing sexual and gender-based violence when I first heard that Female Genital Mutilation (FGM) was violence. I remember being agitated by the turn the discussion took. Though much of that conversation is murky now, I remember repeating the same lines: ‘

FGM is culture; if we can advocate for abortion, then surely we could allow others to practise their culture in peace

’. A colleague then insinuated that such statements were why more girls and women were being harmed – that I was, in fact, supporting violence against women and girls.


Teenage me had just started her activism journey, but carried the authority of someone who thought she knew it all. For her, FGM was a normal part of existence. My mother, aunties, cousins and almost every woman I knew had gone through it. I had heard stories of older women travelling for days to be cut. Being cut was an honour. Families paid the woman who performed the cutting. There was no way, teenage me would think, that love and violence could coexist. So being called a perpetrator on that platform did not sit well with her.


I left pressed to prove someone wrong. I decided to learn more about FGM, hoping to win the next argument. I dove into its history, beyond what I had absorbed socially.


Why were women cut? How had it become part of our history? As I travelled from one district to another, I heard stories about female chiefs, hints from the Sunnah, and other explanations. Whatever argument I would make next had to be concise. It had to convince others – and, by this point, myself – that FGM was not violence. 


But the more I learned and met the women in different locations, the more my need to prove a point faded. The research kept returning me to the same message: FGM is violence. Teenage me found stories of women discovering they had been cut as children. Older sisters fighting to protect younger sisters. Communities and countries organising against the practice. Women whose genitalia had been sewn together until marriage. Girls being forced into marriages, with FGM part of a much larger system of control over their bodies and futures.


And somewhere in that search, she had to confront a question she had never thought to ask: what if something could be culture and still be violent? The more she learnt, the more she was shattered by the harm done to her own body, and to the bodies of millions of girls before her. 


A woman during a march against FGM in Sierra Leone. Photo by

Massah Brockarie.


 


Facing the fear of naming as a survivor


FGM was the first issue I was ever truly scared to write about. There have always been stories of women being kidnapped, physically assaulted, and even killed for advocating against FGM. And the women who sold dresses, the men who sponsored the cutting, these were people I had loved and admired all my life. Talking negatively about a practice they held dear felt like a betrayal of their trust. And, to be honest, I also thought ”I am okay for now. So, what I experienced was not great harm, right?”


Then one day, on a trip travelling back from Waterloo, eastern…Sierra Leone, I saw girls as young as six walking along the streets. Something shifted in me. Suddenly, this was no longer a debate about culture, history or what I had been taught to believe. These were children. Girls who, like me, had yet to understand the lifelong implications of what could be done to their bodies. If I remained silent, this violence would continue to be meted out upon young girls and women across the country. 


I went straight to Facebook and wrote, “

I’m a cut woman; I once believed that this was an African thing. It never was”, and there I named

t the

harm that FGM is.

 I was surprised by how many people agreed with me. Of course, some people told me to stop. Was it the first time to publicly say that? And really, to look at this as a personal experience that connected to millions of other girls and women, and it needed to be named. Not faceless statistics. 


Since then, I have kept writing. I kept sharing my

 story

 and other advocacy work across social media platforms. The first post opened a conversation with my cousin, who had also been cut. We talked about the harm and absurdity of it and promised that our daughters, if we had them, would not be subjected to the same harm.


The bravery to speak about FGM online, and the conversations it sparked, has stayed with me, and it has …

title: Projection / discussion : Jeux vidéo et politique
content:
Projection du documentaire Le jeu vidéo, une affaire d'hommes 

 

? dimanche 18/10 16h à la librairie Publico à l'invitation du Groupe libertaire d'Ivry.


Le jeu vidéo, une affaire d'hommes 

 

? Documentaire de Nostalgeek (2023, 35 min)


Je ne peux pas m'identifier au protagoniste de ce jeu car c'est une femme et je suis un homme. 

 

» Est‐ce que ce genre de déclaration ne cache pas quelque part des soucis un brin plus profonds

 

?


Le jeu vidéo — comme le cinéma, la

BD

, la littérature… — peut servir de support à des idées politiques de tous bords. Ce court métrage s'attaque plus spécifiquement au sexisme 

 

; mais, de façon plus générale, existe‐t‐il des jeux luttant contre toutes les formes de discrimination, contre le capitalisme, l'État, la religion 

 

? Des jeux vidéo anarchistes 

 

?


Le sexisme dans le milieu du jeu vidéo


Les femmes travaillant dans l'industrie vidéoludique constatent une différence de salaire (25,3 % d'écart au bénéfice des hommes). Certains rejettent les designs de personnages féminins non hyper‐sexualisés. Dans les studios de développement français, les femmes représentent 24 % des effectifs alors qu'elles n'en constituaient que 10,6 % il y a 10 ans. Depuis 2018, nous constatons toujours la même disparité selon les catégories de métier, avec une sous‐représentation des femmes dans les métiers techniques (programmation, data). La question du harcèlement au bureau est également régulièrement soulevée. D'autres formes de sexisme évoquées sont le manque de volonté d'inclure des personnages féminins bien représentés dans les jeux vidéo.


Les jeux qui cherchent à mettre en avant des personnes non hommes peuvent entraîner un harcèlement de leurs scénaristes et développeurs : c'est le cas de Amber Scott, scénariste du jeu Baldur's Gate : Siege of Dragonspear, harcelée en 2016. Elle a en effet inclus un personnage principal féminin et un personnage secondaire transgenre dans le jeu, en plus de se moquer du Gamergate

 [

1

]

 dans une réplique. En réponse à ces actions, elle est la cible d'une campagne de harcèlement et le jeu reçoit des retours négatifs en masse.


En juillet 2021, suite à son harcèlement par un manager, une employée du studio américain de jeux vidéo Activision Blizzard se suicide. Deux mille de ses collègues signent alors une pétition protestant contre des méthodes de management, et organisent un mouvement de grève. De manière plus générale, c'est la «

 

 culture Bro 

 

», culture sexiste répandue dans les milieux de la tech, qui est mise en accusation.


Sur les 152 major games publiés en 2022, 61 % des personnages sont des hommes, 39 % des femmes, et 31,7 % des jeux vidéo mettent en scène des personnages exclusivement masculins. Dans les 50 RPGs les plus joués ces 30 dernières années, les hommes parlent en moyenne 2 fois plus que les femmes.


67 % des françaises jouent aux jeux vidéo, elles ont 39 ans en moyenne et représentent 48 % des personnes qui jouent au moins une fois par semaine. Mais 40 % d'entre elles affirment avoir déjà dû se résoudre à cacher leur genre dans des parties en ligne, 46 % des gameuses jugent les contenus qu'elles voient en ligne trop sexistes ou misogynes, et elles sont aussi 40 % à avoir déjà vécu des situations de harcèlement en ligne.


Il n'y a sans doute pas plus de sexistes dans le jeu vidéo que dans le reste de la société : ce triste constat n'est que le reflet de l'état des lieux en général. Mais, comme dans la littérature ou le cinéma, changer le contenu ne devrait‐il pas participer à changer les mentalités 

 

?


Dimanche 18 octobre 2026 à partir de 16 heures


Entrée libre (accueil dès 15 heures)


Librairie du Monde Libertaire, 145 rue Amelot, Paris 11

1

]

Le Gamergate est une série de polémiques née durant le mois d'août 2014 ayant évolué en une campagne de harcèlement sexiste contre des femmes journalistes et développeuses.

author: Sanya Osha
title: Art by Rock Hard African Women
content:
Oftentimes, mass acts of violent rebellion primarily driven by youths are viewed as counterproductive and nihilistic. But it is important to note that this isn’t always the case, as three major examples in African contemporary history demonstrate notably: the anti-colonial theory of violence proffered by Frantz Fanon that galvanised Algeria into civil disobedience and warfare during the colonial era; the Arab Spring that gripped North Africa and parts of the Middle East in 2011; and the #RhodesMustFall movement that rattled South Africa in 2015.  Each of these instances of mass rebellion were largely youth-driven and shook the political status quo in their respective countries, leading to sociopolitical reform and fervent collective contemplation.


In this sense, rebellion in and of itself becomes a thoroughly creative act, a measure to shake up jaded and monolithic political edifices in urgent need of transformation as atrophy and retrogression set in within the body politic. Youths often excluded or marginalised in key decision-making bodies and processes are left with no option but to revolt. And in the act of rebellion, they are not only offering their voice but also their signature as an essential component of the body politic. When dominant political structures become unresponsive to the needs and aspirations of the majority, when they become complacent and incapable of growth and innovation, then the rebellion of youth and other segments of the populace becomes not only unavoidable but also desirable. Indeed, the desirability of revolt as a creative act is the line of thinking behind this discussion. Revolt as a massive glitch in the polity can also be viewed as a rite of purification, a collective cleansing of the communal being before renewed energies are unleashed for social reconstruction.


Having established that the physical act of actual revolt could sometimes have therapeutic and reconstructive properties, it is important to note that Africa has produced many contemporary female artists whose works stand as testaments to powerful creative agency within the continent and defiant feminist sensibilities.


“Strike a woman, strike a rock” (

imbokodo

) is a Zulu proverb that became popular after the 1956 women’s march to Union Buildings in Pretoria to protest the apartheid pass laws. It is possible to explore other equally productive meanings of rock art by rock hard people and, in this instance, the San communities of Southern Africa come to mind. The San, also known as “the First People”, can be found principally in Angola, Namibia, Botswana and, of course, South Africa. Centuries ago, they mastered the art of making paintings and engravings on rock surfaces. These works of art were not merely decorative. They tell stories, communicate healing and enact rituals for communal wellness and cohesion. In spite of colonisation and various forms of oppression, these works of art have endured and this attests to the strength and resilience of the people who created them. Indeed, San communities are littered across the Southern African region despite mounting challenges, and their survival represents a broader African narrative of durability and adaptability. Their story forms the essential backdrop to this article on women who struggle against all kinds of dispossession: political, cultural, economic, and sexist, among other types of oppression.


The work of two black South African photographers, Zanele Muholi

and Ingrid Masondo, can be construed as efforts to debunk the misrepresentations of the black African woman by centuries-long colonial imagery, on the one hand, and — in spite of the constitutional recognition of gay rights — within the matrix of a largely homophobic, patriarchal, post-apartheid South Africa, on the other. Within colonial consciousness, the black female body was preposterously exoticised, anaestheticised, and hypersexualised. By being thrust into a vortex of unruly instincts, the black African female was grossly violated in more ways than one.


Sarah Bartmann was an unfortunate indigene of what eventually became South Africa who was enslaved to be paraded in the freak shows of London and Paris during the nineteenth century on account of her well-endowed posterior ( a contemporary equivalent would be the Brazilian Butt Lift – BBL). Bartmann was constantly dehumanised, abused, and subsequently left for dead for no reason other than her natural physical attributes. Judging by her …

author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Leyte farmer files harassment complaint vs military
content:
By Veronika Barbosa TACLOBAN CITY – A farmer filed a complaint on September 22 with the Commission on Human Rights Regional Office 8 against the Philippine Army’s 93rd Infantry Battalion (IB) due to intimidation against her and her family.

Accompanied by the National Union of People’s Lawyers Eastern Visayas and Katungod Sinirangan Bisayas, Brenda Lagado said that the first incident happened on July 28 in their house in Jaro, Leyte. “We were visited by elements of the Armed Forces of the Philippines. At first, they were just checking in on us but they eventually pressured us to confess that we have connections with the New People’s Army even if we have none.”

In the same month, Lagado said that her 16-year-old cousin was also interrogated by soldiers and alleged military assets.

“He [my cousin] was tending to farm animal when he was approached by seven soldiers and seven other individuals. At first, he was told to wait for a certain Basas who was supposed to talk to him but the latter did not arrive. He was instead confronted by a certain Simon who later grabbed him by the collar, hit him with a piece of chopped wood, and threatened that he will be hanged or electrocuted if he does not cooperate with them.”

Lagado said that his cousin was coerced by at least 14 men to divulge information about certain individuals that the victim does not know about.

She said that in August, a certain Sgt. Andres visited their house and compelled her to go to the barangay hall to purportedly “clear her name” which she refused to do. “We already went to the barangay before but the harassment still continued.”

In the same month, Lagado said that a child development worker of the Daycare Center where her child 3-year-old child was enrolled in, also experienced interrogation. “The teacher told us that a certain Cris Edison Rivera, who we later found out was from the 93rd IB, asked for the name and even live birth of my child. He also interrogated the teacher and asked information about our family.”

On September 11, Lagado received a letter from an unknown sender via express delivery. The letter included an unknown number and contained statements maligning Brenda and her family. “The letter pressured me to cooperate and call the number written on the letter within 24 hours or else they would let my entire family and my husband know that I have a relationship with an NPA rebel.”

“I am scared for my family and worried about my children’s safety. I am scared because the military have pictures of my family and even my children,” Lagado said. In a statement, Katungod SB condemned the 93rd IB’s series of harassment targeted against the Lagado family and their intimidation tactics involving innocent children.

“Children are not the tools of war…they should never be used, threatened, or assaulted to serve the military’s agenda. The 93rd IB, the entire AFP, and the NTF-ELCAC should all be held accountable for using a child and physically assaulting a minor to force the family to surrender or report to the 93rd IB.” Katungod SB called on the Commission on Human Rights to swiftly investigate and to protect the Lagado family against further intimidation and harassment. (DAA)

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Lessons from high school students in rebellion
content:
from

lundimatin

 #536, 05/10/2026


A surprise lesson

. It was the surprise of the start of the school year, one that no one saw coming, let alone predicted. While everyone seemed resigned to waiting for the next presidential election to hope for change, high school students burst onto the scene and shook all political agendas. Starting in a few high schools in the Paris suburbs, the revolt quickly spread throughout France. Without any leading organisation, without a party or union pulling the strings; just groups of students self-organising, blocking the entrance to their schools, and spreading the word among themselves and on social media; a sign that embers were beginning to rekindle beneath the ashes, just waiting for a spark to ignite the blaze.


This has been a spontaneous, unpredictable, and sudden revolt, like all revolts. As with the emergence of the Yellow Vest movement in the fall of 2018, and so many other social uprisings before it, in the fall of 2026, all political attention seemed destined to focus, inevitably, on the upcoming presidential elections, once again reducing aspirations for change to the bleak choice of the ballot box, to delegating power over one’s own destiny to others.


Defying all predictions, and disregarding the electoral calendar with a carefree attitude, the high school students wanted to say, first and foremost, that they existed, that their present and future lives had value. Even though, as minors, they had no right to vote and no added value for political parties.


They had reasons to revolt. Those put forward, relayed by the student unions, denounced overcrowded classrooms, fragmented and restrictive schedules, unfilled teaching positions, and dilapidated and unsanitary school buildings. They also denounced the humiliation and incongruity of the cell phone ban in schools, given that their teachers, like the parliamentarians who voted for it, were constantly glued to their phones. They were treated like children who needed to be punished and disciplined, even though they were young adults who refused to resign themselves to a bleak and undesirable future.


Clearly, behind the structural reasons for the lack of resources and the state’s disinvestment in national education, lie deeper criticisms. At its core, it is a denunciation of the school system of a so-called Republic which, under the guise of formal equality, merely reproduces and perpetuates class and racial privilege and discrimination.


A lesson in sociology

. What is entirely new in the history of student revolts, from 1968 to the present day, is that the movement of autumn 2026 is not led by students from the city center, by offspring of the bourgeoisie who have (temporarily) deviated from their social class, but by high school students from working-class neighbourhoods. Moreover, those most mobilised in the struggle appear to be students from vocational high schools, already steered toward work and excluded from higher education. Furthermore, images of the blockades show that many of the rebellious high school students have Black or brown skin. These are young French people, of course, representing this new France which, while not recognised and appreciated by white supremacists (except, marginally, for the performances of PSG football players and the national football team), embodies its history and its future.


This is very likely why the State and its government decided, from the very first blockades, not to listen to the voices, the grievances, the demands of the striking high school students, but to repress them immediately and brutally. It’s unspoken, hidden, certainly not openly displayed, but how can one not suspect that behind the (completely unnecessary) decision to immediately resort to force in response to the students’ demands, there lies a deep-seated racism embodied by the Minister-Prefect of Police and so many officers under his command? That, like

Éric Zemmour

 and many other descendants of Oran settlers,

Laurent Nuñez

 is consumed by resentment and a visceral hatred towards Arabs and Muslims? That the police, accustomed to hunting down young Arabs and Black people in the housing projects under the pretext of fighting drugs, do not feel justified in beating high school students who fit the same physical profile?


A grammar lesson

. To unleash the full force of the repression, ministers, police officers, and complicit journalists set up the discrediting machine. While acknowledging …

author: TGEU
title: Join our webinar:  Countering Anti-Trans Misinformation – Tools, Tactics and Lessons from Across Europe
content:
Anti-trans misinformation is increasingly shaping public debates about trans rights across Europe. How do these narratives emerge, how do they travel across borders and platforms, and how can we respond effectively?


Join TGEU and the European Fact-Checking Standards Network (EFCSN) for a practical exchange between trans and LGBT organisations and fact-checkers from across Europe.


The webinar will explore common anti-trans misinformation narratives and how they are amplified and adapted in different contexts. It will also examine how fact-checking can help identify, contextualise, and respond to misleading claims.


Speakers from fact-checking organisations and TGEU members will share insights from their national and organisational contexts. A joint exercise and discussion will follow, focusing on approaches that can be adapted to different advocacy and communications contexts.


The session is an opportunity to learn from each other, build connections between the fact-checking and trans advocacy communities, and exchange practical approaches for responding to anti-trans misinformation online.


About the webinar


Date & time:

 12 November 2026, 10 – 11:30 CET

Location:

 Online via Zoom

Cost:

 Free

Target audience:

 TGEU members, trans and LGBT organisations, and activists


register here


Note: Prior registration is strictly required to attend. Unregistered participants will not be admitted to the Zoom session.


Key topics


Common anti-trans narratives: How misinformation about trans people emerges and which narratives keep resurfacing across Europe.


Travelling across physical and virtual borders: How these narratives are amplified and adapted in different national, offline and online contexts.


The role of fact-checking: How fact-checking can help identify, contextualise and respond to misleading claims.


Joint exercise and discussion: A practical exercise and space for mutual learning between the fact-checking and trans advocacy communities, with approaches that can be adapted to different advocacy and communications contexts.
