author: Laura Guido
title: Mormon Church Donates $1 Million to Fight Idaho Abortion Rights Ballot Measure
content:
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints is one of several religious institutions taking a stance on the initiative.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints has donated $1 million to an Idaho political action committee, or PAC, opposing the abortion rights initiative on the ballot this November.

The donation went to the Too Extreme for Idaho Political Action Committee, which opposes the initiative.

“While The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints remains neutral toward political candidates, it actively addresses ballot initiatives it believes carry significant moral consequences,” the church said in a statement. “Accordingly, the Church has joined a coalition of like-minded organizations and individuals in Idaho to dedicate resources toward defeating Proposition 1.”

If passed, the voter initiative would repeal Idaho’s abortion laws, enumerate rights related to reproductive health, and create liability protections for healthcare providers who provide abortion and other reproductive healthcare.

The Idaho Falls radio station NewsTalk 107.9 first reported the donation on Thursday. The Idaho Capital Sun confirmed the donation with a spokesperson for the church on Friday.

The large donation comes after Idaho Attorney General Raúl Labrador published an opinion in August that says churches are allowed to donate money to political campaigns — including for and against Proposition 1 — without disclosing their donors, as long as they don’t ask members to donate specifically for the campaign, Boise State Public Radio reported.

Leaders from the church, widely known as the Mormon church, issued a letter against Prop 1 in September, the Salt Lake Tribune reported. The letter was read to congregations last month, the church’s assistant communications director Brian Whitlock said in an email.

“Our long-held stance on abortion remains clear and unchanged,” the four-member U.S. Central Area Presidency of the LDS Church wrote in the letter.

The church, which opposes elective abortions, posted its stance on abortion online. It allows for possible exemptions in cases of rape and incest, if a “competent physician determines that the life or health of the mother is in serious jeopardy,” or a “competent physician determines that the fetus has severe defects that will not allow the baby to survive beyond birth.”

“Even these exceptions do not automatically justify abortion,” the statement said. “Abortion is a most serious matter. It should be considered only after the persons responsible have received confirmation through prayer.”

Idaho’s abortion ban allows the procedure to prevent the death of the mother and in cases of rape and incest in the first trimester with a police report. Doctors who provide abortions outside of those exemptions face felony penalties, including minimum prison time, and potential civil lawsuits brought by family members of the aborted fetus.

The LDS Church isn’t the first or only faith-based organization to contribute to the campaigns related to the ballot measure, but it is the largest reported donation from a church-affiliated group.

Groups attached to Catholic organizations have contributed $7,161 to the Too Extreme for Idaho PAC, campaign finance reporting shows. The Roman Catholic Diocese of Boise contributed $2,000, and Catholic fraternal groups, called Knights of Columbus Councils, contributed the rest, the Idaho Capital Sun previously reported.

The Catholic Diocese of Boise could not be reached for comment for this story after multiple emails and phone calls. The diocese has publicly opposed the initiative.

Bishop Peter Christensen in late July posted a statement in opposition to the ballot measure and encouraged other members of the church to voice their opposition.

“I strongly encourage you to vote NO this November. Our response must not be rooted in anger or fear, but in steadfast faith, charity, and an unwavering commitment to the truth about human life,” Christensen wrote.

He said the diocese will be encouraging parishes to offer “pro-life themed Masses” and pastors to communicate “awareness raising information in bulletins and parish communications provided by the Diocese.”

The Boise Unitarian Universalist Fellowship contributed $5,000 in September to the PAC created by the initiative’s authors and supporters …

author: Maira Escardovelli
title: Terror das feministas: radicais, deputadas conservadoras disputam poder na extrema direita
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


O terror das feministas. É como se autointitulam Ana Caroline Campagnolo e Eduarda Campopiano, as deputadas estaduais mais votadas em Santa Catarina e São Paulo. Ambas do Partido Liberal (PL), elas se apresentam como amigas em posts nas redes sociais e se dizem admiradoras  de Olavo de Carvalho. Juntas, as duas somaram mais de 2,3 milhões de votos na eleição de 2026. Ao lado delas, ocupando o posto de deputada estadual mais votada do Estado, está Índia Armelau, também do PL, que conquistou 248.504 votos para a Assembleia Legislativa do Rio de Janeiro. 


São

mulheres que se unem ao clã de Michelle Bolsonaro (PL-DF), Damares Alves (Republicanos-DF), Bia Kicis (PL-DF) e Celina Leão (PP-DF) pela pauta anti-identitária e antiaborto

, mas que, segundo especialistas ouvidas pela

Agência Pública

, não pertencem ao mesmo grupo de suas antecessoras, inclusive considerando a construção de narrativas para o eleitorado. 


Na visão de Lívia Reis, coordenadora de Religião e Política no Instituto de Estudos da Religião (ISER), a extrema-direita conquistou uma pluralidade de candidaturas femininas nesta eleição, o que pode criar uma disputa pelo poder de influência entre as próprias eleitas. 


“O Valdemar [Costa Neto, presidente do PL] não está preocupado com o alinhamento ideológico de uma influenciadora, ele quer que ela seja eleita e vote com ele”, argumenta a antropóloga em referência a eleição de Eduarda Campopiano, atualmente com mais de 2,5 milhões de seguidores do Instagram.

 “Vejo que talvez isso seja também um dos atritos que a própria Michelle vai ter com ele, porque ela quer centralizar o PL Mulheres

 e as candidaturas femininas, mas o próprio PL vai apostar em quem quiser”, explica Reis. 


Vereadora de Praia Grande, no litoral paulista, Eduarda Campopiano foi eleita para a Assembleia Legislativa de São Paulo como uma espécie de discípula de Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG), deputado federal mais votado da história do país, com mais de 22 milhões de seguidores no Instagram. Outro aliado é o vereador paulistano Lucas Pavanato (PL), que detém mais de 5 milhões de seguidores na rede social da Meta e foi eleito para deputado federal com mais de 3 milhões de votos. 


“O PL sabe o poder das redes sociais. Todas as candidaturas se forjam ali, eles estão elegendo influenciadores há muito tempo e agora chegaram ao ápice dos candidatos mais votados serem os influenciadores. Por isso, eu diria que a Eduarda chega [ao partido] com tanto poder quanto a Michelle. E vai disputar isso”, explica Reis. 


A esposa do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, preso por tentativa de golpe de Estado, protagonizou em junho deste ano o seu primeiro embate público com o Partido. Após a rejeição da sigla ao nome indicado por ela ao Senado pelo Ceará, o da deputada Priscila Costa (PL-CE), Michelle publicou um vídeo contando que Flávio Bolsonaro a havia desrespeitado durante a formação dos arranjos partidários nos estados. “Ele disse que seria melhor eu ficar fora das decisões do partido. Disse que eu havia chegado ontem e não entendia nada de política”, afirmou a ex-primeira dama.


No vídeo, ela exaltou sua atuação à frente do PL Mulher, ala de mulheres conservadoras do partido: “[em 2024] elegemos 45,8% mais mulheres que em 2020. Foram 1.005 mulheres eleitas”, disse. Com a instauração da crise, que abalou a campanha à presidência de Flávio Bolsonaro, e após se reunir com Costa Neto, Michelle anunciou sua saída da presidência do PL Mulher. 


Na visão de parlamentares próximos ao PL, Campopiano representa um discurso mais radical da extrema-direita, capitaneado por Olavo de Carvalho

, conhecido como o “guru” do bolsonarismo. “Eu acho que ela [Eduarda] vem muito daquela linha do Olavo de Carvalho, que é essa juventude conservadora formada. Mas creio que com a maturidade ela vai entender que a pauta feminina não é uma pauta feminista. A gente vai ter ainda um tempo para fazer esse convencimento”, disse à

Pública

 a senadora Damares Alves, que também afirmou que irá dialogar nesse sentido com a deputada Índia Armelau.   


A pesquisadora do Centro Brasileiro de Análise e Planejamento (CEBRAP) Jacqueline Teixeira aponta que o discurso de Campopiano pode ser entendido a partir dos efeitos produzidos por políticas que começaram, entre 2014 a 2016, a proibir gênero nos parâmetros curriculares. author: Karen Gullo
title: Turkish Crackdown On LGBTQ+ Organizations Threatens Freedom of Expression and Association
content:
EFF strongly condemns Turkey’s state-led discriminatory, oppressive attacks on feminist and LGBTQ+ organisations, media platforms, student groups, and rights defenders and activists within the country.

Since mid-September, access to the websites and social media accounts of a dozen organizations have been blocked by court order, while over 60 members and activists have been detained, their offices and homes raided, mobile phones, laptops and other digital devices seized, and judicial proceedings launched against them.

These actions threaten the very existence of the LGBTQ+ organizations targeted, limiting their ability to carry out legitimate human rights work, deterring participation and support, and chilling the free speech rights of not just these groups, but any organization that even reports on LGBTQ+ oppression.

A little over a week ago, an Istanbul court shut down the website and social media accounts of T24, Turkey’s longest running independent digital news organization—which has covered government-backed campaigns against and earlier crackdowns on gay rights groups—alleging it had aired “LGBT propaganda” over the past year.

It’s all part of Turkey’s efforts to portray LGBTQ+ groups and support networks for those living with HIV as criminal organizations that must be suppressed, purportedly to protect family values. Homosexuality is not illegal in Turkey (unlike Uganda, Nigeria, and Egypt, where it is criminalized), but LGBTQ+ organizations and activists have in recent years faced increased government oppression, including criminal proceedings on allegations related to obscenity and violations of Turkey’s Law on Associations, which regulates the activities of nonprofits.

In its new crackdown, the government is targeting LGBTQ+ groups’ websites and social media channels for alleged obscene posts accessible to children. Kaos GL, Turkey’s oldest gay rights organization, said investigations are being led by the Cyber Crimes Bureau of the Ankara Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office, which took members of its Board of Directors into custody, raided their homes, and searched the organization’s offices, where electronic devices were seized.

According to Human Rights Watch, prosecutors in Istanbul said those targeted were suspected of “founding, leading, or being a member of a criminal organization,” as well as sex work and drug-related offenses. Publicly available law enforcement and judicial documents about the investigation reportedly don’t say which publications or posts are alleged to be obscene.

The prosecutor’s office launched an investigation of the organization and others under Article 226 of the Turkish Penal Code, which regulates the offense of “obscenity” (without clearly defining it), while the overall operation, dubbed “My Family is Safe” and launched as part of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’s “Decade of the Family” program, is being brought under Article 220 of the code. Justifying the crackdown by invoking family values and child safety suggests that the government is trying to enforce a moral code on society based on intolerance of and discrimination against LGBTQ+ people.

Framing the activities of LGBTQ+ rights organizations as violations of organized crime provisions is a new low for Turkey, where free speech and press freedoms have long been under attack. The implication from these raids and investigations is that the organizations’ legitimate civil society work advocating for the rights of queer people—monitoring human rights violations, offering legal aid, running news portals, sponsoring cultural events such as symposiums and film screenings, publishing an online magazine and supporting LGBTQ+ refugees—is suspected of being criminal threatens the basic human rights of the LGBTQ+ community in Turkey.

These actions send a dangerous message to people and organizations exercising freedom of speech and association in support of queer people. Under the penal code, directing a criminal organization is punishable by five to ten years in prison, while merely being a member carries a sentence of two to five years.

EFF joins hundreds of human, civil, LGBTQ+, and digital rights organizations around the world in calling for the immediate release of all those detained for exercising their rights to freedom of expression, association and legitimate human rights work, and the unblocking of all websites and social media accounts of affected organizations.

author: Unknown
title: Bloquons l'offensive transphobe : rassemblement contre le colloque de l'Observatoire de la petite sirène au Sénat
content:
Nous appelons à un rassemblement contre la tenue du colloque annuel de l'Observatoire de la petite sirène au Sénat. Ce moteur de la transphobie en France s'en prend tout particulièrement aux mineur·es trans.


Ce vendredi 16 octobre, jour de l'existransinter, une opération de lobbying transphobe a lieu au parlement. Elle se tient avec le soutien de la sénatrice Jacqueline Eustache-Brinio qui était déjà à l'origine d'une proposition de loi visant à restreindre l'accès des mineur·es aux soins de transition, contre laquelle nous nous étions mobilisé·es en 2024. Empêchons-les d'avancer leur agenda transphobe, rendez-vous à midi devant le Sénat.


Qui est l'Observatoire de la petite sirène (

OPS

)

 

?


Cet autodéclaré observatoire est un collectif regroupant notamment des psychiatres et des psychanalystes, organisant la transphobie en France sous couvert de protection de l'enfance. Parmi leurs actions : lobbying pour retarder voire interdire la transition chez les jeunes, promotion des thérapies de conversion, pression sur des médecins pour interdire des transitions.


La «

 

protection de l'enfance

 

»


Cette prétendue «

 

protection de l'enfance

 

» a des conséquences désastreuses. Les thérapies de conversion, c'est 2 fois plus de tentatives de suicide, 4 fois plus en dessous de 10 ans. Les mineur·es trans empêché·es de transitionner sont davantage exposé·es au suicide. Iels sont littéralement privés de soins. Alors que les détransitions qui les obsèdent tant ne représentent que 0,5% des adolescents ayant commencé une hormonothérapie (Boskey, 2025).


Leur panique morale, des vies broyées


Les dangers dont ils parlent sont fantasmés : la seule inquiétude à laquelle ils répondent c'est à celle de voir des jeunes ne pas rentrer dans le moule cisgenre. Ils ont avant tout honte de ces enfants : ils ne les protègent pas mais les poussent à l'exclusion, à la dépression, au suicide. Leur programme ne met pas qu'en danger des enfants. Retarder les transitions, c'est aussi participer à la précarisation des adultes trans. Et avoir vécu une puberté dans le mauvais genre a des conséquences sur nos vies entières car malgré l'argent et les efforts investis, on ne rattrape pas les années perdues et on vit avec la crainte de ne jamais réussir à être perçu·es comme on le souhaite.


Arrêtons maintenant l'offensive transphobe


Si l'

OPS

 s'attaque aujourd'hui aux mineur·es, ce n'est qu'un premier pas dans le but de s'attaquer plus largement à toutes les personnes trans. C'est cette même obsession pour le contrôle de nos corps et le maintien des normes de genre que l'on voit avec le cas des athlètes par exemple. Ne les laissons pas gâcher la vie des enfants et des futurs adultes trans au nom de leur idéologie. Pour mettre un coup d'arrêt à leur agenda transphobe et pour l'autodétermination de tous·tes, retrouvons-nous au Sénat le 16 octobre à midi (métro Odéon,

RER

 Luxembourg)

 

!

réseaux sociaux

 que le lieu n'a pas été déplacé.

title: MKG: Di Îlonê de 2 rojnamegerên jin hatin girtin û 3 jî hatin desteserkirin
content:
Komeleya Rojnamegerên Jin a Mezopotamyayê (MKG) rapora xwe ya binpêkirina mafên jinên rojnameger a meha Îlona 2026an aşkere kir.


MKGê, di raporê de bal kişand ser astengiyên li qadê, şert û mercên xebatê yên ji bo rojnamegerên jin û sansura li ser çapemeniyê.


MKGê diyar kir ku di meha Îlonê de zext bi awayên cûr bi cûr li ser rojnamegerên jin berdewam kirin û wiha got: 


“Lêpirsîn û dozên li dijî çalakiyên rojnamegeriyê, astengiyên li pêşiya nûçeyan, binçavkirin û girtin, gef û êrîş û sansura dîjîtal qada xebatê ji bo rojnamegeran teng kir. Geşedanên di tevahiya mehê de nîşan dan, raporên nûçeyan û çalakiyên rojnamegeriyê wekî bingehek ji bo tawanbarkirinê têne bikaranîn. Darizandinên bi salane berdewam dikin, dozên nû tên vekirin û berdewama biryarên girtinê nîşan dide ku zexta darazê ya li ser rojnamegeran domdar bûye. Astengiyên li qadê şert û mercên xebatê ji bo rojnamegeran jî dijwar kirin. Destwerdana li ser nûçeyan, dûrxistina rojnamegeran a ji qadê, gef û êrîşan nîşan dan ku gihiştina nûçeyan her diçe bi sînordar dibe. Di meha Îlonê de, qada dîjîtal jî yek ji wan deveran bû ku zext lê zêde bûn. Xwegihandina platformên medya dîjîtal ên gelek koman, rojnameger, sazî û dezgehên medyayê, rêxistinên jinan û parêzvanên mafên mirovan, hate astengkirin. Bi vê yekê di heman demê de xwegihandina raya giştî ya dezgehên agahdariyê jî hatin sînordarkirin.”


“Divê astengiyên li pêşiya rojnamegeran werin rakirin”


MKGê di berdewamiya raporê de bi lêv kir ku zextên li ser rojnamegeran li cihên kar jî berdewam kir. MKGê da zanîn ku ji kar derxistin, mobîng û şert û mercên bêewle zêde bûne û hebûna jinan a di qada çapemeniyê de zehmet bûye û wiha hate gotin: 


“Bûyerên meha Îlonê nîşan didin ku dema rojnameger nûçeyan çêdikin, li qadê dixebitin, di pêvajoyên darazê de û li qada dîjîtal di bin zextê de ne. Binpêkirinên mafên mirovan ên li dijî rojnamegeran nikarin ji azadiya çapemeniyê û mafê raya giştî yê agahdarkirinê cûdatir bên nirxandin. Divê darizandin û çavtirsandina rojnamegeran a ji ber çalakiyên wan ên pîşeyî, astengkirina weşana nûçeyên wan û girtina platformên wan ên dîjîtal bi dawî bibe. Divê rojnamegerên girtî werin berdan û hemû astengiyên li pêşiya xebatên rojnamegeran werin rakirin.”

title: People are always like “rice and beans and vegetables are super healthy” but then decide that…
content:
ecrivainsolitaire

:

queeranarchism

cockatude

queeranarchism

:

totokitty

derinthescarletpescatarian

:

People are always like “rice and beans and vegetables are super healthy” but then decide that burritos are unhealthy. Did the rice and beans and vegetables become bad when I wrapped them up. Do they think tortillas cause cancer. What’s happening here.

Oh, it’s racism, actually. Usually is, but definitely is in this scenario.

Racism with just a dash of protestant ‘if it’s hard work to prepare and unsatisfying to eat, it’s good for you. If it’s easy and you enjoy it and feel satisfied, it’s bad for you’ mixed in there.

Guys… its because 99.9% of burritos made in the US are made by a fast food joint or meant for bachelors to heat up while drunk.

I’m willing to bet lots of people make burritos at home, because that’s a cheap, easy and delicious way to use leftover veggies.

But more to the point: do you realize that you didn’t describe any factor that would make burritos unhealthy? A fast food joint is a location, it can prepare healthy and unhealthy foods. Bachelors can eat healthy or unhealthy foods while drunk. Heating up food instead of preparing it does not make it unhealthy.

Location, demographic and convenience are all cultural markers that we associate with 'unhealthy food’, not actual unhealthy ingredients. So you’re kind of proving the point here.

It’s because they’re Mexican.

Everything in a burrito and everything in a subway sandwich is entirely interchangeable other than the carb around it. But one is made by a white Italian and one by a brown Mexican.

Have you seen all those clean eating diet fads? Notice how they never feature any spices or ethnic ingredients?

Have you noticed that every non-white food family is regularly accused of causing diarrhea? Mexican, Chinese Indian, Vietnamese, Arab.

A couple months ago there was a viral outbreak of disease in lettuce, and everyone immediately attributed it to Taco Bell, not to any of the 200 other food chains that carry lettuce in their ingredients.

During Covid everyone immediately jumped to making jokes about bat soup. Those haven’t stopped, even though by now we know enough about Covid to know better.

Why is it that whenever brown people claim to be victims of racism first we have to spend so much time convincing white leftists that racism is a real thing that happens literally everywhere all the time before even

beginning

 to have the conversation we

actually

 want to have?

Why is it so difficult to believe us?

author: Amy Goodman
title: Nobel Peace Prize Awarded to Jurist Who Led UN Inquiry Into Genocide in Gaza
content:
South African human rights lawyer Navanethem “Navi” Pillay began her career defending anti-apartheid activists.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize has been awarded to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, the South African jurist who led the United Nations commission of inquiry that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. Pillay’s long career in international human rights law includes work as a defense attorney for anti-apartheid activists, president of the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda, a former judge at the International Criminal Court and the U.N.’s high commissioner for human rights from 2008 to 2014.

“Everybody in the human rights movement reveres Navi Pillay,” says war crimes prosecutor Reed Brody, who calls the award “a stinging rebuke to Donald Trump.” Brody, a member of the United Nations Group of Human Rights Experts on Nicaragua, also comments on the Trump administration’s decision to deport a Nicaraguan opposition activist, Jeffrey Jarquín, from the United States, where he was in the process of seeking asylum. Upon his return to Nicaragua, Jarquín was immediately imprisoned at the same facility in which he was once tortured.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman, with Juan González.

The Norwegian Nobel Committee has announced the winner of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. This is the chair of the Nobel Committee speaking in Oslo this morning.

JØRGEN WATNE FRYDNES: The Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 goes to a person who, with exceptional courage and integrity, has led the way towards a more comprehensive global legal order. This year’s laureate has been instrumental in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted. The Norwegian Nobel Committee has decided to award the Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 to Navanethem “Navi” Pillay for her efforts to promote peace and international law.

AMY GOODMAN: The South African human rights lawyer and international jurist Navi Pillay has been the United Nations high commissioner for human rights and a judge at both the International Criminal Court and at an international tribunal investigating the 1994 genocide in Rwanda. Most recently, she led the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.

Navi Pillay is now 85 years old. She was born into an Indian Tamil family in apartheid South Africa. The first woman to start a law practice in Natal, South Africa, in 1967, she began her legal career defending anti-apartheid activists, including Nelson Mandela, exposing torture and helping establish key rights for prisoners on Robben Island. The Nobel Committee also praised her work in South Africa.

JØRGEN WATNE FRYDNES: A common thread runs from her early work, defending Nelson Mandela and others who stood up against apartheid, to her service as a judge in some of the key international court cases of our time.

AMY GOODMAN: Navi Pillay was in Nuremberg, Germany, at an annual conference of human rights lawyers and judges when she got the news this morning.

NAVI PILLAY: Thank you very much. Thank you very much. If you clap a little bit more, I may share this prize with Trump. … The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza naming what’s happening there as genocide.

AMY GOODMAN: Meanwhile, Israel’s Foreign Ministry took to X to denounce the awarding of the Nobel Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, calling it a, quote, “grotesque weaponization of an award to legitimize anti-Israel hatred and prejudice,” unquote.

This is Navi Pillay speaking to Reuters last year about her genocide findings as the chair of the U.N. Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territories.

NAVI PILLAY: Genocide is occurring in Gaza. We haven’t gone into Palestine yet. We will, because this is a permanent commission. And we named the three individuals that we felt were responsible. And we said — and the one is the prime minister, the other the president, and the third is the former minister of defense. And we said that since they acted as agents of the state, then the state of Israel is responsible. …

author: Marcelo Oliveira
title: Mulheres são maioria das vítimas de violência política, mesmo sendo minoria das candidatas
content:
O primeiro turno da campanha eleitoral de 2026 durou 50 dias e registrou 134 episódios de violência política contra candidatos e candidatas, além de agentes políticos.

Um aumento de 11% em relação aos 121 casos registrados no mesmo período da eleição municipal de 2022.


Os 134 episódios representam um caso de violência política a cada nove horas de campanha.

 E apesar das mulheres serem apenas 35% do total de candidatos, elas foram a maioria (52%) das vítimas do primeiro turno, segundo o levantamento.


Os dados integram a 4ª edição da pesquisa Violência Política e Eleitoral no Brasil, realizada pelas organizações de direitos humanos Terra de Direitos e Justiça Global, que pesquisa o tema desde 2016. O levantamento foi divulgado nesta quarta, dia 7 de outubro.


A porcentagem de

vítimas mulheres aumenta

 mais ainda quando a pesquisa separa apenas os casos envolvendo candidatas e candidatos. Dos 134 episódios de violência política durante o primeiro turno, 102 foram dirigidos a pessoas que disputavam o pleito. Desse total, 60 eram mulheres, quase 59% do total.


Para a coordenadora do Setor de Incidência da Terra de Direitos, Gisele Barbieri, “os dados trazem importantes achados para identificar os ambientes em que agentes políticos estão mais vulneráveis e pensar medidas de proteção. Quando eleitas, essas pessoas passam a ser vítimas de violências nos seus locais de atuação, seja no Parlamento ou no Executivo”, afirma.


Machismo e misoginia se misturam nos casos de violência política


A pesquisa mostra que a violência política é marcada pela discriminação de gênero e raça.

Quando se considera o universo completo de 70 casos de violência política contra mulheres, 45 casos envolveram machismo ou misoginia, nove envolveram racismo e cinco envolveram transfobia. Mulheres pretas foram vítimas de 25% dos casos de violência política medidos nesse primeiro turno.


A ameaça foi o tipo de violência política mais recorrente no período, com 64 casos registrados. Na sequência, aparecem 33 episódios de ofensa e 19 de agressão física. Também foram registrados 11 atentados, cinco casos de criminalização e dois assassinatos.


Mais da metade dos casos (71 ocorrências) aconteceu nas ruas, durante atividades públicas de campanha. O ambiente virtual concentrou 31,3% dos episódios.


Além disso, apenas candidatas sofreram ameaças de violência sexual. Em todos os sete casos, as vítimas eram mulheres.


“Enquanto os homens são atacados por sua atuação política, mulheres, pessoas negras e pessoas trans enfrentam também o racismo, o machismo e a transfobia que estruturam a sociedade brasileira”, afirmou em nota Glaucia Marinho, diretora-executiva da Justiça Global.


Policiais e outros agentes públicos foram a maioria dos autores


Em quase 20% dos casos o autor identificado da violência política era um agente público, incluindo parlamentares e forças de segurança.

Até o encerramento da coleta de dados pelas organizações autoras da pesquisa, nenhum dos 134 episódios havia resultado em alguma punição efetiva, limitando-se a medidas cautelares de urgência determinadas pela Justiça Eleitoral.


A região Nordeste liderou o número de casos (48), seguido pelo Sudeste (38). Entre os estados, São Paulo lidera com 16 casos, seguido por Rio Grande do Norte (13), Minas Gerais (12) e Rio Grande do Sul (10).


A presença de policiais entre os autores de violência política já havia sido detectada também em

levantamento

 realizado pela

Agência Pública

 durante o primeiro turno.

voyeurs

Método y locura, Acuso, Saber demasiado,

Gaza

,

Más allá de la desfachatez

La industria del Holocausto.

Nelson Mandela también fue tildado de «terrorista», pero fue fundamental en la lucha por la liberación de su pueblo. Esto es lo que Jimmy Carter exigió en su libro

Palestina: Paz, no apartheid

.

Los políticos occidentales y los principales medios de comunicación han invertido los papeles y han culpado a la víctima de su desgracia. Israel nació del terrorismo

Estado fallido

Israel ha atacado Líbano, Siria, Irak, Irán, Egipto, etc. En una infame operación de falsa bandera, incluso atacó el buque de inteligencia de la Armada de los Estados Unidos USS

Liberty

Israel ha sido un estado paria desde su creación en 1948, e incluso antes.


El genocidio de Gaza no es más que una continuación de la intención criminal de establecer un «Gran Israel» anacrónico e imperialista en medio del mundo árabe y musulmán.


[Fuente:

cartooningforpeace.org

]


Sin duda, los gobiernos de Israel, Estados Unidos y la UE están moralmente en bancarrota.

[7]


Lamentablemente, la

percepción

de la realidad es más determinante que la realidad misma. Dado que nuestras acciones están condicionadas por la información de la que disponemos, nuestro juicio se ve influenciado —e incluso subvertido— por las narrativas odiosas que recibimos de los principales medios de comunicación, y nuestras opiniones se distorsionan por el incesante discurso de odio y la propaganda contra los palestinos. Esto constituye una incitación al odio y a la violencia, en contravención del artículo 20 del Pacto Internacional de Derechos Civiles y Políticos.

Los principales medios de comunicación difunden la versión israelí y suprimen las opiniones disidentes. No solo nos mienten, sino que nos privan de información crucial que cambia radicalmente la situación.


El público es manipulado, pero muchos se dejan manipular. Como escribió Julio César en

De Bello Civili (II, 27, 2): «quae volumus, ea credimus libenter»

(Creemos lo que queremos creer). O peor aún, como decían los romanos …

Lenin: Butcher of the Working Class

Timeline: A Revolution Derailed

The USSR: Force for Global Counterrevolution, Accomplice of Fascism

The Relevance of the Communist Counterrevolution

Part Two: Restless Specters of the Anarchist Dead

Golos Truda, The Voice of Labor

Since the mid-19th century, anarchists have maintained that the key to liberation is not to seize the state but to abolish it. From Paris to St. Petersburg, from Barcelona to Beijing, one generation of revolutionaries after another has had to learn this lesson the hard way. Shuffling politicians in and out of power changes nothing. What matters are the instruments of rule — the police, the military, the courts, the prison system, the bureaucracy. Whether it is a king, a dictator, or a Congress that directs these instruments, the experience on the receiving end remains roughly the same.

This explains why the outcome of the Egyptian revolution of 2011–2013 was not all that different from the outcome of the Russian Revolution of 1917–1921 or the French Revolution of 1848–1851. In each case, as soon as the people who made the revolution stopped attempting to carry out social change directly and shifted to investing their hopes in political representatives, power consolidated in the hands of a new autocracy. Whether the new tyrants hailed from the military, the aristocracy, or the underclass, whether they promised to restore order or to incarnate the power of the proletariat, the end result was roughly the same.

Government itself is a class relation. You can’t abolish class society without abolishing the asymmetry between ruler and ruled . The first condition for any government is that it must achieve a monopoly on coercive force. In struggling to achieve this monopoly, fascist despotisms, communist dictatorships, and liberal democracies come to resemble each other. And in order to achieve it, even the most ostensibly radical party must ultimately collude with other power players. This explains why the Bolsheviks employed tsarist officers and counterinsurgency methods, why they repeatedly took the side of the petite bourgeoisie against anarchists, first in Russia and later in Spain and elsewhere. History gives the lie to the old alibi that Bolshevik repression was necessary to abolish capitalism. The problem with Bolshevism was not that it used brutal force to push through a revolutionary agenda, but that it used brutal force to crush it.

It’s not particularly popular to acknowledge any of this today, when the flag of the Soviet Union has become a dim, receding screen onto which people can project whatever they wish. A generation that grew up after the fall of the Soviet Union has renewed the pipe dream that the state could solve all our problems if the right people were in charge. author: Sophia Sheera
title: Israel Bans Zack Polanski After Green Members Pass ‘Zionism Is Racism’ Motion
content:
Israel has banned Green leader Zack Polanski from entering the country after members of his party approved a motion defining Zionism as a racist ideology. 


The Israeli foreign ministry said in a

post announcing the ban

 on X on Sunday that the new policy legitimised “the destruction of the state of Israel” and was “clearly antisemitic”.


On Sunday, 1,022 party members voted yes to

 the ‘Zionism is racism’ motion

, while 813 voted against it. It reads: “Zionism is a political ideology which called for the creation – and, now it exists, the continuity – of an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population.”


It also asserts the party’s commitment to Palestinian liberation and a full arms embargo against Israel as it continues its genocide in Gaza. 


Following the vote, a

Green party

 spokesperson said: “This has been a serious and deeply felt debate within our membership.” They added the party maintains a “commitment to equality, justice and human rights for all and opposition to racism in all its forms.” 


Four of the Greens’ five MPs – Adrian Ramsay, Carla Denyer, Ellie Chowns and Sian Berry – have

said they oppose the motion

 while Hannah Spencer has not made her view on it public. Former leader

Caroline Lucas urged members to vote no

, arguing it might alienate Jewish members. 


Polanski, who is Jewish, did not vote. He left the conference early to campaign for the Holborn and St Pancras byelection, which takes place on Thursday. 


Polanski has previously expressed concern over the motion and called for two amendments – including one explicitly stating that Jewish people in the party would be safeguarded, and would not be punished for attending Zionist synagogues. 


He also opposed a section of the motion calling for a single Palestinian state, arguing that it wasn’t the job of the Green party to “decide what the future settlement of Palestine and Israel looks like”.   


However, at a byelection hustings last month, he said: “If you’re defining Zionism as a displacement genocide, which is how, in practice, Zionism has become, then that is racism.”


The motion means the Green party is now the first explicitly anti-Zionist political party in the UK. However, while motions at conference inform the party’s long-term vision and policy platform, they do not determine election manifestos.

title: TEV-DEM condemns racist provocation in Hesekê
content:
Following a demonstration featuring anti-Kurdish demands in Hesekê, the Democratic Society Movement (TEV-DEM) warned against attempts to fuel ethnic tensions in the multi-ethnic city. At Friday’s rally in the predominantly Arab neighborhood of Xiwêran (Ghweiran), around 200 people called, among other things, for Kurds to be removed from institutions in Hesekê province.


During the demonstration, in which a particularly large number of children and young people participated, slogans were also chanted against Kurdish national symbols and flags. Kurdish flags were also reportedly burned following Friday prayers. In a statement on Sunday, TEV-DEM described the action as a racist provocation by a limited group and explicitly rejected attempts to portray it as reflecting the views or demands of the Arab population.


“Limited to a particular group”


According to TEV-DEM, the slogans voiced during the demonstration were aimed at inciting racism against the Kurdish population and other sections of society. The position expressed there was limited to a particular group, TEV-DEM stated. “Some of the rhetoric directly targeted the legitimate national and political rights of the Kurds. At the same time, rhetoric was used that fueled social discord and thereby served the enemies of Syria.”


TEV-DEM emphasized that the anti-Kurdish demands must not be attributed to the Arab population of Hesekê. The movement also rejected attempts to portray the provocation as an ethnic conflict between Kurds and Arabs.


Call for an investigation into the incidents


TEV-DEM called on the relevant authorities to launch a transparent and responsible investigation into the incidents, demanding that those who spread hatred and racist incitement be held accountable. At the same time, the movement warned against allowing Hesekê province to become a scene of ethnic conflict.


TEV-DEM said that Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs and other communities should not allow hate speech to turn them against one another but should instead remain committed to dialogue and peaceful coexistence.

author: Sonali Kolhatkar
title: An Abolitionist Vision for the World We Want
content:
A recent New York Times editorial by Tim Wu, a former antitrust adviser for the Biden administration, caught my eye for the criticism it leveled at Democrats for making affordability a central issue ahead of the midterm elections. Wu contends that the party needs to go further and focus not merely on the high price tags of necessities, but on the unfairness of the entire economic system.

While this is a refreshing shift in the right direction, it doesn’t go nearly far enough. It’s true that a majority of Americans across the political spectrum believe our economy is rigged in favor of the rich. But merely pointing out the obvious is unlikely to attract a huge shift in voting toward the Democratic Party.

Moreover, Wu says nothing about the racist rage that has defined President Donald Trump and the Republican Party’s decimation of our democracy, about the devastation to communities of color, immigrants, women, LGBTQ+ people, and other marginalized members of our society. Nor does he acknowledge the corporate harms that Democrats failed to tackle when they were in power and are now being accelerated under Republicans: fossil fuel emissions, tech domination, and AI, harms that disproportionately impactpoor people and people of color.

To Wu and most Democratic Party consultants, these issues are distinct and, depending on the cultural tides, are either worth tackling or anathema.

In fact, they are intimately linked. White supremacy feeds capitalism by distracting poor whites from billionaire-fueled inequality and climate devastation using immigrants and people of color as scapegoats. To take on an unfair economy without addressing the systematically racist impacts of policing, immigration, corporate oligarchy, and the climate crisis does us all a disservice. Moreover, there is an absence of a radical vision for tackling economic and racial justice risks to prevent repeating the same crises in the future.

Democratic Party leaders are falling deeply short by offering little more than undoing Trump’s worst excesses. It is a conservative position to seek a return to the “good old days,” when a predatory capitalist system was overseen by articulate, sensible-sounding statesmen who didn’t embarrass the nation on the global stage, who championed police and prisons as tools of safety, who echoed Trump’s rhetoric on “border security,” who preserved corporate profiteering in healthcare, who embraced endless war as long as it was their party’s doing, and so on.

The Democratic Party is essentially a modern-day conservative party, while Republicans are the extremist, fascist party.

No wonder Americans in general dislike both major parties at roughly the same rate. And while the Democrats’ chances of taking control of Congress appear to be surging ahead of the midterm elections, it is likely because the pendulum is swinging away from Republicans, rather than towardDemocrats and their milquetoast agenda.

So, what can Democrats do to ensure victory?

Frankly, it is not our job as voters—or for that matter, the job of newspaper editorialists—to offer advice to political parties.

Our job as voters, especially in this moment, is to seize power in a system that has rendered us powerless and articulate our demands loudly and clearly. Politicians win our votes by acceding to our agenda. Not the other way around.

Therefore, the far more important question is, what do we, the voters, want?

If we agree that the economic system is rigged against the majority of Americans, then how do we unrig it? Is it as basic as “a promise to level out a lopsided economy,” as Wu advises, while ignoring other issues? Is it as simple as a rallying cry to “tax the rich,” as some Democratic-leaning states are doing?

If we want to end the wild pendulum swings of American politics, which are veering us further into the abyss of authoritarianism with each election, we need a complete reset on all fronts, not merely a return to a more balanced economy.

We require, I would argue, an “abolitionist mindset.”

Black abolitionists, who are better versed than the rest of us on what it’s like to be on the receiving end of systemic harms, have long articulated a vision for a better world where we all can thrive: a world where we reverse the equations of how our collective wealth is spent and where we refuse to let our needs be continually defunded.

Black abolitionists like Angela Davis, Ruth Wilson Gilmore, Mariame Kaba, and Andrea J. Ritchie have already shown …

 Cette loi prolonge une doctrine du maintien de l'ordre qui traque et

 Le danger de l'extrême droite

author: Stephen Prager
title: Trump Escalates Attacks on Ilhan Omar With Federal Raid on Her Home
content:
Homeland Security agents searched the Minnesota representative’s home in Washington, DC, on Monday morning.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Following years of threats from President Donald Trump and other Republicans to deport Rep. Ilhan Omar, the Minnesota congresswoman’s Washington, DC home was raided on Monday morning by agents with the Department of Homeland Security.

The US Department of Justice (DOJ) has confirmed that the raid was carried out as part of a judicially authorized warrant, which it said was part of an ongoing criminal investigation.

Fox News, which first reported news of the raid, said it was part of a probe into the naturalization paperwork filed by Omar’s late father when she became a US citizen in 2000 after immigrating to the US as a refugee from Somalia in 1995.

In September, The New York Post reported that federal investigators were examining whether Omar may have been older than 17 when she obtained citizenship through her father as a minor in 2000. The allegation, which stems partly from a discrepancy in historical records of her birth year, has not been substantiated.

Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, a fellow at the American Immigration Council, argued that the case was “even weaker than it already seems,” since federal immigration law includes a waiver for people who obtain legal status through fraud they were unaware of.

Joyce Vance, who served as the US attorney for the Northern District of Alabama under President Barack Obama, noted that the raid took place just weeks before the November 3 midterms, inside the 60-day window where DOJ typically avoids such dramatic actions.

“To state what’s obvious to prosecutors here, we are within the period before an election where DOJ doesn’t take overt steps in an investigation that might influence its outcome,” she said, adding that it was “another hard norm out the window.”

Omar has not yet commented on the raid as of Monday morning, and the DOJ has not indicated what, if any, specific charges have been filed against her.

BREAKING: Federal agents searched Minnesota Rep. Ilhan Omar's home as part of a criminal investigation, AP sources say. https://t.co/67uyHWqjY9

The search comes after years of demands from Trump and other Republicans for Omar — who has served in the US House of Representatives since 2019 — to be deported, imprisoned, or otherwise removed from office.

In a statement Monday morning, Joel Payne, a spokesperson for the progressive advocacy group MoveOn condemned the raid on Omar as a political attack.

“Rep. Omar is a dedicated public servant and a true ally for working families, and Donald Trump has done nothing but use racist tropes and stereotypes to attack her,” he said. “Now, he’s abusing his power to physically intimidate and harass her.”

Last November, Trump remarked that Omar should be thrown out of the country because she is “always complaining” and referenced her religious attire, referring to it as a “swaddling hijab.” In another post that day, he called for the US to “denaturalize migrants who undermine domestic tranquility.”

He also said Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), the only Palestinian American member of Congress, should be “sent back” along with Omar after the two protested his state of the Union address in February.

Trump has often referenced Omar while calling for all Somali immigrants to be deported from the country — even though most are US citizens. Trump has referred to Somalis collectively as “garbage” and said they have “low IQs.”

Last week, Trump called for the people of Minnesota to “fight back” against Somalis living there in a post on Truth Social, which was widely interpreted as an incitement to violence.

In March, Vice President JD Vance said on a podcast that the administration believed Omar had “definitely committed immigration fraud against the United States of America” and that he’d discussed with senior Trump adviser Stephen Miller — who is not a federal prosecutor — how to “go after” her.

Frauen, die in der Öffentlichkeit ohne Hidschab unterwegs sind, gehören inzwischen in vielen Teilen Irans zum alltäglichen Straßenbild. title: CUNY for Palestine Demands Accountability and Action on Palestine from Mayor Zohran Mamdani
content:
A post shared by Labor4Palestine (@labor4palestine)

New York, New York—On Wednesday, October 7, 2026, CUNY for Palestine and NYC-wide Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP) organizers held a rally at City Hall, endorsed by various Palestine solidarity and community organizations, in support of the Palestinian national liberation struggle. Students joined the protest downtown after walking out of class at several of CUNY’s 26 campuses, including the flagship City College of New York (CCNY). Despite Meta’s attempts to censor organizers’ social media, removing posts from across movement accounts in the lead-up to the event, the protest drew hundreds of students, academic workers and community members from across the city to mark three years of ongoing genocide and resistance in Palestine. The protest also attracted international media attention as the principled demands resonated so deeply across the globe. As one student organizer put it: “We’re glad our rally exposed every normalizer, traitor, and hypocrite, when it comes to the Palestinian cause, but the truth is, the resistance and city of Gaza exposed these realities early on.”

Building on the work of the CUNY Divestment Coalition, student organizers’ demands were expressed clearly in the chants that reverberated across Lower Manhattan: “One: We are the students, Two: We won’t stop fighting, Three: We want divestment now, now, now!”

In the wake of the 2024 Student Intifada, students and educators across the country united behind a campaign targeting their universities’ Boards of Trustees (widely referred to by students as “Boards of Butchers”). These boards are the universities’ financiers and oversee university endowments, making them key pressure points for campaigns aiming to divest funds from “Israel”. As one City University of New York (CUNY) student explained, “CUNY claims to be a people’s university, yet it is governed by a body whose interests are completely at odds with the daily realities and solidarity commitments of our majority working class, Black and Brown student body and the communities they belong to.

Last year, CUNY students won a landmark lawsuit forcing CUNY to disclose all financial records from the last five years. The records, released last month, reveal investments made with New York taxpayer money and CUNY student tuition into weapons manufacturers arming “Israel”; tech companies providing security infrastructure to “Israel” and the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS); private prison contractors including CoreCivic and GEO Group, which operates the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) concentration camp Delaney Hall; and corporations profiting directly from US prison labor, such as 3M, a company that has supplied raw materials to prison labor programs in at least 13 states.

In the opening speech made by a representative of CUNY Law Students for Justice in Palestine (SJP), the speaker emphasized that Palestine is the moral compass of all revolutionaries and that this was in fact the reason why divestment has been a key demand of the national student movement for Palestine and a central focus for NYC student organizers as well. Universities are materially complicit in the genocide through their investments in weapon manufacturing companies such as Lockheed Martin, Elbit, and General Dynamics. The speaker emphasized that students’ push for divestment is therefore the most material form that their solidarity with Palestine can take. “It is our duty to resist [the settler colonial genocide in Palestine], and as students, the least we can possibly do is to demand and push for our universities to divest from death.” In another speech, a representative of the Young Democratic Socialists of America (YDSA) called out CUNY’s investments in Caterpillar, Boeing, Raytheon, and Palantir, emphasizing that they are at the top of the CUNY Divestment Coalition’s list of targets for divestment.

On October 7th, protesters turned their attention to New York City’s Mayor. They disrupted Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s attendance at a vigil hosted by “Israelis for Peace,” a front for “Standing Together,” which the BDS Movement has denounced as “an Israeli normalization outfit that seeks to distract from and whitewash Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza.” The event, held in Union Square, parroted rhetoric used by Western media to slander the Palestinian resistance and manufacture consent for the ongoing genocide in Gaza. title: IWA Campaign Against Wage Theft in Korea
content:
Every year in October, the International Workers' Association (IWA-AIT), a global federation of anarcho-syndicalist organizations, launches its annual campaign against wage theft.

This year's campaign will take place from October 12th to October 16th.

Officially launched in 2020 and celebrating its 6th anniversary this year, this campaign aims to expose all forms of wage theft that plague workers worldwide and encourages direct action to reclaim stolen rights.

Wage theft, in this context, is not simply about employers delaying salaries by a few days.

Any scheme or illegal practice used by employers under a capitalist system to reduce labor costs and maximize profits constitutes wage theft, not just wage delay.

These acts of wage theft occur across borders and, in particular, in South Korea, subtle forms of capital exploitation and structural wage theft continue to this day.

First, there is the deprivation of rights disguised as legal compliance. This refers to the practice of forcing workers, even those under the supervision and control of employers, to become "sham freelancers" or enter into service/civil contracts to save on labor costs and avoid obligations related to four major social insurance programs and severance pay.

Even the courts have recognized a de facto employer-employee relationship in some cases, such as with youth soccer team coaches and sports instructors, and have ordered the payment of vacation pay and severance pay regardless of the contractual title. However, capital continues to exploit loopholes in contractual arrangements to steal workers' legal rights.

Second, there is the normalization of unpaid labor. In IT, office, and manufacturing settings where working hours can be clearly defined and accurately measured, the practice of deducting overtime, night shift, and holiday pay under the guise of a "comprehensive wage system" is a prime example. The Supreme Court has repeatedly affirmed that comprehensive wage agreements are invalid when working hours can be accurately measured. Recently, the Supreme Court also rejected the notion of an implied comprehensive wage agreement for intern doctors and recognized their right to overtime pay. Despite this, employers manipulate work records or simply do not keep them, effectively exploiting workers' hard labor for free on a daily basis.

Third, there are illegal practices targeting vulnerable groups such as young people and those new to the workforce. Unlawful "unpaid probationary periods" are often imposed on young people and those new to the workforce who lack knowledge of labor laws, resulting in the exploitation of their labor without compensation. Even reductions in wages during the probationary period, as stipulated by the Minimum Wage Act, are only permitted under strict conditions, but these are often ignored in practice.

Furthermore, exploitation occurs by imposing illegal penalties and reducing wages for migrant workers who are vulnerable due to their precarious immigration status.

Although the Labor Standards Act prohibits penalties and discrimination based on nationality, cases of employers forcing these illegal contracts by exploiting vulnerabilities in immigration status or employment relationships are also problematic.

Finally, there is a subcontracting structure designed to evade responsibility. The multi-layered subcontracting structure, involving main contractors, subcontractors, and staffing agencies, is a facade created by the main contractor to avoid legal responsibility for workers.

When subcontractors go bankrupt or abscond, leaving unpaid wages, the main contractor often claims that "it was only a contract between the subcontractor and the worker," effectively shirking their responsibility. While the current Labor Standards Act Article 44 and the revised Wage Claim Guarantee Act partially stipulate joint and several liability for the direct superior contractor, the national legal system narrowly recognizes the main contractor's responsibility, leaving loopholes for the main contractors to exploit.

As a result, the livelihoods of subcontracted workers are left vulnerable to structural risks.

How have workers around the world fought back?

Branches of the IWA in Spain, Poland, Australia, and Slovakia, among other countries, have not relied solely on complex court rulings or decisions by national agencies.

This is because legal and national systems often favor employers or are designed to delay action, exhausting …

title: US-based Filipino migrants protest prolonged ICE detention of slain journalists’ son
content:
Supporters of Mark Mabasa from the Tanggol Migrante Movement and other groups stage a protest in front of Adelanto City Hall after Mabasa's hearing was postponed. Photo by BAYAN USA

Mabasa’s detention is part of a broader pattern of attacks against migrants seeking safety and a better life in the US.

Filipino migrant organizations in the United States rallied behind asylum seeker Mark Mabasa, son of slain Filipino journalist Percival “Lapid” Mabasa, after the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) extended his detention for at least another month.

Mabasa was detained in California as his family sought political asylum in the US following the assassination of his father, veteran journalist Percival “Lapid” Mabasa, on October 3, 2022.

His father was the second journalist killed under the Marcos Jr. administration. His killing remains unresolved, with suspect Gerald Bantag, former chief of the Bureau of Corrections, still at large.

The Mabasa family sought asylum in the US after receiving death threats following the journalist’s killing.

On October 2, a day before the fourth year of his father’s killing, overseas Filipino organizations gathered outside Adelanto ICE Processing Center where Mabasa was being detained to demand his immediate release.

The groups were denied entry to the facility, forcing them to hold the protest outside Adelanto City Hall, five minutes away from the detention center.

Mabasa’s continued detention comes amid the Trump administration’s intensified campaign of mass arrests and deportations of migrants in the US.

ICE arrests reached nearly 50,000 in July alone, reportedly the agency’s highest monthly arrest total during US President Donald Trump’s second term.

The Trump administration also ordered federal immigration agents to increase arrests to meet daily quotas. Under the directive, each ICE officer is expected to make at least 75 arrests daily, potentially raising daily arrests from several hundred to as many as 3,000.

The administration likewise announced plans to revoke up to 200,000 B1 and B2 visas issued between 2016 and 2026, including those who sought or are seeking asylum, according to reports.

For Filipino migrant organizations, Mabasa’s detention is part of a broader pattern of attacks against migrants seeking safety and a better life in the US.

“This should not be commonplace for government leaders to sit idly by as the rights and welfare of their nationals are violated,” said Tanggol Migrante.

The group criticized the Marcos Jr. administration for its failure to defend Filipinos facing immigration-related attacks in the US. “We have yet to see Marcos Jr. and his representatives, such as Ambassador Jose Manuel Romualdez, come to the defense of migrants in the U.S. facing these attacks.”

“The actions of the Philippine government are meager in comparison to other governments standing up for the rights of their nationals,” Tanggol Migrante said.

“His murder in 2022 exposes how easily corrupt officials take advantage of their positions in power to silence those who speak out and how they avoid accountability for their crimes to this day,” said Tabs Gabriel of Malaya Movement USA and Kilusang Bayan Kontra Kurakot Southern California.

Gabriel said that Mabasa “is no stranger to corruption and political persecution,” noting that his father was an outspoken radio broadcaster who criticized corruption and state violence under the Duterte and Marcos Jr. administrations.

BAYAN USA said that it received reports that the Philippine government has been cooperating with US authorities by providing information on Filipinos in the country.

“Migrants are ultimately still left to fend for themselves in inhumane conditions such as unclean drinking water, rat feces-infested food, and medical neglect. This situation is not unique to Mark but is faced by all migrants languishing in these inhumane facilities,” said Joell Manguerra of BAYAN USA. “More and more of our kababayan are breaking through their fear to fight back because we have learned that it’s only through people power that we can win our freedom.”

Migrante USA criticized Philippine officials for allegedly choosing to cooperate with the US government in the detention and deportation of overseas Filipinos rather than intervene on their behalf.

“When our government prioritizes the demands of a foreign government over their own nationals, it is a systems failure that shows the need for systems change,” Kai Marie of …

title: Solo el martirio de millones de migrantes puede garantizar la victoria del imperio capitalista.
content:
Producto de La globalización neoliberal la crisis de los refugiados es una de las tragedias más masacrantes de la historia contemporánea. Son millones de fugitivos que luchan por hacer realidad esa consigna de

“vencer o morir”

.  Pasa el tiempo y torturados por la angustia existencial  para  los “nuevos bárbaros” no existen barreras infranqueables, ni murallas, ni fosos, ni campos electrificados o minados, ni alambre de púas, ni accidentes geográficos, desiertos, montañas, ríos, mares u océanos; ni tampoco ejércitos o armadas que los detengan. Europa es el cielo si lo comparamos con el infierno del que escaparon donde reina la miseria, la inseguridad, la violencia, las enfermedades o el hambre.


Los conflictos bélicos -ya sean de alta o baja intensidad- se extienden a lo largo y ancho del planeta: en Afganistán, Kurdistán, India, Pakistán, Irán, en Palestina, Líbano, Afganistán, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Somalia, Eritrea, Etiopía, Sudán, Camerún, Nigeria, Mali, República Centroafricana, Burkina Faso, R.D Congo, Yemen, etc. 

Esto significa más refugiados, más desplazados susceptibles de engrosar el éxodo bíblico.  Todos al asalto Primer Mundo opulento y desarrollado

 por la frontera turca, los Balcanes o las islas griegas en el Mediterráneo,  la costa Libia, argelina o tunecina hasta alcanzar la isla de Lampedusa en Italia, o por Ceuta y Melilla cruzando el estrecho de Gibraltar para desembarcar en las playas de Andalucía; o desde Senegal o Gambia o Mauritania con rumbo a las Islas Canarias y en América  al asalto del imperio americano por el río Bravo o el Mar Caribe; en Asia por el mar de la China, el Mar de Timor y el Océano Índico hasta las costas de Australia.


Se ha bombardeado y demolido sistemáticamente pueblos y ciudades, quieren aplastar a

 la población civil, enterrarlos vivos como se ha comprobado en Siria, el Líbano, Palestina, el Yemen y la única posibilidad de supervivencia es cruzar la frontera de la UE.


El número de refugiados que tiene a su cargo

ACNUR

(Agencia de la ONU para protección y asistencia de los refugiados) es de unos 30 millones, mientras la cifra global de refugiados es de 42 millones. Las personas víctimas del desplazamiento forzado en el mundo sube hasta los 118 millones.


 


Cualquier país de la Unión Europea está obligado por ley internacional a recibir y estudiar solicitudes de asilo político o de carácter humanitario sin depender estrictamente de una nacionalidad especifica sino de los motivos individuales de persecución

. Aunque se aplican normativas de retorno estrictas para casos rechazados si se les califica como migrantes por causas económicas. El estatuto de refugiado o el de asilo político de la UE les asegura recibir todos los meses una paga y beneficiarse de las ayudas estatales, alojamiento, educación o sanidad.


 


África actualmente tiene una población aproximada de 1.500 millones de habitantes de los cuales más de 50% son pobres de solemnidad y que si tuvieran posibilidad de elegir emigrarían sin ninguna duda a Europa

. Y no lo hacen a EE.UU porque geográficamente los separa el océano Atlántico. Con solo un 2 o 3% (8 millones) que lograran entrar en Europa crearían una crisis social insostenible y el sistema colapsaría.


Hoy en día ya no se capturan esclavos en África para venderlos en los mercados negreros porque son los propios nativos quienes pagan a las mafias, a los contrabandistas, a los coyotes para que los conduzcan hasta la tierra de promisión. Media humanidad se niega a aceptar esa sentencia que reza:

“Nacer pobres para morir pobres”

. Qué más da morir de inanición en el desierto o ahogados en el mar Mediterráneo o en el océano Atlántico porque de hecho ya están muertos.


 


Los sin tierra, los sin techo, los analfabetas, los huérfanos, los hambrientos y sedientos también quieren participar en el gran banquete capitalista

, esos seres invisibles pertenecientes al mundo de ultratumba huyen despavoridos en busca de ese espejismo que se trasmite en vivo y en directo que transmiten las cadenas de televisión a través de las antenas parabólicas, el Internet o los teléfonos celulares. 

El bombardeo publicitario es más poderoso que una lluvia de obuses o misiles

. Seducidos por la propaganda del lujo y la opulencia de ese mundo delirante de la “gran Babylon” de rascacielos dorados donde el genio de la lámpara maravillosa es capaz de cumplir todos nuestros deseos.

title: KHRN reports enforced disappearances of five Kurdish opposition figures in Iran
content:
The security agencies of the Islamic Republic of Iran, specifically the Ministry of Intelligence and the Intelligence Organization of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), have increasingly deployed enforced disappearance against members of Kurdish opposition groups since June 2025, following the outbreak of the 12-day Israel-Iran conflict, which also involved US military strikes.


At least five Kurdish political activists have since been subjected to enforced disappearance: Mohsen Ghaderi, Sara Rashidi Kachlanlou, Zahra Pirdehghan, Parvin (Akhtar) Rasegh Qizilbash and Sirwan Habibi. They were arrested in Baneh, Paveh, Orumiyeh, and Kamyaran, and subsequently subjected to enforced disappearance.


Despite credible eyewitness testimonies and evidence confirming their detention by Iranian government security forces, Iran’s judicial authorities have not formally registered their detention. Security agencies also continue to deny their families information about their whereabouts or custody status.


This situation places the detainees outside the protection of the law, depriving them of access to legal counsel, communication with their families and necessary medical care.


These enforced disappearances have emerged amid a shift in detention practices following the recent regional hostilities and the bombardment of several security facilities.


The emerging pattern involves the relocation of detainees to unofficial detention facilities, denial of due process and restrictions on communication with legal representatives and family members.


Previously, individuals arrested in the Kurdish region were generally transferred to designated intelligence detention centres in provincial capitals. Security agencies are now increasingly holding detainees in secret facilities or relocating them to detention facilities in neighbouring provinces, including Hamadan and East Azerbaijan.


In all five documented cases, state agencies have refused to acknowledge responsibility for the arrests. Relevant local courts have consistently refused to provide information, effectively blocking families from pursuing legal avenues to establish the fate and whereabouts of their relatives.


As a result, all five detainees have been completely cut off from the outside world, with their current whereabouts and conditions remaining unknown.


The following section documents the circumstances surrounding the arrests and subsequent enforced disappearances of the five Kurdish political activists.


Mohsen Ghaderi


Political affiliation: Free Life Party of Kurdistan (PJAK)


Date of arrest: 22 June 2025


Location: Hangeh-Zhal border area, Baneh


Detaining agency: IRGC Intelligence Organization


Mohsen Ghaderi was arrested alongside a local border worker (kolbar) in the Hangeh-Zhal border area of Baneh on 22 June 2025.


Following their arrest, both men were taken to an IRGC facility in Baneh before being transferred to the IRGC Intelligence Organization’s Shahramfar detention centre in Sanandaj.


The kolbar, who was released on bail after three months, confirmed that no military engagement had taken place at the time of their arrest.


However, the IRGC Intelligence Organization twice summoned Ghaderi’s family in mid-2025, claiming that he had been killed during a military confrontation and prohibiting the family from holding a funeral service.


Local inquiries and accounts from residents contradict the Iranian authorities’ narrative, indicating that both individuals were taken into custody without any armed confrontation.


Ghaderi was last seen at the Shahramfar detention facility in September 2025. Unconfirmed reports indicate that he may subsequently have been transferred to an IRGC intelligence detention facility in Orumiyeh.


The Iranian authorities had previously made false claims regarding Ghaderi’s death following a July 2021 ambush in Bukan. Ghaderi later publicly rejected those claims in a video message.


Despite evidence of his detention, the authorities have not acknowledged his current custody status or disclosed his whereabouts.

content:
Καλούν οι:

Οριζόντια Κίνηση και Ανάρες, ομάδα δράσης και αλληλεγγύης


Αφίσες/Καλέσματα:


Οριζόντια Κίνηση – για την Αναρχία και τον Ελευθεριακό Κομμουνισμό


Μικροφωνική – Συγκέντρωση σχετικά με τον νέο αντι-μεταναστευτικό νόμο


Πέμπτη 8/10, 19:00, Στάση Μετρό Αγίας Σοφίας


Οριζόντια Κίνηση – Για την Αναρχία και τον Ελευθεριακό Κομμουνισμό


Σχετικά με τον νέο αντι-μεταναστευτικό νόμο


«Το μεταναστευτικό κατά την άποψή μου μπορεί να λυθεί με δύο τρόπους, οι οποίοι σιγά σιγά πρέπει να λέγονται ξεκάθαρα. Ο πρώτος τρόπος είναι η φύλαξη των συνόρων, να καταλάβουμε τι εννοούμε, φύλαξη των συνόρων δεν μπορεί να υφίσταται αν δεν υπάρχουν απώλειες, και για να γίνω κατανοητός, αν δεν υπάρχουν νεκροί…Πρέπει να περνάνε χειρότερα. Η ζωή τους, η κόλαση, να φαντάζει παράδεισος σ’ αυτά που θα ζουν εδώ πέρα»


Τα παραπάνω αποτελούν δηλώσεις του φασίστα υπουργού μετανάστευσης και ασύλου Θάνου Πλεύρη το 2011, όντας τότε μέλος του ακροδεξιού κόμματος ΛΑΟΣ, μαζί με άλλα στελέχη της ΝΔ. Στην εποχή μας, το μεταναστευτικό παρουσιάζεται ως μία από τις μεγαλύτερες «απειλές» για την Ευρώπη. Κυβερνήσεις και μέσα ενημέρωσης καλλιεργούν συστηματικά τον φόβο, το μίσος και τον ρατσισμό, μετατρέποντας τους ανθρώπους που αναγκάστηκαν να εγκαταλείψουν τα σπίτια τους σε αποδιοπομπαίους τράγους για κάθε κοινωνικό πρόβλημα, καλώντας ανοιχτά ακόμα και σε δολοφονίες εναντίον τους. Στην Ελλάδα βλέπουμε συστηματικά να καλλιεργούνται τέτοιες αφηγήσεις σχεδόν από ολόκληρο το πολιτικό φάσμα της βουλής, που αποτελείται κατά βάση από φιλελεύθερους, ακροδεξιούς και φανατικούς χριστιανούς.


Την ίδια στιγμή, τα πραγματικά αίτια της μετανάστευσης μένουν κρυμμένα πίσω από τις ακροδεξιές ρητορικές. Οι περισσότεροι άνθρωποι δεν εγκαταλείπουν τον τόπο τους από επιλογή. Φεύγουν εξαιτίας πολέμων, δικτατοριών, φτώχειας, περιβαλλοντικών καταστροφών. Αυτές οι άθλιες συνθήκες προκαλούνται διαχρονικά από τα δυτικά καπιταλιστικά κράτη και τις πολεμικές και οικονομικές διακρατικές συμμαχίες (ΝΑΤΟ, ΕΕ). Σε Αφρική, Δυτική Ασία, Νότια Αμερική, η αποικιοκρατία και αργότερα οι ιμπεριαλιστικές επεμβάσεις διαλύουν υποδομές και οικονομίες και αποσυνθέτουν κοινωνίες εδώ και αιώνες, ώστε το δυτικό Κεφάλαιο να μπορεί να εκμεταλλευτεί τον τοπικό πλούτο, τις αγορές και τους εμπορικούς δρόμους. Σπέρνουν την διχόνοια, τους εμφυλίους πολέμους, οπλίζουν δικτατορικά καθεστώτα, υποβοηθούν τις γενοκτονίες.


Στην πρόσφατη περίπτωση των μεταναστ(ρι)ών στην Θέουτα, που προσπάθησαν να “εισέλθουν παράνομα στην Ισπανία και την Ε.Ε.” παρακινούμενοι/ες από αγνώστου προελεύσεως fake news σε σχέση με την δυνατότητα “νομιμοποίησής” τους, έχουμε την περίπτωση μιας εκ των τελευταίων ευρωπαϊκών αποικιών, έναν “Ισπανικό” θύλακα σε Αφρικανικό έδαφος, που σε μια αντιστροφή της ιστορικής πραγματικότητας, δέχθηκε δήθεν “οργανωμένη εισβολή”. Οι περισσότεροι/ες από τους/τις χιλιάδες μετανάστ(ρι)ες που πέρασαν τα “Ευρωπαϊκά” σύνορα, στο έδαφος βέβαια της δικής τους ηπείρου, επέστρεψαν σύντομα οικειοθελώς, αλλά και μετά την βίαιη απάντηση του δήθεν προοδευτικού Ισπανικού Κράτους. Οι λιγοστοί που έμειναν, υφίστανται την ρατσιστική βία από “ντόπιους”, δηλαδή Ισπανούς πολίτες, υποκινούμενη από οργανωμένους φασίστες, με επιθέσεις στους καταυλισμούς τους και παρεμπόδιση της διανομής τροφίμων από ανθρωπιστικές οργανώσεις.


Η αντιμετώπιση, λοιπόν, αυτών των ανθρώπων από την λεγόμενη «πολιτισμένη Δύση» αποτελεί ένα δείγμα της απανθρωπιάς και του μίσους που καλλιεργείται απέναντι στους μετανάστες. Τα τελευταία χρόνια έχουν καταγραφεί αμέτρητα περιστατικά από διεθνείς οργανισμούς και οργανώσεις ανθρωπίνων δικαιωμάτων σχετικά με παράνομες επαναπροωθήσεις, αυθαίρετες κρατήσεις, βίαιες συμπεριφορές και δολοφονίες στα σύνορα.


Στην Ελλάδα όλα αυτά συμβαίνουν σχεδόν σε καθημερινή βάση, τόσο στα θαλάσσια σύνορα, όσο και στον Έβρο και το μεγαλύτερο ποσοστό των περιστατικών αυτών δεν φτάνουν ποτέ στα αυτιά μας. Το λιμενικό, οι συνοριοφύλακες, πολλές φορές μάλιστα μαζί με παραστρατιωτικές μονάδες, χτυπούν, ληστεύουν, βιάζουν και πνίγουν μετανάστες και μετανάστριες στα σύνορα. Τρανό παράδειγμα αποτελεί το ναυάγιο της Πύλου με τους τουλάχιστον 600 δολοφονημένους μετανάστες και μετανάστριες (ανάμεσά τους και πολλά παιδιά).


Ταυτόχρονα, η πραγματικότητα για όσους και όσες επιβιώνουν το πέρασμα των συνόρων, αλλά εντοπίζονται από τις ελληνικές αρχές, είναι εξίσου βασανιστική. Ο εγκλεισμός σε καμπ κολαστήρια, που στερούνται ακόμη και των πιο υποτυπωδών υποδομών, ιδίως σε σχέση με την υγεία και την περίθαλψη, δημιουργεί μια ανυπόφορη …
