title: Effleurer l'avenir. Notes sur le technofascisme
content:
« L'avenir appartient à ceux qui savent perforer le présent »

 [

1

]

, écrit Cindy Coutant au début de son excellent

Pénétration terminale

, dernière publication des éditions Audimat. Perforer, c'est traverser ; mais traverser d'une façon bien particulière : traverser en vue d'atteindre, d'arriver – traverser

pour

 arriver. Perforer semble être cet impératif de l'époque que, il y a presque trente ans, un groupe d'auteurs anonymes décrivait ainsi « il faut supprimer le trajet ; il est impératif d'

arriver

 seulement »

 [

2

]

.


Perforer, c'est donc performer afin d'atteindre le plus rapidement, le plus efficacement possible, c'est trouer tout ce qui sépare de la fin, c'est performer l'atteinte. Cette performance ne va pas sans force, sans efficience, sans vigueur, elle est la promesse de la technologie, et des discours qui la sous-tendent relevant d'une « grammaire rigide de la perforation »

 [

3

]

. Il est question partout dans l'ouvrage de cette rigidité érectile comme imaginaire et cap du technofascisme. Seul un être rigide peut, en effet, « tout défoncer sur son passage »

 [

4

]

 – c'est-à-dire arriver à ses fins. Mais ce passage n'est pas infini, il ne peut être une dérive, liquide ou molle, un détour à jamais inachevé, figures du looser – de l'échoué – qui ne parvient pas. La perforation, la pénétration doivent être terminales. Coutant reprend l'expression à la balistique (une science des balles, une science

des projectiles

, donc,

une

science

 du projet

) :


La

pénétration terminale

 désigne la capacité opérationnelle de pénétration d'un projectile durant l'ultime phase de sa trajectoire : précision d'impact, capacité de percée, étendue des dommages selon sa nature anti-personnelle ou anti-matérielle. Si la balistique étudie les trajectoires sous tous leurs aspects, la balistique terminale est la branche scientifique qui étudie le moment où le projectile n'a plus d'options ; lorsqu'il ne corrige plus sa course, ne négocie plus sa vitesse, ne compose plus avec l'espace traversé. La trajectoire est verrouillée, l'horizon se referme en ligne d'impact : le projectile doit défoncer, et qu'il atteigne exactement sa cible ou qu'il la manque, il va le faire. La terminalité est tout à la fois une fin de parcours et le moment où l'action quitte le champ des possibles pour devenir exécutoire

 [

5

]


La balistique terminale s'intéresse donc au point de non-retour

 [

6

]

, qui porte mal son nom dans la mesure où ce moment est celui de l'impact, c'est-à-dire de l'arrivée : dans le projet, toute arrivée est un retour, puisqu'il s'agit d'atteindre ce qui a déjà été projeté au préalable, de parvenir là où on s'était imaginé aller,

de

retourner

 à

ce qui avait été projeté

. Et c'est ce qui explique, aussi, pourquoi l'imaginaire du technofascisme, qui est l'imaginaire de la projection par excellence, est un imaginaire nostalgique, réactionnaire : car, d'une certaine manière, tout projet est nostalgique, tout projet est une façon de retourner, retour en forme d'aller vers ce qui avait été prévu. La terminalité est le moment du passage à l'acte, en même temps que la preuve de la capacité à passer à l'acte, à être davantage qu'une pure puissance n'ayant pas éprouvé sa bravoure. La terminalité performe donc cette capacité à passer à l'acte – performance de son actualité en tant que, on va le voir, sujet masculin blanc occidental. La performativité/perforativité, que l'on pourrait à présent désigner par le syntagme perfor(m)ativité, peut apparaître alors comme une forme d'agentivité qui expliquerait certaines violences faites à tout ce qui est hors-norme, comme l'imaginent Véronica Gago et Luci Cavallero :


les féminicides, travesticides, transféminicides, lesbicides répandent l'idée d'un pouvoir absolu au niveau de la quotidienneté. Il n'est pas nécessaire d'avoir du « pouvoir institutionnel », il n'est pas nécessaire d'« être un grand homme », pour exercer ce pouvoir de tuer. Et, pour cela même, cet accès au pouvoir devient si attractif entre pairs. L'accès au gouvernement – au plus grand pouvoir institutionnel démocratique – d'une personne comme Milei, qui revendique de manière sinistre et efficace le pouvoir brutal de « ceux qui n'ont pas de pouvoir » (ceux qui ne sont pas la caste), « libère » un mode d'exercice du pouvoir que nous caractérisons comme passage à l'acte des « discours de haine » émis par l'État

 [

7

]


Perfor(m)er sa virilité, sa capacité à atteindre, sa rigidité …

While these words originally come from Social Anarchism and Organisation by the FARJ, this edited and abridged version represents our organizational understanding of this text which has been essential to the development of the Center for Especifismo Studies and the continuation of Militant Kindergarten. We have composed, numbered, and subtitled the following paragraphs by adapting our “Reading Guide” without page numbers or ellipsis to make for a smoother reading:

By especifismo, we refer to a conception of anarchist organization that has two fundamental axes: organization and social work/insertion. These two axes are based on the classical concepts of differentiated actuation of anarchism in the social and political levels (Bakuninist concept) and specific anarchist organization (Malatestan concept).

Synthesis advocates a model of anarchist organization in which are all the anarchists (anarcho-communists, anarchosyndicalists, anarcho-individualists etc.). So, it presents many of the characteristics that we criticize. We recognize that within synthesist organizations there are also serious militants committed to social anarchism, so we do not want the criticisms to seem generalized. Although we never question whether these organizations are anarchist (for us, they all are), they do not, in most cases, converge with our way of conceiving anarchist organization. There are diverse anarchist organizations that do not come out of the especifismo current. So, especifismo implies much more than to advocate anarchist organization. We understand anarchism as an ideology, that is, a “set of ideas, motivations, aspirations, values, a structure or system of concepts that have a direct connection with action – that which we call political practice”. Especifismo advocates an anarchism that, as an ideology, seeks to conceive a model of performance that transforms the society of today into libertarian socialism by means of the social revolution. title: La Crique, un futur lieu anti-autoritaire pour partir à l'abordage
content:
Appel à contributions pour acheter un local dans l'est parisien 💰


Difficile de rester insensible face au fonctionnement insensé du monde dans lequel on vit. L'argent est roi, les puissants s'enrichissent sur le dos de milliards d'autres personnes, sur le pillage et la destruction du vivant. Leur soif de pouvoir s'accompagne de conquêtes, de colonisations et de guerres.


Des murs sont érigés, les frontières renforcées, les indésirables chassé-es ou enfermé-es.


Les discours réactionnaires pullulent, légitimant le passage à l'acte des racistes, transphobes et homophobes de tous poils.


Pour que ça passe et que chacun ferme sa gueule, on nous vend des smartphones et la démocratie. Les caméras et les flics partout viennent compléter un contrôle de plus en plus large, optimiser la gestion intéressée de nos vies et empêcher toute rébellion.


Mais partout, des gens tentent de briser le cours des choses, rompre la normalité, résister à ce qui nous est imposé. C'est dans ces brèches que nous nous sommes rencontré-es ces dernières années : squats, manifestations et blocages en tous genres, mouvements, assemblées, collectifs, espaces de débrouille…


Sans être d'accord sur tout, nous partageons l'envie d'en découdre avec ce monde.


Pourtant, ces derniers temps, nous avons aussi constaté qu'il y a de moins en moins de lieux pour se rencontrer, débattre, et s'organiser. Pour qui aspire à un bouleversement de l'ordre social, cette question est primordiale. D'autant plus face à une vague autoritaire mondiale qui paraît inexorable.


C'est de là que vient l'envie de dénicher une Crique entre deux immeubles pour y ancrer sa barque. Un espace de débats, de partage de savoirs, de convivialité, de contre-information, de diffusion d'idées mutines et de pratiques de luttes offensives.


La Crique sera ouverte à toutes celles et ceux qui se retrouvent sincèrement dans le constat que ce monde est à saborder dans une perspective émancipatrice pour tou-tes, et qui veulent s'organiser sans capitaine, de manière anti-autoritaire et autonome.


Anti-autoritaire ça veut dire de manière horizontale, d'égale à égale, sans chef ni politicard.


Autonome ça veut dire agir par nous-mêmes. Le lieu n'est pas l'organe de transmission d'un parti ou d'un syndicat. Les voies qu'il explore sont donc anti-électorales.


Il ne s'agit pas de constituer un groupe politique avec une ligne précise. Mais dans cette période de confusion des idées, il semble important d'assumer une certaine base commune.


Ce futur lieu veut défendre une perspective révolutionnaire, c'est à dire la provocation d'un changement radical et l'avènement d'un monde libéré de toute autorité. Tous les combats doivent être menés de front contre les oppressions et les normes.


Combattre l'État, le capitalisme et la propriété privée. Combattre le racisme, le validisme, le genre, l'hétéronormativité et le patriarcat.


Combattre l'industrie et la technologie qui saccagent la planète et nous dépossèdent toujours plus de nos moyens de subsistance.


Combattre la démocratie dont l'objectif est de pacifier et de faire accepter l'ordre des choses. Les partis vendant un changement radical viennent simplement récupérer la colère et aménager l'existant.


Combattre les dominations partout où elles se trouvent que ce soit au niveau de l'État, de la famille, ou de nos assemblées.


Ce que nous imaginons faire dans la Crique est large et non exhaustif, ça dépendra des complicités et des idées que chacun-e amènera dans ses cales.


Lire des brochures sur le logement et la gentrification, organiser une manifestation sauvage après un énième meurtre policier, débattre sur les méthodes pour se débarrasser du nucléaire, imaginer une action contre la construction d'une nouvelle prison, chiller autour d'un café, rêver d'un blackout de l'économie, faire l'arpentage d'un livre sur l'histoire coloniale de la Kanaky, planifier la perturbation d'une conférence transphobe, faire un événement de solidarité autour de la guerre au Soudan, débriefer après une opération répressive, discuter pour faire écho à des révoltes ailleurs, accueillir une assemblée de mobilisation contre la guerre, se réunir avant d'aller recouvrir la ville de slogans contre le patriarcat, mater un film où à la fin on gagne, et aussi des ateliers pratiques, affiches, anonymat numérique, débrouille pour l'élec... et si on a assez d'oseille : aménager l'espace pour des concerts, des cantines, une piscine anti-olympique. 🏊

title: AKP’li yıllarda TOKİ: İhale rejimi ve arsa düzeni
content:
Bugün milyonlarca emekçiyi girdaba sürükleyen barınma krizi, AKP iktidarı boyunca TOKİ ile Emlak Konut eliyle kurulan düzenin içinde mayalandı. Konut krizinin sermaye çevrelerinde, menkul simsarlarında ve onların sözcülüğünü yapanlarda nasıl anlatıldığı bellidir: “Yeterince konut üretilmiyor, arz talebi karşılamıyor, fiyatlar ve kiralar bu yüzden yükseliyor”. Uydurulan çözüm ise “daha çok inşaat, daha çok imar, daha çok kredi”. Bu kesime göre konut içinde yaşanacak bir yer değil, arzı ve talebi olan bir metadır. Kriz de ancak daha fazla meta üretilerek giderilecek bir piyasa aksaklığı olarak görülür. Aynı dil iktidarın da dilidir: Bakan Kurum 500 bin konutluk kampanyayı "hem konut fiyatları hem kira fiyatları düşsün diye" başlattıklarını kaydetmişti.

Oysa TOKİ ve Emlak Konut'un yirmi yılı bu reçeteyi sınayan büyük bir deney gibi duruyor. TOKİ Başkanı Ömer Bulut'a göre idare 2003-2022 arasında 1 milyon 170 bin konut üretti. Emlak Konut da kendi verisine göre 2003'ten bu yana 260 bin bağımsız birim geliştirdi. Yalnızca 2020-2022 arasında 247 bin TOKİ konutu yapıldı. Ev sahipliği oranı tam da bu yıllarda geriledi. Simsarların reçetesi devlet eliyle uygulandı, ama emekçinin barınma sorunu çözülmedi.

Demek ki mesele kaç konut yapıldığı değil, konutun kimin için ve neye göre üretildiğidir. Emekçi için konut başını sokacağı bir dam, ailesiyle birlikte ertesi güne hazırlandığı bir barınaktır. Sermaye için ise satıldığında kâr, elde tutulduğunda değer artışı getiren bir varlıktır. Birincisinin ölçüsü ihtiyaç, ikincisininki satış fiyatıdır. TOKİ ile Emlak Konut'un kurduğu düzen ağırlığı açıkça ikincisine verdi. Kamu, konut üretimini barınma hakkına göre değil, sermaye kriterlerince göre örgütledi.

Bunun en açık itirafı, 2003-2011 arasında TOKİ Başkanı, ardından Çevre ve Şehircilik Bakanı olan Erdoğan Bayraktar'dan geldi. Bayraktar 2012'de TBMM kürsüsünde, devletin Ataşehir, Ataköy, Bahçeşehir, Kayabaşı, Mavişehir ve Eryaman'daki arazilerini gelir paylaşımı modeliyle "1,5 misli, 2 misli, 5 misli değerle değerlendirdik" diyordu. Nitekim bakanın gurur kaynağı, kamu arazisinin emekçiye konut olması değil, satış değerinin katlanmasıydı. Kamu toprağı, devletin eliyle rant aracına dönüştürülüyordu.

Bu dönüşüm bir iş bölümüyle hayata geçti. TOKİ kamu arazisini topladı ve imara açtı; Emlak Konut bu araziyi müteahhide bağladı. Kamunun imar kararıyla değerlenen toprağı, inşaat sermayesinin hasılatına dönüştü. TOKİ'nin 500 bin konutluk kampanyasına 8 milyon 840 bin kişi başvurdu. Kentin merkezindeki kamu toprağı sermayeye satılacak projelere bağlandı. Emekçiye ise çeperde, kurayla dağıtılan ve taksitleri memur maaş artışına endeksli bir borç kaldı. Nüfusun yüzde 27'sini oluşturan kiracılar bu düzenin hesabına neredeyse hiç girmedi.

Elbette barınma krizinin başkaca nedenleri de var: Ücretlerin baskılanması, enflasyon, faiz politikası, depremin enkazı ve iç göç... Ancak devletin kentsel toprak ve konut üzerindeki “en güçlü aracı” TOKİ, yirmi yılı aşkın süre boyunca konutu emekçinin barınma ihtiyacına göre değil, sermayenin satış değerine göre düzenlemek için kullandı. Krize karşı kamunun elinde olması gereken kaldıraç, krizi üreten mantığın içinde çalıştı.

2001: Tasfiye halindeki Emlak Bankası'nın varlıkları TOKİ'ye devredildi. Bakanlar Kurulu kararıyla 7 bin 852 konut TOKİ'ye geçti.

2001-2002: Emlak Bankası'nın Emlak Konut'taki payları TOKİ'ye devredildi. Şirket gayrimenkul yatırım ortaklığı statüsü aldı ve TOKİ, Emlak Konut'un ana hissedarı oldu.

31 Temmuz 2003: 4966 sayılı Kanun, Toplu Konut Kanunu'nu değiştirerek TOKİ'ye konut sektörüyle ilgili şirketler kurma ve kurulmuş şirketlere ve finans kurumlarına ortak olma yetkisi verdi. Aynı düzenleme, kâr amaçlı projeler yapmanın da yolunu açtı.

2003: 4734 sayılı Kamu İhale Kanunu'na eklenen bir hüküm, TOKİ'ye kamulaştırma, mülkiyet, arsa temini ve uygulama projesi şartları aranmadan yapım ihalesine çıkma imkânı tanıdı.

5 Mayıs 2004: 5162 sayılı Kanun, Toplu Konut Kanunu'nun TOKİ'nin plan yetkisini düzenleyen 4. maddesini değiştirdi. TOKİ, gecekondu dönüşüm alanlarında ve kendi arsalarında her ölçekte imar planı yapma yetkisi aldı. Belediyece üç ay içinde onaylanmayan planları kendisi onaylayabilir hale geldi.

title: Geschichte von unten: Jeden Monat ein neues, faires T-Shirt von „Working Class History“ – für LeserInnen des LabourNet Germany zum reduzierten Preis, der zudem auch uns unterstützt!
content:
Dossier


Seit November 2021 ist das neue Projekt „T-Shirt of the Month“ von

dna merch


 in Zusammenarbeit mit der Bildungsinitiative

Working Class History


 online. LabourNet ist Teil des Projekts und kann die Shirts Euch daher mit dem Discount-Code etwas günstiger anbieten. Jeden Monat gibt es ein faires, genossenschaftlich genähtes T-Shirt, das einer Geschichte oder einer Persönlichkeit aus dem Archiv von Working Class History gewidmet ist. Es kann einen Monat lang weltweit vorbestellt werden und wird dann in der jeweiligen Auflage produziert und verschickt. Mit den Shirts werden die Forschungs- und Bildungsarbeit von Working Class History, eine Näherinnen-Kooperative in Kroatien sowie Basisgewerkschafter*innen in Südasien unterstützt. Die Designs kommen von Künstler*innen und Aktivist*innen aus der ganzen Welt. LabourNet-Leser*innen können beim Kauf der Shirts sparen und gleichzeitig unsere redaktionelle Arbeit unterstützen. Für jedes mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code gekaufte Shirt bekommt ihr 5% Rabatt und wir eine Vermittlungsgebühr bzw. Spende. Siehe weitere Infos und die Shirts/Hoodies/Pullover:


[Mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code] Das Oktober-2026-Shirt von Working Class History/dna: La Revolution Est Femme (Frankreich 1789)


„

Das Design dieses Monats ist den Tausenden von Frauen in Paris gewidmet, die am 5. Oktober 1789 einen entscheidenden Wendepunkt der Französischen Revolution herbeiführten. Verärgert über die hohen Brotpreise und den Brotmangel, plünderten sie das städtische Waffenlager und belagerten das Schloss von Versailles. Eine Augenzeugin hörte die Frauen sagen: „Die Männer hatten nicht genug Kraft, sich zu rächen, und sie würden beweisen, dass sie besser seien als die Männer.“ Die Frauen verlangten eine Zusammenkunft mit König Ludwig XVI., um Brot und Fortschritte bei der Ausarbeitung einer neuen, überarbeiteten Verfassung zu fordern, welche die Macht der Monarchie einschränken und neue Rechte für die Bevölkerung festschreiben sollte. (…) Wieder einmal hatten wir das Glück, die italienische Tätowierkünstlerin Fede Borgia für die Gestaltung eines Motivs zu gewinnen, das diese inspirierende Geschichte weiblicher Stärke einfängt. Sie gab ihrem Werk den französischen Titel „La Révolution est femme“, was auf Deutsch „Die Revolution ist weiblich“ bedeutet. Auf dem Schild im Hintergrund ist „Du Pain“ zu lesen – „Etwas Brot“, ein Verweis darauf, dass die hohen Brotpreise und der Brotmangel der Auslöser für die revolutionären Aktionen der Frauen waren

…“ Siehe mehr

Informationen und Bestellung in verschiedenen Versionen bei dna merch

[Mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code] Das September-2026-Shirt von Working Class History/dna: Mehr Als 108 (Paraguay 1959)


„

In der Nacht zum 1. September 1959 stirbt der Radiomoderator und Tänzer Bernardo Aranda bei einem Brand in seinem Zimmer im Asunción Stadtteil Barrio Obrero. Der Fall wird nie aufgeklärt. Die von den USA unterstützte Militärdiktatur Alfredo Stroessners zieht trotzdem einen Schluss: Weil auch schwule Männer bei Aranda verkehrten, muss einer von ihnen verantwortlich sein. In den folgenden Tagen verhaftet und foltert die Polizei gezielt Männer, die als homosexuell gelten. Die regierungstreue Zeitung El País nennt schließlich die Zahl der Festgenommenen: 108. Angeklagt wird niemand, weder für Arandas Tod noch für das, was den Verhafteten angetan wurde. Bis heute wird „108″ in Paraguay als abwertender Begriff für queere Menschen verwendet. Zugleich entstand aus dieser Geschichte auch Widerstand. : Bereits Ende September 1959 erschien ein anonymer Protestbrief in derselben Zeitung, heute anerkannt als erster dokumentierter Akt queeren Widerstands im Land. Sein Jahrestag, der 30. September, wird inzwischen als Tag des queeren Gedenkens in Paraguay begangen

title: Cagnard prend fin, la lutte continue
content:
En cette rentrée, Cagnard a décidé de clôturer ses activités politiques. Dans ce texte, nous nous retrouvons à quelques-un·e·s pour tirer le bilan de l'existence du collectif et situons sa trajectoire dans la séquence politique que nous traversons. Nous exprimons là notre avis sur la tenue et fermeture de cet espace d'organisation alors que le groupe voit la fin de ses activités comme un constat qui s'impose à lui-même. Diverses lectures découlent de la situation parmi les membres restants.


Il est ainsi à noter que, pour certain·es d'entre nous, ce sont le manque d'effectifs et de motivation qui bloquent aujourd'hui le groupe.


Cette ligne identifie l'impossibilité de l'action future du groupe dans les tensions inter-personnelles qui ont pu apparaître au fil de notre activité et dans un manque de renouvellement de nos effectifs. L'accueil de nouveaux membres aurait alors pu permettre de diluer les divergences politiques, de mettre une distance entre les susceptibilités inter-personnelles ou de voir partir des camarades tout en laissant de nouvelles forces assumer les tâches organisationnelles laissées vacantes.


D'autres camarades voient poindre des problématiques liées à notre fonctionnement, notre ouverture et notre composition. C'est afin de préciser cette lecture que nous écrivons ce texte.


En premier lieu, nous détaillons les enjeux qui ont motivé la création du collectif. Puis, nous revenons sur l'actualité politique du groupe et livrons des éléments d'analyse du contexte. De nouveaux impératifs se dessinent constamment dans la lutte : notre réflexivité doit servir à ajuster nos perspectives politiques à l'aune des obstacles que nous traversons et des tâches qui émergent.


Cagnard, sa création et ses objectifs


Cagnard a été créé en mars 2025 avec pour ambition de former un groupe autonome et ouvert sur Marseille. À rebours des logiques affinitaires et de cooptation, des camarades ont souhaité initier un projet de rupture avec les institutions traditionnelles du mouvement – partis et syndicats – qui assume dans le même temps la nécessité et l'accessibilité de l'organisation politique. Dans un cadre de composition, des personnes de sensibilités politiques diverses se sont organisées sur la base de perspectives communes, à commencer par l'intensification des mouvements sociaux et leur défense face à la répression.


Nous avons œuvré à la diffusion de pratiques de défense, soutenu les inculpé·es face à la Justice et animé des ateliers de formation politique. Il est crucial de battre en brèche les dynamiques de spécialisation lorsqu'elles entravent la participation effective des camarades à l'organisation politique. L'action de rue se doit d'être massive et ne doit pas être l'apanage d'une élite éclairée. Quant à la défense juridique, elle ne doit pas être abandonnée à des spécialistes du droit. Ces deux pendants du renforcement d'un mouvement doivent se trouver aux mains du plus grand nombre de camarades.


Nous entendions défendre ces lignes, ce qui entraînait parfois de porter la rupture au sein du mouvement social, dans la rue et au sein des espaces d'organisation. Plus largement, nous cherchions à soutenir le débordement face à la répression, le dépassement des mots d'ordre défensifs, sectoriels et des cadres de lutte institués, et à exacerber les contradictions en leur sein.


La théorie n'étant qu'un moment de la pratique, la tenue d'ateliers de formation politique et culturelle devait servir à affûter nos perspectives d'intervention dans les mobilisations naissantes et celles à venir. La composition devait nourrir l'intelligence collective : loin de penser que la contradiction affaiblit le mouvement révolutionnaire, nous sommes convaincu·es qu'elle le renforce et qu'elle doit être entretenue. Au-delà du dogmatisme et du sectarisme, l'ouverture de nos espaces visait un objectif clair : défendre et construire l'autonomie politique, dans le prolongement de ce que ce champ a su porter d'anti-capitalisme, d'anti-étatisme et d'indépendance vis-à-vis des partis et organisations syndicales. Il s'agissait aussi d'accroître nos forces de lutte, de propager l'auto-organisation pour gagner en puissance collective.


Tout au long de son existence, le collectif a fait preuve d'une activité politique constante. Toutefois, ces derniers mois, ses membres ont éprouvé des contradictions dans la mise en œuvre de ces objectifs. Notre modèle politique éprouve des limites certaines.

author: Gary Chartier
title: Con il Mercato, Contro il “Capitalismo”
content:
Di

Gary Chartier

. Originale pubblicato il 25 gennaio 2013 con il titolo

Embracing Markets, Opposing “Capitalism”

. Tradotto da Enrico Sanna.


Articolo scritto da 

Gary Chartier

 e pubblicato su 

Bleeding Heart Libertarians

 il 22 marzo 2011.


Essere libertari significa opporsi all’uso della forza che impedisce uno scambio spontaneo e pacifico. Ma non significa approvare il capitalismo.


Il senso di una tale affermazione dipende da cosa si intende per “capitalismo”. Per qualcuno è semplicemente il libero scambio. In tal caso è corretto affermare che non esiste un vero e proprio contrasto tra capitalismo e libertarismo.


Ma a volte si intende qualcos’altro. L’informazione stampata e digitale, ad esempio, per “capitalismo” intende “l’attuale sistema economico”. Ma è anche relativamente diffusa l’accezione di “capitalismo” come “il potere che i capitalisti, detentori di una grossa fetta di beni capitali, hanno sul posto di lavoro e sulla società”. Secondo i principi libertari di cui parlo il capitalismo non è né l’una né l’altra cosa.


Il sistema economico attuale è,

in misura molto significativa

, un sistema che esclude lo scambio pacifico e spontaneo. Un intreccio di privilegi legali e normativi favoriscono chi è ricco e ben posizionato a spese di tutti gli altri (pensiamo ai brevetti e i copyright, ai dazi, alla limitazione dell’attività creditizia, alle licenze professionali, alle norme edilizie, eccetera). Il complesso militar-industriale assorbe quantità incredibili di denaro, è il caso di dire sotto minaccia, dalle tasche della gente per versarle nei conti bancari di società d’appalto e clientele. Sussidi di ogni genere alimentano un insieme di attività privilegiate e no profit. Inoltre lo stato riconosce la proprietà di terre prese con la violenza o con mezzi legali arbitrari e poi distribuite a singoli e gruppi di favore. Le economie di Stati Uniti, Canada, Europa occidentale e Giappone non sono a pianificazione centralizzata, lo stato non sancisce (gran parte de)i mezzi di produzione, ma dato il suo coinvolgimento a più livelli nel garantire e promuovere i privilegi economici è difficile dire che il nostro sistema economico è libero. Se questo è “capitalismo”, chi vuole la libertà ha buone ragioni per essere scettico.


I privilegi che caratterizzano l’attuale ordine economico, comunque lo si chiami, attirano soprattutto chi ha più potere di condizionamento politico e ricchezza. È una rete che finisce per rafforzare i privilegi dei capitalisti sul posto di lavoro. I privilegi limitano il lavoro autonomo (innalzando i requisiti di capitale o i costi d’ingresso e riducendo le risorse disponibili per avviare e mantenere un’attività). Restringendo le alternative al lavoro salariato e imponendo limiti all’attività sindacale, e riducendo così il potere contrattuale collettivo, lo stato finisce per rafforzare il potere dei datori di lavoro. In breve: non si comprende il potere attuale dei “capitalisti” se non si conoscono le mascalzonate dello stato. Ancora una volta: se questo è “capitalismo”, chi vuole la libertà ha buone ragioni per essere scettico.


Qualcuno potrebbe dire che, se la parola “capitalismo” indica spesso un fenomeno sociale detestabile, altrettanto spesso indica un sistema economico che pone al centro la libertà. Non so in che proporzione e con quale peso. So però che il “capitalismo” è visto negativamente da tempi immemori (“capitalista” è inteso in senso spregiativo da sostenitori entusiasti del libero mercato come

Thomas Hodgskin

 nella prima metà dell’Ottocento) e oggi è ancora così. Mi capita molto spesso, quando sento parlarne positivamente, di pensare che è una sorta di parola portmanteau (come

sottolinea opportunamente

 Roderick Long) che significa “libero scambio”, “situazione attuale”, “potere dei capitalisti” o un insieme di tutto ciò. È una parola corrotta. Quando nei paesi in via di sviluppo la gente scende in piazza e urla contro il “capitalismo”, intendendo non la vera libertà ma il dominio imperiale del governo statunitense e i suoi alleati, credo che sia importante che i libertari sappiano distinguere questo regime statale oppressivo da quello invocato da chi vuole la libertà.


Gli editorialisti del

Wall Street Journal

 o di

Faux News

 e i vari portavoce delle élite economiche e politiche possono continuare a chiamare “capitalismo” tutto quello che gli fa comodo. Non sono libertari, i quali non hanno nessuna ragione di emularli. Volere un mercato libero (o …

author: Fozzie
title: Chapter 25: The General Law of Capitalist Accumulation
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to Marx's Capital volume one, chapter 25.

Marx’s opening remarks on the “composition of capital” harken back to the analysis in Chapter 15 on relative surplus value. There we saw how efforts to offset reductions in the working day by raising productivity involved capitalists replacing troublesome workers with compliant machinery. He suggests that the introduction of more machinery per worker can be formulated as a rise in the technical composition of capital, something we can represent symbolically by MP/LP, the material configuration of means of production and labor-power.(1) Looked at from the point of view of of value invested, increased expenditure on machinery raises the value composition of capital, or c/v, a ratio of the value invested in constant capital, c, to that invested in variable capital, v. However, because the value composition can change independently of any change in the technical composition,(2) Marx calls the value composition—when changes are only due to changes in the technical composition—the organic composition of capital. To differentiate, we can represent the organic composition of capital as co/vo. So, c/v can change, even if co/vo does not; but any change in co/vo is also a change in c/v. Therefore, whenever he refers to changes in the organic composition he is talking about a change in the technical composition, but in value terms. Eventually—especially in Volume III of Capital—we find that Marx’s analysis of some tendencies to crisis are formulated in terms of the organic composition of capital.(3)

Although we can analyze these various “compositions of capital” at every level of the economy, from individual enterprises through branches of industry to the total social capital, it is “with this [last] alone that we are concerned here”.(4) In other words, the subject is the expansion of the total social capital. It is therefore vital to be clear about what Marx means by accumulation.

Had he defined accumulation merely as an expansion of the total social capital, it would be easy to confuse accumulation with economists’ concepts of “growth”, or, taking qualitative changes into account, with concepts of “economic development”. But he doesn’t leave it at that; he carefully defines accumulation in social terms as the reproduction “of the capital-relation on an expanded scale, with more capitalists, or bigger capitalists, at one pole, and more wage-laborers at the other pole.”(5) In other words, what is being accumulated are the antagonistic class relationships of capitalism. Unlike economists who recognize neither classes nor class antagonism, and think of growth in terms of production functions such as Q = f(K, L), where factors of production K (capital) and L (labor) produce output (Q) that grows as the economy expands, Marx re-emphasizes here that his interest is precisely those antagonistic relationships within which K (MP or c), L (LP in action or v) and Q (C’ and M’) are only elements or moments.

He then proceeds to discuss the dynamics of accumulation in terms of the relationships between the classes. In this first section he assumes that the composition of capital (by each definition) remains the same, so that when capitalists invest, their money buys both more means of production (MP) and more labor-power (LP). (He relaxes this assumption in the next section.) Under this assumption, capitalist investment increases the demand for labor-power and puts upward pressure on wages as capitalists compete for available workers.(6)

Marx then brings this association between investment and the demand for labor to bear on the analysis of the fluctuations in business activity. He recognizes how downturns and upturns were recurring periodically, but his real interest lay not their periodicity but how major downturns constituted crises for capitalism. That is to say, large-scale layoffs, rising unemployment and increased poverty can lead to worker-led uprisings and a crisis for capitalist control. Unlike economists who prefer the term business cycle, optimiostically presuming that downturns will always be followed by upturns, for Marx each major crisis opened the possibility of the revolutionary overthrow of capitalism.

Assuming a constant composition of capital, as he does in this section, rapid accumulation was achieved by capitalists hiring more labor, sometimes buying new machines and processing more raw materials to produce more output, whether in agriculture …

author: radical.guide
title: Mutual aid is core infrastructure
content:
Mutual aid is a core infrastructure of resilient communities when systems fail, in disaster and crisis, and in normal times. It provides assistance and builds relationships, trust, collective capacity, and solidarity, before and after the crisis. Resilience takes infrastructure and equipment, and it takes people organizing and taking care of one another.


From the "Mutual Aid Disaster Relief Search and Rescue" workshop at the 2026 International Workshops.


A Radical Guide is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that builds movement infrastructure, including a global directory of radical spaces, mutual aid programs, and educational resources for people doing liberation work around the world.

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Örtüşen Ordular
content:
Yazan: Benjamin Tucker


Çeviren: Gorthim


Çevirilen Asıl Metin


PDF Linki


Son zamanlarda “Twentieth Century” dergisi tanımlama konusunda epey çaba sarf ediyor. Oysa tanımlama çok titiz bir iştir ve bana öyle geliyor ki, “Twentieth Century” dergisinin yazı işleri bürosunda bu iş her zaman gereken özenle yapılmıyor.


Örneğin şuna bir bakın: Bir sosyalist, “her sektörün, ilgili tüm tarafların karşılıklı yararı için, devletin cebir kullanması yoluyla koordine edilmesi gerektiğine inanan kişidir.”


Ünlü yazarların, yukarıdakinden esasen hiçbir farkı olmayan sosyalizm tanımları ortaya koydukları doğrudur — bunlardan biri de General Walker’dır. Ancak bu köşelerde, General Walker’ın hem sosyalizm hem de anarşizm hakkında konuşurken tamamen yolunu kaybetmiş olduğu ayrıntılı bir şekilde kanıtlanmıştır. Aslında bu tanım temelden hatalıdır ve yalnızca devlet sosyalizmini doğru bir şekilde tanımlamaktadır.


Başka bir alanda buna benzer bir tanım şöyle olabilir: Din, İsa’nın Mesih olduğuna dair inançtır. Bunun Hristiyan dininin doğru bir tanımı olduğunu varsaysak bile, dinin kendisi için bir tanım olarak açıkça yanlıştır. Hristiyanlığın bu bölgede diğer tüm din biçimlerini gölgede bırakmış olması, ona dini fikrin tekelini elinde tutma hakkı vermez. Benzer şekilde, son on ya da yirmi yıl içinde devlet sosyalizminin diğer sosyalizm biçimlerini gölgede bırakmış olması da ona sosyalist fikrin tekelini elinde tutma hakkı vermez.


Sosyalizm, kendi başına ne özgürlük ne de otorite anlamına gelir. Kelimenin kendisi, uyumlu bir ilişkiden başka bir şey ifade etmez. Aslında, o kadar geniş bir terimdir ki, tanımlanması zordur. Bu konuda kesinlikle özel bir otoriteye ya da yetkinliğe sahip olduğumu iddia etmiyorum. Sadece şunu savunuyorum: Sosyalizm kelimesi, yıllardır genel kullanım ve mutabakatla çeşitli düşünce ve görüş okullarına genel bir terim olarak uygulandığı için, onu tanımlamaya çalışanlar tüm bu okulların ortak unsurunu aramak ve onu bununla özdeşleştirmek zorundadırlar; bu kelimeyi herhangi bir okulun kendine özgü doğasını temsil edecek şekilde kullanmaya hakları yoktur. “Twentieth Century” dergisinin tanımı bu sınamayı hiçbir şekilde geçemez.


Belki de bunu karşılayan bir tanım şudur: Sosyalizm, ilerlemenin esas olarak insanın çevresine etki etmesinden ziyade, çevrenin insan üzerinde etki etmesiyle sağlanacağına dair inançtır.


Bunun çok genel olduğu gerekçesiyle eleştirileceğini tahmin ediyorum ve bu eleştiriyi kabul etmeye meyilliyim. Bu tanım, açıkça “sosyalist” olarak adlandırılmaya hak kazanan herkesi kapsıyor, ancak muhtemelen böyle bir unvanı olmayan herkesi dışlamıyor.


Tanımı biraz daraltalım: Sosyalizm, ilerlemenin bir sonraki önemli adımının, servet sahiplerinin haraç almaya zorlayacak antisosyal bir güç elde etmelerini sağlayan her türlü ayrıcalığın ortadan kaldırılmasını da içerecek şekilde, insanın çevresinde ekonomik nitelikte bir değişim olması gerektiği inancıdır.


Bu tanımın daha da iyileştirilebileceğinden hiç şüphem yok ve bu yöndeki öneriler ilgi çekici olacaktır; ancak bu, en azından mevcut tefecilik temelli ekonomik sisteme karşı her türlü protesto biçimini kapsama yönünde bir girişimdir. Kendimi her zaman büyük Sosyalist hareketin bir üyesi olarak görmüşümdür ve sırf Karl Marx’ın takipçisi olmadığım için General Walker, Bay Pentecost ya da başka herhangi biri tarafından bu hareketin dışında bırakılmaya ya da tanımlanmaya itiraz ediyorum.


Şimdi, “Twentieth Century” dergisinin bir başka tanımını ele alalım: Anarşizmin tanımı. Bu tanımın yer aldığı makalenin sayısını bilmiyorum ve tam olarak alıntı yapamıyorum. Ancak bu tanım, işbirliğine olan inancı kesinlikle anarşizmin temel bir unsuru olarak gösteriyordu. Bu, sosyalizmin tanımı kadar hatalıdır. İşbirliği, anarşizmin temel bir unsuru değildir; tıpkı cebirin sosyalizmin temel bir unsuru olmadığı gibi. Anarşistlerin çoğunluğunun işbirliğine inanması, onları anarşist yapan şey değildir; tıpkı sosyalistlerin çoğunluğunun cebre inanmasının onları sosyalist yapan şey olmaması gibi. Sosyalizm ne özgürlüğün yanındadır ne de karşısındadır; anarşizm özgürlüğün yanındadır ve başka hiçbir şeyin ne yanındadır ne de karşısındadır. Anarşi, işbirliğinin anasıdır — evet, tıpkı özgürlüğün düzenin anası olması gibi; ancak tanım olarak özgürlük düzen değildir, anarşizm de işbirliği değildir.


Anarşizmi, eşit özgürlük ilkesiyle bağdaşan en yüksek düzeyde özgürlüğe olan inanç olarak tanımlıyorum; ya da başka bir deyişle, başkalarına saldırma özgürlüğü hariç her …

author: Unknown
title: Проект «Инициатива наказуема» объявляет набор на курс по анархизму
content:
Обучение в Петербурге предполагает обзор либертарных идей. Слушатели составят общее представление о направлениях анархизма — от древних времен к Прудону, Кропоткину и современным теоретикам. Предполагается рассказать, какие бывают организации анархистов, в чем преимущества и недостатки разных моделей, какие есть механизмы принятия решений. Консенсусу отведен отдельный практикум.

Предусмотрены занятия, представляющие из себя нечто вроде деловых игр или маленьких стратегических сессий, где будут планироваться действия в перспективе одного или нескольких лет. Пойдет разговор о том, как могут быть применены идеи (в основном, Кропоткина и Букчина) в соответствии с реалиями нашего времени и географического положения.

Кроме этого, есть слоты для свободных тем по запросу обучающихся. Подробности и запись — здесь.

author: Trojka
title: Nasze ulice, Wasze granice – Relacja Toruńskiej Grupy Anarchistycznej
content:
To może tylko nasze wrażenie. Jednak wierzymy, że nie urodziłyśmy się po to, żeby zagrać w „życie”, bo wiemy, że ta plansza nie powinna tak wyglądać. I nie będziemy pionkami. Ani systemu, ani politycznych szachrajek. Nie będziemy narzędziem w cudzej manipulacji.


Wczoraj szłyśmy i szliśmy wszystkie i wszyscy właśnie z tą myślą.


Było po toruńsku. Z lekką obsuwą. Ale jak mawiają nasi lokalni bardowie: „Wy macie zegarki, ale my mamy czas”.


Początek był mocny. Huraganowy. I, niestety, dość przewidywalny. Bo przecież wiemy, jak często w takich sytuacjach działa policja. Nasze demo było legalnie zgłoszone, a mimo to prawo do spokojnego przejścia po mieście najwyraźniej komuś przeszkadzało.


Prawicowa kontrmanifestacja jeszcze przed rozpoczęciem naszego wydarzenia ustawiła się z nazistowskim banerem i zaczęła wykrzykiwać swoje hasła. Akustycznie było nawet ciekawie — kilkanaście głosów w trakcie mutacji tworzyło coś na kształt bardzo osobliwego chóru słowików. Tyle że zgodnie z ustalonymi prawnie zasadami kontrmanifestujący powinni znajdować się co najmniej 100 metrów od nas.


Nie znaleźliśmy szczególnego powodu, żeby udawać, że tego nie widzimy. Zbieraninę cherlawych weszpolaczków przed utratą baneru uratowała policja. Po odbiciu naszych przyjaciół z rąk policji wyruszyliśmy w drogę.


Ważną drogę. Przez Bydgoskie Przedmieście.


To najbardziej zaludniona dzielnica miasta, określana jako zdegradowana. Miejsce, którego mieszkańcy mierzą się z wykluczeniem wynikającym z sytuacji ekonomicznej, problemów uzależnieniowych i systemowej opresji.


Szłyśmy i szliśmy wolno. Te drugie dema chodzą szybko. Po żołniersku.


My szliśmy inaczej. Z hasłami anarchistycznymi. O pomocy wzajemnej, szacunku, równości. O tym, że razem można próbować wyjść z obłędu, który systemowo oczekuje od nas nienawiści jako dowodu wspólnoty kulturowej.


W marszu rytm wystukiwała nam niezawodna samba. Rytmy oporu rozbrzmiewały nadając rytm naszym krokom.


Był też soundsystemowy rower prowadzony przez wybitną, specjalistyczną ekipę, która serwowała RAP. Prawdziwy – antyfaszystowski, antyrasistowski. Bo taki jest rap z założenia.


Mówiłyśmy i mówiliśmy o mechanizmach ludobójstw, o kapitalistycznej opresji, o przemocy władzy i systemu. Dawałyśmy głos osobom, które doświadczyły rasizmu i ksenofobii. Apelowałyśmy o wyobraźnię.


Bo bez wyobraźni bardzo łatwo jest zaakceptować świat, w którym cudze cierpienie staje się czymś odległym. Statystyką. Nagłówkiem. Problemem „kogoś innego”. A przecież każda przemoc zaczyna się od odebrania komuś człowieczeństwa.


Po drodze zatrzymałyśmy się również przed byłym domem Nestora Machno. Nie zabawił u nas długo – musiał uciekać. Pozostali za to jego towarzysze, zmarli na emigracji, których mogiły stoją na cmentarzu przy ulicy Grudziądzkiej. Cmentarzu obok którego przechodziła nasza demonstracja.


W pewnym momencie okazało się, że policja nie zamierza pozwolić nam dojść do zaplanowanego punktu zakończenia demonstracji. Trasa została więc zmieniona.


I wiecie co?


Wyszło nam to na plus.


Żałujemy tylko, że wcześniej tego nie rozkminiłyśmy.


Nowa trasa prowadziła obok dwóch dworców. Widzieliśmy ludzi w drodze. Ludzi z bagażami, plecakami, torbami. Ludzi zmierzających gdzieś — pewnie do „nieopodal”, może dalej, może tylko na kilka przystanków.


Ale każda osoba, która choć raz taszczyła bagaż przez dworzec, rozumie, czym jest trud drogi.


A czym jest droga bez konkretnego celu?


Drogą w niewiadomą?


O tym też mówiłyśmy.


O ludziach, którzy są w drodze nie dlatego, że wybrali przygodę, ale dlatego, że zostali do tej drogi zmuszeni. O przekraczaniu granic. O tym, że granice są tworzone przez ludzi i przez ludzi mogą zostać przekroczone.


Nasze ulice.


Wasze granice.


Zakończyłyśmy demonstrację na dworcu Toruń Miasto. Zgromadzenie zostało nienachalnie zamknięte, a my skierowałyśmy się na słuchanie antyfaszystowskiego rapu.


Oczywiście policja zdążyła jeszcze coś pomylić, jak zwykle. Tym razem pomylili człowieka z kimś innym. Padła wersja, że miał zrywać flagi kontrmanifestacji — tej, której w ogóle nie powinno być tak blisko nas.


Tyle że to nawet nie był on. Ale my znamy ten rodzaj przemocy – znamy policyjne prowokacje. Znamy tę specyficzną mieszankę rozluźnienia politycznego i etycznego, która pozwala pomylić człowieka, wydarzenie, odpowiedzialność i fakty, a potem zachowywać się tak, jakby nic się nie stało.


Ponownie udało nam się zabrać z rąk pałkarzy potencjalną ofiarę całej sytuacji. Ponownie się …

author: Unknown
title: Gary Dean Jaworski - Pitirim A. Sorokin’s Sociological Anarchism
content:
Author

: Gary Dean Jaworski

Title

: Pitirim A. Sorokin’s Sociological Anarchism

Date

: 1993

Notes

: Paper presented at the 62

nd

 Annual Meeting of the Eastern Sociological Society, Arlington, Virginia, April 1992. The author gratefully acknowledges the advice of Robert K. Merton, Lewis A. Coser and two anonymous reviewers for this journal.

Source

:

journals.sagepub.com

.

History of the Human Sciences

, 1993, Vol. 6 No. 3 © 1993 SAGE (London, Newbury Park and New Delhi) pp. 61–77.

doi: 095269519300600304


Introduction


 Pitirim A. Sorokin (1889–1968) was a Russian emigre, an internationally renowned sociologist, the first chairman of the Department of Sociology at Harvard University, a president of the American Sociological Association, among many other honors, and a gadfly to the discipline of sociology (Sorokin, 1950a, 1963a, 1963b). Robin M. Williams, Jr (1980 : 103), a former student of Sorokin’s at Harvard, called his teacher a sui generis thinker and a man who thinks otherwise. He was a thinker who, as Nietzsche might have said, was ‘out of season’ with the discipline with which he identified.


 Sorokin was a lone scholar during the ascendancy of team research (cf. Merton, 1959), a pessimist during a period of postwar optimism, an antipositivist during the reign of positivism, an internationalist during the rise of American sociological hegemony, an advocate of cyclical theories of change while the contrasting view of liberal progressivism prevailed, and a grand theorist during a period of skepticism and hostility toward such theories.


 But times change. At present, when there is a renewed appreciation for grand theory (e.g. Skinner, 1985), when there is a return to cyclical theories of change (e.g. Kennedy, 1987), when there is a renewed interest in altruism (Piliavin and Chamg, 1990), and when, with the evident conclusion of the cold war and collapse of state communism, there is a revived interest in global harmony (see Goldfarb, 1989), the time is ripe for a re-examination of Sorokin’s work. The challenge of this undertaking has been accepted by scholars both here and abroad. Not only is a Russian scholar writing Sorokin’s comprehensive intellectual biography,

[1]

 but in the United States Barry Johnston (1986, 1987, 1991) continues his efforts to elucidate Sorokin’s life and work.


 The present essay contributes in a modest way to this re-examination. It does not provide an analysis of Sorokin’s work in its entirety, which, given the extensiveness of his output, would be a monumental task (e.g. Cowell, 1952). Rather, the present study investigates an important but neglected strain in Sorokin’s oeuvre, the anarchistic dimension of his work. With few exceptions, such as Tiryakian’s (1968) encyclopedia article on Sorokin, most studies fail to mention Sorokin’s links to the anarchist tradition. Yet, my recent survey of Sorokin’s published writings and unpublished correspondence demonstrates the centrality of this tradition to his works.

[2]

 A re-examination of his writings along these lines is long overdue.


 In what follows I first establish the pertinence of this line of thought to an understanding of Sorokin’s work and, second, explore the ethical project of Sorokin’s writings and reveal its roots in ethical anarchism. In the conclusion, I draw implications for future Sorokin studies and for contemporary theorizing.


Sorokin as ‘Conservative, Christian Anarchist’


 Pitirim Alexandrovich Sorokin was born in a rural village in the north of Russia in 1889. The beauty of the terrain, its pristine rivers and lakes, vast forests and flowery meadows, provided an aesthetic counterpoint to the simple but harsh conditions of life. Sorokin’s mother died when he was about 3 years old, and his father, an itinerant artisan, and a loving man when he was sober, became depressed and violent during his occasional alcoholic binges. Leaving home to escape their father’s domination and wrath, Pitirim Alexandrovich and his older brother moved from village to village while earning their living in their father’s trade, as gilders of religious icons and other cult objects (Sorokin, 1963b: 4–7).


 Sorokin’s background in the village communities of northern Russia at the turn of the century provided fertile ground for developing sensibilities favorable to the anarchist tradition in at least two respects. First, the Russian anarchist literature, such as the writings of Peter Kropotkin, was consistent …

author: Redazione_web
title: Milano viale Monza. 50 anni di vita della sede
content:
Domenica 27 settembre ci siamo ritrovati in sede per ricordare i suoi primi 50 anni di vita.


Numerose le presenze, significativa la mostra di locandine e foto d’epoca, nutrito il programma. Dopo un intervento introduttivo che ha illustrato il senso della giornata – non un retorico ricordo del passato, ma uno sprone a guardare avanti e a misurarsi con gli ostacoli e le problematiche del presente – sono intervenuti Federica Ermacora, Lorenzo Pezzica e Alberto ‘Abo’ Di Monte.


Federica Ermacora ha presentato, insieme a Selva Varengo, il suo ultimo lavoro,

Contro-immaginari. Municipalismo libertario e femminismo comunitario

, edito da Quaderni di Paola, incentrato sul superamento dello Stato/nazione e sulle possibili alternative fondate sull’autogestione e sulla partecipazione attiva. Un intervento sostanzioso che ha preso in esame il comunalismo, il municipalismo libertario e l’esperienza della Comunità di comunità che tesse i territori in reti orizzontali e femministe suggerendo proposte concrete per scardinare le logiche di dominio e ripensare la giustizia sociale ed ecologica.


Dopo una breve pausa ha preso la parola Lorenzo Pezzica che ha parlato di un fatto che non è avvenuto, ma che avrebbe dovuto tenersi: le Olimpiadi Popolari di Barcellona del 19 luglio del 1936. Un evento poco conosciuto, sul quale esistono ancora pochi studi, organizzato in alternativa alle Olimpiadi di Berlino, vetrina del nazismo, e che vide l’arrivo nella città catalana di migliaia di atleti da tutto il mondo. Gli stessi atleti che, proprio il giorno dell’inaugurazione dei giochi, furono sorpresi dal golpe militare e dall’insurrezione popolare. Molti di loro scesero nelle strade al fianco del proletariato in armi, imbracciarono i fucili sulle barricate e alcuni entrarono nella Colonna Durruti. Un’occasione interessante di riflessione, quella sviluppata da Pezzica, anche sul ruolo degli storici nello studiare e nel tramandare gli avvenimenti.


Ha concluso gli interventi Alberto ‘Abo’ Di Monte che, con un ampio intervento, ha illustrato il lascito dell’Olimpiade

Impopolare

 di Milano sia dal punto di vista economico, sia da quello ecologico e sociale, ricordando anche i morti sul lavoro nei cantieri. Sebbene manchino ancora dati certi, quello che appare evidente è l’incremento indefinito dei costi, che vanno a gravare sul pubblico, e l’incertezza sulla conclusione di opere ancora in fase di progettazione; il tutto in un quadro di gestione del territorio milanese che ha mostrato tutta la sua valenza speculativa, a scapito delle infrastrutture sociali (chiusura di spazi, liquidazione di occupazioni storiche, chiusura di molte librerie indipendenti, ecc.).


Dopo la squisita cena, organizzata da Antonio, e le due torte preparate da Rosaria – una per il 50° della sede e l’altra per il compleanno di Alessio – ha preso il via il concerto di Alessio Lega. Partendo dai canti dei Moti di Lunigiana, Alessio ha percorso il lungo filo dell’emigrazione italiana fino all’America degli IWW (Industrial Workers of the World) e ai canti di Joe Hill: un concerto che, nello stile di Alessio, fatto di parole, musica e canzoni, ci ha accompagnato lungo una storia ricca di lotte, sofferenze, vittorie e sconfitte, sempre con il pugno alzato e mai in ginocchio. Una bellissima conclusione per una giornata ricca di presenze, di stimoli, di suggestioni e, soprattutto, di relazioni.


——————————————


Descrivere cos’è la sede della Federazione Anarchica Milanese e dell’Ateneo Libertario in viale Monza 255 significa, in qualche modo, parlare di una parte sostanziosa dell’anarchismo milanese dell’ultimo mezzo secolo.


Per farla breve – ma non tanto – la vita della nostra sede, e quindi della nostra attività attuale (e, si spera, futura) prende respiro da quel gruppo che affonda le proprie radici nei primi anni Settanta, con la costituzione di “Lotta Anarchica”, aderente alla Federazione Anarchica Italiana. Era il 1971 e il collettivo era inizialmente composto da compagne e compagni provenienti dal Gruppo Libertario del Politecnico e dal Movimento Anarcocomunista di Lambrate, che si ritrovavano inizialmente nella mitica Aula F della facoltà di Architettura. Costituito il gruppo, la sua sede divenne prima il Circolo Pinelli di Via Scaldasole, poi uno scantinato in via Mamiani a Crescenzago. author: heinhtetkyaw
title: An Anarchist Perspective on Israel, Palestine, and the Endless Cycle of Violence
content:
From October 7 to the Present: States at War with Human Beings The Israeli–Palestinian conflict cannot be said to have begun on October 7, 2023, just as it cannot simply be reduced to a war between “two nations.”

The roots of this catastrophe go back decades: to the end of the British Mandate, the 1948 war, the establishment of the State of Israel, the displacement and expulsion of more than 700,000 Palestinians, and the emergence of what Palestinians call the Nakba — the catastrophe. Following the 1967 war, the occupation of the West Bank, East Jerusalem, and Gaza, the expansion of Israeli settlements, and extensive restrictions on Palestinians’ lives and freedom of movement further entrenched structures of inequality and domination. Today, nearly 5.9 million Palestinian refugees are eligible for services provided by UNRWA.From an anarchist perspective, the question is not simply: “Which state has the right to govern which territory?” The more fundamental question is: Why should human beings have to submit to states, armies, borders, and military institutions in order to live, enjoy freedom, and secure their safety? October 7: A Crime That Cannot Be Justified On October 7, 2023, Hamas forces and several other Palestinian armed groups attacked southern Israel. Approximately 1,200 people were killed, and 251 were abducted and taken to Gaza. Civilians were among those targeted in the assault. According to the findings of the United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry, hostage-taking, murder, torture, and other acts against civilians constituted war crimes. From an anarchist standpoint, no occupation, repression, or historical injustice can justify the deliberate killing of civilians or the taking of hostages. But this principle must be applied consistently, without exception. If killing an Israeli child is a crime, killing a Palestinian child is equally a crime. If taking an Israeli civilian hostage is a crime, depriving an entire civilian population of water, food, medicine, and security cannot be justified as a “right to self-defence” either. From “Revenge” to Collective Punishment Following October 7, the Israeli government launched a large-scale war in Gaza. The scale of killing, destruction, displacement, and deprivation of basic necessities went far beyond a limited military operation against armed groups.In 2024, the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry reported that Israeli operations in Gaza involved war crimes and crimes against humanity, including murder, extermination, forcible transfer, torture, and the use of starvation as a method of warfare. The same Commission also identified Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups as responsible for war crimes committed during the October 7 attack. In September 2025, the same Commission went a step further, concluding that, based on its investigation, Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. This is a finding by a UN Commission of Inquiry; it is not the same as a final ruling by the International Court of Justice in the genocide case, and the two should not be conflated. South Africa's case against Israel remains before the International Court of Justice. In November 2024, the International Criminal Court also issued arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and Yoav Gallant on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity. These decisions, however, do not constitute final convictions; they are part of an ongoing international judicial process. An Anarchist Is Neither a Supporter of the Israeli State nor of a Palestinian State This is where the difference between an anarchist perspective and many prevailing narratives becomes clear. Anarchism fundamentally opposes turning human beings into soldiers serving a state. From this perspective:

The State of Israel, even if it regards the protection of its citizens as its responsibility, has no right to pursue security through mass killing and military domination over another people.

Hamas, even if it describes itself as a resistance movement, has no right to kill civilians or take hostages in the name of the Palestinian people. No state, army, or armed organization owns human lives.

“National security” cannot be used to justify depriving millions of people of their freedom and dignity.

The suffering of one community must never become an excuse for repressing another.

Victims must not be turned into soldiers serving state ideologies.From this perspective, the binary choice between …

author: Alfredo Seguel
title: Masiva marcha anticolonial de PPOO en Chile denuncia genocidio, militarización y más de 100 presos políticos mapuche
content:
Una multitudinaria marcha anticolonial se realizó este 12 de octubre en el cerro Welén, Santiago, convocada por la resistencia mapuche urbana y organizaciones sociales. Denunciaron el genocidio europeo, la militarización del Wallmapu, la persecución judicial y los más de 100 presos políticos mapuche en el presente. También en otras localidades se realizaron manifestaciones con alta asistencia.


A 534 años de la invasión europea: pueblos originarios y organizaciones sociales desbordan el centro de Santiago en la marcha del 12 de octubre


Una masiva y concurrida marcha anticolonial se realizó este lunes 12 de octubre a las 10:00 horas en el cerro Huelén (Santa Lucía), en Santiago, convocada por diversas organizaciones de pueblos originarios y agrupaciones sociales chilenas. La concentración, que reunió a cientos de personas, tuvo como fin “expresar las fuerzas de la resistencia y autonomía” en una fecha que, según señaló la convocatoria, “evoca la brutalidad, saqueo y genocidio europeo sobre la población preexistente del Abya Yala”. El llamado fue efectuado por la resistencia mapuche urbana en Santiago, en momentos en que desde el Wallmapu se convoca a manifestarse de manera unitaria por las diversas comunidades al sur del río Biobío.


La jornada, que se desarrolló con alta participación y diversos actos culturales, tuvo un fuerte componente de denuncia. Los organizadores señalaron que “son más de 100 los prisioneros políticos mapuche”, mientras se encuentran procesados los comuneros de los emblemáticos casos Lautaro y Grollmus, “entre cuyos aspectos en común comparten la utilización fraudulenta de testigos protegidos en su contra por parte de las fiscalías”. Según los convocantes, “el Ministerio Público chileno, sin pruebas concretas ni evidencias contundentes, pretende encarcelar por más de mil años a los comuneros involucrados a discreción en las causas mencionadas, con el fin de castigar de forma racista y ejemplar, a jóvenes comprometidos con la recuperación de tierras, con los derechos de su gente y con la cosmovisión mapuche”.


La marcha también abordó el contexto de militarización del territorio ancestral. Los convocantes recordaron que “desde el gobierno chileno anterior las zonas de resistencia indígena están bajo el estado de excepción, la militarización del territorio originario y la doctrina de seguridad interior del Estado”. Sin embargo, advirtieron que “el daño en todos los planos contra niños y ancianos para beneficio de las industrias extractivistas y el latifundio colonial, sólo ha multiplicado las voluntades de lucha mapuche y unido sus fuerzas”.


La convocatoria, que se extendió durante toda la mañana y parte de la tarde, incluyó cantos, danzas y diversas intervenciones, reafirmando la demanda de autonomía y recuperación de tierras. La movilización se replicó en distintos puntos del país y en el extranjero, en una jornada que los pueblos originarios conmemoran como un día de resistencia.

author: ROAPE
title: Fanon’s continuing presence and revolutionary Sudan
content:
Each generation must out of relative obscurity discover its mission, fulfil it, or betray it.


– Frantz Fanon,

The Wretched of the Earth

, 1968


I do not come with timeless truths … Every human problem must be considered from the standpoint of time.


– Frantz Fanon,

Black Skin, White Masks

, 2008


 


Introduction


Fanon was very aware of his time. And yet one hundred years after his birth, he remains strangely present, as if we are repeating the same history, the long durée of the unfinished anticolonial revolutions (see Gibson 2021). Published in 1961, Fanon’s last book,

The Wretched of the Earth

, is a product of his experience and reflections on Africa’s anticolonial struggle, including its first crisis in the Congo in 1961. Written as an intervention and addressing the readers as comrades, Fanon introduces the colonised challenge to the colonial world not as a rational confrontation of points of view, ‘but the untidy affirmation of an original idea propounded as an absolute’ (Fanon 1968, 41). Aware that colonialism carved up the continent into colonial fiefdoms, Fanon recognised that while the social struggle takes on a national form, it would inevitably degenerate into the regional, ethnic and racial lines often promulgated by colonial rule

if

 it did not put into practice a ‘minimum humanist’ programme (Fanon 1968, 163).


Challenging the imperial countries who speak of humanism but kill human beings wherever they find them, Fanon ends the book returning to the question of rehumanising the world, ‘For Europe, for ourselves, and for humanity, comrades, we must turn over a new leaf, we must work out new concepts, and try to set afoot a new [hu]man’ (Fanon 1968, 316). This was his idea of African liberation. Yet, on the hundredth anniversary of Fanon’s birth, not only has Africa become proportionately poorer and more unequal over the past 30 years but the post-independence ‘wa-Benz’, the newly embourgeoisified African ruling elites or simply ‘new whites’ (Nzongola-Ntalaja 2012, 40) – the ‘little greedy caste … with the mind of a huckster, only too glad to accept the dividends that the former colonial power hands out to it’ (Fanon 1968, 175) – keep reappearing.


While often dismissed as an advocate of violence rather than a thinker of African liberation, what is often elided in discussions of Fanon’s thought is the connection between the necessity of violence against settler colonies and Fanon’s criticisms of the military and the need for demilitarisation. This article focuses on what an engagement with Fanon’s thought could offer Sudanese revolutionaries. Understanding such an engagement dialectically, Fanon emphasised the importance of subjectivity in the ‘situation’ (and what Fanon also called the ‘lie of the situation’ (see Fanon 2018, 525)), which takes on a specific perspective because the Sudanese revolution involved millions of people in a non-violent revolution against military rule. It is this movement for life and liberation that must not be forgotten in the face of the reality of a counter-revolutionary military civil war that has led to daily human catastrophe for the Sudanese people.


While the Sudanese revolution began as a rejection of military rule, regional and world powers, including the United Nations (UN), have played a significant role in supporting the so-called civilian partnership of the Transitional Military Council, established in 2019, and have continued to support the armed forces following the 2021 military coup. The repeated failure of ‘international diplomacy’, notes Muzan Alneel (2023a), ‘is mainly due to the counter-revolutionary doctrine that animates its participants’.

1


The first section of this article discusses Fanon’s idea of demilitarisation and decolonisation. The second section, on the Sudanese revolution, discusses the importance, and legacies, of the resistance committees, while the final section returns to Fanon’s idea of revolutionary humanism in the praxis of anticolonial organisations.


National military or African solidarity through a corps of volunteers?


Fanon’s idea of an African legion was proposed in his speech delivered in December 1958 at the First All-African People’s Conference in Accra, Ghana. In an article in the Algerian National Liberation Front’s

El Moudjahid

author: infolibre
title: Συγκεντρώσεις αλληλεγγύης στον παλαιστινιακό λαό, την Τετάρτη 7/10
content:
Την Τρίτη 7/10 συμπληρώνονται τρία χρόνια απο την έναρξη της αιματηρής γενοκτονίας του παλαιστινιακού λαού από το κράτος – δολοφόνο Ισραήλ και τη συμμαχία του με τις  ΗΠΑ και το ΝΑΤΟ. Πάνω απο 75.000 νεκρούς παλαιστίνιους των οποίων το 1/3 αποτελούν παιδιά μετράει η γενοκτονία η οποία 3 χρόνια μετά βρίσκεται ακόμα σε εξέλιξη και το Ισραήλ και οι ΗΠΑ συνεχίζουν την προσπάθεια καθολικής επίθεσης στις χώρες της Μέσης Ανατολής. Την ίδια μέρα, σωματεία, οργανώσεις και συλλογικότητες καλούν σε συγκεντρώσεις αλληλεγγύης στον παλαιστινιακό λαό, σε διάφορα σημεία της χώρας, διαδηλώνοντας ενάντια στην γενοκτονία και κατοχή της Γάζας από το κράτος – δολοφόνο Ισραήλ αλλά και στη πιστή συμμετοχή του ελληνικού κράτους σε αυτήν.


Καλέσματα:


Αθήνα, στις 18.00, στο Πάρκο Ελευθερίας


Θεσσαλονίκη, στις 19.00, στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


Καρδίτσα, στις 19.00, στη κεντρική πλατεία


Ηράκλειο, στις 19.00, στη πλατέια Λιονταριών


Αθήνα:


Πρωτοβουλία Αλληλεγγύης στον Παλαιστινιακό Λαό Εργατικών Σωματείων και Συλλογικοτήτων –

Ένωση Παλαιστινίων Εργαζομένων Ελλάδας


Τρία χρόνια από την εισβολή στη Γάζα – Καμία συνενοχή | 7/10, 6μμ, πάρκο Ελευθερίας


Καμία σιωπή. Αλληλεγγύη στον Παλαιστινιακό λαό


Όλοι/όλες στη συγκέντρωση την Τετάρτη 7 Οκτώβρη 2026, ώρα 6μμ., στο πάρκο Ελευθερίας και στην πορεία προς τις Πρεσβείες ΗΠΑ και Ισραήλ


Η

Πρωτοβουλία Αλληλεγγύης στον Παλαιστινιακό Λαό Εργατικών Σωματείων και Συλλογικοτήτων

 καλεί τους εργαζόμενους, τους συνταξιούχους, τη νεολαία και τα συνδικάτα σε μαζική κινητοποίηση την Τετάρτη 7 Οκτώβρη 2026, με αφορμή τη συμπλήρωση τριών χρόνων από την έναρξη της εισβολής στη Γάζα του κράτους-δολοφόνου του Ισραήλ. Διαδηλώνουμε για να απαιτήσουμε τον άμεσο τερματισμό της γενοκτονίας του παλαιστινιακού λαού, το τέλος της κατοχής και την πλήρη απεμπλοκή της Ελλάδας από το σφαγείο στη Μέση Ανατολή.


Τρία χρόνια μετά την 7η Οκτώβρη 2023, ο Παλαιστινιακός λαός βρίσκεται αντιμέτωπος με μια άνευ προηγουμένου συστηματική προσπάθεια εξόντωσης και εθνοκάθαρσης. Τα επίσημα στοιχεία του Γραφείου Συντονισμού Ανθρωπιστικών Υποθέσεων του ΟΗΕ (OCHA) αποτυπώνουν το μέγεθος της φρίκης: πάνω από

74.900 νεκροί

 Παλαιστίνιοι -στη συντριπτική τους πλειονότητα γυναίκες και παιδιά- και περισσότεροι από

174.000 τραυματίες

, ενώ χιλιάδες παραμένουν θαμμένοι κάτω από τα συντρίμμια.


Στη

Γάζα

, το κράτος του Ισραήλ έχει ισοπεδώσει σχεδόν το σύνολο των ζωτικών υποδομών: νοσοκομεία, σχολεία, δίκτυα ηλεκτροδότησης, σταθμοί αφαλάτωσης και αντλιοστάσια νερού έχουν καταστραφεί ολοσχερώς. Ο πληθυσμός στερείται ακόμη και το πιο βασικό ανθρώπινο δικαίωμα, την πρόσβαση σε πόσιμο νερό και τροφή, αντιμετωπίζοντας έναν τεχνητά επιβεβλημένο λιμό και την εξάπλωση επιδημιών.


Την ίδια στιγμή, το σιωνιστικό κράτος κλιμακώνει τον πόλεμο και στην κατεχόμενη

Δυτική Όχθη

. Με πάνω από 1.000 νεκρούς, καθημερινές πολύνεκρες στρατιωτικές επιδρομές σε καταυλισμούς προσφύγων (Τζενίν, Τουλκάρμ), αθρόες κατεδαφίσεις σπιτιών, βίαιους εκτοπισμούς ολόκληρων κοινοτήτων και πάνω από 1.600 καταγεγραμμένες επιθέσεις φασιστών εποίκων με την κάλυψη του ισραηλινού στρατού, επιχειρείται η de facto προσάρτηση των παλαιστινιακών εδαφών.


Αυτό το διαρκές έγκλημα δεν θα μπορούσε να συντελεστεί χωρίς την ενεργή στήριξη, χρηματοδότηση και τον εξοπλισμό του Ισραήλ από τους ιμπεριαλιστές. Οι

ΗΠΑ

, το

ΝΑΤΟ

 και η

Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση

 δεν κάνουν απλώς «πλάτες» στο κράτος- δολοφόνο, αλλά αποτελούν συνενόχους πρώτης γραμμής.


Με αμύθητα πακέτα στρατιωτικής βοήθειας, διαρκή αποστολή οπλικών συστημάτων και διπλωματική ασυλία, η Ουάσιγκτον και οι Βρυξέλλες νομιμοποιούν την εθνοκάθαρση στο όνομα της δήθεν «αυτοάμυνας» του Ισραήλ, εξυπηρετώντας τα δικά τους γεωστρατηγικά και οικονομικά συμφέροντα στη Μέση Ανατολή.


Η γενοκτονία του Παλαιστινιακού λαού έχει και τη σφραγίδα όπως έχει και τη σφραγίδα της

Ελληνικής Κυβέρνησης

, που προχωρά σε περαιτέρω εμβάθυνση της στρατιωτικής συνεργασίας με το κράτος-δολοφόνο του Ισραήλ, επιβεβαιώνοντας το ρόλο της ως τοπικού τοποτηρητή των αμερικανονατοϊκών σχεδιασμών. Στα τέλη του Αυγούστου, μάλιστα, η

κυβέρνηση Μητσοτάκη

 υπέγραψε στο Τελ Αβίβ την απαράδεκτη διακρατική συμφωνία για την «

Ασπίδα του Αχιλλέα

», με προϋπολογισμό άνω των

3 δισ.

 ευρώ (που σε βάθος χρόνου αναμένεται να φτάσουν τα

5 δισ.

 ευρώ), με τη γιγαντιαία συμμετοχή ισραηλινών αμυντικών εταιρειών.


Για την

Πρωτοβουλία Αλληλεγγύης στον Παλαιστινιακό


Λαό Εργατικών Σωματείων και Συλλογικοτήτων

, η επιλογή αυτή αποτελεί ακόμη ένα βήμα στρατιωτικής πρόσδεσης …
