author: Antisystemic
title: Εξέγερση και αντι-εξέγερση στη Γαλλία
content:
Εξέγερση και αντι-εξέγερση στη Γαλλία


“Η βία αυτή δεν είναι σήμερα αστήρικτη, ασήμαντη, παραβατική. Λέγει ουσιαστικά πράγματα για τη ζωή των πληθυσμών των προαστίων και άρα για ολόκληρη την κοινωνία […] Η βία αυτή είναι υγιής, γιατί εναντιώνεται στη διατήρηση της αδικίας και του κοινωνικού χάους […]”.


Michel Ganozzi, La violence d’une partie de la jenuesse des banlieues est legitime, necessaire et saine


Οι λαϊκές εξεγέρσεις στη Γαλλία τα τελευταία χρόνια τείνουν να μετατραπούν σε μόνιμο γνώρισμα της πολιτικής και κοινωνικής πραγματικότητας. Ο κύκλος της βίας εξαπλώνεται και έλκει σταδιακά όλο και περισσότερα ταξικά υποκείμενα στη συγκρουσιακή ακολουθία του. Κάποιοι σχολίασαν ειρωνικά ότι τα “μπάχαλα” έχουν γίνει το νέο εθνικό σπόρ των “Γάλλων”. Προσπαθούν έτσι να απαξιώσουν τη σημασία των γεγονότων και να εμφυσήσουν την ιδέα μιας, αντεστραμμένης έστω, εθνικής ομοψυχίας. Την ιδέα της ύπαρξης μιας “εθνικής” τάσης, εκεί που στην πραγματικότητα υπάρχει μονάχα σύγκρουση, αντίφαση και φυγόκεντρες δυνάμεις που παλεύουν να αποκτήσουν την αυτονομία τους απ’ το κέντρο της κρατικής εξουσίας. Εκεί δηλαδή όπου υπάρχει μόνο η σταδιακή αποσύνθεση αυτού που αποκαλούμε “έθνος” ως ζώσας κοινωνικής πραγματικότητας.


Άλλοι επιχειρούν να στρέψουν επιδέξια την μία μερίδα των εξεγερμένων ενάντια στην άλλη, καλλιεργώντας το μίσος και τον ταξικό ρατσισμό, που αποτελεί τον κύριο μηχανισμό ιδεολογικής κυριαρχίας του νεοφιλελευθερισμού στις καπιταλιστικές μητροπόλεις. Αυτό για παράδειγμα είναι το περιεχόμενο της στρατηγικής “εθνικής σωτηρίας” που συνιστά την αιχμή του δόρατος της εκλογικής προπαγάνδας της Μαρίν Λεπέν. Η κινητοποίηση της λευκής μάζας των δυσαρεστημένων μικροαστών της ενδοχώρας, οι οποίοι πριν κάποια χρόνια συσπειρώθηκαν στις μεγαλειώδεις αντικυβερνητικές διαδηλώσεις των Κίτρινων Γιλέκων, ως αντίβαρο στις εξεγερσιακές διαθέσεις του προλεταριάτου των πόλεων, καθώς και του πολυεθνικού λούμπεν προλεταριάτου των προαστίων. Αν κάποιο συμπέρασμα προκύπτει αβίαστα από αυτή τη συνεχή κοινωνική αναταραχή στη Γαλλία, είναι η έκδηλη αδυναμία του  νεοφιλελεύθερου κράτους να οικοδομήσει ένα ταξικό μπλοκ που θα του εξασφαλίσει την απαραίτητη κοινωνική αποδοχή και θα εγγυηθεί την μακροημέρευση της κυριαρχίας του.


Το πρόβλημα βέβαια με αυτόν τον επαναλαμβανόμενο κύκλο εξέγερσης και αντιεξέγερσης είναι η αδυναμία που επιδεικνύουν εξίσου οι επιμέρους ανταρσίες κι εκστρατείες κοινωνικής ανυπακοής που συγκροτούνται αυθόρμητα από-τα-κάτω, να συμμαχήσουν σε ένα ενιαίο κίνημα και να καταφέρουν το οριστικό χτύπημα στη νεοφιλελεύθερη χούντα του Μακρόν που παραπαίει. Μπαίνουμε εδώ στον πειρασμό να θυμηθούμε τον ιστορικό Eric Hobsbawm που κάποτε είχε γράψει ότι κατά την πρώτη εποχή της κυριαρχίας της, στα χρόνια που ήταν ακόμη σε εξέλιξη η βιομηχανική επανάσταση, η αστική τάξη είχε μάθει να ζει με τα περιοδικά ξεσπάσματα αγανάκτησης των προλετάριων. Είχε μάθει να τα θεωρεί ως ένα αναγκαίο κακό, όπου όμως “δεν δικακυβευόταν τίποτε […] πέρα από κάποια περιουσιακά στοιχεία που μια πλούσια χώρα μπορούσε κάλλιστα να τα αντικαταστήσει”.i Με άλλα λόγια, οι αστοί έδειχναν μια ανοχή σε αυτές τις παροδικές εξεγερσιακές εκρήξεις των φτωχών, διότι είχαν καταλάβει ότι αυτό ήταν τίμημα που έπρεπε να καταβάλλουν για να εξαγνίσουν την κυριαρχία τους.


Παρ’ όλα αυτά, η απελπισία των ελίτ στη Γαλλία έχει φτάσει σε τέτοιο σημείο ώστε επιστράτευσαν το παραμύθι των “πρακτόρων της Μόσχας” που δήθεν υποδαυλίζουν τις κοινωνικές ταραχές σε ολόκληρη τη χώρα.ii Εδώ τα διδάγματα από το υπερσυντηρητικό εργαστήρι της εμπόλεμης Ουκρανίας είναι κάτι παραπάνω από πολύτιμα. Λίγο μετά τη λαϊκή εξέγερση που ανέβασε στην εξουσία την ακροδεξιά χούντα του Μαϊντάν, ο τότε πρωθυπουργός Γιάτσενιουκ αποκάλεσε τους ανθρώπους που διαμαρτύρονταν στους δρόμους για την απότομη αύξηση στις τιμές του πετρελαίου θέρμανσης και τις περικοπές στις δαπάνες για την υγεία και την παιδεία, “πράκτορες των Ρώσων” και πέμπτη φάλαγγα που ενεργούσε καθ’ υπόδειξη του εχθρού, δηλαδή της Ρωσίας.iii Να λοιπόν που η ρωσοφοβική προπαγάνδα για το μαύρο χέρι του “Μόσκοβου” είναι σαν τη διαφήμιση της κοκα-κόλα. Πάει με όλα. Παρά την προφανή γελοιότητα της, η θεωρία του “ξένου δάκτυλου” που απεργάζεται στο παρασκήνιο την αποσταθεροποίηση των ευρωπαϊκών κοινωνιών είναι το τελευταίο καταφύγιο των ευρωπαϊκών πολιτικών και οικονομικών ελίτ που έχουν απωλέσει τα κοινωνικά στηρίγματα τους και βυθίζονται σε μια κρίση νομιμοποίησης της εξουσίας τους. Είναι επίσης ένα τρόπος για να τεθούν εκτός του “υγιούς” κορμού της …

author: Unknown
title: Adam Gary Lewis - Cultures of Anarchist Anti-Colonialism
content:
Author

: Adam Gary Lewis

Title

: Cultures of Anarchist Anti-Colonialism

Subtitle

: Considering Anarchist Prefigurative Possibilities for the Future

Date

: 2026

Notes

: *A text edited for the workshop “Cultures of Anarchist Anti-Colonialism” at the 2026 Hamilton Anarchist Bookfair. **Note: This zine is a heftily edited version of chapters, ideas, and discussions that appear in the 2026 PhD dissertation. I have aimed to condense this work, and dispense with some of the excess academic referencing, language and theory. This is not to suggest that these elements cannot be useful to anarchists, but in the spirit of generating wider forms of discussion I present this initial edited version. The interviews referenced here come from my conversations with 17 anarchists in Southern Ontario, that span a range of cities, communities, and scenes, and encompass a range of complex social identities. In particular, I highlight the words and perspectives of Indigenous participants. Pseudonyms were used to help to maintain some aspect of anonymity. I hope these ideas further some of the ongoing and important conversations on anarchism and anti-colonial politics both here in Southern Ontario, but also further afield as well. My heartfelt and ongoing thanks to all who participated and supported this project over many years, and all the anarchist crews in Southern Ontario. Of course for those with more academic and theory oriented desires I invite you to check out the full dissertation work as well: Adam Gary Lewis. 2026. Cultures of Resistance, Cultures of Potential: Anarchist Value-Practices, Settler Colonialism, and Indigenous Resurgence. PhD Dissertation. York University.

Source

: Retrieved on October 4, 2026 from https://anarchistnews.org/content/cultures-anarchist-anti-colonialism


Someday, somewhere, today’s empires are tomorrow’s ashes.


—Propagandhi


 Commitments to resist settler colonialism and articulate affinities with Indigenous struggles carry potentials for greater forms of anti-colonial politics within anarchism. Such commitments are important points of resistance and action within anarchism, but they are often limited, and require greater expansion in both theory and practice in order to actually generate disruptive forms of anarchist anti-colonialism.


 Anarchists have long named settler colonialism as a key form of oppression and domination that needs to be opposed, alongside more standard anarchist oppositions like the state and capitalism. This is most readily visible in intro to anarchism books, zines, and discussions. Opposition to colonialism is nestled alongside the wide range of opposition to all forms of oppression and domination that characterizes contemporary anarchist politics. In many of these accounts, and especially those that are more theoretical in nature, there is little discussion as to what this sort of anti-colonial opposition might look like. There may be vague nods to support for Indigenous resurgence, or wider histories of complicity with international forms of anti-imperialist struggle, but rarely is there more detailed discussion of how committed form of anti-colonial politics might be enacted in here and now –in specific places at specific times– and with direct reference to the histories and flows of struggle that might disrupt anarchism for the better.


 This results in a tendency to leave colonialism among a wider laundry list of things to be opposed, and lacking in greater qualification and consideration of what this means as practical forms of politics. How, then, are anarchists actually seeking to practically, materially, and intentionally oppose settler colonialism, and support Indigenous resistance and resurgence? This zine attempts to shed light on some of the everyday ways that anarchists in Southern Ontario are engaging this work, and how they are thinking about the relationship between anarchism and anti-colonial politics.


 I consider how spirituality, history, relationships to land and place, and prefigurative imaginations for the future interact with anarchist anti-colonialism. I begin with spirituality as a tension that is perhaps even less discussed amongst anarchists, but which intersects directly with Indigenous resurgence politics, given the centrality of Indigenous cosmologies, grounded normativities, and relationships to land. The limited anarchist approach to spirituality is a stumbling block for anarchist affinities with Indigenous struggles, as well …

author: Kévin Drif
title: The North African family French critics couldn’t see
content:
Since her 2016 debut feature

Raw

, the French auteur Julia Ducournau’s films have been a staple of the body horror genre. Her movies reflect an unapologetic approach to exploring physical transformation and the “monstrous feminine,” an idea coined by feminist film scholar Barbara Creed to underscore the significance of gender and sexuality in the construction of monstrosity. In Ducournau’s films, female characters strive for emancipation from social and familial norms through cannibalism or transhumanism. Yet while

Raw

 and her sophomore feature

Titane

 (2021) center white protagonists,

Alpha

 (2025), her third film, foregrounds the complex dynamic of a family of North African descent, marking a significant departure for the auteur. Curiously, this demographic difference has been almost entirely absent from discussions of the film.

Set between the 1980s and 1990s,

Alpha

 follows its 13-year-old eponymous character; her mother, who is a doctor; and her uncle Amin as they confront a mysterious virus that transforms bodies into blue-veined marmoreal statues that eventually turn to dust. Critics have understandably focused on the epidemic narrative, the stigma attached to the infected, and its evocation of the AIDS crisis, but in doing so, they have overlooked another dimension of the story:

Alpha

 is one of the few contemporary French films to place a family of North African origin at the center of a national trauma.

Ducournau hardly conceals the central family’s roots. She casts actors of Algerian, Moroccan, and Iranian descent and the characters move between French and dialectal Arabic. In one scene that features the most cinematic French postcolonial locality — the

banlieue

 —

Alpha

 joins her extended family to share a couscous meal for an Eid celebration. The problem here is not simply that reviewers omitted demographic details but that their silence in effect reproduces a broader tendency and difficulty within French cultural discourse to see race, acknowledge colonial history, and address postcolonial belonging even when it permeates the screen.

Approaching

Alpha

 through a postcolonial lens opens more interpretative possibilities. Consider the body itself, a central concern of Ducournau’s cinema:

Alpha

’s makeshift tattoo, which symbolically binds her to Amin, evokes traditions of Amazigh inking while also drawing attention to the postcolonial body as a site of inscription, memory, and belonging. The gesture turns the body into a site where cultural memory can persist without being explicitly articulated;

Alpha

’s body becomes a postcolonial archive — a place where histories and affiliations that remain largely unspoken can nonetheless be inscribed, carried, and transmitted. Furthermore, the film’s concern with body regulation recalls the colonial politics of visibility explored by Frantz Fanon in his writings on French Algeria, where the control of bodies, especially female bodies through the practice of unveiling, functioned as a mechanism of domination.

Alpha

’s epidemic narrative also takes on new meanings when viewed through the history of North African migration. The AIDS crisis in France disproportionally affected marginalized communities. According to

a 1999 study

 led by the French Institut de veille sanitaire, or Institute of Health Surveillance, between 1978 and 1998, immigrant populations accounted for 14 percent of AIDS cases in France, when they only represented 6 percent of the adult population at the time. Drug users of North African origin infected through contaminated needles, much like Amin, represented the main mode of contamination for heterosexual men and accounted for 45 percent of North African immigrant cases. Still, they remain largely absent from narratives of the epidemic. This omission and silence of the infected is the result of the religious taboo attached to the disease and the larger structural disinterest in these populations. Ducournau’s attention to Amin gestures towards histories that have largely escaped commemoration.

Alpha

’s imagery of suffocation, disease, and social abandonment invites reflection of the lives and afterlives of colonial violence beyond France. The calcification of infected bodies recalls forms of historical petrification through which colonial atrocities are rendered distant, abstract, and invisible within French national memory. The structural and social segregation imposed on the sick in the film, illustrated in the …

author: Joshua W.J. Brown
title: The New Native Needs a Theory of Obligation, Not a Blood Test
content:
The New Native should not become the old Native with a better genealogy.


That is the danger I keep hearing underneath the question

The Elephant

 has been asking this year. The “New Native” in this series is not a newly discovered ethnic group. It is a political figure emerging from a Kenyan public that has begun to act as though citizenship might mean more than being represented upward by an ethnic kingpin, disciplined by a church, managed by a civil servant, or frightened back into the inherited categories of the colonial state.


Akal Mohan sees the consolidation of a Kenyan identity beyond old orders of tribe, clan and denomination. Wangui Kimari traces the state’s fear of the “detribalized native”, then and now: the urban African who does not stay where authority says identity belongs. Joe Kobuthi reads the 2024 rupture through theology and the failure of a state that has demanded something close to sacred obedience. Across the series, the New Native becomes legible precisely when older intermediaries stop being able to explain the citizen to himself.


But once “native” is liberated from colonial administration, a second problem arrives. What is it going to mean?


If native means only ancestry, the term can become a blood test. If it means only citizenship, it can become historical amnesia. Neither answer is adequate for a country in which people can be equal citizens while communities still possess radically unequal historical relationships to land, dispossession, state violence, migration and political power.


Kenya’s own constitution already knows this, even when political language forgets.


One country, more than one kind of right


Chapter Three of the constitution does not grade citizenship by antiquity. A Kenyan citizen is a citizen. Citizenship may be acquired by birth or registration, and citizens possess the rights, privileges and benefits of that status. The constitution does not say that a person becomes more Kenyan because his ancestors arrived first, or less Kenyan because a grandparent crossed a border.


Then Chapter Five does something equally important: it refuses to pretend that equal citizenship has dissolved collective history. Article 63 recognizes community land, including ancestral lands and lands traditionally occupied by hunter-gatherer communities. The Community Land Act recognizes customary rights and gives them legal force. Article 56 requires affirmative measures for minorities and marginalized groups.


These provisions are not an embarrassing inconsistency in the constitutional order. They are a clue.


Equal citizenship and historically specific rights can coexist because they answer different questions. Citizenship asks: who belongs to the political community, and on what civic terms? Ancestral land rights ask: what relationship does a particular community possess to a particular place, and what happened to that relationship? A remedy for dispossession is not a superior passport. A passport is not a land restitution programme.


Conflate those categories and the state gets two convenient escapes. It can tell a dispossessed community that everyone is equal now, therefore the old theft no longer requires a specific remedy. Or it can tell citizens descended from later-arriving populations that they may live under the law but can never fully belong because history placed their ancestors in the wrong column.


Both moves turn time into an alibi.


The Ogiek case is about more than recognition


The Ogiek litigation makes the first danger impossible to romanticize away.


In 2017, the African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights found Kenya responsible for violations involving Ogiek land, property, natural resources, culture and development. In 2022, the Court ordered reparations, including compensation and measures to secure Ogiek ancestral land rights. In December 2025, after years of implementation failure, the Court found Kenya had still not made the ordered compensation payments, had not completed the identification, delimitation, demarcation and collective titling of Ogiek ancestral land, and had not begun the consultations required to resolve concessions and leases affecting that land.


That matters to the New Native argument because it shows why a purely civic vocabulary is insufficient. “We are all Kenyans” cannot do the work of a title, a payment, a boundary, a consultation, or the restoration of a legal relationship to ancestral land.


Universal equality is not the …

title: Manifestation DECOLONIZE « solidarité avec les Autochtones des Amériques »
content:
Dans le cadre de la Journée internationale de solidarité avec les Autochtones des Amériques, le 12 octobre et des célébrations des 30 ans du Congrès National Indigène au Mexique (

CNI

)


Du Chiapas à la Kanaky, de Palestine à Abya Yala / Turtle Island ...


Venez participer à la manifestation déclarée ce lundi 12 octobre à 18h Place d'Iena à Paris


Le 12 octobre 1492, Christophe Colomb «

 

découvrait

 

» soit disant, un nouveau continent sur la carte du monde :

l'Amérique pour les colons

, désormais nommé

Abya Yala

 par les

peuples originaires

.


Aujourd'hui, les institutions célèbrent la «

 

rencontre

 

» entre deux mondes et la multiculturalité qui en résulte. Une commémoration

qui passe sous silence l'extermination, l'exploitation, le racisme, les viols et les multiples formes de violence

 qui ont permis la

colonisation

 et la

domination européenne

. Une manière aussi pour les nations «

 

souveraines

 

» de dissimuler que les violations des droits à la terre et à la culture des peuples originaires sont toujours d'actualité sous leurs gouvernements.


1492

 est sans aucun doute une

référence incontournable

 de

l'histoire de la colonisation

 et des États modernes qui célèbrent la «

 

Découverte

 

». Pour le mouvement indigène d'Abya Yala, la date du

12 octobre

 est le

symbole

 d'une

lutte continentale pour le droit à l'existence et à la dignité des peuples originaires.

 Mais il ne s'agit pas seulement d'une opposition symbolique entre calendriers et mémoire, entre celle d'en haut et celles d'en bas :

la lutte pour la dignité des peuples, la défense des territoires et la résistance aux guerres impérialistes, coloniales et capitalistes

 sont encore, partout, d'actualité.


Ces dernières décennies, du Chiapas à la Kanaky, la

prédation coloniale

 et la

voracité capitaliste

 propagent la guerre par la destruction des territoires et le

dépeuplement généralisé des populations «

 

indésirables

 

»

. L'éco-génocide en Palestine depuis 2023 en est un témoignage poignant.


Aux quatre coins du monde, on observe

l'avancée terrifiante de la fascisation, du culte identitaire d'une nation

 ou d'une civilisation fantasmée,

la militarisation des États

 et la

répression des contestations sociales et des soulèvements populaires

. En France, le processus de fascisation de la société est favorisé par le

désespoir lié à la crise structurelle violente

 qui affecte les conditions d'existence d'une partie considérable de la population et un arsenal politique et médiatico-juridique particulièrement offensif. Sur les continents américain et européen,

le fascisme se banalise dangereusement

 pendant que des partis politiques d'extrême droite s'installent durablement, par les urnes, dans les centres impériaux de la modernité capitaliste.

Le ravage écologique et la brutalité systémique obscurcissent l'horizon d'un lendemain meilleur

 à mesure que les crises s'amplifient.


Face à ces constats inquiétants, le temps n'est pas à la résignation. Au contraire, c'est le moment

de prolonger les rencontres

 et d'

approfondir les complicités

, de respecter ce qui nous distingue et d'écouter ce qui nous lie pour apprendre ensemble de celles et ceux qui,

 en bas et à gauche, combattent les guerres «

 

intérieures

 

» et coloniales, les replis identitaire, l'écocide terrestre et les génocides en-cours.

 Le temps présent est celui de l'apprentissage et de l'approfondissement de l'organisation, à l'aune de la

résistance séculaire des peuples originaires d'Abya Yala, de la lutte contre

ICE

 à Minneapolis ou du sumud palestinien.


C'est pourquoi,

à l'occasion des 534 ans de la résistance des peuples originaires d'Abya Yala

, plusieurs collectifs et syndicats vous invitent à rejoindre

Lundi 12 octobre à 18h00 à la manifestation pour la journée internationale de la résistance indigène

. Nous marcherons

de Iéna jusqu'à la place du Trocadéro

 pour affirmer, jusqu'au coeur de l'Europe, notre solidarité avec les peuples originaires d'Abya Yala dans leur lutte permanente pour la vie, une vie digne et bonne pour toutes et tous et contre le capitalisme, la colonisation et le patriarcat.


Que la rencontre soit celle des résistances qui partagent un horizon d'émancipation en commun,


Nous vous attendons nombreux.ses

 

!

CSPCL


Comité de Solidarité Internationale avec les Autochtones des Amériques - …

ΚΥΡΙΑΚΗ 4/10 | 6.00μμ | ΣΦΕΝΤΟΝΑ [Συγγρού 24, 2ος όροφος]


Αγωνιστική Πρωτοβουλία Μισθωτών Τεχνικών


Εκδήλωση-βιβλιοπαρουσίαση «Οργή λαού – για την υπόθεση του Ηρακλή Μαραγκάκη»


…στον αυτοδιαχειριζόμενο χώρο ΑΝΑΤόΠΙΑ.


Βιβλιοπαρουσίαση της έκδοσης «Οργή λαού – για την υπόθεση του Ηρακλή Μαραγκάκη» από την πρωτοβουλία για την ιστορική καταγραφή και την επαναστατική μνήμη από την κατάληψη Ευαγγελισμού.


Ενημέρωση για την υπόθεση της δολοφονίας του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη από την ελληνική αστυνομία από τον Αναστάση Μανιουδάκη (γιο του Κώστα Μανιουδάκη και μέλος σχετικών με την υπόθεση συνελεύσεων).


Η εκδήλωση γίνεται με την πολιτική στήριξη της πρωτοβουλίας ενάντια στην κρατική επιθετικότητα και ατιμωρησία (δικαιοσύνη για τον Κώστα Μανιουδάκη).


Εκδήλωση για την αντίσταση στον Λίβανο, την Παλαιστίνη και τη Συρία – Συνέλευση Αλληλεγγύης στην Παλαιστινιακή Αντίσταση


Λευτεριά στην Παλαιστίνη, λευτεριά στον Λίβανο.


Η

7η Οκτωβρίου

 ήταν μια πράξη αντιαποικιακής και αντιιμπεριαλιστικής αντίστασης. Μια συνέχεια της αντίστασης που χρονολογείται από τη στιγμή της ίδρυσης του κράτους του “Ισραήλ” το 1948, αλλά και ακόμη νωρίτερα, κατά τη διάρκεια της βρετανικής αποικιακής κατοχής. Ήταν ένας λαός και ένα κίνημα που ξεσηκώθηκαν ενάντια στην κατοχή. Η ημέρα αυτή θα συνεχίσει να τιμάται ως τέτοια για τις επόμενες γενιές, ακόμη και αν οι σιωνιστές και οι ιμπεριαλιστές προσπαθήσουν με κάθε μέσο να ελέγξουν και να αλλάξουν το αφήγημα. Τα αλεξίπτωτα πλαγιάς που πετούσαν πάνω από τον φράχτη προς την κατεχόμενη Παλαιστίνη, ο φράχτης που περιέκλειε τη Γάζα και γκρεμίστηκε από τους ανθρώπους που εκδιώχθηκαν από τη γη τους πριν από δεκαετίες: αυτές οι εικόνες δεν θα ξεχαστούν και θα παραμείνουν στη μνήμη μας ως σύμβολα της αντίστασης του Παγκόσμιου Νότου.


Η απάντηση της σιωνιστικής οντότητας, με την υποστήριξη των ΗΠΑ, υπήρξε ανελέητη. Από τον Οκτώβριο του 2023 γινόμαστε μάρτυρες μιας γενοκτονίας που μεταδίδεται ζωντανά και πολλών φρικαλεοτήτων που διαπράττονται από τη σιωνιστική οντότητα και τους ιμπεριαλιστές των ΗΠΑ (με την υποστήριξη ευρωπαϊκών κρατών). Η Γάζα έχει ισοπεδωθεί από τους βομβαρδισμούς και, παρόλο που γίνεται λόγος για κατάπαυση του πυρός, συνεχίζουν να βομβαρδίζουν και να πυροβολούν αδιακρίτως. Ο Λίβανος και η Συρία τελούν υπό κατοχή και δέχονται συνεχείς επιθέσεις από τη σιωνιστική οντότητα. Οι κυβερνήσεις αυτών των περιοχών καταστέλλουν την αντίσταση και την εναντίωση στη Δύση και το “Ισραήλ” στα εδάφη τους, ενεργώντας ως εντολοδόχοι των ΗΠΑ. Όλα αυτά συμβαίνουν ενώ το “Ισραήλ” καταλαμβάνει όλο και περισσότερα εδάφη, αποσταθεροποιώντας περαιτέρω την περιοχή.


Το κράτος του “Ισραήλ” και οι ΗΠΑ καταστρέφουν ορισμένες από τις αρχαιότερες περιοχές με συνεχή κατοίκηση στην ιστορία του πολιτισμού, στην Παλαιστίνη, τον Λίβανο, τη Συρία και το Ιράν. author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: Imperial Nostalgia: History, Sovereignty, and the Unfinished Work of Decolonization in the Horn of Africa
content:
History in the Horn of Africa is rarely allowed to remain history. An ancient civilization becomes evidence of modern sovereignty. A medieval dynasty becomes proof of national continuity. Territory incorporated during one political era is later remembered as though it had always belonged to the state that governed it.


This habit has become especially visible as the Red Sea has returned to Ethiopian political discourse. Ethiopia is landlocked and has obvious economic reasons to seek dependable maritime trade. But there is a fundamental difference between negotiating the use of a port and claiming that a neighboring country possesses territory that properly belongs to Ethiopia. That distinction disappears when Assab is described as a “lost Ethiopian port.”


Ethiopia did not lose a sovereign port in 1993. Eritrea recovered sovereignty over territory that had been incorporated into Ethiopia after the violation and eventual termination of an internationally established federal arrangement. To describe this as Ethiopia “losing the sea” begins the story at the moment of Ethiopian possession and ignores how that possession came about.


This is what I mean by imperial nostalgia.


Imperial nostalgia is not merely admiration for emperors or attachment to an earlier age. It is a way of remembering political space. Territory once incorporated into an empire is remembered not simply as territory once governed, but as territory that naturally belonged there. Incorporation becomes ownership, ownership becomes entitlement, and independence can then be remembered as national loss.


Christopher Clapham’s notion of an Ethiopian “manifest destiny” is useful at the margins of this argument, although I invoke him cautiously and not to validate Ethiopian historical claims. The phrase captures a mentality in which expansion can stop looking like expansion when incorporation is presented as the fulfillment of history. Manifest destiny looks forward. Imperial nostalgia looks backward and imagines that a geography produced through expansion was the natural order all along.


The deeper problem is the projection of modern states backward into political worlds that did not organize themselves according to contemporary borders. Aksum is an obvious example. Its political and commercial world crossed territories that are now divided between Eritrea and Ethiopia and formed part of a much larger Red Sea system.

UNESCO’s account of Aksum

 describes an ancient civilization. It does not describe a modern territorial state possessing a contemporary claim to the Red Sea.


Calling Aksum simply “ancient Ethiopia” imports the political geography of today into antiquity. Calling it “ancient Eritrea” would make the same mistake. Civilizations, languages, religions, trading networks, and archaeological landscapes regularly cross the boundaries of modern states. Shared history does not create shared sovereignty.


I explored this problem more fully in

There Is No Timeless Eritrea or Ethiopia

. The point is not to diminish the history of either country. It is to stop asking ancient civilizations to perform the work of modern territorial law. Aksum should be studied as Aksum rather than recruited into a contemporary argument over Assab.


Richard Reid examined this problem directly in

The Trans-Mereb Experience: Perceptions of the Historical Relationship between Eritrea and Ethiopia

. Reid is useful because he is skeptical of efforts on either side to recruit antiquity into modern nationalism. The same history can be arranged to prove a supposedly eternal Ethiopia or, in the opposite direction, an Eritrea with no meaningful historical relationship to communities south of the Mereb. Neither approach is good history.


Even the word Ethiopia should make us cautious. The Greek term

Aithiopia

 did not refer neatly to the bounded territorial state called Ethiopia today. Recognizing this does not make modern Ethiopia less legitimate. It simply acknowledges that political names, communities, and territorial states change over time.


Eritrea should be approached in exactly the same way. Fred Halliday, writing in 1971 while the Eritrean war was still underway, acknowledged in

“The Fighting in Eritrea”

 that Eritrea in its modern territorial form had been defined under European colonialism. That fact does not weaken Eritrean sovereignty. It places Eritrea within the history of modern Africa.


Most African states inherited territorial forms created or …

title: England under occupation: neither great nor glorious
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


The corrupt cabal which

runs the modern world

 [1] seems to enjoy giving inappropriate, in fact inverted, names to the manufactured events through which it advances its vile agenda.


Thus the

nightmarish bloodbath

 with which it destroyed old Europe was called The

Great

 War [2] and a century later the

techno-totalitarian heist

 it tried to pull off on the basis of a fake pandemic was called The

Great

 Reset. [3]


This was doubly the case in 1688 with England’s

Glorious Revolution

, since this was neither a revolution nor a glorious moment for the people of that country – it was rather an invasion and full seizure of power by the network whose contemporary form I term

ZIM

, the zio-imperialist mafia. [4]


This entity, which

Mees Baaijen

 calls Glafia (global mafia), [5] had originally been based in Venice, then moved to Holland and, at the end of the 17th century, switched to London to use England as the springboard for the commercial, financial and industrial imperialism that we today call globalism.


This was the second assault on the country by such characters, who had also formed the financial wing of the Norman invasion and occupation starting from 1066, as I explained in ‘

How England was “colonised”

‘. [6]


Researcher Will Keyte (

pictured

) provides some useful 17th century context in an excellent and important October 2026

video

 on the

TheRealMagnaCarta1215

 channel, which is part of an in-depth series on the misnamed Glorious Revolution. [7]


He says of the mid to late 1600s: “It’s a fascinating and dangerous period of change, all of it, and not the kind of change that ultimately resulted in benefit for the people. The depth of the skullduggery is just unimaginable”.


He begins with Oliver Cromwell, who led the parliamentary side in the English Civil War from 1642 to 1651, and whose victory resulted in the beheading of the Stuart king Charles I and Cromwell installing himself as Lord Protector of the Commonwealth of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1653 until his death in 1658.


Keyte notes that Cromwell received “massive financial backing from Amsterdam and rich individual financiers” – I have

previously highlighted

 his particularly close connections to Rabbi Menasseh Ben Israel. [8]


That article focuses on the Invisible College, the precursor of the Royal Society, created in 1660, and Keyte mentions that latter body as being part of the new network rising to prominence in London at the time.


“Essentially, the undercurrent, or the sort of strain of influence, was certainly a banking one, mixed with early pre-formal masonry”.


He explains that the masonic guilds had originally been literally made up of stonemasons, but that changed and others were allowed entry. “This allowed merchants, lawyers, scientists, academics, to come into that organisation and be members – and they could network independently of the authorities of the Church and the Crown”.


“Cromwell had allowed these changes during the interregnum in relation to the influence of wealthy bankers in the City – he’d sort of promoted their influence.


“But when the Crown was restored in 1660, when Charles II came to the throne, he was not able to reset those changes… So you’ve got this heavy influence of these rich money people. These wealthy players remained the dominant influence in the City”.


Keyte says that the 1666

Great

 Fire of London (

there’s that adjective again!

) “hit at perhaps the most vulnerable point, economically, and many have asked in history ‘was that a false flag event?’ Many people have said that it is”.


“What’s interesting about that is the timing, because you’ve just had the Plague of London as well [‘The

Great

 Plague of London’

according to


Wikipedia

 [9], I see!]. I don’t know whether that was a false flag as well… You’ve got everything coming together at the same time. You’ve got forces at work – because it didn’t work in the interregnum, they couldn’t get rid of the old constitution of England, they couldn’t quite do it…


“You constantly got these efforts now, following the Restoration of the monarchy, to try and bring about a situation where we’re going to finally bring an end to the ‘old’ constitution and implement the kind of financial revolution that they wanted to have, to weaponise England and take it where it went in the hundred years succeeding that”.

title: +++ Die Demo ohne Inhalt meldet sich zu Wort +++
content:
Gegen Ihre Repression


Am Sonntag, 11.10.2026, geht es wieder auf die Strasse. Und es hängt ein dunkler Schatten über dem Tag. Das war zu erwarten und wir möchten uns dazu nun positionieren. Klar ist, wir werden auf die Strasse gehen, denn die Berner Shitshow des letzten Jahres lassen wir so nicht stehen.


Zunächst eine erneute Einordung der aktuellen Lage


Die Schweiz ist eine Mörderin. Zum einen bietet sie ein ruhiges Hinterland für andere Mörder*innen wie UBS, Palantir, Glencore, Syngenta, die Weltbank oder Valcambi. Andererseits bringt sie als Teil des US-imperialen Blocks seit hunderten von Jahren unsere Geschwister auf der ganzen Welt um. Auch wenn gerade alle Augen dem seltsam faszinierenden Spektal der Trump-Administration zuschauen, fallen weiterhin echte Bomben, werden weiterhin echte Menschen verdrängt, sterben weiterhin echte Kinder. Kurz: die Lage hat sich nicht verbessert, sie ist nur nicht mehr so interessant für die bürgerliche Presse. Für uns heisst das nur, dass alle bereits bestehenden Analysen zu Krieg und Genozid weiterhin anzuwenden sind. Sie zu wiederholen, sparen wir uns an dieser Stelle. Wer es noch nicht kapiert hat, wird für den Moment wohl selbst dahinter kommen müssen (gäu Alec).


Zur Demo


Wir wissen, viele Menschen sind verunsichert und trauen sich aufgrund der Repression nicht mehr, an diesem Tag ihre Wut auf die Strassen zu tragen. Schöne neue Demokratie. Genau diese Menschen wollen wir mit diesem Communiqué ansprechen.


Wir nehmen an, ihr wollt euch grundsätzlich auch nicht von der Repression unterkriegen lassen. Aber das von Medien, Politik und Bullen kreirte Klima macht einfach keine Lust die "Demokratie" zu leben. Wir verstehen das und haben eine Antwort: Eine kreative Anti-Kessel-Demo. Ein Konzept, um am 11. Oktober auf die Strasse zu gehen und trotz Repression ein Ereignis zu schaffen, das uns im Widerstand gegen unseren mörderischen Staat und im Kampf für eine andere Welt zusammenbringt und unsere Banden stärkt. Um nichts über die aktuellen Entwicklungen zur Anti-Kessel-Demo zu verpassen und am Tag selbst optimal vorbereitet zu sein, ist es wichtig, dass du dem Demoticker beitrittst. Die Links dazu findest du unten im Beitrag.


Zur Frage der Bewilligung


Wir leisten Widerstand gegen den Schweizer Staat und lassen unser Handeln darum nicht von ihm bewilligen. Was wäre das auch für eine witzlose Logik.


Für die Repression ist die Bewilligung immer der erste Angriffspunkt. Und angegriffen wird, wenn es der Polizei beliebt. Oder was war das bitte am Smash WEF dieses Jahr? Einer bereits aufgelösten Demo in den Rücken prügeln?

Diese Kontrolle des Diskurses erlaubt es dem Staat der Öffentlichkeit zu vermitteln, unser Widerstand sei nicht legitim, verwirrt, sinnfrei oder sonst irgendwie falsch. Und unser Aufruf vorallem eine Ansage zur totalen Eskalation. Das wurde einwandfrei klar aus den bereits veröffentlichten Beiträgen, siehe NZZ, BZ, Blick. Die Demo ist zur Projektionsfläche für alle möglichen Ängste und Unzufriedenheiten der Bürgerlichen geworden. Das ist bei linken Demonstrationen nicht ungewöhnlich, doch gerade der 11. Oktober 2025 wird immerwieder als Referenzpunkt verwendet, um die Verschärfung staatlicher Repression und Überwachung zu rechfertigen. Um verfassungswidrige Repression gegen uns zu legitimieren und unsere Inhalte unsichtbar zu machen. author: Wildcat #116
title: 1976 – 1991: Das Albartus-Papier der Revolutionären Zellen
content:
Die Jahre 1976 und 1991 markieren zwei deutliche Abstürze in der Geschichte der radikalen Linken in der BRD. Bezeichnenderweise kam Ende 1991 das Albartus-Papier der Revolutionären Zellen auf 1976 zu sprechen: die Flugzeugentführung von Entebbe. Anlässlich des 50. Jahrestags haben wir in der aktuellen Wildcat einen langen Artikel, der diese Verbindungen aufzudröseln versucht: »Entebbe und die Folgen«. Hier eine Kürzestfassung plus update:


Im Juni und Juli 1976 herrschte in Europa eine Hitzewelle. Die Temperaturen in Deutschland stiegen wochenlang regelmäßig über 30 Grad auf Spitzenwerte bis 36 und 37 Grad.


Politisch endete vor 50 Jahren das »rote Jahrzehnt«: 24. März 1976 Militärputsch in Argentinien. Am 9. Mai 1976 starb Ulrike Meinhof. Anfang Juni brach auf dem »Pfingstkongress« ein breiter Teil der radikalen Linken mit der Militanz und machte sich auf in die Institutionen. Am 10. Juli begann die Chemiekatastrophe in Seveso. Im August das Massaker von Tel al-Zaatar. Am 6. Oktober der Militärputsch in Thailand.


Auch kulturell war 1976 schlimm: ABBA »Dancing Queen«, Jürgen Drews »Ein Bett im Kornfeld«, Boney M. »Daddy Cool«. Kurz danach kamen dann die BeeGees »Stayin’ Alive« – der Sound zum Deutschen Herbst!


Für die deutschen Maoisten der diversen K-Gruppen lag 1976 zwischen dem Besuch von Franz Josef Strauß bei Mao (Januar 1975) einerseits, dem Krieg Vietnams gegen Kambodscha und den »Reformen« von Deng Xiao Ping (beides im Dezember 1978) andererseits. Die meisten fielen vom Glauben ab, viele von ihnen gründeten die Grüne Partei, andere später die Antideutschen. Diese eroberten nach 1991 die Hegemonie in der radikalen Linken.


Die Flugzeugentführung nach Entebbe…


Seit Anfang 1976 eskalierte der libanesische Bürgerkrieg. Nach monatelanger Belagerung stürmten Falangisten am 12. August das Lager von Tel al-Zaatar und töteten Tausende palästinensische Flüchtlinge.


Im Zusammenhang damit entführte ein deutsch-palästinensisches Kommando aus RZ und PFLP-EO am 27. Juni 1976 ein Flugzeug nach Entebbe und forderte die Freilassung von politischen Gefangenen. In der Nacht zum 4. Juli befreiten israelische Spezialkräfte die meisten der Geiseln. Das wird von gewissen Kreisen bis heute als das beste Kommandounternehmen aller Zeiten bejubelt (etwa: »Mit der Geiselbefreiung von Entebbe zeigte Israel vor 50 Jahren, wie man den Terror bekämpft« Nius 2. Juli 2026). Benjamin Netanjahu, dessen älterer Bruder bei der Befreiungsaktion starb, hat seine gesamte politische Karriere auf »Entebbe« und den »Kampf gegen den Terrorismus« aufgebaut.


»Die Aktion von Entebbe wurde rasch zu einem Vorwand für verschiedene Akteure, die bislang mit dem Milieu der radikalen Linken verbunden waren, sich von Internationalismus und Antiimperialismus ganz zu lösen.« (Gerhard Hanloser: »Desaster mit Nachspiel«)


Wegweisend war der Anti-Repressionskongress des Sozialistischen Büros Anfang Juni (»Pfingstkongress«). Am Abschlusstag hatte der spätere Außenminister Joschka Fischer vor 20.000 Besuchern in der berühmten Römerberg-Rede mit seiner militanten Vergangenheit gebrochen. Später hat er – die Dinge chronologisch auf den Kopf stellend – auf seinem Weg ins Außenministerium immer mal wieder betont, »Entebbe« sei das Ereignis gewesen, das ihn vom Saulus zum Paulus gemacht habe. Dabei lieferte es nur nachträglich den Vorwand.


»Entebbe« ist bis heute wirkmächtig. Das sah man an den Dutzenden von Artikeln und mehreren Büchern, die zum 50. Jahrestag erschienen. Das sah man aber auch daran, dass im März 2023 Mitglieder der Entebbe-Spezialeinheit eine der schärfsten Kritiken an Benjamin Netanjahu in einem offenen Brief formulierten. Netanjahu opfere den Staat Israel und das israelische Volk für seine eigenen Interessen, diffamiere Demonstranten gegen die Justizreform als Anarchisten und alle, die ihn nicht unterstützen, als Terroristen; er hetze Israelis gegeneinander auf.


… und die beginnende Institutionalisierung der radikalen Linken


1976 hätte auch anders ausgehen können. Im Juli hatten Chemiearbeiter in Seveso gestreikt, um die Katastrophe überhaupt öffentlich zu machen – aber sie hatten nicht mehr die Macht wie Jahre zuvor, die Wirtschaftspolitik des Landes neu zu orientieren. Die massenhaften Schüler- und Studentenproteste in Soweto seit Juni waren größtenteils selbst organisiert und schienen politisch endlich eine Alternative zum ANC zu eröffnen. Anti-Zionism has entered the phase of sabotage. Lobbying governments to sanction Israel has been replaced with breaking drones and dismantling factories; boycotts traded for slashed truck airlines and arson; rallies and peace marches superseded with red paint and shattered office windows. It is a medium of tactics signaling a shift in the repertoire of collective action undertaken against Zionist Imperialism. This form of resistance did not emerge out of Al Aqsa Flood – but it too signals a new terrain upon which Palestine will be fought. It deserves an uncompromising theory of struggle.

The time has arrived for us to create something new. The mainstream Palestine Solidarity Movement has demonstrated its inability to effectively counter the growing international Zio-fascist alliance. It continues to rely on outmoded, outdated and counterinsurgent formulas of struggle while putting considerable effort into restricting, internally-policing, ignoring and countering the most dynamic, effective and generative aspects of Anti-Zionism that have emerged over the past six years.

Inside its performative rallies, on the edges of its peaceful pickets and fake boat blockades, circulated anonymously on social media: militant Anti-Zionist resistance.

Interpersonal opportunism, peace policing and activist influencers only explain a part of the problems many of us have experienced since October 7th 2023. Individuals, spokespeople and careerists are provided platforms by the rest of us in a movement that remains confined to theories, ideas, strategies and weapons of struggle which we must now finally discard. author: Rodrigo Acuña
title: Cubans See Hope in Reforms But Worry Over How the US May Thwart Them
content:
Residents of Havana discuss the obstacles facing the revival of the Cuban economy amid the US fuel blockade.

Residents of Havana discuss the obstacles facing the revival of the Cuban economy amid the US fuel blockade.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Last month, Cuban Prime Minister Manuel Marrero Cruz declared that 158 new economic and social measures, out of an original package of 176 approved in July by the Cuba’s National Assembly, were being implemented and backed by 197 legal decrees. The measures include allowing private business to import medicines and other goods, loosening restrictions on private tourism, and authorising privately owned banks — under Central Bank supervision — on a regulatory basis equivalent to state banks. Adding to these measures, the National Assembly for the first time permitted foreign capital to invest directly in Cuban private businesses instead of having to operate exclusively through state-controlled structures. Private companies also will no longer be restricted to a maximum of 100 employees.

According to Daniel Torralbas, a London-based Cuban economist, the National Assembly’s new measures are “the most profound economic reform programme … since the 1959 revolution.” Headed by Fidel Castro, the government in Havana between the mid and late 1960s nationalized a vast array of U.S.-owned businesses that controlled major shares in key industries such as public utilities, mining, railways and infrastructure, and land and agriculture.

Mauricio Alonso, a 68-year-old former nuclear engineer who lives in Havana and now runs an Airbnb rental, is embracing the government’s new economic measures.

“On a personal level this is going to benefit me,” says Alonso, “because it’s going to allow, for example, me — since I’m self-employed — to partner with foreigners, to team up, to be part of a larger organization, and to carry out actions with my lodging business, and so on.” Working with travel agencies, in Alonso’s view, will now be made easier with the lifting of restrictions. “If I qualify, if I get accredited as such,” says Alonso, “I can carry out the work of a tour guide without any kind of problem.”

During the 1980s, Alonso worked at the Central Electronuclear de Juraguá, near the city of Cienfuegos, which was being built with the aid of the Soviet Union to become Cuba’s first nuclear power station. Alonso says that, “when the Soviet Union collapsed in late 1991, work on the plant came to a halt in 1992.” Although Alonso continued working in the nuclear sector until 1995, he “realized that the project couldn’t go on — due in part to [the] intense pressure from the U.S. government.” At that point, he decided to “switch to the private sector and start renting out rooms” after inheriting a large apartment from his mother.

Had Cuba’s nuclear power station become operational, it is doubtful the island would be facing its current energy crisis.

Despite a small recovery between 2021 and 2022, after Cuba’s GDP in 2020 contracted by 10.9 percent as COVID-19 effectively shut down international tourism, the island’s economic crisis has been worsened by the Trump administration’s fuel embargo. When U.S. President Donald Trump began to take action against Venezuela’s oil shipments to Cuba in 2025, which approximated 26,500 barrels per day, Cubans saw a serious reduction of fuel on the island. On January 29, the Trump administration formalized the oil sanctions on Cuba by signing Executive Order 14380, which did not simply add another sanction on the island, but instead, created a mechanism to penalize third countries that supply oil to Cuba. Should a country provide crude oil or petroleum products, then the United States government can impose further tariffs on that country’s goods entering the U.S.

For Amalia Díaz Pérez, a 21-years old recent graduate in philosophy from the University of Havana, the Trump administration’s oil embargo disrupted her final year of study. Speaking to Truthout, she said:

The total blockade of fuel imports — with only one ship arriving in nine months — caused public transportation to disappear and reduced daily electricity availability to a minimum. Consequently, my study conditions and most of my daily recreational activities were affected. Compounding this situation, household chores became increasingly difficult due to the strain of the nationwide fuel shortage placed on water and …

title: Flávio Bolsonaro y Lula van a segunda vuelta en Brasil
content:
Con casi el 100% de las mesas escrutadas, Flávio Bolsonaro se impone con el 47,05% de los votos y suma en total 56.082.216 votos. Este resultado no le alcanza para ganar la presidencias, por lo que se disputará una segunda vuelta con el actual presidente Lula Da Silva que consiguió 45,14% de los votos, que equivalen a 53.799.870. Las elecciones se dan en un contexto de extrema polarización, incertidumbre e injerencia del imperialismo yanqui. El resultado de las elecciones brasileñas tiene un especial peso en la balanza de las fuerzas políticas en Latino América. Tanto por el tamaño de la economía de Brasil como por la polarización entre el actual presidente Lula y el hijo de Bolsonaro subordinado al alineamiento del continente a Trump, el Escudo de las Américas y su doctrina de seguridad Donroe.

Por La Izquierda Diario.


Distintos analistas sostienen que el voto indeciso fue el que sorprendió en esta primera vuelta al volcarse a favor de Flavio Bolsonaro, que quedó dos puntos arriba de Lula. Este resultado refleja lo que las encuestas captaron días antes, una mejora de Bolsonaro quien capitalizó el voto útil de otras fuerzas conservadoras.


La presión del imperialismo parece haber surtido efecto como en la Argentina en las elecciones intermedias de 2027. Allí con el respaldo de dinero y la amenaza de retirar el apoyo y hundir las finanzas del Estado, de la mano del Secretario del Tesoro yanqui Scott Bessent. En Brasil, la amenaza se materializó con el cierre de consulados y la embajada por una supuesta cuestión de seguridad que la Policía Federal investigó y descartó. Además, está el antecedente de Venezuela y todas las acciones de presión con aranceles, y otras presiones diplomáticas sobre el gobierno de Lula.


Por otro lado, en todos estos años de gobierno petista no se cambió la estructura de la nación dependiente del imperialismo, así como tampoco se resolvieron las diferencias sociales, el racismo ni la concentración de tierras en manos de los latifundistas. Los salarios bajos y las familias endeudadas demuestran eso. No es solo el grave tema de las apuestas on line, son los ingresos de las familias, cada vez peores.


Cronología de este domingo 4 de octubre


22:41


«Brasil quiere un cambio»


Después del triunfo en primera vuelta, el candidato opositor Flávio Bolsonaro habló desde su bunker en Brasilia y aseguró que «Brasil quiere un cambio», sin hacer mención a la fallida presidencia de su padre.


También afirmó que este resultado muestra el fin del PT (Partido dos Trabalhadores) y dijo estar muy contento con los resultados regionales.


22:25


Un resultado inesperado


A poco de conocerse los resultados oficiales, Lula habló dió un discurso diciendo que el resultado lo había sorprendido y hasta aseguró que había confiado en que ganaba en primera vuelta.


Pensando en el próximo round, le dijo a sus seguidores que en la segunda vuelta «mostraremos la verdadera foto de Brasil.» También afirmó que su campaña se centrará en convencer a todos los que se ausentaron de las urnas de la importancia de ir a votar.


22:01


Segunda vuelta confirmada


Con casi el 100% de las mesas escrutadas, Flavio Bolsonaro se impone con el 47,05% de los votos y suma en total 56.082.216 votos. Este resultado no le alcanza para ganar la presidencia, por lo que se disputará una segunda vuelta con el actual presidente Lula Da Silva que consiguió 45,14% de los votos, que equivalen a 53.799.870.


Muy lejos se ubica el tercer candidato, Augusto Cury, con algo menos del 3%. Cury adelantó que no apoyará a ningún candidato en la segunda vuelta.


20:30


El Partido Liberal acumula gobernadores


Según resultados proyectados, los candidatos del partido de Bolsonaro fueron electos en Rio Grande do Sul, Rondonia, Roraima y Santa Catarina, donde reelige. Además, disputa en una segunda vuelta los estados de Paraná y Rio de Janeiro, donde actualmente gobierna, para un posible total de 6 estados.


San Pablo, el distrito electoral con mas peso y centro económico más importante del país, queda en manos del mismo gobernador de la ultraderecha, Tarcísio de Freitas, que no es del partido del Bolsonaro PL, sino de otro de la derecha, República. author: CMI Argentina
title: Claudio Katz: “Hay que construir la izquierda para derrotar a Milei”
content:
Tras la repercusión de la Marcha de la Bronca, Claudio Katz analizó el rol de la izquierda en la coyuntura actual, donde juegan cada vez más fuerte dos variables: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico.


Las incógnitas sobre el peronismo, la apuesta del establishment a perpetuar el esquema de ajuste, explotación laboral y saqueo del país que logró establecer durante la actual gestión, la impunidad de la Corte Suprema y la agresividad del imperialismo estadounidense en la región son datos ineludibles del escenario presente ante los cuales la izquierda deberá plantearse nuevas tácticas y compromisos, consideró Katz, si quiere llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder.


Indymedia: – ¿Cómo ves el papel de la izquierda luego de la Marcha de la Bronca?


Claudio Katz:

 – Está cumpliendo un papel muy positivo ante todo en la acción callejera. La marcha fue un éxito

 por la

 concurrencia y el impacto de un acto político, que traspasó la resistencia social y democrática a los atropellos de Milei. Contrastó frontalmente con la capitulación de la CGT que deja pasar el ajuste.


La movilización alcanzó el nivel más alto de una convocatoria de

la izquierda. Superó lo conseguido con la “Plaza del No” en los años 90 y con las grandes concentraciones que en el pasado articulaba el

PC. Exhibió un nivel de politización muy superior a las marchas piqueteras e ilustró nuevamente cómo gravita la izquierda en las coyunturas de inmovilidad del peronismo.


Esa indefinición del justicialismo se vio por ejemplo cuando ganó Alfonsín, durante el neoliberalismo de Menem o en la época de Alianza. Actualmente, vuelve a aflorar por momentos y por eso hubo cierta presencia de militantes o simpatizantes del peronismo en la marcha. Igualmente te diría que el dato más significativo fue la centralidad de Myriam

Bregman. La movilización consolidó su protagonismo y la consiguiente incidencia de la izquierda en las próximas elecciones.


Indymedia: –

Pero cuál es la proyección electoral efectiva de Myriam, porque las encuestas resaltan una imagen muy positiva sin equivalencia en la intención de voto…


Claudio Katz: – Hay infinitas especulaciones sobre esa relación y no tiene mucho sentido obsesionarse con el tema, cuando falta más de un año para la elección. El número de votos que lograría el FIT-U depende de escenarios muy

abiertos con dos variables centrales: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico, que podría repetir lo ocurrido tantas veces en la Argentina.


Foto:

Nicolas Solo ((i))


Nadie sabe si el gobierno podrá sostener el tipo de cambio hasta el 2027. La recesión, la pobreza y el endeudamiento podrían desencadenar el mismo tipo de rebelión que sepultó a De la Rúa o la protesta masiva que derrotó a Macri. No cabe duda que la izquierda estará en la primera línea de ese eventual estallido.


Pero en cualquier caso su crecimiento dependerá de lo que suceda con el peronismo y en ese campo hay varios cursos posibles de división o cohesión y de amoldamiento conservador o resurgimiento progresista.


Por el momento se verifica una gran fractura en el justicialismo, entre corrientes de adaptación y crítica al modelo que la clase dominante apuntala con Milei. En general predomina la postura de no decir nada a la espera de lo que más conviene. Pero mientras tanto, un fascista como Cúneo participa del espacio de Kicillof, que a su vez emite mensajes de adaptación tipo Alberto Fernández y elude comentarios básicos de denuncia del genocidio de Palestina. Pero lo que haría como presidente es un misterio. Conviene recordar que nadie imaginaba el giro progresista de Néstor y Cristina antes del 2001 y sería un error ignorar la recomposición que logró el peronismo al calor de la gestión kirchnerista.


Indymedia: –

 ¿Por qué importa ese dato?


Claudio Katz: – Porque conforma el escenario en el que actúa la izquierda. Desconociendo ese hecho es muy difícil desenvolver estrategias para derrotar a Milei, revertir el ajuste y reconquistar los derechos populares. Ese camino transita por llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder, mediante frentes comunes y acuerdos de lucha con los sectores dispuestos a reconstruir el país, apostando a un gobierno que en sus primeros días de gestión revierta de un plumazo todo lo hecho por Milei.


Foto:

Nicolas Solo ((i))

title: Antiimperialistische Aktionswoche 7. - 11. Oktober
content:
Aufruf zur Antiimperialistischen Aktionswoche


💥Vor fast einem Jahr sind in Bern tausende Menschen zusammengekommen, um ein Ende des Genozids in Gaza und ein freies Palästina zu fordern. Und die Schweizer Kompliz*innenschaft dabei zu konfrontieren. Der Widerstand auf den Strassen Berns war kräftig und gebündelt. Verständlich, nachdem wir in Lausanne, Genf, Basel, Zürich, Lugano, Bern und so vielen anderen Orten verschiedene Unis besetzt und bereits unzählige Demos und andere Aktionen organisiert hatten, die ungehört blieben. Während der Genozid weiterhin geläugnet wurde. Unsere Wut über den Genozid in Gaza, die Kolonisierung Palästinas und den Imperialismus liess entsprechend die Strassen beben und verschlug dem Staat die Sprache. Er hatte keine andere Wahl, als sein wahres Gesicht zu zeigen und zu versuchen unseren Widerstand gewaltsam im Keim zu ersticken. Er hatte keine andere Wahl, als am Rattenschwanz zu ziehen, der der Öffentlichkeit als Verschärfungen der Repressionsmassnahmen und der Roadmap für nationale Sicherheit präsentiert wird.


👉Ob in Lugano, Genf, Lausanne, Bern, Zürich oder Basel: Überall spüren wir die Gewalt des Schweizer Staats. Er beschützt mit Schlagstock und Gummischrott auf Ausbeutung beruhendes System. Er beschützt - indem er unseren Aufstand unterdrückt - die Interessen der Grosskonzerne, welche Rekordprofite am Krieg, am Genozid und der Vernichtung unseres Planeten und dem Leben von hundertausenden von Menschen erzielen.


❤️‍🔥Doch wir lassen uns davon nicht einschüttern und bilden weiterhin überregional Banden! Wir lassen uns nicht beeindrucken von ihrer Propagandamaschinerie, wir lassen uns nicht beeindrucken von Bullen, Geheimdienst und sonstigen Taugenichtsen. Wir lassen uns im Gegenteil vom unbeugsamen Widerstand gegen die koloniale Kontinuität und den Imperialismus beeindrucken. Und darum rufen wir auf zur Antiimperialistischen Aktionswoche:

Vom 7.10. - 11.10.2026, vom Mittwoch bis zur grossen Demo am Sonntag.


✊Wir richten uns mit diesem Aufruf an alle Gruppen, Kollektive, Netzwerke, Einzelpersonen und Organisationen überall in und ausserhalb der Schweiz! Wir richten uns an all jene, die so unglaublich wütend sind, wie wir. Die wütend sind auf den Zustand dieser Welt. Lasst uns kreativ werden, organisieren wir Workshops, Filmevents, Theater oder Vorträge zu Austerität, Repression, Militarismus, Genozid, Zionismus, Klimakrise oder Imperialismus und vieles mehr, um der westlichen Propagandamaschinerie die Stirn zu bieten. Denn entgegen der Aussagen von Alec von Graffenried, sind wir weder ein Sauhaufen noch herrscht in Gaza Frieden! Lassen wir die Fassade der heilen und ach so gutmütigen Schweiz weiter bröckeln.


🇵🇸Lasst uns kreativ, bunt, laut und kämpferisch sein.


Wir alle sind Kinder derselben Wut.


Wir sehen uns am 11. Oktober um 15:00 Uhr auf den Strassen von Bern.

Vielleicht hast du noch andere kreative Ideen, wie wir für die Demo mobilisieren können? Umso besser, je mehr Ideen umgesetzt werden, desto grösser wird unsere Demo! author: ROAPE
title: What is the Real Marxist Tradition in Africa?
content:
John Molyneux’s classic statement of Marxist theory and practice

What is the Real Marxist Tradition

? was first published in 1984. The short book provided an incredibly sophisticated description of Marx’s method, and his relentless and insistent focus on the core agency of the working class.


Only the working class – however it is interpreted, described or labelled in social theory – can deliver a revolutionary anti-capitalist project. There cannot be, Molyneux argued, any substitute – no enlightened project of state development, or ‘socialist’ military leadership who deliver socialism on behalf of working people. Molyneux – in restating Marx’s central tenet – emphasised the role of the working class in their self-emancipation. Marx was the original prophet of the self-emancipation by working people. Without this class, and this project, there is simply no Marxism, no socialism, and no possibility of international revolution.


For an African audience the book speaks to multiple failed projects of socialism delivered by military coups, ‘enlightened’ governments and guerrilla movements. Each of these movements at different times dressed themselves in the language of Marxism, class and anti-imperialism but systematically broke genuine efforts at working class power.


What is the Real Marxist Tradition

? speaks directly to those on the continent trying to find a way to a genuine and emancipatory theory and practice of liberation.


Molyneux’ brilliant short book has now been reissued by the UK based publisher Bookmarks, and the Ugandan publisher Editor House Facility (EHF) who focus on readers across the African continent.


The new issue of the book comes with a major new introduction by the Ghanian socialist Gyekye Tanoh. Tanoh writes about the development and transformation of the working class on the continent since Molyneux wrote the book, and the continued capacity of this class to bring about socialist and revolutionary transformation across Africa.  


Join us for the launch of the African edition of

What is the Real Marxist Tradition?

 on 22 October at 18.30 (BST) with Gyekye Tanoh, Tafadzwa Choto

, 

Martin Empson and Mark Thomas. Reserve your place 

here

.


For readers based in Africa, John Molyneux’s 

What is the Real Marxist Tradition?

 can be purchased through Editor House Facility


here

. 


Endorsements of the book:


‘John Molyneux cuts through a century of distortion to recover Marxism’s authentic, revolutionary essence. This classic work distinguishes between living theory and dead orthodoxy, showing that Marxism is not a relic of the past but a vital method for understanding and transforming the world. It is essential reading for anyone seeking to understand capitalism and how to change it. For young activists and students alike, it is a must-read as it offers a powerful weapon for today’s struggles.’ 


Tafadzwa Choto

, International Socialist Organisation, Zimbabwe


‘In this book, John Molyneux undertakes a principled exercise by applying Marxism as a “method of analysis” to Marxism itself. He thereby provides not just a description of what Marxism is, but a method for detecting what isn’t. His application of this exercise—in the form of an autopsy of the interests and classes represented by three self-proclaimed Marxist tendencies—provides a valuable model for defining Marxist politics and organizations in our own contexts while enabling us to avoid the “hybrid ideologies of the petty bourgeoisie.” This is crucial, for us in the Global South, where reality differs greatly from that of Europe, thereby demanding a Marxism of contextualized design, not rigid imitation. The method offered is therefore a vital tool in enabling Marxist projects capable of fulfilling its role in “guiding revolutions to victory.” Such is true whether in the Global South or in global contexts marked by increasing economic complications and the co-option of Marxism by bourgeois ideologies fighting for survival amid the clear failure of neoliberal models … One need not agree with all of Molyneux’s conclusions to find his method a timely and indispensable resource.’


Muzan Alneel

,Marxist researcher and writer from Sudan

What is the Real Marxist Tradition in Africa?

title: «12 de Octubre, nada que celebrar»: pueblos originarios marchan contra los desalojos y la extranjerización de la tierra
content:
Marcha del Contrafestejo del 12 de octubre de 2024. Foto: archivo Nicolás Parodi / Página 12


Bajo la consigna “¡Nada que celebrar, muchas luchas que sostener!”, la Organización de Comunidades y Pueblos Originarios (ORCOPO) convocó a una marcha y contrafestejo para este lunes 12 de octubre, a las 18, en Plaza de los Dos Congresos. La jornada de lucha denunciará el avance de los desalojos, la criminalización de las comunidades indígenas, la extranjerización de la tierra, los proyectos extractivistas, la entrega, el saqueo y el despojo, en un escenario de creciente conflictividad territorial luego del reciente fallo de la Corte Suprema. La convocatoria se da en el marco de la confirmación judicial del desalojo de la Lof Inalef, en Río Negro, y una nueva amenaza contra la Lof Melo, en Neuquén. Ambos casos se suman a otros conflictos territoriales que atraviesan comunidades originarias en distintas regiones del país y que, para las organizaciones indígenas, evidencian una ofensiva sobre sus territorios en paralelo con el desmantelamiento de herramientas de protección y la reactivación de la derogación de la Ley de Tierras Rurales. También exigen justicia por Rafael Nahuel y libertad para quienes permanecen detenidos por luchar.

Por ANRed.

Aunque el máximo tribunal fundamentó su resolución en la falta de legitimación del Centro de Ex Combatientes Islas Malvinas La Plata (CECIM) para promover la demanda y no resolvió la constitucionalidad del decreto, su decisión volvió a dejar sin efecto los límites específicos a la extranjerización establecidos por la ley.

los efectos del artículo 154 del DNU 70/23 (el cual había derogado la Ley de Tierras Rurales), por lo que vuelven a regir temporalmente los límites a la compra de tierras por parte de extranjeros

. Sin embargo, se volvió a instalar una

.

Río Negro

la comunidad informó que la Cámara de Apelaciones en lo Civil de Bariloche confirmó la sentencia que ordena el desalojo de su territorio

title: Çelik: No budget’ for students’ demands, yet 7.4 billion TL transferred to foundations
content:
As universities begin the autumn semester of the 2026–2027 academic year, a student at Istanbul Technical University (ITÜ) was expelled from a dormitory run by the Credit and Dormitories Institution (KYK) on the grounds that they had failed to pass the preparatory year in a single semester. With nowhere to stay, the student was forced to take refuge in the university library for days. They are now trying to continue their education while working to support themselves.


The experience of the ITÜ student is one example of the problems faced by thousands of students who are forced to work to continue their education, only to be labelled academically unsuccessful as a result and deprived of their right to housing.


Being a university student in Turkey is increasingly becoming less an educational experience and more a struggle for survival. The monthly scholarship or student loan of 4,000 TL (some 73 euros) provided to undergraduate students by the Ministry of Youth and Sports is not even enough to cover their basic needs, particularly in the face of rental prices and living costs in major cities.


Students forced working while studying


Rapidly rising rents for private dormitories and apartments in major cities have made KYK dormitories virtually the only housing option for students. Unable to receive sufficient financial support from their families due to the deepening economic crisis, students are forced to work in insecure and harsh conditions to make ends meet. When they cannot devote enough time to their studies as a result, the system labels them “unsuccessful”. This “failure” is then punished by depriving them of one of the most fundamental human rights: the right to housing.


ANF spoke with Senem Çelik of the

We Cannot Afford to Live Movement

, which has been working for days to bring the expulsion of an ITÜ student from a KYK dormitory to public attention, about the housing crisis and poverty experienced by students.


Referring to the mother who appealed for help on Instagram for her son, who had been expelled from his dormitory, saying, 'I don’t want my son to be left on the street. He hadn’t slept for two days, and neither have I,' Senem Çelik described what had happened: “Recently, we heard the desperate plea of a mother who explained that her child had been expelled from the dormitory for having to repeat a year. A fellow student at ITÜ has been trying to get through each day and continue their education since the semester began, sometimes staying in the library and sometimes at friends’ homes. The reason our fellow students have had to continue their education this way is that they have been forced to work while studying, which in turn has meant having to repeat the year.”


Stating that the

We Cannot Afford to Live Movemen

t has been working for years to bring the housing crisis facing young people to public attention and secure concrete gains for students, Senem Çelik said the housing problem could not be explained solely through economic indicators. She pointed out that the way university bureaucracies operate, treating students as secondary concerns, and their proposed solutions, which run counter to the ordinary realities of life, further deepen the injustices students experience.


Çelik said university students face not only housing difficulties and poverty but also declining educational quality, the failure of democratic mechanisms within universities to function, sexism in academia and harassment. She added that these problems cannot be considered separately from the deep poverty and the condition of being “excluded from citizenship” experienced by broad sections of society.


Senem Çelik said: “For example, struggles against the injustices experienced by students affected by earthquakes require us to connect with all citizens whose needs are ignored for the sake of profit and to support their struggles. Campaigns against poor living conditions in student dormitories bring together all students who cannot afford to heat their homes with natural gas or even pay for their meals.”


She added: “Alongside the exclusion of the public from all mechanisms of governance and oversight, students at universities, which should be centres of science and free thought, are increasingly being excluded from all decision-making and oversight mechanisms as universities are privatised and run like companies. Students do not even have a say in matters concerning their own living spaces in the dormitories …
