author: Helmut Weiss
title: „Was wir nicht verdienen, zahlen wir nicht“ – eine landesweite Initiative in Spanien organisiert Mietstreik
content:
Dossier


„…

Es ist wahrlich kein Aprilscherz. Am 1. April 2020 treten nun viele Familien, Selbstständige sowie kleine und mittlere Firmen im ganzen spanischen Staat in den Mietenstreik. Mietergewerkschaften, wie sie ausgehend von Katalonien ab 2017 wie das „Sindicat de Llogaters i Llogateres“ gegründet haben, und soziale Organisation rufen zum Streik gegen fehlende Notmaßnahmen der sozialdemokratischen Regierung für die einfache Bevölkerung auf. Die 200 Initiativen schlagen vor, ab April die Miete nicht mehr zu bezahlen. (…) Eigentlich hatten sich die Mietergewerkschaften wegen explodierender Mieten gegründet. Sie forderten bisher vor allem stärkere Mieterrechte und eine Regulierung der explodierenden Mieten, vor denen spanische Gesetze praktisch nicht schützen. Einige der Aktivisten hatten Hoffnungen in die neue Regierung gesetzt, doch sie wurden massiv enttäuscht

…“ – aus dem

Beitrag „Mietenstreik wegen Coronavirus in Spanien“ von Ralf Streck am 01. April 2020 bei telepolis


 über die landesweite Initiative. Siehe dazu die weitere Entwicklung und Hintergründe:


„Ni una Maricarmen más“: Zwangsräumung der 87-jährigen Maricarmen Abascal treibt massive Proteste gegen Wohnungsnot und Mietwucher über Madrid hinaus an 


Die 87-jährige Maricarmen, deren Zwangsräumung die Bewegung in Spanien radikalisiert hat, ist vor der erkämpften Rückkehr in ihre Wohnung erschöpft gestorben 


„

Die 87-Jährige ist am Mittwoch im Krankenhaus Gregorio Marañón in Madrid verstorben, wie die Mietervereinigung in einer Erklärung bestätigte (…) In dieser Erklärung, die auch von ihrer Familie und ihrer Anwältin unterzeichnet wurde, erinnern sie daran, dass sie seit der Zwangsräumung im Krankenhaus lag. „Zwar wurde eine historische Einigung erzielt, die ihr die Rückkehr in ihre Wohnung ermöglicht hätte, doch diese Lösung kam viel zu spät“, bedauern sie. Die Unterzeichner sind der Ansicht, dass die Ereignisse nach ihrer Zwangsräumung – Massendemonstrationen, Zeltlager auf den Plätzen, vorgezogene Wahlen und der Aufruf zu einem Generalstreik – „einen Wendepunkt in der Geschichte dieses Landes“ darstellen, warnen jedoch, dass „der Preis, den wir dafür gezahlt haben, zu hoch war“. Und sie verabschieden sich mit der Bitte, die sie ihnen immer wieder gesagt hat: „Kämpft, kämpft weiter für das, was euch gehört.“


Dank des gesellschaftlichen Drucks stand zum ersten Mal in Spanien eine zwangsgeräumte Person kurz davor, in ihr Zuhause zurückzukehren, nachdem der Eigentümer bereit war, einen neuen Mietvertrag abzuschließen. Dennoch hatten die Zwangsräumung und die vorangegangenen Versuche Maricarmen körperlich stark mitgenommen, sodass sie sich in ihren letzten Lebensjahren nur noch im Rollstuhl fortbewegen konnte und bei den alltäglichen Verrichtungen auf Hilfe angewiesen war. Hinter ihr lagen fast sieben Jahre gerichtlicher Auseinandersetzungen, um in ihrem Zuhause bleiben zu können. In den letzten Monaten hatte sich ihr körperlicher Zustand verschlechtert. Sie hatte an Muskelmasse verloren, hatte Schwierigkeiten beim Essen und sagte, dass sich sogar ihre Stimme verändert habe. „Es hat mich in jeder Hinsicht beeinträchtigt. Ich bin jetzt nicht mehr ich selbst“, erzählte sie zwei Tage, bevor sie ihr Haus verließ

…“ span.

Artikel von Lucía Franco und Beatriz Olaizola vom 7.10.2026 in El Pais online


 (maschinenübersetzt) und auch:


Der Verband der Mieterinnengewerkschaften ruft zu einer Schweigeminute und einem Generalstreik für Maricarmen auf


„

Heute, Freitag, um 12 Uhr mittags an allen Arbeits- und Bildungseinrichtungen im ganzen Land. Der Aufruf des Verbandes der Mieterinnengewerkschaften erfolgt, nachdem sich die PP und Vox am Donnerstag geweigert hatten, in der Madrider Regionalversammlung eine Schweigeminute für Maricarmen einzulegen, mit der Begründung, sie wollten „nicht zu ihrer politischen Instrumentalisierung“ in einer „interessengeführten Kampagne“ beitragen, obwohl gerade die Verstorbene selbst dazu aufgerufen hatte, für die politische Sache gegen Zwangsräumungen und für menschenwürdigen Wohnraum zu kämpfen und sich zu mobilisieren. (…) Deshalb bitten wir dich, alle Arbeitnehmerinnen und Arbeitnehmer sowie die gesamte Gesellschaft, morgen, Freitag, um 12 Uhr mittags an allen Arbeits- und Bildungseinrichtungen des Staates eine Schweigeminute einzulegen. Außerdem bitten wir dich, dich darauf vorzubereiten, dass wir am 11. November einen historischen Generalstreik durchführen. Wir werden nicht aufhören, bis wir alles verändert …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: The Greens Are Still Relevant. They Just Need a Strategy
content:
Labour has held on in former prime minister Keir Starmer’s vacated seat of Holborn and St Pancras – a constituency the party has never lost since its creation in 1983 – with Green leader Zack Polanski coming in second. Camden council leader and Starmer ally Sagal Abdi-Wali won 45% of the vote, down 3.75% on Labour’s 2024 general election result, while the Greens more than tripled their vote share, taking 33%.


There are certainly some reasons for optimism among Green supporters this morning, while Polanski is asked on the mainstream media round if he’ll now be standing down as party leader until all our ears bleed. (Answer, no he won’t.)


The Cortado


          Get your shot of political analysis from

Ash Sarkar

 and

Steven Methven

, every Monday and Friday morning.


First name:


Email:


I agree to the

Privacy Policy


      Sign up error:

. Try again later.


      Thanks for signing up.


The Greens took more of the vote last night than their combined 2024 vote share with Starmer’s nearest challenger, the independent and former South African MP Andrew Feinstein. The local campaign group born out of Feinstein’s challenge to Starmer on his record on Gaza, the Camden People’s Alliance, endorsed Polanski this time around.


While turnout was down on the last election – 2024’s “loveless landslide” – at 39% compared to 54%, we saw a 13% Labour to Green swing.


Ultimately, around 3,000 votes separated the victorious Abdi-Wali (12,292) and Polanski (8,928), and prime minister Andy Burnham can breathe a sigh of relief that the first major electoral test to his premiership is won.


There’s no doubt that Abdi-Wali benefitted from the ‘Burnham bounce’. She might be smiley and local, but her council carries

an appalling record on housing

 in the borough – a brief she was directly responsible for as Camden’s former housing lead – and she was tainted by her association with Starmer and the Starmite project that,

according to a valuable

 two-part

Tribune deep-dive

, birthed her candidacy.


There was something vaguely nauseating about Abdi-Wali campaigning on a message of “hope” for the people of Holborn and St Pancras when

on top of being council leader

 from May of this year, her party has always held the seat – including with a sitting prime minister. If Labour was going to bring hope to this constituency, it would’ve done it already.


But Abdi-Wali,

‘ming-vased’ by her party

, received remarkably little mainstream press scrutiny throughout the campaign (

remind you of anyone?

), as the – allow me a moment to adjust my chic tinfoil hat – political-media class closed ranks against the Greens.


The drop in last night’s

Lib Dem vote share

 alone can be taken as a suggestion of negative mobilisation against the Green party, who’ve weathered months of bad faith attacks after the political and media establishment swung back into action following

a Polanski tweet

 around the Golders Green stabbing.


Polanski’s personal approval ratings continue to show the strain, with the Green leader dipping four points below Nigel Farage on -28 in a

More in Common poll

 on Wednesday. The same pollster also has Westminster voting intention for the Greens

on 8%

, while

YouGov shows 11%

 – down from a March high of 21%. It’s unlikely that a deluge of

negative attention

 and the resurgence of an antisemitism narrative over the Greens’ recently-passed ‘Zionism is Racism’ conference motion will have helped matters, either.


While the result of this hotly-contested byelection was ultimately closer than the bookies’ odds (16/1 on Polanski yesterday) made out, Gorton and Denton this was not. The terrain has changed, and the Greens have not yet adapted quickly or robustly enough with it. Burnham in Number 10 requires a different approach for the party to

the one that worked

 under Starmer’s toxic premiership.


But

in her acceptance speech

 this morning, Abdi-Wali accepted key parts of the Greens’ electoral programme – public ownership of water and addressing the housing crisis. Polanski’s party is reshaping Labour in the face of everything the political and media elite can throw at it.


There’s no question of Green irrelevance, only of Green strategy. In my book, that’s a reason to be hopeful.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Xindian Eviction Case Illustrates Recurrent Dynamics
content:
A FORCED EVICTION case in Xindian has drawn concern from Taiwanese civil society, with long-term residents of a historic structure possibly forced to vacate it in the near future.

In particular, the eviction case revolves around the Tsai Jin-mu house, which has been inhabited by the Lai family for eighty years and was built by their grandfather, Tsai Jin-mu. The Lai family previously sought to seek cultural preservation status for the structure, as an example of architecture that dated to the Japanese colonial period. However, this was denied by the Cultural Bureau of the New Taipei City government in June, which concluded that the bricks used in the structure are similar in size to those that date from the Japanese colonial period, but that this could not prove that the structure indeed dated from then.

Other structures in the neighborhood have already been demolished, starting from 2006, because of the construction of the Liugong Canal. Nevertheless, the Lai family was unexpectedly sued in 2014, demanding the return of the land, having found out that the Irrigation Association had sold the land in 2012 to a developer for a low price without notifying. Although the Lai family had expressed a desire to purchase the land 60 years prior, at the time, the Irrigation Association had claimed that the land was government property that was hard to deal with.

Consequently, litigation over the property has been ongoing for over a decade. Though the Lai family has housing plates and taxation documents, and the house had a household registration and allowed for the payment of utility bills and taxes, the Lai family has lost many of the lawsuits it filed over the land. Among the justifications for the rulings were not filing applications for the land, though previously the Lai family had been ruled to have the rights to apply for the land.

In 2021, the Control Yuan published a report stating that the Irrigation Association had treated the land as unused in its auction process, which was procedurally incorrect. Experts on land use in Taiwan have highlighted the case as one that touches on issues of transitional justice, given that the dispute over the property rights stems from the various historical transitions Taiwan saw in the 20th century. Likewise, the International Tribunal on Evictions has raised concerns about the case.

The residents of the home have been successful in securing stays of demolition in the past. Nevertheless, it is possible that the Tsai Jin-mu House will prove to be a case similar to when other communities were forced out of their homes in Taipei, with examples in the past decade including the Huaguang Community and Daguan Community. Though the Lai family has hosted screenings and otherwise linked with Taiwanese civil society groups, there is not as much attention to cases of forced urban evictions as there was in the years prior to the Sunflower Movement, even with a KMT mayoral administration in charge of New Taipei. What comes next remains to be seen.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "She Put Her Body on the Line": Maricarmen, 87, Dies; Her Eviction Sparked Spain Housing Protests
content:
The 87-year-old pensioner in Spain whose eviction from her lifelong home sparked nationwide protests has died. María del Carmen Abascal, better known as Maricarmen, died on Wednesday just hours before she was set to sign a new rental agreement. She was forcibly removed from her Madrid apartment last month on a stretcher after the private investment company that owns the building hiked her rent. After massive public outcry, the landlord had agreed to allow her back into her apartment.


Independent Spanish journalist María Carrión says that although Maricarmen’s story galvanized much of the country, evictions like hers are “a daily occurrence” in Spain.


“Rents have gone up 80% in the last 10 years, while salaries have not kept up,” Carrión says. “Young people cannot leave their homes. They cannot become independent or start families. And this is what people are trying to change from the street.”

title: Das Projet-Evasions braucht Cash Money
content:
Das Projet-Evasions ist ein mehrsprachiges Netzwerk anarchistischer Freundschaften, das seit 2019 besteht. Nach sieben fröhlichen Jahren, in denen wir unsere kleinen Aktivitäten* durchgeführt haben, ist es nun an der Zeit, euch um Unterstützung zu bitten.


Mit „kleinen Aktivitäten“ meinen wir: Dinge zu tun, in denen wir Sinn, emanzipatorisches und revolutionäres Potenzial sowie anarchistische Perspektiven sehen. Mit „Dingen“ meinen wir die Erstellung zahlreicher Inhalte (Bücher, Broschüren, Artikel, Podcasts, Audio-Clips, Aufkleber, Zeitschriften, Postkarten, Spiele, Ausstellungen, Plakate), die Durchführung von

Workshops und Präsentationen,

Wir erstellen Inhalte, weil wir diese teilen wollen, sowie Werkzeuge, die andere Menschen nutzen können. Meistens erstellen wir unsere Inhalte selbst, manchmal arbeiten wir aber auch mit externen Personen zusammen. Wir geben alle gedruckten Versionen zum frei wählbaren Preis heraus; jede Person kann frei entscheiden, je nach ihren eigenen Möglichkeiten, was sie dafür geben kann und will. Parallel dazu sind alle

digitalen Versionen

 unserer Produktionen kostenlos auf unserer Website verfügbar.


Das Geld, das wir haben, wird größtenteils für die Druckkosten verwendet. Auch wenn wir hauptsächlich mit einer befreundeten Druckerei zusammenarbeiten, die uns unglaublich unterstützt, bleiben die Druckkosten unser größter Ausgabenposten. An zweiter Stelle stehen die Versandkosten, die jedes Jahr steigen. Bei Sendungen ins Ausland sind die Porto- und Zollgebühren oft höher als die Druckkosten der Publikation, die wir verschicken. Daneben kaufen wir auch regelmäßig Bücher und andere selbstveröffentlichte Publikationen, die wir zum freien Preis weitergeben, und in den besten Zeiten unserer Finanzlage konnten wir mehrmals inhaftierte Anarchist*innen und Projekte, die auf der Suche nach Geld waren, unterstützen sowie in seltenen Fällen einen Teil unserer Reisekosten und unserer Arbeitzeit finanzieren. An letzter Stelle unserer Ausgaben stehen die Kosten für unsere Website und ein paar logistische Kleinigkeiten.


Zum Zeitpunkt der Abfassung dieses Textes beläuft sich unser Kontostand auf genau 741 Schweizer Franken und 123 Euro, und wenn wir ihn wieder auffüllen möchten, dann deshalb, weil wir mehrere Projekte haben, die bald bereit sein werden, in den Druck zu gehen. author: Joshua Carroll
title: Journalists Arrested Under Terrorism Act at Protest Against Israeli Arms Company
content:
Police in Leicester arrested at least five journalists under the Terrorism Act while they were reporting on a protest outside a drone factory owned by an Israeli arms company.


The

journalists

 were detained for two hours last Thursday at a UAV Tactical Systems factory

owned by

 Elbit Systems, which makes weapons that are used in Israel’s genocide in Gaza.  


Those arrested included two reporters for the Leicester Gazette and three freelance photojournalists. Police only let them go once they shared information to prove they attended the protest in their capacity as journalists, Press Gazette reported. 


A photographer who goes by the name Just Barold on social media was

among those detained

. 


“Multiple journalists including myself were arrested under section 13 of the Terrorism Act for going to work,” he wrote. “An officer told me that I would be de-arrested as soon as I gave my details despite identifying myself as a journalist with a press card.


“Our arresting officer was unable to articulate what caused the suspicion but it did instantly vanish when they got my name, address and date of birth.” 


Press advocacy group Reporters Without Borders said in a statement that it was “deeply concerned to hear of the arrest of journalists covering a protest in Leicester, particularly given they had identified themselves as such to police.”


It added: “No journalist should have to weigh the risk of arrest against their duty to inform the public. If reporters cannot cover protests freely, the public is left in the dark about events it has a right to know about. Policing and government must ensure that journalists are free to do their jobs without interference.”


In total, police

arrested 35 people

 at the protest under section 13 of the Terrorism Act. Some of the protesters held signs reading, “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action”. The proscribed group has frequently targeted and damaged factories owned by Elbit Systems.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Protesters Say India's Democracy Is "Rotten" as Modi Gov't Purges Voter Rolls, Arrests Thousands
content:
Tens of thousands of people in India have taken to the streets in recent days to protest the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls, a large majority of which are believed to be opposed to Narendra Modi’s ruling

BJP

 party. The demonstrations, joined by leaders from India’s opposition parties, are being led by students and the youth-led

“Cockroach” movement

. Tens of thousands of security forces, including paramilitary and police, were out on the streets over the weekend cracking down on the uprising, detaining protesters en masse, including lawyers, journalists and protest leaders.


The demonstrations “represent an outpouring of anger, of frustration at what many Indians feel is the fact that their democracy has been taken away,” says Shoaib Daniyal, political editor of

Scroll

, who was arrested on Saturday along with 7,000 other protesters. He points out that “the deletions have affected Muslims far more than they have affected other Indians.”


On Monday, in one of largest recent protests in India’s capital of New Delhi, India’s main opposition leader, Rahul Gandhi of the Congress Party, led a march to the Supreme Court of India. “This march has become a people’s march, with all of them heading towards this constitutional authority, which they feel should safeguard the rights of Indian people, especially this very basic right to vote,” says Jahnavi Sen, managing editor of

The Wire

.

author: anred
title: Córdoba: desbordan los talleres y se prepara la marcha del 39° Encuentro Plurinacional
content:
Foto: prensa del 39 Encuentro Plurinacional


En el segundo día del Encuentro Plurinacional de Mujeres, Lesbianas, Travestis, Trans, Bisexuales, Intersexuales y No Binaries, los talleres debieron desdoblarse ante la masiva participación. Este domingo, la agenda continúa con asambleas y actividades culturales, mientras crece la expectativa por la marcha que recorrerá las calles de Córdoba desde las 18.

Por ANRed


La ciudad de Córdoba es escenario de una nueva jornada de debates, organización y actividades culturales en el marco del 39° Encuentro Plurinacional de Mujeres y Diversidades. Desde distintos puntos del país y de la región, miles de encuentreras y encuentreres participan de los talleres, que debieron desdoblarse en múltiples oportunidades para dar lugar a la cantidad de personas presentes.


Durante este domingo concluyó la segunda ronda de diálogo y comenzaron los preparativos para elaborar las conclusiones, que serán leídas este lunes durante el acto de cierre. En paralelo, continúan desarrollándose asambleas, propuestas culturales e iniciativas impulsadas por activistas y colectivas en distintos puntos de la ciudad.


La jornada del sábado estuvo marcada por la marcha contra los travesticidios, transfemicidios y transhomicidios, que reunió a activistas y organizaciones para denunciar las violencias que atraviesan las diversidades.


Una marcha para cerrar la jornada


A partir de las 18, las calles de Córdoba serán escenario de la marcha del 39° Encuentro, que partirá desde la intersección de Olmos y Maipú y avanzará hasta la avenida Concepción de Arenales, donde se realizará la festi-peña de cierre.


Según informó la organización, una delegación de compañeras de pueblos preexistentes abrirá el camino de la movilización mediante una ceremonia espiritual y política. La cabecera reflejará la participación de activistas, organizaciones sociales y políticas, colectivas y agrupaciones que formaron parte de la Comisión Organizadora.


Mientras los talleres avanzan hacia sus conclusiones, el Encuentro vuelve a poner en las calles la fuerza de la organización colectiva y el intercambio de experiencias, debates y luchas de mujeres y diversidades de distintos territorios.


La cobertura y las novedades de la jornada pueden seguirse a través de Instagram, en la cuenta @39encuentropluri.cba.

title: Gebze'de 10 Ekim anması: "Emek, barış ve demokrasi talebinde ısrarcıyız"
content:
Hasret Gültekin Kozan [email protected]

Gebze Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri'nin çağrısıyla Kent Meydanı'nda yapılan anmada, 11 yıl önce Ankara Gar Katliamı'nda yaşamını yitirenler anıldı. Açıklamada asıl sorumluların korunduğu vurgulanırken adalet mücadelesinden vazgeçilmeyeceği belirtildi.

10 Ekim Ankara Gar Katliamı'nın 11'inci yılında Gebze Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri'nin çağrısıyla Kent Meydanı'nda anma ve basın açıklaması gerçekleştirildi. Katliamda yaşamını yitiren 104 can için saygı duruşunda bulunuldu.

"10 Ekim'i unutma unutturma", "Katil IŞİD, işbirlikçi AKP" ve "Onlara sözümüz barış olacak" sloganlarının atıldığı anmada basın açıklamasını Eğitim Sen Kocaeli 2 No'lu Şube Başkanı Sinan Kaya okudu.

Kaya, 11 yıl önce ülkenin dört bir yanından savaşa karşı barışı, sömürüye karşı emeğin hakkını, baskıya karşı demokrasiyi savunmak için Ankara Garı önünde buluşulduğunu hatırlatarak, "IŞİD'in gerçekleştirdiği çifte bombalı saldırı sonucunda 104 arkadaşımızı, yoldaşımızı, canımızı yitirdik. 500'den fazla arkadaşımız yaralandı. Aradan 11 yıl geçti; acımız ilk günkü kadar taze, öfkemiz ilk günkü kadar diri" dedi.

Kaya, 10 Ekim'in yalnızca bir katliam değil, bu topraklarda barışı kalıcı kılmak isteyenlere yönelik alçakça bir saldırı olduğunu belirterek, "O gün katledilenler, savaşa karşı barışın sesini yükseltmek için oradaydı. Onlar biliyordu ki barış, yalnızca silahların sustuğu bir çatışmasızlık hâli değildir; adaletin, eşitliğin ve bir arada kardeşçe yaşama iradesinin adıdır" diye konuştu.

Açıklamada, ülkenin onlarca yıldır süren çatışmanın sona ermesi için yeniden tarihî bir eşiğin önünde olduğuna dikkat çekilerek, silahların bırakılması ve çatışmaların durması yönünde atılan adımların ülkenin demokratik geleceği açısından önemsendiği ifade edildi. Ancak gerçek ve kalıcı barışın yalnızca silahların susmasıyla kurulamayacağı vurgulanan açıklamada, "Evrensel ve kalıcı bir barış ancak sosyal adalet temeline dayanır" ilkesi hatırlatıldı.

Kürt sorununda kalıcı barışın, inkâr ve güvenlik politikalarıyla değil demokratik siyaset zemininde mümkün olduğunun savunulduğu açıklamada, barış sürecinin toplumun tüm kesimlerinin iradesine dayalı yürütülmesi gerektiği kaydedildi.

10 Ekim 2015'te katledilenlerin demokrasi, düşünce ve ifade özgürlüğü, örgütlenme ve toplanma hakkı için orada olduğuna dikkat çekilen açıklamada, halk hızla yoksullaşırken, gelir dağılımı adaletsizliği artarken itiraz eden herkesin terörle ve düşmanlıkla yaftalandığı bir düzen kurulmak istendiği belirtildi. Kayyım politikaları, seçilmiş belediye başkanlarının tutuklanması, grevlerin yasaklanması ve dijital sansürün yaygınlaşması bir aczin göstergesi olarak nitelendirildi.

Kaya, "11 yıldır adalet arıyoruz" diyerek yargılama süreçlerinde faillerin bir kısmının cezalandırılmış olsa da katliamın arkasındaki asıl sorumluların korunduğunu söyledi. Tüm istihbarat bilgilerine rağmen önlem almayanların, güvenlik bürokrasisindeki ihmallerin ortaya çıkarılmadığını ifade eden Kaya, "Devlet, başkentin ortasında, izinleri alınmış bir mitingde 104 insanın katledilmesinde dahi kendi sorumluluğunu kabul etmiyorsa, yarın herhangi bir kentte benzer bir katliam yaşanabilir ve yine 'bizim kusurumuz yok' diyebilir" diye konuştu.

Açıklamada, "Katliamın tüm sorumlularının açığa çıkarılması ve ihmali olan tüm kamu görevlilerinin yargılanması için yürüttüğümüz adalet mücadelemizden asla vazgeçmeyeceğiz. Emeğin, barışın ve demokrasinin egemen olduğu bir Türkiye'yi mutlaka kuracağız" ifadelerine yer verildi.

Açıklamanın ardından katliamda hayatını kaybedenlerin fotoğrafları yere serildi, üzerlerine karanfil bırakıldı ve oturma eylemi gerçekleştirildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Demonstrations in Europe demand freedom for Abdullah Öcalan
content:
Protests were held in cities across Europe to mark the anniversary of the 9 October International Conspiracy. Through marches, rallies and public information campaigns, Kurds and their supporters protested the international conspiracy and raised their voices for Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom.


DÜSSELDORF


A mass press statement and march were held in Düsseldorf, Germany, under the leadership of the European Kurdish Women’s Movement. Kurds and their supporters gathered outside Düsseldorf Central Station (Hauptbahnhof), chanting slogans including “Bê Serok Jiyan Nabe” (Life Without a Leader Is Impossible), “Bijî Serok Apo” (Long Live Leader Apo) and “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” (Woman, Life, Freedom). Alongside photographs of Leader Apo, demonstrators carried banners and placards demanding his freedom.


Before the press statement, a group of Iranian individuals reportedly attempted to provoke tensions at the gathering. The situation was calmed after representatives of the democratic Kurdish organisations organising the event intervened, while German police removed the group from the area.


 


The statement began with the Kurdish national anthem, “Ey Reqîb”, followed by a minute of silence. Ehmed Kobanê, Co-Chair of the NRW Federation, and Ayten Kaplan, speaking on behalf of the European Kurdish Women’s Movement, then addressed the crowd.


Kobanê stated that the 9 October International Conspiracy had targeted the Kurdish people's struggle, organisation and leadership. He said international law had been disregarded despite Leader Apo’s efforts to promote peace. Describing the process of building a democratic society and pursuing peace as an opportunity for the peoples of Turkey and the Middle East, Kobanê stressed that Leader Apo must be free for the process to succeed.


Ayten Kaplan said they were struggling to build a democratic society, secure recognition for all identities and cultures, and establish peaceful coexistence. Noting that Kurds had been criminalised in Germany for years, she said people were being arrested for demanding a peaceful solution to the Kurdish question and opposing war. Kaplan called on European states, particularly Germany, to fulfil their responsibilities and take steps to secure Öcalan’s freedom.


Following the speeches, demonstrators began a march carrying banners reading “Ji Rêber Apo re Azadî, ji Pirsgirêka Kurd re Çareserî” (Freedom for Leader Apo, a Solution to the Kurdish Question) and “Die Zeit ist gekommen – Freiheit für Abdullah Öcalan, Frieden in Kurdistan!” (The Time Has Come – Freedom for Abdullah Öcalan, Peace in Kurdistan!). The march continued along Düsseldorf’s Königsallee boulevard and concluded with slogans calling for freedom and a democratic solution.


BERN


Kurds and their supporters gathered at Weissenplatz in Bern, the capital of Switzerland, to protest the 9 October International Conspiracy and demand  Öcalan’s physical freedom. A banner reading “Freedom for Öcalan, Status for Kurdistan” was displayed, while demonstrators chanted “Bijî Serok Apo” and “Freedom for Öcalan”.


Following a minute of silence in memory of the martyrs of the Kurdistan Freedom Struggle, Dilan Çetinkaya, Co-Chair of the Swiss Democratic Kurdish Community Centres (CDK-S), addressed the rally.


 


Çetinkaya stated that the 9 October conspiracy had targeted not only Leader Apo but also the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom. She said that, despite 28 years having passed, the conspiracy had failed to achieve its objectives. Highlighting the decisive role played by Öcalan’s resistance on İmralı Island in the Kurdish struggle, she stressed that his physical freedom was necessary for the Peace and Democratic Society Process to move forward.


Hekîm Hetûtî, a representative of PJAK, also spoke at the rally. He stated that the international conspiracy had aimed to break the Kurdish people’s will for freedom and dismantle their struggle. Hetûtî said Leader Öcalan’s ideas and paradigm had also played a decisive role in the freedom struggle in Rojhilat Kurdistan (Eastern Kurdistan). He drew attention to repression against Kurds in Iran and the situation of political prisoners held in its prisons. Hetûtî called for the struggle to be intensified across all four parts of Kurdistan and throughout Europe.


Sema Doruk, speaking on behalf of TJK-E; Robin Klein, representing Rise Up for Rojava; and Kurdish politician Serhed Agirî also addressed the rally. The speakers condemned the international conspiracy …

author: groundxero
title: Blackboxes and Such: New Delhi on the Eve of 10 October, and the Seeds of India’s Undeclared Neo-Emergency
content:
The administrative streets of central New Delhi have now become a terrifying labyrinth of surveillance and armed lockdown – except for the VIP residents who live there, and the exotic nightly businesses that entertain them.

Mouli Sharma

 report on New Delhi on the eve of October 10.


 


10 October 2026, New Delhi:

 At the stroke of the midnight hour on Saturday in the administrative district of India’s capital, a quiet terror overtook the once – illusorily – safe expanse.


 


Preparations for the coming morning’s protest call, for people to take the streets all over the capital, not just the “designated” protest site of Jantar Mantar that has now become a designated “detention” site with an indefinite application of the controversial Section 163 (which empowers district and other magistrates to issue ‘special prohibitory orders’ and temporarily suspend constitutional freedoms in a given region during ’emergencies’) that has since expanded to the India Gate region, the Kashmere Gate region, and then through 54 other localities over ten days of continued protests, began early in the morning a day prior.


 


First, the office of the Joint Commissioner of Police (Transport Range) at Jai Singh Road issued an unprecedented order for the indefinite suspension of Metro rail entry and exit ways (as well as a reduction of train frequencies) in an unprecedented 57 stations, due to ostensible (and unspecified) suspicions of “mob movement”.


 


“In view of the proposed protests at Jantar Mantar and other locations in New Delhi District in 10.10.2026 and the likelihood of unruly mob movement towards sensitive locations, frequency of Metro trains passing through the following Metro stations may be reduced and their entry/exit gates may be closed from 9:00 PM on 09.10.2026, continuing on 10.10.2026 till the situation normalises,” said the notice issued to the Managing Director of the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), Vikas Kumar on Friday.


 


A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymlayla Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was hearing the petitions challenging the curbs imposed in Delhi, and observed on the same day that the total shutdown of the services would affect the rights of citizens who are entitled to avail them. But these services nevertheless remained closed from 9PM onwards, at least within the New Delhi region.


 


Next was a network blackout. Internet services were suspended in a 4km radius extending from the Jantar Mantar protest site an hour after the transport lockdown. A “top secret” circular from the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police Special Cell, Manishi Chandra, instructing private service providers including Airtel, VI, Jio, along with MTNL Delhi to indefinitely suspend internet services in the region began circulation during the late evening of the 9th, and the over 50 kilometre square expanse was consequently turned into a complete blackbox.


 


***


 


Pushing 10 PM outside the barricading of the site nearest to the Kerala Bhawan, while the networks were still on, the police were bashful. The speakers hanging from trees announced that any violations of “the prohibitions under the order” issued under Section 163 of the BNSS would be punishable by law, but when asked what these prohibitions are, or if this order could be produced such that public could indeed heed its prohibitions, officers present at the scene stood clueless.


 


Come dawn, Vikas Meena, Harnit Singh Sudan and Bharat Bhushan pulled a few reporters to the side, reassuring them that no press would be detained or obstructed during the protests, provided that press themselves did not obstruct the detentions of common folk.


 


“We request that you stay far away and do your job,” Meena said. “If we are detaining someone, don’t try to stop us or come close to us or film what is happening. We have no problem with the press, but recently, journalists have started intervening in our processes and asking questions while we conduct our operations, which makes it difficult for us to distinguish them as press.”


 


When pushed on the precise details and prohibitions listed in the magisterial order, though, Meena repeats a familiar refrain: “Where is the order? It must be somewhere. You’ll have to ask the New Delhi DCP. I’m not from the district, so I don’t know.”


 


Ask at the station, though, over a hundred journalists have, but DCP Sachin Sharma has refused to respond in plain terms, and even …

title: Honduras kriminalisiert Proteste gegen den Anstieg der Benzinpreise und Reformen des Energiesektors
content:
„In mehreren honduranischen Städten haben in der vergangenen Woche Proteste gegen den Anstieg der Benzinpreise und Reformen des Energiesektors stattgefunden. (…) Für den 28. September hatte der Transportsektor zu Protesten aufgrund der hohen Benzinpreise aufgerufen. Den Protesten schlossen sich weitere Bevölkerungsteile an. In den Städten Tegucigalpa, San Pedro Sula und Villanueva sowie Choloma, Cofradía, El Progreso und Gracias de Lempira kam es zu Straßenblockaden und Besetzungen. Neben den Benzinpreisen stiegen auch die Preise für Grundnahrungsmittel im laufenden Jahr erheblich an, und eine Erhöhung der Strompreise wurde jüngst von der Regierung angekündigt. Die Kosten für den Warenkorb des Grundbedarfs in Honduras zählen im Verhältnis zur geringen Kaufkraft der Bevölkerung zu den höchsten des Kontinents. In den Städten Cofradía und Choloma im Department Cortés kam es zu Auseinandersetzungen zwischen Polizeieinheiten und Demonstranten…“

Beitrag von Johannes Schwäbl vom 7. Oktober 2026 in amerika21


 und mehr daraus:


Weiter aus dem

Beitrag von Johannes Schwäbl vom 7. Oktober 2026 in amerika21


 („Honduras kriminalisiert Proteste“):

„(…) Am 22. September verabschiedete der Nationalkongress das „Sondergesetz zur Bekämpfung terroristischer Vereinigungen, Maras und Banden sowie zur Stärkung des nationalen Strafvollzugssystems“. Dieses Gesetz weitet die strafrechtlichen Maßnahmen gegen als terroristisch eingestufte Strukturen aus und ist Teil der Umsetzung der von den USA unter der Bezeichnung „Escudo de las Américas“ (Schild der Amerikas) vorangetriebenen regionalen Sicherheitspolitik. Kritiker:innen bemängeln an dem Gesetz die ungenaue Definition der Straftatbestände und warnen davor, dass das Gesetz auch gegen indigene Organisationen, bäuerliche Verbände und Gemeinschaften eingesetzt werden könnte, die sich gegen den Raub der Gemeingüter und extraktivistische Projekte in ihren Gebieten zur Wehr setzen. Bereits im Mai und Juni hat die Regierung von Nasry Asfura das umstrittene Gesetz zur Stärkung und dem Schutz des agrarindustriellen Sektors (Dekret 107–2026) sowie Reformen der Strafprozessordnung (Dekret 84–2026) beschlossen. Im August wiesen Experten der Vereinten Nationen die Regierung von Honduras in zwei Mitteilungen darauf hin, dass sowohl das Gesetz als auch die Reformen der Strafprozessordnung nicht mit nationalen und internationalen Standards vereinbar seien. Dies betrifft die Definition des Straftatbestands der terroristischen Vereinigung. Dabei wird insbesondere die Gleichsetzung von organisierter Kriminalität und Terrorismus als kritisch gesehen.“


Der Beitrag

Honduras kriminalisiert Proteste gegen den Anstieg der Benzinpreise und Reformen des Energiesektors

author: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan
title: Wird es am 17. Oktober stattfinden?
content:
Spontane Kommentare zur aktuellen Schülerrevolte


1.


Die Schülerrevolte ist die Speerspitze der für den 17. Oktober angekündigten Bewegung.


2.


Die „Gruppen“ von Schülern aus Arbeitervierteln bilden die eigentliche treibende Kraft innerhalb und gegen die aktuelle Jugendbewegung. In gewisser Weise ist diese Kraft weniger Teil der Schülerbewegung als vielmehr die Fortsetzung der Revolte für Nahel. Sie hat weder Forderungen noch Vertreter, sie findet sich nicht in den Codes der Linken wieder und lehnt bürgerliche Höflichkeit ab. Sie will ihre Rache.


3.


Die Universitäten sind den Oberschulen gefolgt und haben sich der Dynamik der Blockaden angeschlossen. Sie könnten ihrerseits einen qualitativen Sprung bewirken, indem sie beispielsweise eine Besetzungsaktion starten, die von anderen Bereichen der Gesellschaft – ob Schüler oder nicht – aufgegriffen und weiterverbreitet werden könnte. Diese Hypothese wird jedoch durch die erdrückende Dominanz der studentischen Gewerkschaftsorganisationen vereitelt, die der Spontaneität der Gruppen, dem kollektiven Erfindungsreichtum und der auto-subversiven Praxis wenig Raum lassen.


4.


Wenn man von „Blockaden“ an den Oberschulen spricht, befindet man sich bereits in einer Form der Reduktion und Vereinfachung der Praktiken der Schülerrevolte. Es gibt Sabotageakte (angezündete Türen, umgestürzte Tore, „E-Blockaden“ gegen Fernunterricht) und Racheakte (gegen die Hierarchie in der Schule und die Polizei draußen), städtische Guerillataktiken (Barrikaden) und wilde Streiks (Arbeitsniederlegungen in den Pausen und zeitversetzte Blockaden), und schließlich etwas in der Art eines Spiels, das darauf abzielt, die Macht lächerlich zu machen (Slogans über Macron und seine Lehrerin, Superhelden-Verkleidungen im Gegensatz zu den Uniformen der Unterdrücker).


5.


Die Gewerkschaften können sich mit der Idee des 17. Oktober nicht anfreunden, da sie sie zu sehr an die Gelbwesten erinnert. Sie müssen vorgeben, sich der Bewegung anzuschließen, um besser die Kontrolle darüber zu erlangen – sowohl durch das Verhandlungsmonopol als auch durch die Entscheidung über den Zeitplan. Wenn l’intersyndicale zum 6. Oktober gemeinsam mit den Schülern aufgerufen hat, dann nur, um den Aufruf zum 17. Oktober besser zu entschärfen, den sie auf einen Zwischentermin vor ihrer Mobilisierung am 5. November reduzieren möchte.


6.


An den Oberschulen unterscheidet sich die Linke von den anderen politischen Kräften in der Form, nicht aber im Inhalt. In der Form drängt die Linke die Schüler in eine Opferrolle, wodurch sie sich als die „verantwortungsbewussten Erwachsenen“ präsentieren kann. Man denke an die Menschenketten aus Eltern und Lehrern oder auch an gewählte Vertreter, die den Einsatz von LBD-Waffen durch die Polizei anprangern. Dabei fällt auf, dass Schlagstöcke, Schutzschilde, Helme und andere übliche Bestandteile des Arsenals der Demokratie weitaus seltener in Frage gestellt werden.


7.


Inhaltlich schließt sich die Linke den anderen politischen Kräften in ihren Bemühungen um eine Befriedung an. Genau das geschieht, wenn sie Forderungen herausstellt, die mit ihrem Programm vereinbar sind, und damit gleichzeitig dazu beiträgt, die „guten“ Schüler (die als legitim erachtete Forderungen haben) von den „schlechten“ Schülern (diesen „Randalierern“ ohne Ideen oder echte politische Motive) zu separieren.


8.


Im Gegensatz zur Linken haben wir weder Fahnen, die wir schwenken könnten, noch ein Tempo, das wir vorgeben müssten, noch Lektionen, die wir erteilen müssten.


9.


Wie soll man mit der Begeisterung für den „17. Oktober“ umgehen und mit der Art und Weise, wie bestimmte Teile der Jugend ihn als Echo der Gelbwesten-Bewegung präsentieren? Auch wenn eine neue Generation seine symbolische Kraft voller Hoffnung zu beschwören scheint, ist es keineswegs sicher, dass das Wiederverwenden des Objekts uns helfen wird, seinen Geist wiederzufinden. Dennoch ist es vielleicht genau das, was von uns erwartet wird: es sich überzustreifen und zu sehen, ob es – wenn auch nur vorübergehend – ein Gefühl der Zugehörigkeit verkörpert, mit dem sich andere identifizieren und dem sie sich anschließen können, ohne es sich dabei anzueignen. Auf die Gefahr hin, lächerlich und anachronistisch zu wirken und es sofort wieder beiseitezulegen.


10.


Die spektakulären Aktionen der Schülerrevolte gehen auf das Konto von Banden, die sich organisieren und sich auf diese Weise zu erkennen geben. Das Tragen von Under-Armour-Outfits täuscht …

author: Unknown
title: Father of journalist Ahmet Polad: My son is not receiving medical treatment in prison
content:
Kurdish journalist Ahmet Polad (real name Mehmet Nizam Aslan) is not receiving adequate medical care at Marmara Prison in Silivri, in Istanbul, despite serious health problems. His father, Adil Aslan, who visited him on October 6, told Mezopotamya Agency (MA) about his son’s untreated injuries and the consequences of eight months in captivity under the Islamist group HTS in Syria. The journalist was handed over to Turkey’s National Intelligence Organization (MİT) in early September and subsequently imprisoned in Istanbul’s Metris Prison.


Months of uncertainty about his fate


Adil Aslan described the desperate search for his son, who had been abducted while working as a journalist in Syria. For a long time, the family did not know whether he was still alive. The first clues came from former prisoners. One eyewitness reported the abduction of Polad and his German colleague Eva Maria Michelmann. On April 11, a released prisoner confirmed having seen the journalist in detention. At the same time, the family learned that he had been injured. “For days, I did not know whether my son was still alive. The fact that former prisoners came forward as eyewitnesses gave us at least a little hope. I never gave up searching for him,” Adil Aslan said.


By late April, evidence increasingly suggested that Polad was being held captive by HTS. The family hired a lawyer in Damascus and issued a power of attorney through the Syrian consulate in Istanbul. According to his father, however, the documents were confiscated. HTS subsequently once again denied holding Polad captive. “We began to fear more and more that Mehmet had been killed. Those were extremely difficult days. His mother and I could not sleep at night.”


Handover to Turkish intelligence


On September 8, the family finally learned that Aslan had been taken to Idlib with his hands tied and his eyes blindfolded, where he was handed over to the Turkish National Intelligence Organization (MİT). “My son was forced to remain in MİT custody for two days with a sack over his head. After that, he was taken to the police in Ankara,” his father reported.


On September 11, Adil Aslan received a phone call from the Istanbul police. He was informed that his son was being held by the counterterrorism unit. Initially, he was denied permission to visit him. The journalist is now being held at Marmara Prison in Silivri, which is regarded as a detention facility for political opponents. As a confidentiality order has been imposed on his investigation file, the family still does not know the specific charges against him.


“Journalism is never a crime”


“Mehmet was detained in a place where he was conducting research for his reporting. When he was abducted, he had nothing with him except his camera,” Adil Aslan explained. He said that only civilians had been held in the cells and that nothing was known about their subsequent fate. The father condemned HTS violence against the people of Syria, referring in particular to the massacres of Alawites and Druze. “Two years ago, these people were still considered terrorists, and now they have supposedly formed a government. They oppress and massacre people.”


The father stated that his son had been subjected to physical and psychological torture during his eight months in captivity. “These are all crimes against humanity. We do not accept this. No one should accept it. Everyone must speak out. Journalism is never a crime,” he stated.


Polad forced to treat his own wounds


During his visit on October 6, Adil Aslan observed that his son’s health had continued to deteriorate. However, Polad was trying to downplay his condition to avoid worrying his family. “He says he is fine so that we won’t worry. But he still has shrapnel embedded in his hip. He went on a hunger and thirst strike for months, and his health is not good. He also suffers from scabies. He has not been taken to a hospital for treatment for any of these conditions.”


The journalist also has to care for his wounds himself. “When I asked him about his injuries, he told me that he changes the dressings himself. As a result, his wounds keep becoming infected.”


Finally, Adil Aslan appealed to the public and human rights organizations to stand up for the prisoners: “I call on all humanity to put an end to this oppression. There are many people in the same situation as us.”

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Indigenous Peoples' Day: Leonard Peltier on Resistance, New Film & Fighting for Freedom
content:
On Indigenous Peoples’ Day, we feature a conversation with one of the world’s most prominent champions for Indigenous rights, Leonard Peltier. “Indigenous Day is a day that’s been long overdue for any type of recognition,” says Peltier. “I am not going to give up, because we are not free yet. We are in danger. Trump and these organizations, they’re talking about doing away with our reservations and our treaties and everything else. … We’re going to stay here. You’re not going to get rid of us.”


Peltier is a longtime political prisoner who spent nearly half a century behind bars for a crime he says he did not commit — the 1975 fatal shooting of two

FBI

 agents. In the final hours of his administration last year, President Biden commuted Peltier’s sentence, but his conviction has not been overturned, and he remains under home confinement on the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Reservation in Belcourt, North Dakota.


“It was one crime against the justice system after another in order to frame Leonard for the assassination of these two federal agents,” says David France, co-director of the new documentary

Free Leonard Peltier

. “And although he and his team were able to prove over and over that every bit of evidence used against him in his conviction was brought into question, he was never able to get a retrial.”

Did the Science Wars Take Place? The Political and Ethical Stakes of Radical Realism By: William Gillis Center for a Stateless Society, 2025{1}

I follow William Gillis—veteran anarchist activist and writer, and trained physicist—on Bluesky because he’s funny, and because he makes me think. If you share his burning hatred for fascism, a sneering (remember that word) contempt for establishment liberalism, and deep disgust for Stalinists, “tankies” and other authoritarian Leftists, I’d recommend it. It also helps if you like Star Wars and Star Trek.

One reason why I enjoy his work is that he flips a lot of widely held assumptions about anarchist beliefs. For example, the clichéd response to the concept of prison/police abolition is that anarchists (or libertarian communists) must be foolish utopians who think that everyone is deep-down good. On the contrary, Gillis’s closely argued position is that some people are just plain “bad,” due to whatever combination of nature and nurture, but that these “bad” people are precisely the ones who will become cops and judges. Hence, abolition of those structures, and their replacement with informal social incentives based on game theory, is the only way to stop bad people.[1] It’s also fun, when you’re watching liberals discuss why “prison abolition” couldn’t work because the only alternative is lynch mobs, to toss in Gillis’s article on the moral imperative to Kill Your Local Rapist and see what happens.[2]

But I’ve always appreciated Gillis’s commitment to science as a concept and, more importantly, as a practice. We live in increasing conditions of “weaponised unreality”[3] where the ascendent form of “postmodern fascism” is built around not Blackshirts fighting in the streets but the creation of an “alternative reality” based on social media bubbles and captured mass-media outlets of the FOX/GB News variety, in which the downwardly mobile masses voluntarily segregate themselves. Expanding from its origins in Christian “creation science” and the tobacco industry, populist science denial has been weaponized over decades to prevent any serious attempt at mitigating climate change—and, more recently, has pushed forward from outrage at COVID-19 restrictions to “antivaxxers” apparently rejecting the germ theory of disease itself.

A strict adherence to scientific materialism used to be the common sense of the Marxist movement. In the era of the Industrial and Scientific Revolutions, with the world being turned upside down, the Communist Manifesto spoke enthusiastically about the possibility of “subjection of Nature’s forces.” The only problem was that the tools of science (and the fruits of its successes) were in the hands of the bourgeoisie, who had used it to defeat feudal oppression and were keeping it away from the exploited proletariat. In Ferdinand Lassalle’s famous phrase quoted by Rosa Luxemburg, the key to the golden future was to bring workers and science together.[4]

CRS et penn arm

Selon les personnes et les dossiers, les procureurs décident de relâcher sans suite ou de convoquer plus tard.

author: Craig Brittain
title: Lessons from jail: Barry York’s 'A Pentridge Memoir'
content:
A Pentridge Memoir: A political prisoner's story, including a history of the Victorian Prisoners' Action Committee 1973–1976 By Barry York Self-published Sept, 2026 RRP $34.95

In 1972, three student radicals from Melbourne’s La Trobe University — Barry York, Fergus Robinson and Brian Pola — were sent to Pentridge Prison for being in contempt of the Supreme Court of Victoria.

The three were seen as ringleaders of one of the radical student groups causing major problems for the authorities in the late 1960s and early ‘70s, during the Vietnam War.

There had been no trial, they’d been given no chance to defend themselves, and there’d been no sentencing. As far as they knew they were going to jail forever. A Pentridge Memoir: A political prisoner’s story is York’s personal account of this harrowing experience: what it was like to be sent to a high security prison for the “crime” of being an effective political activist on a university campus.

York, Robinson and Pola had been instrumental in organising mass meetings and protests against Australia’s involvement in the war. They staged anti-Apartheid protests against the all-white South African Springbok rugby team's tour, and contributed to the resignation of La Trobe University Chancellor, Sir Archibald Glenn, after he was exposed as being the managing director of Imperial Chemicals Industries (ICI). ICI was directly connected to Australia’s Vietnam War effort, and the Apartheid regime in South Africa.

La Trobe came up with a novel way of dealing with objectionable left-wing student leaders. “The La Trobe Three”, as they came to be known, were suspended from the university, but, on top of this, the University Council took out an injunction against them in the Supreme Court, barring them from setting foot on campus.

There were meetings and protests in support of the banned students. Even political enemies thought they’d been unfairly treated, and the Council was seen as interfering with students’ right to freedom of speech and assembly.

Naturally the La Trobe Three ignored the injunction, and were eventually arrested and incarcerated.

However, the administration’s bright idea of locking them up and throwing away the key backfired spectacularly. Against all odds, they stuck it out, and weren’t broken.

York vividly describes what prison was like for a young student who’d never even been in trouble with the police, let alone been in jail before:

“What stays with me most were the nights in A Division, locked in my cell, lights out, no escape — and the sounds echoing from H Division, the prison’s maximum security wing. Thuds. Kicks. Fists. Screams. The screws in H didn’t merely enforce discipline. They enjoyed inflicting pain on men who couldn’t fight back. They beat defenceless men — unarmed, caged.

“Then there was the crying. A prisoner in an observation cell in our own division, just wailing. Not weeping — wailing. Hour after hour, this long haunted howl of anguish that cut through everything. I couldn’t block it out; it became part of the atmosphere, the texture of the night.

“And I can’t forget the young man in the cell beside mine. He died during the night. Alone.”

York spent 44 days in prison; Robinson, 4 months; and Pola, 3 months.

York and Robinson were Maoists, members of the Communist Party of Australia (Marxist-Leninist), while Pola was a member of the Moscow-aligned Communist Party of Australia (CPA).

They came out stronger for the experience and were fortunate in being committed communists with knowledge of history and Marxist theory to support them. They understood jail was just another part of the class struggle.

They had a sense of identity and purpose that other prisoners didn’t have. They knew they were political prisoners and, as such, had something to live up to. They had committed no crime. They were in jail for protesting the crimes Australia was committing in an imperialist war; and the crimes of the university, as they saw it, denying freedom of speech and assembly to its students.

They didn’t give in. They never “purged” their contempt by apologising to the Supreme Court.

Eventually, La Trobe backed down. The Vice-Chancellor made an offer — which Ted Hill, their Communist lawyer, recommended they accept. They agreed to renounce violence (they’d never been in favour of violence and hadn’t committed any) on condition that the university also renounced violence — such as its use of police against protesting students. The university then …

content:
Marco Rubio | Fotoğraf: Gage Skidmore/Flickr CC BY-SA 2.0

Nobel Barış Ödülü’nün İsrail’in eylemlerini soykırım olarak tanımlayan eski Uluslararası Ceza Mahkemesi (UCM) yargıçlarından Navanethem Navi Pillay’a verilmesinin ardından ABD Dışişleri Bakanı Marco Rubio, mahkemeye yaptırım kararı aldıklarını açıkladı.

Yaptırım kararı alındığını sosyal medya hesabından duyuran Rubio, “Başkan Trump, UCM’nin Amerikalıları yargılamasına asla izin vermeyecektir. İşte bu nedenle bugün ABD, UCM’ye yaptırım uyguluyor. Mahkemenin üyesi değiliz ve bu mahkemenin Amerikan vatandaşları üzerinde herhangi bir yetkisinin olduğunu kabul etmiyoruz. Ya UCM tehditlerine son verecek ya da biz UCM'yi ortadan kaldıracağız. Bunu yapmazlarsa ABD, Amerikalılar tehdit altında kalmayana kadar UCM'yi adım adım yıkmaya devam edecektir” ifadelerini kaydetti.

Kararın Nobel Barış Ödülü’nün açıklanmasının ardından alınması ise dikkat çekti. Nobel Komitesi, 2026 Nobel Barış Ödülü'nü barışın ve uluslararası hukukun geliştirilmesine yönelik çabaları nedeniyle Birleşmiş Milletler’in (BM) eski İnsan Hakları Yüksek Komiseri ve Uluslararası Adalet Divanı yargıcı Navanethem Navi Pillay’a verdi. Güney Afrika’daki apartheid rejimine karşı mücadele eden Pillay, Uluslararası Ceza Mahkemesinden İsrail’in Gazze’deki eylemlerini soruşturan BM komisyonuna kadar uluslararası hukuk alanında önemli görevler üstlendi.

title: Bulletin n°2 de l'Assemblée Anticarcérale Paname & Environs - été 2026
content:
Ce bulletin est édité par l'Assemblée Anti-Carcérale Paname & Environs, qui se réunit mensuellement. La prochaine assemblée sera le 25 octobre à 16h à la Parole Errante. Pour contribuer, témoigner, nous raconter des choses, être tenu·e au courant des nouvelles de l'assemblée ou y participer, il est possible d'envoyer un mail à l'adresse suivante : paname-anticarcerale @ riseup . net


La prison est l'un des symbole les plus éloquents de la puissance de l'État, de sa capacité à réprimer, enfermer et isoler l'ensemble des individu·es qui menacent son existence. La prison est au centre même de l'appareil colonial qui constitue l'État français : elle sert à mater et punir les révoltes des colonies comme récemment en Kanaky, Guadeloupe ou Martinique, à intensifier le tri aux frontières comme à Mayotte, et à tracer des frontières intérieures en incarcérant massivement les populations racisées, colonisées et les plus pauvres. Une des prouesse des États dits «

 

démocratiques

 

», est d'avoir réussi à faire de la notion d'enfermement un impensé pour toute une partie de la population. Une situation si lointaine que l'on ne prend même pas la peine de l'envisager, alors que c'est pourtant le quotidien de beaucoup de personnes...


Rompre l'isolement des/avec les détenu·es est alors devenu rapidement pour les mouvements anticarcéraux un moyen d'affaiblir l'appareil carcéral et l'État colonial. En exposant la voix des personnes enfermé·es, on se donne le moyen de penser «

 

la prison

 

» (son fonctionnement, ses outils, etc.), mais aussi de la rendre moins «

 

extérieure à nos vies

 

». Attaquer les lieux d'incarcération - par les mots, la solidarité, le feu ou la bombe - c'est alors s'attaquer à ses outils privilégiés.


L'Assemblée Anticarcérale Paris & Environs a pour vocation d'être un espace d'organisation ouvert se réunissant mensuellement afin d'agir collectivement en solidarité avec les mouvements des prisonnier·es et tisser des liens avec les prisonnier·es et leurs proches.


Ce bulletin "mensuel" se veut un moyen de diffuser la parole, en revenant sur des mouvements ou luttes dans les prisons, et faisant sortir les nouvelles de l'intérieur. Il se veut aussi comme un outil internationaliste pour mettre en lien la répression de toutes les luttes, diffusant nouvelles d'affaires et de procès, luttes et lettres de prisonnier·es du monde entier. Il nous paraît d'autant plus important de pouvoir les diffuser sur papier lorsque l'on considère l'attaque des États-Unis contre Autistici/Inventati ayant conduit à la disparition de noblogs.

author: Mario Trujillo
title: Resisting the Menace of Federal Data Consolidation
content:
In the past two years, the federal government has unlawfully consolidated data exposing our private information.

This consolidation has been chaotic but generally came in three rolling waves: It started with DOGE, moved to agency-to-agency data sharing with ICE, and then attempted data-driven purges of state voter rolls.

We all deserve to live in a world where the data we use to pay our taxes, receive benefits, and vote is not combined and weaponized against us. The amalgamation of data leads to mistakes, abuses, and a lack of trust in institutions meant to protect us. Overall, it can chill our participation in society. This is particularly true for groups disfavored by this administration—especially immigrants and protesters.

Congress highlighted similar abuses—including the creation of enemies lists and snooping on activists and federal employees—following the McCarthy and Watergate eras. And the increasing use of computers to magnify those harms led Congress to pass a slate of protections like the federal Privacy Act of 1974.

The good news is that many people have stepped forward to resist the federal government’s unprecedented and unlawful data consolidations. Many groups, including EFF, have filed lawsuits to enforce our data privacy laws, and many states have, too. Legislators at the federal and state levels have worked to expose and oppose these surveillance programs. And many people have protested for their right to data privacy.

Existing data privacy protections have been essential in the past two years, but they can be improved. This should include: narrowing loopholes and increasing enforcement in existing laws, limiting the government’s purchase of data on the commercial market, and passing a comprehensive consumer privacy law.

Starting on January 20, 2025, President Trump created DOGE—essentially renaming an existing agency originally meant to modernize government technology. Rather than engage in modernization, DOGE quickly obtained high-level access to sensitive databases across the government that store millions of people’s personal records—including at the Office of Personnel Management (OPM), the Social Security Administration, and the Treasury Department.

DOGE was staffed with people with little government or cybersecurity knowledge and who often had conflicts of interest. DOGE’s early aim was not always clear, aside from gaining “prompt access to all unclassified agency records” and the “sharing and consolidation” of those records.

The result? The indiscriminate firing of government employees and the decimation of important agencies that focused on consumer protection and foreign aid. It also resulted in clear misuses of data. For example, while working with DOGE at the Social Security Administration, one individual signed an outside agreement with an advocacy group with the aim of using SSA data to find evidence of alleged voter fraud and “overturn election results in certain States.”

DOGE’s data access and consolidation violated the federal Privacy Act, which limits the sharing and consolidation of government databases. Many groups stepped in to sue. For example, EFF and our co-counsel at Lex Lumina LLC and Democracy Defenders Fund, on behalf of two public employee unions (AFGE and AALJ), sued the OPM for unlawfully disclosing federal workers’ information to DOGE. After EFF and others secured early victories, the government sought to end the lawsuits by firing many DOGE agents and removing their access to records. A great deal of damage remains in need of a judicial remedy.

Even as DOGE’s influence diminished, federal agencies have attempted to share, compare, and seize large databases, in order to target immigrants. In some cases, they have succeeded. This happened with tax records at the IRS, Medicaid data from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and public housing data from the Department of Housing and Urban Development. The Department of Agriculture also sought to collect databases regarding Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Programs (SNAP) from states.

Many groups have filed lawsuits to block this anti-immigrant-motivated data consolidation, alleging it violates privacy protection laws. EFF filed amicus briefs in support of two of these lawsuits: Centro de Trabajadores v. Bessent, which concerns IRS data; and California v. HHS, which concerns Medicaid data (and where we teamed up with EPIC and Protect Democracy). Most recently, states have stepped up to challenge …

author: EDRi
title: EDRi-gram, 8 October 2026
content:
What has the EDRi network been up to over the past few weeks? Find out the latest digital rights news in our regular newsletter. In this edition: Turning up the heat – Commission backs social media bans, Apple held accountable, summer to-dos, & more!

This EDRi-gram edition includes a real snapshot of the disconnect between the kind of technology and protections people and communities around the world need, and the kind that are being pushed at us by lawmakers and companies either for the sake of profits, as easy fixes to structural societal issues or more sinister reasons.

Take the EU’s recently announced KIDS ACT. We unpack the many shortcomings of the proposal which is a missed opportunity to address the root cause of why online platforms are harmful to children – and everyone else. We also look at the Cloud and AI Development (CADA) Act, a part of the EU’s Tech Sovereignty Package announced earlier this year. What was sold as a way to jumpstart the EU’s “sovereign AI” ambitions seems to be set to hurt digital rights and environmental protections instead, while also imposing an unreliable technology onto us.

Elsewhere, Austria will soon get to find out what happens when AI systems are allowed to issue legally binding government decisions without any human oversight. EDRi-member epicenter.works detail the draft proposal and all the ways it could backfire.

None of the above is without resistance from those of us working to protect your rights. Dutch EDRi-member Bits of Freedom have launched a new campaign demanding a ban on Meta’s “pervert glasses”, aka, AI glasses which can be used to film people without them knowing. Meta was clearly paying attention – their viral satirical video on these glasses was removed from Instagram.

From critical campaigns, and urging EU countries to not treat data protection and “competitiveness” as opposing goals as they discuss the Digital Omnibus, to legal action against Big Tech corporations preying on our minds – we’re fighting back.

Next week, at our flagship annual event #PrivacyCamp26, we’ll be asking the real questions – where does technology come from? Who shapes it? And what would self-determination look like if it were defined by the people, not dictated by profits or a state’s agenda? We hope to see some of you attending!
