title: #39EncuentroPlurinacional: la defensa del agua en Mendoza
content:
Marta Salas, defensora del agua de Mendoza, denunció la política represiva contra quienes se oponen al extractivismo y la contaminación en esa provincia:


Marta Salas


“Hemos tenido 40 detenidos, entre ellos una compañera jubilada, que estuvo apresada casi 6 días. Eso demuestra que el gobernador Cornejo ha superado muchos niveles de represión”, apuntó.


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por Indymedia Argentina (@indymedia.argentina)


Y detalló: “Nosotros en Mendoza somos una tierra desértica, con una fragilidad hídrica muy grande. Toda plantita que ves vos en Mendoza es porque detrás de esa plantita hay un ser humano y hay agua, si no, no hay nada. Entonces, para nosotros el agua es de una importancia, es decir, ya desde chicos que venimos educados para cuidarla”.


“Y ahora como Cornejo quiere cambiar la situación económica de Mendoza, según él, con la minería, todo eso se va a contaminar, porque las minas están en las cuencas del recurso hídrico nuestro”, agregó.

Eugenia Figueroa

title: SOHR calls for the release of young men arbitrarily abducted from Afrin to Turkey eight years ago
content:
In a statement issued on Saturday, the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (SOHR) confirmed that the Turkish state had released four Kurdish men whom it had abducted from Afrin approximately eight years ago. The Observatory said that other people detained in the village and surrounding areas continue to be held in prisons in Turkey.


According to SOHR’s statement, in August 2018, Turkish civilian police, accompanied by intelligence officers, detained 13 young men from the village of Omar Uşaqî in the Afrin region and one person from a nearby village, on the allegation that they had links to the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria.


The detainees were reportedly first held in a school in their village, where they were beaten and subjected to torture, before being transferred to a school in a neighbouring village. SOHR also reported that large sums of money were demanded from their families before the men were transferred to Samsun Prison in Turkey.


At a trial held in Hatay on 12 December 2019, 11 of the detainees were sentenced to various prison terms, including life imprisonment.


SOHR called on the Turkish authorities to disclose the fate of all Kurdish detainees from Rojava, investigate allegations of torture and ill-treatment, and review the sentences imposed. The Observatory also called for the release of those being held arbitrarily and for those responsible for the violations to be held accountable.

title: DBP Co-Chair Uçar: Lasting peace can be achieved through women’s active participation in the process
content:
The Democratic Regions Party (DBP) organized a women’s gathering in Dersim under the slogan “We Are Building the Language of Peace.” The gathering, attended by numerous women as well as representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, addressed the role of women in the peace process and the importance of organized struggle.


Speaking at the gathering, DEM Party Dersim MP Ayten Kordu emphasized the importance of women’s organization, stating that women should be at the heart of the peace process.


Kordu said they would continue their efforts to broaden the scope of the Gülistan Doku case and stressed that women should participate more actively in the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


DBP Co-Chair Çiğdem Kılıçgün Uçar stated that peace cannot be addressed solely over the relationship of Kurds and Alevis with the state.


Emphasizing that the state must also make peace with women, workers, and nature, Uçar criticized attempts to limit the process to political alliances.


Describing the discussion of the Kurdish issue in the Grand National Assembly of Turkey as a historic turning point, Çiğdem Kılıçgün Uçar said, “So who brought these parties together? You did. Mr. Öcalan is the politician who has spoken most clearly and offered a perspective on peace and democracy.”


Uçar added, “When we talk about negotiations, it is our struggle that will compel the state to take action. The more women participate in the peace process, the more lasting peace will be.”

title: Guerrillas: We will continue our struggle until Leader Öcalan gains physical freedom
content:
Guerrillas from the HPG (People's Defense Forces) and YJA-Star (Free Women's Troops) spoke to ANF on the occasion of the 29th anniversary of the international conspiracy against Abdullah Öcalan on October 9, 1998. Forced to leave Syria amid intense political and military pressure on the country, the Kurdish leader went through a months-long odyssey through various countries before he was taken captive in the Kenyan capital Nairobi and handed over to Turkey on 15 February 1999. He has been incarcerated in İmralı Island Prison since and has not been seen his conditions improved despite the ongoing peace and democratic society process.


‘Leader Apo foiled the conspiracy through his resistance’


HPG guerrilla Azad Herekol began his remarks by condemning the international conspiracy and commemorated with respect and gratitude those who set themselves on fire in the “You Cannot Darken Our Sun” protests in response to the imprisonment of the Kurdish leader.


Emphasizing that the conspiracy against Öcalan aimed to destroy the Kurdish people and the peoples of the Middle East, Azad Herekol said the following: “The dominant powers knew very well that the struggle of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] was not only for one people, but for all oppressed societies. That is why they feared Leader Apo’s ideas and resorted to such a method. The international conspiracy involved not only imperialist powers but also collaborators. The aim of the conspiracy was to eliminate the oppressed peoples’ hope for freedom by subjecting the Kurdish people to genocide. The struggle for freedom initiated by Leader Apo was not limited to the Kurdish people; over time, it also paved the way for all oppressed peoples.


 


Through this conspiracy directed against Leader Apo, they sought to neutralize the struggle of the peoples of the Middle East. Leader Apo thwarted the conspiracy through his defiant stance and prevented those behind it from achieving their objective. Following Leader Apo’s capture, the aim was to eliminate the Freedom Movement. However, Leader Apo foiled this conspiracy through his resistance, and 28 years have passed since. As time went on, the struggle for freedom grew stronger, the unity of the peoples became stronger with each passing day, and Leader Apo’s struggle continued to develop. This struggle enabled the people to become increasingly conscious of freedom and to see Leader Apo’s struggle as their own.


After Leader Apo was taken captive, we joined the Freedom Movement. As HPG guerrillas, our aim and objective is to struggle against the international conspiracy. We have complete faith in our Leade regarding the Peace and Democratic Society Process that has been initiated, and we are ready to carry out the struggle expected of us during this process. We will continue our struggle until Leader Apo gains physical freedom. We will continue to struggle until we realize the dreams and goals of our fallen comrades. With this stance, we will thwart the conspiracy and further strengthen our determination to struggle.”


‘The struggle continues on the basis of the Leader’s ideology’


YJA-Star guerrilla Zîlan Sozdar Cudi said that despite the international conspiracy and all the attacks, the Kurdish people have managed to remain standing and continue their struggle to this day:


“Leader Apo’s resistance on İmralı Island has enabled the people to remain standing in every respect. The aim of those behind the conspiracy was to capture the Leader and eliminate both him and the Kurdish people’s struggle. The Leader was taken captive, but they failed to achieve their fundamental objective of subjecting the Kurdish people to genocide and eliminating Leader Apo. To this day, the Kurdish people continue to stand strong and carry on their struggle through the ideas of the Leader. Leader Apo’s struggle on İmralı has ultimately thwarted the conspiracy.


 


I was born in the year Leader Apo was captured. He has been held captive for years. For this reason, the feelings of revenge within us grow stronger with each passing day. As a YJA-Star guerrilla, I see the resistance waged by Leader Apo and the process he most recently initiated as an important part of the struggle for freedom. The Peace and Democratic Society Process stands before all of us as a task required by the present circumstances. Until we free our Leader, we will not compromise our militant and vengeful stance, nor will we allow those behind the conspiracy to achieve their …

title: Gravestones of Kurdish martyrs buried en masse in a pit in Cudi region
content:
The Cuma Bilika and Binevş Edessa Martyrs’ Cemetery, where PKK members are buried in the village of Sipîndarok on the slopes of Mount Cudi in Şırnak, was destroyed in a bombing in 2015. Visits to the cemetery have since been prevented on the grounds that the area is a “military security zone.”


Cîhan Zîlan (Hatice Erbağ), who is buried in the cemetery, was killed in a clash in Cudi on March 31, 2006. Her brother Faysal Erbağ, who had been searching for her grave for 20 years, and his wife Bilmez Erbağ spotted her gravestone in footage previously recorded by the Mezopotamya Agency (MA). They subsequently traveled approximately 1,500 kilometers from Bursa to Cudi to reach the cemetery. The family was accompanied by the Şırnak Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture with Families Who Lost Their Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations (MEBYA-DER).


During the visit, it was discovered that gravestones had been buried en masse in a pit dug near the cemetery’s parking area. Following rainfall, some of the gravestones have surfaced.


Denouncing the burial of the gravestones, MEBYA-DER Şırnak executive Fahrettin Salgucak said: “The stones caught our attention at the entrance to the cemetery. When we looked, we saw gravestones with names written on them. A pit had been dug here and the gravestones had been buried in it. With the rainfall, the stones have resurfaced. There is nothing like this anywhere else in the world. They are even afraid of our gravestones; they have buried those too. We have only just discovered this.”


Stating that MEBYA-DER does not accept the situation, Salgucak said: “We are in a peace process. This kind of destruction now needs to be repaired. These cemeteries must be restored, and the road leading to the cemetery must be reopened. We want families to be able to come and go freely. This family has traveled all the way here from Bursa. Because of the commercial interests of certain individuals, families are unable to visit the cemeteries freely.”


Although Faysal Erbağ found his sister’s gravestone, he was unable to determine which grave belonged to her because the stones had been moved away from the graves. Erbağ then collected a handful of soil from each grave to take to the grave of their late mother in Van. The cemetery visit concluded with flowers being laid on the graves.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: España: Los traidores hacen más daño que el enemigo
content:
Camaradas,


Los que viven de la política.


Lo que más daño ha hecho a la izquierda no son solo los ataques de la derecha: son los oportunistas, los que únicamente tienen proyectos personales y usan la política para colocarse y solucionarse la vida. Gente para la que la militancia es una escalera, no un compromiso con la clase trabajadora.


Los traidores destruyen desde dentro.


Siempre nos hacen más daño los traidores que los enemigos declarados. Al enemigo lo vemos venir; el traidor engaña y destruye desde dentro. Son quienes desmovilizan a la izquierda real, porque esa es precisamente su función y para eso los utiliza el sistema.


Los de los mil nombres y las mismas caras.


Han hecho muchísimo daño los de los mil nombres con las mismas caras, los de la señora del dato, los colocados por pandillismo político: personajes más preocupados por mantenerse que por cambiar las cosas. Desgraciadamente, no se van a ir ni con agua caliente. Son resistentes al insecticida y jamás se someten a primarias. La bien pagada y los suyos siguen a lo suyo.


Ni engañados ni desmovilizados.


No nos dejemos engañar por la ultraderecha, que nos quiere robar todo, ni desmovilizar por el oportunismo. Son dos caras del mismo problema: una nos quita derechos y la otra nos quita las ganas de defenderlos.


El voto del mal menor no basta.


Debemos frenar a la ultraderecha en las urnas con el voto del mal menor, pero sin olvidar que, si seguimos sin empujar, si no reconstruimos el campo de la izquierda y si no recuperamos la conciencia de clase, tarde o temprano el desastre ocurrirá y acabaremos como la Argentina de Milei.


Milei, de gira por el Estado español.


El mismo desastroso Javier Milei vendrá al Estado español a hacer campaña por la ultraderecha, arrodillada, como él, ante el amo Trump y el Israel genocida de Netanyahu. Que nadie se llame a engaño: lo que viene a vendernos ya sabemos cómo acaba para quienes trabajan.


La tarea es clara: organización, conciencia de clase y una izquierda que no esté al servicio de los que se colocan.


¡Hasta la victoria siempre!


André Abeledo Fernández

title: Ex-Scottish Leader on Starmer’s Gaza Legacy
content:
This week marked three years since the Hamas attack of October 7th, and the beginning of the Israeli state’s genocidal onslaught against the Palestinian people. In that time, Western leaders from Joe Biden and Donald Trump to Keir Starmer and now Andy Burnham have refused to call the genocide what it is, despite the consensus of genocide scholars. One outlier among Western leaders during this period has been Humza Yousaf. He was the first Western leader to demand a ceasefire, just days into the onslaught.


The former first minister of Scotland, and first Muslim leader of a Western nation, has written a book about his time in government, ‘Under Fire: My Family’s Escape from Gaza and the Cost of Leadership’. On Downstream this week, Aaron Bastani sat down with him to hear first-hand what it was like governing Scotland, while his family were trapped in Gaza. 


 


How did he and his family manage the first few days and weeks of the genocide, while balancing his responsibilities as Scotland’s leader? What kind of pressures did he face internally, and externally, to support Israel? How did he make decisions in government, and how did he take the decision to stand down? title: Message from the mountains of Kurdistan to the 39th International Women’s Gathering in Argentina
content:
The 39th International Women’s Gathering, bringing together thousands of women from different regions of Abya Yala, has begun in Córdoba, Argentina. During the three-day gathering, women will share their experiences through meetings and various activities and discuss strategies for advancing their struggles.


Ahead of the opening, members of the Kurdish Women’s Movement conveyed their greetings to the participants and also to Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, who has been incarcerated in İmralı Island since 1999. A video message sent from the mountains of Kurdistan was then screened.


Speaking on behalf of KJAR (The Community of Free Women of Eastern Kurdistan) and the Kurdish Women’s Movement, Zîlan Vejîn greeted the 39th International Women’s Gathering and emphasized the importance of the common struggle.


Zîlan Vejîn stressed that Abdullah Öcalan’s philosophy offers an answer for peoples and women around the world.


 


The video message was enthusiastically received by the participants with great enthusiasm and slogans such as “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî” [Woman, Life, Freedom].


Before the beginning of the three-day gathering, a ritual, according to the traditions of different original people of Abya Yaha, was held. The gathering’s activities will continue over the next two days, with the participation of women from across Abya Yala, representing various feminist movements, including indigenous ones. Workshops, demonstrations, film screenings, and various other activities are also scheduled as part of the event.

title: Unknown assailants vandalize the facility of the Families of Martyrs in Til Temir
content:
In the northeastern Syrian town of Til Temir, a facility belonging to the Council of Families of Martyrs was attacked and damaged by unknown assailants. The perpetrators tore down the sign bearing the council’s name and set a fire on the roof of the building. It is not yet known who was behind the attack.


The Council of Families of Martyrs, which organizes the relatives of members of the Kurdish freedom movement and the YPG/YPJ defense forces who have fallen in combat, issued a statement condemning the attack.


The Council stated that the attack violated the sanctity of the site and its moral and humanitarian significance. It called for the circumstances surrounding the incident to be clarified, those responsible to be identified and held accountable under the law.


The Council also called for the necessary measures to be taken to protect civil and social institutions in order to prevent such attacks from recurring.

title: Mehmed Uzun commemorated in Amed on 19th anniversary of his death
content:
On Sunday, relatives, companions, and representatives of political parties and civil society organizations gathered at the grave of Kurdish writer Mehmed Uzun in Mardinkapı Cemetery in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır) to mark the 19th anniversary of his death on October 11, 2007. The commemoration, organized by the Association of Kurdish Writers, paid tribute to Uzun’s contribution to the development of modern Kurdish literature and his commitment to the Kurdish language.


His brother, Mustafa Uzun, thanked those present for attending. Mehmet Ildoğan, who had met the writer in Adıyaman, recalled how Uzun had inspired him and many others to develop a passion for literature. “We have only one Mehmed Uzun, not twenty,” Ildoğan said. “His works will light our way like a torch.”


Writing against language bans and cultural oppression


Herdem Merwani, co-chair of the Association of Kurdish Writers, described Uzun as one of the pillars of Kurdish literature. He said the association would continue its efforts to preserve and further develop this literary heritage.


Adem Avcı, the doctor who cared for Uzun during his battle with cancer, also paid tribute to his life’s work. He recalled that Uzun had fallen ill while in exile and had wanted to spend the final years of his life in his homeland. Avcı called on Kurdish writers to preserve Uzun’s legacy.


Lawyer and politician Serhat Bucak highlighted the significance of exile in Uzun’s literary development. “Mehmed Uzun was an immensely valuable writer. He had to go to Sweden. I wish he had not been forced to leave. But perhaps without that exile, he would not have become the Mehmed Uzun we know today,” Bucak said. He added that one day Uzun’s works would be taught at universities.


“He left behind timeless works”


Serra Bucak, co-mayor of Amed, emphasized that Uzun had transformed the painful experiences of his people into literature and had continued to write in Kurdish despite the bans. In doing so, she said, he made a significant contribution to Kurdish literature. “Mehmed Uzun left behind timeless works. I hope that many more Mehmed Uzuns will emerge,” Bucak said.


The commemoration will continue with a panel discussion at Sümerpark.

The victim who is able to articulate the situation of the victim has ceased to be a victim: he or she has become a threat.


 James Baldwin,

The Devil Finds Work


Raise your hand, bite your tongue Conversation is over and done


We let ‘em out, we let ‘em in


We’ll let ‘em know when it’s the tipping point, the tipping point

 Tears for Fears,

The Tipping Point


Author’s note:


 This is a section of my book,

What is to Be Undone

.


 And it is not necessarily easy reading.


 The book has a singular focus: we face an impossible moment in this global, dying civilization. In the violent fits of fascistic might, we see the old colonial apparatus showing itself in full light. For many of those held captive by it, the reality of its systemic brutality has been kept at bay. And for the rest, that brutality has been a lived experience.


 The veneer is quickly fading, and the costs of this technological nightmare are exponentially impossible. We face a world where climate instability has shaken every facet of life as our species has known it.


 Everywhere, the consequences of this Empire flood our lives, and that will only continue.


 The point is this: civilization is dying, but we don’t need to share its fate.


 It is never too late to fight the Leviathan. And I don’t say this in a way to instill false hope or naivety: there is no guarantee we survive this.

That is all the more reason to fight

.


 How the book unfolds is meant to identify the falsehoods civilization is built upon: to lay waste to ideas that History has led the victor by divine right. Civilization is a willingness to brutality, and it has advanced, not by ingenuity, but by opportunism and cruelty.


 This chapter is a plea to understand how deeply civilization’s narratives burrow, showing how vital it is to divest from this horror by facing our own.


 The path of the book is a series of challenges to the way we view and interact with this world, culminating in a plea to understand that the fires have come for this Empire, and they inevitably will again.


 We need to understand what we face, because all life depends upon it.


 By dragging it into the light, we free ourselves to act in kind.


 This section draws me in as a character because it had to. I did not intend for that to be the case, but it came out this way. As such, there are content warnings for triggering sections.


 If necessary, please heed them.


 I’ve been struggling to write this. I really have.


 I keep asking myself why, but it’s because I’m dancing around it all. I know why.


 What I had planned to write and what I need to write are two different things.


 There are many aspects about this book, in particular, that kind of hedge me out of my own comfort zone. There is no doubt that’s important, especially when the book is ultimately about seeing civilization and its realities from literally any other perspective than that which civilization sells us.


 I know how hard that can be. Because these things unfold infinitely, don’t they? We’re moving from the artificial safety of preordained boundaries. We want to believe that there’s an adult in the room, for all the horrors that civilization can throw at the world. We want to believe that there’s a bottom for how much evil individuals and organizations are capable of unleashing.


 The truth is that there isn’t.


 You and I might have boundaries and limits, but those that seek power and control just do not have those things. You see, civilization didn’t invent horror. It didn’t invent the capability of doing …

title: Hein Htet Kyaw - On the Question of Ethno-Nationalist Burmese Federal State
content:
Author

: Hein Htet Kyaw

Title

: On the Question of Ethno-Nationalist Burmese Federal State

Subtitle

: In Favor of Geographical Multicultural Federalism

Date

: 10 Oct 2026

Notes

: English Version of

https://sea.theanarchistlibrary.org/library/hein-htet-kyaw-on-burma-ethnostate?__language=en

Source

:

redandblackanarchists.com.au


Regarding "Bamar State"


 Today, the political and federalist demand for a "Bamar State" has become a preliminary political and federal roadmap for a third-way coalition outside the NLD/NUG factions.


Why is a "Bamar State" Needed?


 The political and federal demand for a "Bamar State" has emerged due to several reasons.


 In the article

"The Eight-State Principle Must Be Fundamental"

 published in the May 2022 issue of

New Society Journal

 (Vol. 3, No. 10), the author Lun Nway Nyein from Democratic Party for a New Society wrote:


 · "It is completely unacceptable for any single ethnic group to hold disproportionate rights or powers under any pretext. To be precise, it is unacceptable that the Bamar ethnic group has taken 7 units while other ethnic groups have taken less."


 Similarly, quoting an interview on Federal FM titled

"Why a Bamar State Should Exist"

 with Maung Saungkha, commander of the Bamar People's Liberation Army (BPLA):


 To establish an equal state-structure, a Bamar State must be included. This will foster an understanding of ethnic fraternity between Bamar and non-Bamar groups.


 The term "Pyi-ma" (Mainland) should no longer be used as it implies greater importance; instead, it should simply be called the "Bamar region."


 Thus, I understand the political and federal demand for a "Bamar State" as an effort by other ethnic minority groups to check the political overreach and excess federal units claimed by successive rulers—from U Nu to U Ne Win, down to present-day leaders—who claimed to represent the majority Bamar ethnic group.


 At the same time, when discussing the federal structure of the state alongside the "Bamar State," we can observe ongoing debates over whether the design should be purely ethnic-based, geographic-based, or an ethno-geographic hybrid model.


 In an excerpt from

Essential Interim Constitution in 2022 (Part 10)

 broadcast by NST, U Aung Htoo, an influential intellectual regarding the law (especially the constitutional laws) and the founder of the Legal Aid Network stated:


 “States flying a nationalist flag should be designated as "National States."


 “New states can be formed if other existing states accept them (e.g., Kachin, Shan).”


 “States inhabited by a diverse mix of different ethnic groups should be designated as ‘Multi-National States’ (e.g., Yangon Region).”


 In a September 21, 2022 interview with CNI News, Saya Than Soe Naing, a former member of Communist Party of Burma who currently is a heterodox political commentator remarked:


 · "Our country cannot be organized purely along ethnic lines, nor can it easily be divided purely by geography. We need to consider both factors together."


The Historical Concept of a "Bamar State"


 To trace the concept of a "Bamar State" back through history, we must start with the Eight-State Shan Federal Proposal.


 Around 1960, when the Shan Proposal was first presented to the public, U Tin Aye, a lecturer at the Yangon University Translation Department, was among its key proponents.


 I also recall reading from past interviews that in 2013, Dr. Aye Maung, chairperson of the Rakhine Nationalities Development Party, discussed the eight-state concept at the Taunggyi Conference of the Nationalities Brotherhood Federation (NBF) in Shan State.


 Furthermore, the concept of a "Bamar State" was reportedly deliberated during the first session of the Union Peace Conference held in Naypyidaw in 2016 (pro-military agenda).


"Bamar State and the Eight-State Model"


 In the article

"The Eight-State Principle Must Be Fundamental"

 in the May 2022 issue of

New Society Journal

 (Vol. 3, No. 10), author Lun Nway Nyein wrote:


 · "No ethnic group should hold excessive rights, power, or territorial units, whether formally or substantively. The Bamar ethnic group must take a single Bamar State, just like the other ethnic nationalities. This is what it means to base our system on the Eight-State principle."

title: Küçükçekmece'de yıkımı yapılan 7 katlı bina çöktü
content:
İstanbul'un Küçükçekmece ilçesinde kentsel dönüşüm kapsamında yıkımına başlanan 7 katlı bina, çalışmalar sırasında çöktü. Çökmenin etkisiyle çevredeki binalar, doğal gaz ve su tesisatları ile aydınlatma direği zarar gördü. Binanın çökme anı cep telefonu kamerasıyla kaydedildi.

Olay, dün öğle saatlerinde İnönü Mahallesi 2'nci Yıldız Sokak'ta meydana geldi. Kentsel dönüşüm kapsamında bitişik nizamda bulunan 7'şer katlı iki binanın yıkımına başlandı. Ekiplerin binalardan birinde yürüttüğü çalışmalar sırasında diğer bina aniden çöktü.

İhbar üzerine olay yerine polis, sağlık ve itfaiye ekipleri sevk edildi. Çöken binadan kopan parçalar çevredeki yapılara ve tesisatlara zarar verirken, ekiplerin incelemesinde enkaz altında kimsenin kalmadığı belirlendi.

Mahalleli Kibar Yıldırım, binanın yıkım sırasında çöktüğünü belirterek, "Dün kentsel dönüşüm kapsamında bu binanın yıkımı gerçekleşti. Yanlış yıkımdan dolayı bina bir anda çöktü. Bizim en büyük sevincimiz, binanın aynı yere çökmesi. Çünkü 7 katlı bir binaydı. Bina da değil, site şeklinde bir bloktu. Yaklaşık 54-55 daireli olabilen bir blok. Bir anda durduğu yere çöktü, yan yatsaydı karşıdaki bütün binaların hepsini götürürdü" dedi.

Yıkım çalışmalarına ilişkin daha önce yetkili kurumlara başvurduğunu söyleyen Yıldırım, gerekli önlemlerin alınmadığını öne sürdü.

Yıldırım, "Ben defalarca belediyeyi aramama rağmen, Çevre ve Şehircilik Bakanlığı'nı aramama rağmen, hatta dün bütün kurumları aradım. Çoğu bana cevap vermediği halde ben dün 112 Acil'i aradım. Oradan emniyete bağlandım. 'Bakın, bizim bu sokakta kentsel dönüşüm sebebiyle yıkım var ama yıkım çok yanlış yapılıyor. Burada bir facia olacak, gelip müdahale edin' dedim. Oradan birkaç arkadaş da geldi. Hatta emniyetten birkaç arkadaş da geldi ama 'Burada bizim yapacağımız bir şey yok, sadece güvenlik önlemi alabiliriz' dediler. Ancak belediyeden ve diğer kurumlardan kimse yıkım sırasında burada değildi" ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Milano: un migliaio di persone in piazza della Scala contro lo sviluppo incontrollato dei data center
content:
Un migliaio di persone si sono radunate sabato 10 ottobre in Piazza della Scala a Milano hanno risposto all’

appello lanciato dalla Rete nazionale dei Comitati Stop Data Center 

e manifestato nel pomeriggio per esprimere preoccupazioni e denunciare le criticità che lo sviluppo di questi impianti hanno sul territorio, in primis lombardo

. 


Chiedono in particolare una 

moratoria sulle nuove autorizzazioni fino alla definizione di regole più precise 

su impatti ambientali, urbanistica e un coinvolgimento reale dei cittadini nelle scelte rispetto a questi impianti.


Sollevano diverse criticità, tra le quali la mancanza di una valutazione complessiva: in Lombardia,  nell’area milanese in particolare, sono molti i progetti che insistono sul territorio, spesso a pochi chilometri di distanza. Servirebbe, secondo i rappresentanti della rete, analizzarli con uno sguardo d’insieme e non singolarmente.


Da piazza della Sacala la corrispondenza di 

Giulia della redazione

. 


L’intervento in piazza di 

Enrico Duranti, della rete dei comitati stop data Center e di Sergio Manera, professore di Fisica all’università di Pavia


da

Radio Onda d’urto


Di seguito il comunicato della

rete nazionale Stop Data Center


𝐂𝐄 𝐋’𝐀𝐁𝐁𝐈𝐀𝐌𝐎 𝐅𝐀𝐓𝐓𝐀! 𝐆𝐑𝐀𝐙𝐈𝐄 𝐀 𝐓𝐔𝐓𝐓𝐄 𝐄 𝐀 𝐓𝐔𝐓𝐓𝐈!


Un immenso e di cuore 𝐆𝐑𝐀𝐙𝐈𝐄 𝐚 𝐭𝐮𝐭𝐭𝐢 𝐢 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐢 𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐚𝐥𝐢, vera anima della nostra Rete e insostituibili sentinelle dei territori! E un grazie gigantesco a ciascuna persona, associazione e realtà che oggi è scesa in piazza, ci ha sostenuto e ha fatto sentire la propria voce. È grazie alla tenacia, al presidio costante e all’impegno di tutti noi se la manifestazione di oggi, 10 ottobre, è stata un 𝐒𝐔𝐂𝐂𝐄𝐒𝐒𝐎 𝐒𝐓𝐑𝐀𝐎𝐑𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐀𝐑𝐈𝐎!


La 𝐑𝐞𝐭𝐞 𝐍𝐚𝐳𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐝𝐞𝐢 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐢 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐩 𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐚 𝐂𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫 ha fatto sentire un urlo forte, chiaro e inarrestabile: il nostro territorio non si svende!


Ribadiamo a gran voce che la 𝐌𝐎𝐑𝐀𝐓𝐎𝐑𝐈𝐀 è la chiave di volta per fermare questa colonizzazione! Serve uno 𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐩 𝐢𝐦𝐦𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐚𝐭𝐨 ai progetti devastanti per tutelare i beni comuni.


Vedere così tante persone unite, fianco a fianco con la stessa passione e determinazione, ci riempie di orgoglio e ci carica di un’energia incredibile. Abbiamo dimostrato che di fronte al consumo scriteriato di risorse e alla cementificazione selvaggia dei mega data center, le comunità sanno organizzarsi e lottare insieme!


𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐨 𝟏𝟎 𝐨𝐭𝐭𝐨𝐛𝐫𝐞 𝐬𝐞𝐠𝐧𝐚 𝐮𝐧 𝐩𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐢 𝐬𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐭𝐚: 𝐧𝐨𝐧 𝐬𝐢𝐚𝐦𝐨 𝐩𝐢𝐮̀ 𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐨𝐥𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐥𝐭𝐚̀ 𝐢𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐞, 𝐬𝐢𝐚𝐦𝐨 𝐮𝐧 𝐦𝐨𝐯𝐢𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐨 𝐧𝐚𝐳𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐞 𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐞, 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐨 𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐬𝐚𝐩𝐞𝐯𝐨𝐥𝐞!

Non ci fermeremo qui. 𝐋𝐚 𝐥𝐨𝐭𝐭𝐚 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐮𝐚, ma oggi abbiamo dimostrato a tutti la forza e la determinazione della nostra rete!

title: İstanbul Modern’de “Panorama: Hayaller ve Yerler” sergisi sona eriyor
content:
İstanbul Modern’de farklı kuşaklardan 18 sanatçının çalışmalarını bir araya getiren “Panorama: Hayaller ve Yerler” sergisi, 18 Ekim’de sona eriyor. Sergi, düşsel manzaralar, kurgusal portreler ve alternatif mekân tasarımları üzerinden izleyiciyi dünyayla kurduğu ilişkiyi yeniden düşünmeye çağırıyor.

İstanbul Modern’in birinci kat galerilerine yayılan sergi, sanatçıların 2010’lu yıllardan bu yana ürettiği çalışmalardan oluşuyor. Yerleştirmelerden hareketli görüntülere, yapay zekâ uygulamalarından arşivsel malzemelere uzanan seçki, farklı sanatsal üretim biçimlerini bir araya getiriyor.

Sergide Larissa Araz, İlgen Arzık, Emre Baykal, Silva Bingaz, Hasan Deniz, Umut Erbaş, Cem Ersavcı, Ece Gökalp, Cemre Yeşil Gönenli, Ege Kanar, Zeynep Kayan, Metehan Özcan, Yusuf Sevinçli, İrem Sözen, Selim Süme, Kerem Uzel, Begüm Yamanlar ve Cansu Yıldıran’ın çalışmaları yer alıyor.

Küratörlüğünü İstanbul Modern Artistik Direktörü Çelenk Bafra ile Fotoğraf Küratörü Demet Yıldız Dinçer’in üstlendiği serginin küratöryel ekibinde Selen Erkal ve Şevval Yürüten de bulunuyor.

“Panorama: Hayaller ve Yerler” sergisine eşlik eden Türkçe ve İngilizce katalog, serginin çerçevesini farklı yazılarla ele alıyor. İstanbul Modern Fotoğraf Danışma Kurulu üyeleri Refik Akyüz, Serdar Darendeliler ve Orhan Cem Çetin’in yanı sıra Çelenk Bafra ve Demet Yıldız Dinçer’in yazılarını içeren katalog, İstanbul Modern Mağaza’dan edinilebiliyor.

“Panorama: Hayaller ve Yerler” sergisi, 18 Ekim’e kadar İstanbul Modern’de ziyaret edilebilir.

title: Gian Piero Godio: «Il “nuovo nucleare” è uguale al veccho. Meloni ha scelto un sistema energetico centralizzato»
content:
Il cosiddetto “nuovo nucleare” ricorre ancora alla fissione dell’atomo e continua a produrre scorie radioattive che si accumulano sul nostro territorio. Da quarant’anni, i rifiuti liquidi ad alta attività dell’impianto Eurex di Saluggia sono sempre nello stesso posto nel Vercellese e non sono state neanche solidificate. Del deposito nazionale non c’è neanche l’ombra e, anche per questo, l’Italia è sotto procedura di infrazione europea. Come se non bastasse, il Maxi Data Center “Cavour Hyperscale Campus” previsto a Trino (Vc), come tutti i grandi Data Center, suscita forti preoccupazioni energetiche, ambientali ed etiche. Per funzionare, limitandoci al solo aspetto energetico, richiede di essere alimentato con 400 MW continuativi di energia elettrica, pari a 3 miliardi e mezzo di chilowattora: più del triplo del consumo di tutti i settori della intera provincia di Vercelli (1 miliardo di kWh/anno). Questi nuovi enormi consumi vanificheranno la transizione energetica, essendo persino superiori alla produzione di tutto il fotovoltaico installato in Piemonte (3 miliardi di kWh). E a Trino rispunterà una nuova centrale atomica


Ripubblichiamo ’intervista di FABIO BALOCCO con GIAN PIERO GODIO, 

ambientalista

, apparsa su

Italia Libera.


Segnaliamo anche che a proposito di questi temi si terrà un incontro pubblico promosso da

Legambiente del Vercellese e della Valsesia

 a Trino, stretto tra data center e nucleare.


Gian Piero Godio in una manifestazione ambientalista


► 

Gian Piero Godio ha lavorato per molti anni al Comitato Nazionale per l’Energia Nucleare (Cnen) come responsabile della unità di Automazione e Calcolo scientifico dell’impianto nucleare di riprocessamento Eurex

 di Saluggia, in Piemonte. È proprio facendo quel lavoro che ha constatato quanto il nucleare fosse pericoloso per i lavoratori, per l’ambiente e per il suo legame con le guerre, e così si è sentito in dovere di far conoscere a tutti questi aspetti poco pubblicizzati, entrando a far parte attiva, già negli anni ’80, dei movimenti ecopacifisti e successivamente delle associazioni ambientaliste Pro Natura e Legambiente, delle quali fa parte tuttora, oltre ad essere referente dell’Osservatorio dei Cittadini sul nucleare [

nota

].


— 

Tanto tuonò che piovve: dopo anni che si parla del ritorno all’energia nucleare, pare che ci siamo, il governo ha approvato il Ddl delega per la realizzazione di nuove centrali. Si parla di nucleare sostenibile: è così? E in cosa le nuove centrali si differenzierebbero dalle vecchie?


«Può mai esistere il nucleare sostenibile, può esistere la guerra giusta? Sono una contraddizione, un ossimoro. In ogni caso, persino formalmente, il Regolamento Delegato (Ue) 1214 del 2022 prevede che un impianto nucleare possa ritenersi sostenibile se:


– lo Stato dispone di impianti di smaltimento finale in esercizio per tutti i rifiuti radioattivi a più bassa radioattività; 


– di un piano per l’entrata in funzione, entro il 2050, di un impianto di smaltimento di rifiuti radioattivi ad alta attività; 


e mi risulta che l’Italia su questi temi sia addirittura in procedura di infrazione. Per quanto riguarda le “nuove” centrali non potrebbero che essere del tutto simili alle “vecchie” che in Italia già conosciamo bene: innanzitutto continueranno ad utilizzare la fissione nucleare e, conseguentemente, a produrre ulteriore plutonio e ulteriori scorie radioattive; poi viene detto che saranno “più piccole” delle precedenti, cioè tra i 100 e i 200 MW, ma le ex centrali nucleari di Latina e del Garigliano erano rispettivamente da 200 e da 150 MW … e poi, se saranno da 100 MW, per fare anche solo il 10% dell’energia elettrica necessaria al 2050 ne occorreranno quasi un centinaio, allegria!».


Il ministro dell’Ambiente e Sicurezza energetica Gilberto Pichetto Fratin “abbracciato” dai nuclearisti italiani


— 

Dato che dietro ogni scelta di carattere economico c’è una lobby che spinge, nel caso di specie ti chiedo: quale business c’è dietro? Si sa o si può ipotizzare?


«

A mio parere il Governo più che il nucleare in sé, vuole scegliere quello che definirei il “modello nucleare”, cioè non una singola tecnologia, ma un sistema energetico centralizzato e a favore dei grandi interessi industriali, evitando i processi di democrazia partecipativa e le autonomie locali attraverso decreti d’urgenza o procedure autorizzative speciali. title: L’Italia scende in piazza per la Palestina
content:
Sabato 10 ottobre tante piazze italiane si sono riempite dei colori della bandiera palestinese dando uno slancio a questo inizio di autunno di lotta.


Credits to

jujjio


All’appello internazionale e nazionale per una giornata di mobilitazione dal titolo “La fine del genocidio è la fine del sionismo” hanno risposto coordinamenti e comitati locali, collettivi, e in generale, una buona parte di popolazione che continua, seppur con ritmi diversi rispetto allo scorso autunno, ad avere uno sguardo lucido e netto sul genocidio in Palestina. Soprattutto riconoscendo l’esigenza fondamentale di scendere in strada e attivarsi con protagonismo.


I riflettori della stampa mainstream si sono spenti sulla guerra permanente voluta da Netanyahu e sul piano esplicitato ormai da tempo di sterminio programmato di una popolazione intera. Quello che però è davvero significativo, e apre una breccia di possibilità nella contrapposizione alla guerra e ai voleri dei governi occidentali, è il fatto che la capacità e l’irriducibilità della resistenza dei palestinesi è ciò che giunge come messaggio chiaro sino alle nostre latitudini. E non solo in Europa, ma in giro per il mondo ieri sono state decine e decine di migliaia le persone a riempire le piazze per la Palestina.

Il significato che la Palestina continua ad avere per la popolazione italiana, nella sua eterogeneità, è il fatto di dare la possibilità di raccogliere diverse istanze con una radice comune: sentirsi popolo che non vuole accondiscendere ai piani criminali che il governo ha per noi. Che la Palestina abbia saputo liberarci non è uno slogan, è sentimento comune di chi oggi sa che vuole prendere parte in un movimento generale chiaro e netto su parole d’ordine semplici: fine del genocidio, contro la guerra e il riarmo della società, con la resistenza dei popoli oppressi.


In questa fase in cui prende avvio la campagna elettorale quel che risulta chiaro in maniera diffusa è che non ci sono governi amici, chi si schiera con la Palestina è anche chi non intende affidarsi a chi conduce interessi nemici al popolo. Oggi si dà una discrimine forse inedita: la possibilità che chi vede il marcio della politica istituzionale assuma anche la necessità di rendersi protagonista di un processo di trasformazione.

title: Эррико Малатеста - Идеал и Реальность
content:
Автор

: Эррико Малатеста

Название

: Идеал и Реальность

Дата

: 1 февраля 1924

Источник

: Pensiero e Volontà, год 1-й, №3


ИДЕАЛ И РЕАЛЬНОСТЬ


 Оставим в стороне «философские» определения, то есть сложные, туманные... и бесплодные. Идеал означает: то, чего желают. Реальность означает: то, что есть.


 Специфически человеческой чертой является быть недовольным тем, что есть, всегда желать чего-то лучшего, стремиться к большей свободе, к большей силе, к большей красоте. Человек, который находил бы всё хорошим, который думал бы, что всё, что есть, должно быть таким, и не должно и не может измениться, и который спокойно приспосабливался бы, без борьбы, без протеста, без порыва к бунту, к положению, которое ему создают обстоятельства, был бы меньше, чем человеком: он был бы... растением, если вообще позволительно так говорить, не клевеща на растения.


 Но, с другой стороны, человек не может быть и не может делать всё, что хочет, потому что он детерминирован, принуждён не только грубой внешней природой, но и действием всех других людей, социальной взаимозависимостью

[1]

, которая, хочет он того или нет, связывает его с судьбой всего человеческого рода.


 Следовательно, нужно стремиться к тому, чего хочешь, делая то, что можешь.


 Тот, кто приспосабливался бы ко всему, был бы жалким существом, сравнимым, как я говорил, с растением. Тот же, кто полагал бы, что может делать всё, что хочет, не считаясь ни с волей других, ни со средствами, необходимыми для достижения цели, ни с обстоятельствами, в которых он находится, был бы просто ловцом облаков, обречённым быть вечно жертвой, не продвинув ни на шаг дело, которое ему дорого.


 Итак, проблема для нас, анархистов – поскольку цель этого нашего издания

[2]

 состоит в том, чтобы приносить посильную пользу анархическому движению, – проблема для нас, анархистов, которые рассматривают анархию не как прекрасные грезы, о которой мечтают при свете луны, а как способ индивидуальной и общественной жизни, который нужно реализовать для наибольшего блага всех, – проблема, говорим мы, состоит в том, чтобы направлять наши действия так, чтобы получать максимальный полезный эффект в различных обстоятельствах, которые история создаёт вокруг нас.


 Не следует игнорировать реальность; но если она плоха, нужно с ней бороться, используя все средства, которые сама реальность нам предоставляет.


 Когда разразилась мировая война, пагубные последствия которой пока ещё очевидны, – тогда в некоторых кругах, которые называли себя и, возможно, даже были ранее революционными, много говорили о «реальности». Все полусознательные люди, все те, кто искал почётный предлог, чтобы загладить свои юношеские заблуждения и примкнуть к любой кормушке, все уставшие, которым не хватало честного мужества объявить себя таковыми и удалиться в частную жизнь, – а таких было много среди социалистов и немало также среди анархистов, – приняли и проповедовали войну «потому что это был факт», опираясь на присоединение к этой поддержке войны некоторых благородных людей и кое-где, добросовестно, совращённые ошибочным пониманием истории и всей лживой пропагандой, поверили, что речь действительно идёт об освободительной войне, и участвовали в ней, расплачиваясь лично.


 И сегодня не недостаёт тех, кто присоединяется к фашизму «потому что это факт», и скрывают, и думают оправдать свою преданность и своё предательство, говоря о фашизме, как раньше о войне, что его цель революционна.


 Да, мировая война и «мир», который из неё последовал, – это реальность, как были реальностью все прошедшие войны, все массовые убийства и все торги народами. Реальность – фашистская дубинка, как была реальностью немецкая палка, «которая не укротила Италию!».


 К сожалению, реальностью являются также все угнетения, вся нищета, вся ненависть, все преступления, которые терзают, разделяют и унижают людей.


 Неужели же нужно всё принять, всему подчиниться, потому что такова ситуация, которую создала нам история?


 Весь человеческий прогресс состоит из борьбы против природных реалий и социальных реалий. А мы, желающие максимального прогресса, наибольшего возможного счастья для всех человеческих существ, осаждены и теснимы со всех сторон враждебными реалиями, и против этих реалий мы должны бороться. Но чтобы бороться с ними, мы должны их знать и учитывать.


 Анархия, чтобы восторжествовать или хотя бы просто продвигаться к своему торжеству, должна быть задумана не только как сияющий маяк, который освещает и притягивает, но и как нечто …

content:
Jeudi 15 octobre

Et si nos vies étaient beaucoup plus orientées par l'armée que nous ne le pensons

À partir d'expériences de vie, cette conférence s'intéresse à la manière dont les valeurs militaires irriguent notre société, notre économie et notre rapport au vivant.


20h30

?


Analyse de la fabrication d'un désir d'enfant et de ses échappatoires. (par Jane Sautière. Nullipare)De quoi est constitué mon désir d'enfant : d'où vient-il

 

? Quels besoins cache-t-il

 

?


Et si avoir ou ne pas avoir d'enfants n'était pas qu'une question individuelle

 

? Quels sont les enjeux sociaux et politiques qui régissent les désirs d'enfant

 

?


D'une éducation genrée qui prédispose à des rôles au stigmate de la vieille fille à chat, je cherche des voix d'émancipation à la sacro-sainte institution de la famille hétéronormée.


Je voudrais interroger l'ahurissant mystère de ne pas avoir d'enfant comme on interroge l'ahurissant mystère d'en avoir.


 Vendredi 16 octobre


18h30 – Les histoires d'une jeune femme indocile


De la méritocratie à l'éducation populaire et aux joyeuses expérimentations collectives (par Françoise)Éduquée et attirée par la douce voix de la méritocratie ,à 18 ans, j'ai bifurqué vers l'éducation populaire et plongé au cœur de joyeuses aventures collectives .


Aujourd'hui, je souhaite partager ce que j'ai compris de mes apprentissages dans ces espaces de coopération et donner l'envie et l'élan de s'engager dans des expérimentations collectives … Une nécessité pour rendre un autre monde possible

 

!


20h30 – Femmes en agriculture :

 le sexisme est dans le pré… le féminisme aussi

 

! (par Sandrine)


À partir de son expérience de paysanne engagée, Sandrine essaye de comprendre pourquoi les femmes sont systématiquement la variable d'ajustement dans les fermes. Pourquoi elles ne sont que 25% des chef-fes d'exploitation alors qu'elles sont 50% dans les filières d'enseignement agricole

 

? C'est quoi, être une femme dans l'agriculture en France en 2026

 

? Tentative de plaidoyer pour un féminisme paysan…


Samedi 17 octobre


14h30 - De rivières en abysses, le vertige d'une prise de conscience


Le voyage d'une femme vers l'éducation à l'environnement, son lien avec la santé, ses paradoxes et sa dimension politico-économique

; lutter pour construire ensemble un futur désirable

 

!

Conférence gesticulée sur l'exploitation associative, le racisme et les silences féministes autour des violences (par Angelica E.)Dans «

 

Consultation gratuite : la carte qu'on retourne jamais

 

», Angélica raconte comment une journée ordinaire — enfin, presque : sa voiture explose après qu'elle s'est garée sur une place de deal — vient faire remonter à la surface tout ce qu'elle taisait depuis longtemps. Ce jour-là, elle se rend à une réunion de bilan où elle découvre l'ampleur du laisser-aller de son équipe, se fait couper la parole par une collègue qui parle à sa place de son propre travail, et rentre chez elle en réalisant les dégâts sur sa voiture. C'est la goutte de trop : elle craque, s'effondre, et sera arrêtée un an et demi pour épuisement professionnel avant de quitter définitivement l'association. title: „Kinder des Zorns“ bekennt sich zu Brandstiftung in Marzahn
content:
Eine bisher unbekannte Gruppe hat am Montag wohl einen Stromausfall in Marzahn ausgelöst. In einem Schreiben gibt sie sich kapitalismuskritisch.


In der Nacht zu Montag sorgten Unbekannte mit einem Brandsatz an einer Kabelbrücke für einen kurzzeitigen Stromausfall in einem Gewerbepark in Marzahn. Durch die beschädigten Stromleitungen mussten 19 Gewerbebetriebe vorübergehend vom Stromnetz getrennt werden. Ab 9 Uhr morgens konnten sie laut Stromnetz Berlin wieder per Notstromaggregat versorgt werden.


Noch am selben Tag erschien ein Schreiben auf der linken Internetplattform Indymedia. Darin bekennt sich eine Gruppe namens „Kinder des Zorns“ zu der schweren Brandstiftung. Es scheint das erste Bekenntnis der Gruppe zu einer solchen Tat zu sein, zumindest unter diesem Namen. Der mutmaßlich vorsätzlich herbeigeführte Stromausfall galt laut dem Schreiben speziell den Unternehmen Swissbit Germany AG, Finetech und Emerson/Flexim an der Boxberger Straße.


Die Sabotage begründen die „Kinder des Zorns“ damit, dass die drei Unternehmen Dual-Use-Produkte fertigen. Solche Produkte werden sowohl in zivilen Bereichen als auch für militärische Zwecke verwendet. „Wir wollen die Abläufe kapitalistischer Ausbeutung wirksam und unmittelbar unterbrechen und den Pro­fi­teu­r*in­nen von Krieg und Umweltzerstörung spürbare wirtschaftliche Verluste zufügen“, begründet die Gruppe ihr Vorgehen. Zusätzlich solle mit der Aktion dem Image von Berlin als Investitionsstandort für Technologie und Rüstung nachhaltig geschadet werden.


Nach den massiven Auswirkungen für die Ein­woh­ne­r*in­nen in Berlins Südwesten durch den Anschlag auf eine Kabelbrücke in Lichterfelde im Januar habe die Gruppe die Entscheidung für die Sabotage der Stromleitungen „nicht leichtfertig getroffen“. Sie habe sich trotzdem für die Brandstiftung entschieden, weil andere Protest- und Aktionsformen gescheitert seien.


Abgestimmt auf „Verteidigungsprogramme“


Die Unternehmen Swissbit, Finetech und Emerson machen kein Geheimnis aus den Anwendungsgebieten ihrer Produkte. Swissbit stellt Speicherlösungen her, die besonderen Umwelteinflüssen trotzen können sollen und darüber hinaus über eine Verschlüsselung verfügen – abgestimmt auf „Verteidigungsprogramme“.


Finetech stellt Maschinen her, mit denen Teile für Halbleiter gefertigt oder repariert werden können sollen. Unter den Kundenanwendungen im Bereich „Verteidigung, Militär und Sicherheit“ listet das Unternehmen unter anderem Nachtsichtgeräte, Infrarotsensoren und Laserscanner. Emerson stellt Druck- und Temperatursensoren her, welche ihre Anwendung unter anderem in gepanzerten Fahrzeugen sowie der „Verteidigungsüberwachung“ finden sollen.


Laut einer Pressemitteilung der Polizei Berlin hat der für politische Strafsachen zuständige Staatsschutz des Landeskriminalamts die Ermittlungen übernommen. Eine Anfrage der taz, ob das Bekennerschreiben für authentisch gehalten wird und wie groß die Auswirkungen des Stromausfalls tatsächlich waren, beantwortete die Polizei bis Redaktionsschluss nicht.


passiert am 7.10.2016

author: Sebastian Lotzer
title: The Last Day of Summer – Für Achim / Postscriptum
content:
“I can see you in the morning when you go to school


Don’t forget your books, you know you’ve got to learn the golden rule


Your teacher tells you stop your playing, get on with your work


And be like Johnnie-Too-good, don’t you know he never shirks


He’s coming along


After school is over, you’re playing in the park


Don’t be out too late, don’t let it get too dark


They tell you not to hang around and learn what life’s about


And grow up just like them, won’t you let it work it out


And you’re full of doubt”


Supertramp – School


Mein Lieber, der letzte Tag des Sommers, jener Tag, der noch einmal alles verspricht und nichts hält – ist nun also zwei Tage her, und die Dunkelheit und die Kälte legen sich über dieses hoffnungslos verlorene Land. Der deutsche Herbst. Ich muss an die Szenen vom 27. Oktober 1977 auf dem Dornhaldenfriedhof denken, die Beisetzung von Jan, Gudrun und Andreas. Die Bullen in ihren Ledermänteln, die sofort geschichtliche Assoziationen hervorrufen, überall Straßensperren, Reiterstaffeln, das Rattern des Hubschraubers über den Gräbern. Trotzig bahnen Hunderte sich den Weg durch das Herbstlaub, “Mörder, Mörder” – Rufe, Festnahmen, Ausnahmezustand. Bis in den Tod hinein. Die Hippiefrau, die mit ihrer kleinen Tochter an der Hand nach der Beerdigung die kleine Straße vom Friedhof weg entlang geht, ab und zu bleibt sie stehen, wenn ein Auto vorbeikommt und hält den Daumen nach oben, in der Hoffnung mitgenommen zu werden. Die Trostlosigkeit, die Einsamkeit, und doch zugleich auch die vage Hoffnung in einer Szene – dass es weitergeht, dass das Leben immer einen Weg findet, auch wenn sie uns unter Beton und im Trakt begraben. 77 war die komplette Niederlage. Nicht nur der Illegalen, auch der restlichen radikalen Linken, einige Monate später kam TUNIX, noch einmal mit ein paar tausend Leuten durch die Berliner Innenstadt. Steine vor dem Knast und dem Amerikahaus, dann folgte der Diskurs, die Gründung der taz und der Grünen, Spontis wurden zu Abgeordneten und später Ministern, irgendwie überlebten die K-Gruppen noch ein paar Jahre. Dann war da nichts mehr. Nichts mehr.


Die Revolte der Jugendlichen in der Schweiz, den Niederlanden und in Deutschland 79/80 kam aus diesem Nichts. Den Schmerz, die Ohnmacht und die geschichtliche Niederlage hatten sie geerbt, auch wenn ihnen das gar nicht bewusst war. Ständig war deshalb von Beton und Eis in ihren Liedern und Parolen die Rede, es ging nicht mehr darum, eine Welt zu gewinnen, sondern sich im geschichtlichen Untergang trotzig und wütend auf die Hinterbeine zu stellen, ein letztes, mutiges Gefecht um der Würde und der alten Traditionen willen, in allen WGs und besetzten Häusern hingen Indianerbilder an den Wänden – eben “Begrabt mein Herz am Heinrichplatz”. Noch einmal die Unterdrücker und Kolonialisten einen blutigen Preis zahlen lassen. Von Wounded Knee 1977 zum perfekt konspirativ organisierten Plan, 36 zu einem selbstbestimmten Zeitpunkt komplett mit Barrikaden absperren und diese militant zu verteidigen, war es nur ein geschichtlicher Katzensprung – auch wenn dieser ebenso grandiose wie größenwahnsinnige Plan nie in die Realität umgesetzt wurde. Dann also doch wieder Diskurs und Verhandlungen – Spaltung und Verträge, noch heute leben Teile der “Szene” zu Mietpreisen, für die sie sich eigentlich zu Tode schämen müssten, während um sie herum die letzten Türken aus den Altbauten vertrieben werden und die Mieter in den angrenzenden Betonlöchern des sogenannten ehemaligen “sozialen Wohnungsbaus” das drei,-vier,-oder sogar fünffache an Miete im Monat blechen müssen. Alle lieben den Verrat, aber keiner die Verräter. Doch ich schweife ab.


Warum ich dir noch einmal schreibe..?! Du erinnerst dich an meinen Brief vom 12. September dieses Jahres? [1] Natürlich. Du hast nie etwas vergessen. Der “17. Oktober”, die vage Hoffnung auf die “Auferstehung” der Gilets Jaunes, die in Frankreich schon geradezu sakral verehrt werden. Es kommt erstens anders, und zweitens, als man denkt. Ich hatte die vage Ahnung, dass nach dem Hitzesommer, der in Frankreich weitaus dramatischer als hierzulande stattgefunden hatte, sich etwas unter der Oberfläche zusammenbraut, was im Herbst zum Ausbruch drängen würde. Ich hatte keine genaue Vorstellung davon, was und wie, aber wie bei einem alten Spürhund kribbelte es mir in der Nase. Doch ich hatte keine Ahnung, was nun kommen würde. Niemand hatte dies.


Angefangen hat alles am Lycée Saint-Exupéry in Créteil, wir erinnern uns: “Man …

title: Renewed ISIS attack in Hawija
content:
In recent days, ISIS militants have stepped up their activities in several areas and resumed attacks on Iraqi army forces along the border between the provinces of Kirkuk and Salahaddin.


Late last night, ISIS militants attacked an Iraqi army checkpoint in the village of Bur Xeliye, in the town of Denaniş on the outskirts of Hawija district in Kirkuk province.


Heavy clashes broke out between the two sides, and the militants were ambushed by security forces as they retreated. A number of militants were killed and wounded, while others managed to escape.


This was the third such attack carried out by ISIS militants along the same line.

title: Tree felling by village guards in Besta
content:
Uninterrupted tree felling has been ongoing for seven years in the Cûdî and Gabar mountains and the Besta region. As a result of this ecological devastation, a large part of the Besta region has been left barren.

It has been learned that the trees are being felled by village guards brought to the area from Hosyan village, in the Pervari (Berwarî) district of Siirt (Sêrt).

title: Sustam: Those who sow insecurity reap revolt in France - Part Two
content:
ANF spoke to Associate Professor Engin Sustam, a sociologist at Paris 8 University, about the causes of the student protests in France, their connection to the tradition of struggle stretching from 1968 to the present, and their potential to develop into a broader social opposition movement. 


Part one of this interview can be read

here

. 


France has a strong tradition of student and youth movements stretching from 1968 to the present. Where do you place today’s mobilization within this historical continuity? What distinguishes it from previous student movements?


Of course, we can place this mobilization, the involvement of high school students and the forms of protest within a historical context. The 1968 movement, as we know, began primarily in universities rather than high schools. The Sorbonne and later Paris 8 University, as a different kind of experience, became important centres of this process. We should not forget that there was a broader dynamic of revolt across the world at the time.


There was the Vietnam War and the protests against it, anti-militarist movements, as well as workers’ strikes that intensified with the transition to the post-industrial era after the Second World War and struggles against social injustice. The 1968 movement emerged within this context. Today, however, we are dealing with a different context.


To put it very clearly, we are now living in an era of fascism that has become entrenched in power and globalized. This is no longer a question of whether we have entered such a period or not. We are now living under the shadow of fascism, perhaps right at its centre. The rise of fascist movements, far-right governments and the policies of social injustice pursued by governments are seriously affecting the lives of university and high school students.


‘We are living under the shadow of fascism’


Today’s movement therefore has a historical background that can be traced back to 1968. But I am not sure whether it will produce a new 1968. We need to wait and see. It is far too early to make such an assessment or analysis.


I think there is another issue that is even more important. Police violence in France has increased disproportionately. Security-related legislation was adopted in the National Assembly last July in particular. The mechanisms of violence we are witnessing today should also be understood in this context. These regulations have made the police feel more empowered to use violence.


Placing all the violence, vandalism and clashes that have emerged alongside political mobilization in education solely on high school students is a discourse used only by the far right. But the far right does not look at the other side of this: it does not want to see how the state has armed itself or how state institutions and apparatuses have disproportionately become one of the forces driving urban violence.


One of the clearest examples of this came in the most recent municipal elections. A major controversy erupted after Bally Bagayoko was elected mayor of Saint-Denis. There was an uproar over a Black politician winning the election. This is the point France has reached. Racism has reached such a level that we are witnessing extraordinary forms of it.


For this reason, perhaps we need to look even further back than 1968. We are seeing the atmosphere of violence that existed before the Second World War re-emerge in different forms. The period from the 1920s to the 1940s saw historical experiences such as the emergence of fascism in Italy, the Franco regime, Hitler and the Gestapo. Today, we are confronting examples of this operating in different forms and on a more global scale.


All of these developments need to be considered together. I think the protests by high school students should be understood precisely from this perspective. We need to ask why this political and social anger cannot find another way to express itself.


Do you see the movement having the potential to extend beyond students and converge with trade unions, workers and other sections of society in the coming period? Trade unions are already protesting today. Could this movement develop into a broader opposition movement or produce a political rupture?


One thing is very clear: there is an election ahead. Serious polarization has already begun in France. There is an intense political conflict particularly between La France Insoumise (LFI) and Rassemblement National (RN), in other words, between the left …

title: Mining project in Kasor could trigger landslides and earthquakes, says report
content:
An expert report has been submitted to the case file in a lawsuit concerning the “Mineral Exploration Project Using Trenching and Drilling Methods,” planned by Kılıç Kardeşler Mining Construction Engineering and Project Services Industry and Trade Limited Company in the Kasor Basin, in the Kulp (Pasur) district of Diyarbakır (Amed). The report stated that the project area is classified as pastureland and lies within the Long-Distance Protection Zone of the Silvan Dam, highlighting various risks related to water resources, air emissions, landslides, erosion and biodiversity.


The expert report, prepared following an on-site inspection on 17 July 2026, stated that the environmental assessments and proposed measures for the project lacked sufficient technical justification across several areas of expertise.


An expert examination was conducted as part of a lawsuit filed before the Diyarbakır 1st Administrative Court seeking the annulment of the decision that an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) was not required. During the site inspection, the expert panel heard the parties' arguments, conducted observations and examinations of the project area, took photographs and documented its findings in the report.


The examinations carried out by experts from different fields concluded that the environmental assessments and proposed measures outlined in the project introduction file lacked sufficient technical justification.


The report particularly highlighted missing baseline data on water resources, the proximity of the project area to active landslide zones, earthquake risks, erosion and soil conditions, and potential impacts on habitats and biodiversity.


In its concluding section, the report found that the “EIA Positive” decision issued for the “Mineral Exploration Project Using Trenching and Drilling Methods” was not appropriate.


Mining activities could cause erosion


The mining engineering assessment stated that approximately 360 cubic metres of waste rock and ore were expected to be extracted from two trenching areas. However, due to the steep terrain, the project file did not specify any measures to prevent the extracted material from sliding or rolling downhill.


The report stated that an initial 0.5-metre layer of overburden would be removed and that no drilling or blasting operations would be carried out. Nevertheless, transportation activities during overburden removal and site levelling would generate dust, while the project file did not adequately set out measures to suppress or eliminate it.


The expert panel warned that, given the steep topography, allowing excavated waste material to move uncontrolled down the slopes could cause erosion. The report stated that settlements and agricultural land at lower elevations could be affected.


The report also highlighted the risk of waste material sliding on sloping terrain, warning that the failure to specify necessary protective measures could pose a danger to occupational safety.


The report stated that although the mineral exploration activities would be temporary, vegetation would be stripped from the trenching and drilling platforms. It also found that the project introduction file did not provide sufficient technical details of a concrete rehabilitation plan for filling in the trenches and restoring the land to its original condition after the activities were completed.


Water resources could be damaged


The expert report also drew attention to the proximity of the drilling sites to water sources that supply drinking and irrigation water in the region, as well as to meandering watercourses. It stated that the project introduction file did not adequately analyse the possibility of groundwater layers mixing during core drilling or damage to the aquifer structure. The report concluded that the project, in its current form, was inadequate in assessing the potential impacts of mining activities.


The environmental engineering assessment found that dust and exhaust emissions from transportation activities had not been adequately assessed. The report stated that dust calculations for the project covered only the transportation of materials within the site, while the impact of vehicle traffic along the 3.2-kilometre access road had not been taken into account.


It also stated that the amount of exhaust emissions from construction machinery and generators had not been established through a valid mass flow rate calculation.

title: Parlak: Framework Law must be formalized without delay
content:
As the process, brought into a new phase by the Call for Peace and a Democratic Society announced publicly by Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025, approaches its second year, attention has shifted to the practical steps to be taken following the adoption of the framework law by Parliament.


The Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration was adopted by the Grand National Assembly of Turkey on 10 August 2026, with 467 votes in favour. The bill stipulated that certain provisions could be implemented only after assessments by security institutions and confirmation of those assessments through a decision by the National Security Council (MGK).


Following the adoption of the framework law, a Monitoring and Evaluation Board and related bodies were established under the Presidency. Discussions continue over how to advance the process through lasting measures that build confidence.


DEM Party MP for Hakkari (Colemêrg), Vezir Coşkun Parlak, spoke to ANF about the process.


‘The National Security Council must fulfil its historic responsibility’


Parlak said that the overwhelming majority of MPs who voted in favour of the framework law had assumed a historic responsibility, and that the National Security Council (MGK) must demonstrate the same sense of responsibility. He added: “Just as the large majority in the Turkish Grand National Assembly that voted for the framework law fulfilled its historic responsibility, the National Security Council must also fulfil its responsibility without dragging the process out. Delaying the process and postponing a decision on bringing the law into force serves no purpose for Turkey.


On the contrary, this kind of delaying tactic could infect the process and make the work of circles seeking to sabotage it easier. If the National Security Council confines the Kurdish question solely to armed conflict and treats it merely as a security issue, this will be seen as a persistence in previous approaches. The MGK must not delay this historic step, which could open the way forward for Türkiye and shape the next hundred years of its future.”


‘The courage to confront the Kurdish question must be shown’


Pointing out that the National Security Council is among the leading institutions that must confront the Kurdish question on legal and political grounds, Parlak continued: “The National Security Council is among the foremost institutions that must first confront the Kurdish question on legal and political grounds. It must demonstrate the same courage shown by Parliament and have the courage to confront the Kurdish question at last. The MGK must properly assess the boldest step taken in the last hundred years by Öcalan, as well as the courageous response Devlet Bahçeli gave to it, and adopt an appropriate position.


One of the most important steps was the commission established in Parliament at Öcalan’s insistence. Through this commission, Öcalan brought a formal dimension to the talks he had been conducting with the state. By placing a historic responsibility on a parliament that had been rendered dysfunctional for years, he helped restore its functionality and enabled the will of the people to influence the process in a positive direction. With the framework law passing through Parliament by an overwhelming majority of 467 votes, the Kurdish question has, in Öcalan’s words, been brought onto a ‘legal and political footing’. The involvement of Parliament, the Presidency and other affiliated official institutions in the process has been an extremely important step. It has ensured that the state as a whole is involved in this issue.”


‘Öcalan must be recognized as a negotiating counterpart’


Parlak said that the Monitoring and Evaluation Board and its affiliated bodies, established under the framework law, were important for the practical implementation of the process. He drew attention to the responsibilities assigned to the Presidency.


Parlak said: “The establishment of the Monitoring and Evaluation Board under the Presidency, together with its four affiliated boards, in line with the framework law, marks the most important stage reached so far in making the work more practical and accelerating it. This is because direct responsibility has been assigned to the highest office of the state.

title: Now is a good time to start thinking about HOW to make this flop.
content:
Here’s a few known facts about the wizard school show and its creator:

Her net worth is somewhere in the region of $1.2 billion

The show’s budget is absurdly huge, with episodes estimated to have $100 million budgets and one set piece even being valued at $1.2 billion by itself. For comparison, the entire budget of Rings of Power was ~$150 million for an entire 16-episode season. This is 8.3% of her net worth per episode.

The creator is not footing that bill herself, Warner Bros is.

Warner Bros just went through one of the largest and most controversial corporate mergers in US history and is probably in some degree of economic chaos at the moment.

Warner Bros, more now than ever, is not going to settle for just breaking even on its investment. They’re going to want 3-5 times return, minimum.

Indomitable enemies seldom need to beg. WB has already made her issue a public statement because she was generating too much bad PR for the project. That means it’s a point of vulnerability.

Therefore, doing whatever you are able to make the show an utter flop might just ruin her financially. You have the chance to materially contribute to the destruction of a billionaire.

You are Technically correct, as I stated above the author likely isn’t going to get single-handedly dumpstered by this show cratering hard enough to kill the dinosaurs twice. It’s not her personal bill, though it performing poorly would negatively impact a bunch of different stock values that meaningfully contribute to her net worth.

This is presently the only media project based on her work, it is Incredibly expensive (even just by the more modest estimates of its budget, the above are widely-circulated guesses more than anything else), and despite her best efforts she has not once managed to come close to the success of the original. This is not new material, it’s an episodic rehash of what she wrote 20 years ago.

So, in the event that this collapses, she has nothing else. Her own vitriol has been damaging patronage to locations and merchandise sales for the last straight decade. If this show doesn’t take off, virtually no-one is going to greenlight more of the same exact property for another 10 years. She’ll be the Mister Blobby of mid-tier 90s juvenile fantasy novels.

Now you may rightly point out that I also cited her net worth as being $1.2 billion, which I’m sure I don’t have to say is more than any human on Earth needs to live the rest of their lives pretty cosy (and she’s only got another 30 at best).

But it will mean she can’t finance bigotry nearly as liberally anymore. No more stuffing money into lawsuit funds, no more financing political chaos, and no more Thanos-snapping anyone that dares obliquely denigrate her. Not overnight, certainly, but it will eventually make her bleed if she doesn’t stop.

Now is a good time to start thinking about HOW to make this flop.

There was a campaign in 2023 to make the video-game flop and that campaign failed completely. The game raised 17 times what it cost to make. That 17 times return on investment on the last big product is why Warner Bros believes the massive investments in the show are going to be worth it.

If all we do is talk online about how important it is to make sure this sho flops and how we will personally block anyone who mentions watching it - (so: if we do exactly what people were doing in 2023 and nothing more) - we will fail as badly as we failed in 2023. A better plan is necessary.
